children.translated_text: Homage to the venerable <s>Mahāgaṇādhipati</s>, the great lord of hosts.
Having bowed to the one skilled at protecting from the fear of worldly existence, he sets forth the <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>,
a commentary well fitted to the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>, one that reaches a straightforward meaning for those who approach it.
In the <s>Kurala</s> family, an ocean of virtues, there was <s>Hariharamiśra</s>, known for acknowledged greatness.

children.text: tatputro bhuvi mahito maheśa iti nāmavikhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His son, honored on earth, was famous by the name <s>Maheśa</s>.
In that lineage, joined with the spirit of learning, his son, a master through the words now presented,
<s>Caturbhuja</s>, whose mind was intent on understood meanings, acted through the inherited power born in his own line.

children.text: jyeṣṭho'bhūd bhuvi pārijātakataruḥ khaṇḍelavālānvaye tatputraḥ kila nāthaballavasudaḥ prāṇair yaśo'rthānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: The eldest, a pārijāta tree on earth in the <s>Khaṇḍelavāla</s> lineage, had a son, the beneficent <s>Nāthaballava</s>, endowed with life, fame, and wealth.

children.text: tatputreṇa ca sāvareṇa patinā bandhasya dharmārthinā gīrvāṇāśu rugoñcajena satataṃ tenātra yatnaḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By his son <s>Sāvara</s>, lord of the undertaking and seeking <s>dharma</s> and wealth, this effort was constantly made here, he being of the <s>Rugoñca</s> line and skilled in Sanskrit speech.

children.text: iha śāstrārambhe ācāryaśrīmadgovindapādāḥ śiṣṭasamayaparipālanārthe śāstrasya deśayato gurupādasya bhagavato vastunirdeśarūpaṃ maṅgalam ācaranti jayatītyādi ||
children.translated_text: Here, at the beginning of the treatise, the revered teacher <s>Govindapāda</s>, in order to observe the convention of the learned, performs the auspicious opening, in the form of indicating the subject matter, for the blessed guru who teaches the treatise, with the words beginning jayati.

children.text: maṅgalalakṣaṇaṃ yathā āśīr namaskriyā vastunirdeśo maṅgala iti ||
children.translated_text: The definition of an auspicious opening is as follows: blessing, an act of homage, and indication of the subject matter are called <s>maṅgala</s> (auspiciousness).

children.text: vastunirdeśaḥ pañcadhā yathāsti bhāti priyaṃ rūpaṃ nāma cetyaṃśapañcakam ||
children.translated_text: Indication of the subject matter is fivefold: being, shining, dearness, form, and name are the five parts.

children.text: ādyaṃ trayaṃ brahmarūpaṃ śaktirūpaṃ tato dvayam iti ||
children.translated_text: The first three are the form of <s>brahman</s>; the latter two are the form of <s>śakti</s>.
That <s>Hara</s> triumphs, that is, he exists in complete superiority.
The statement that he sees the whole world is an indication of the subject matter; it means that he is the seer.

children.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ apāṇipādo javano grahītā ||
children.translated_text: And so the <s>śruti</s> says: Without hands and feet, he is swift and a grasper.
He sees without eyes; he hears without ears.

children.text: sa vetti vedyaṃ na ca tasya vettā tamāhur agryaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam iti ||
children.translated_text: He knows what is to be known, and there is no knower of him; they call him the foremost, ancient Person.

children.text: yasya hṛdayasyaiva rasarūpiṇī karuṇā ghṛṇā jātā prādurbhūtā ||
children.translated_text: Compassion, which is of the nature of <s>rasa</s>, has arisen and manifested in his very heart.

children.text: kiṃbhūtvā galitvā dravitvā galitasya sthānāccyutir iti yuktam ||
children.translated_text: In what state? Having melted, having become fluid; for what has melted, displacement from its place is reasonable.
This compassion is situated in the heart alone.
The indeclinable eva expresses exclusion of any other place.
Rasarūpiṇī means: she whose own form is <s>rasa</s>, that is, <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
And there is a statement to this effect.

children.text: raso jalaṃ raso harṣo rasaḥ śṛṅgārapūrvakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> means water; <s>rasa</s> means joy; <s>rasa</s> is an aesthetic flavor beginning with the erotic.

children.text: svādvādiṣu ca niryāse pārade'pi raso viṣe
children.translated_text: Among tastes and the like it is sap or extract; it is also <s>rasa</s> in the sense of mercury and poison.
Thus it has many meanings.
In general its form is liquidity; in particular, as <s>rasa</s>, it is usefulness to all.
And so there is the statement in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
It is the one fire for burning away sins committed from birth, and it has the form of a lion against the elephant of poverty and suffering.

children.text: kiṃbhūtasya harasya dainyagadākulaṃ jagat saṃsāraṃ paśyataḥ dainyayaṃ ca gadāśca tair ākulaṃ vyāptaṃ dainyaṃ dīnabhāvo dāridryaṃ gadā vyādhaya iti ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind is <s>Hara</s>? He sees the world of transmigration, the whole world, afflicted by wretchedness and disease; it is filled with wretchedness and diseases. Wretchedness is lowliness and poverty, and diseases are illnesses.
Akhila is a word denoting all-inclusiveness.
As in the <s>Mañjarī</s>:

children.text: yasya rogasya yo yogastenaiva saha dāpayet
children.translated_text: Whatever preparation is proper for a disease, one should administer it together with that very one.
The lord of <s>rasa</s>, <s>Hara</s>, removes the diseases of men, elephants, and horses.
So it says.
And another opinion says:
The sequence of the compendium is stated there even without explicit mention of <s>rasa-bhasma</s> (mercurial ash).
Even what is not stated should be understood there in each case for the pacification or treatment of the limb.
So it says.
Now the word beginning with pīta is taken up.

children.text: anena padyena kavirharajasya hareśca samatvaṃ sūcayati ||
children.translated_text: By this verse the poet suggests the equivalence of <s>haraja</s> (that which is born of <s>Hara</s>) and <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: sa purāṇakavivarṇito harajo jayati sarvotkarṣeṇa vartate harādīśvarājjāto harajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>haraja</s>, described by the ancient poets, triumphs, existing in complete superiority; what is born from <s>Hara</s>, the Lord, is <s>haraja</s>.
It is imagined as <s>Hari</s>, that is, like <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: kiṃbhūto hariḥ pītāmbaraḥ pīte ambare vastre yasya saḥ dukūlayugmatvāt ||
children.translated_text: What kind of <s>Hari</s>? He is pītāmbara, yellow-robed, one whose garments are yellow, because there are two fine cloths.

children.text: punaḥ kimbhūto balijit baliṃ balināmānaṃ daityaviśeṣaṃ jayatīti tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, what kind? He is balijit, so called because he conquers <s>Bali</s>, the particular demon named <s>Bali</s>.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃbhūtaḥ nāgakṣayetyādi nāgānāṃ śeṣādīnāṃ kṣayāya nāśāya bahalarāgo bahuprīto yo 'sau garuḍaḥ khageśvaraḥ tatra carati gacchati tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, what kind? The phrase beginning nāgakṣaya means: <s>Garuḍa</s>, lord of birds, who is intensely eager for the destruction of serpents such as <s>Śeṣa</s>, moves there; therefore he is so called.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ vidalitetyādiḥ viśeṣaṇena dalito dūrīkṛto bhavasya saṃsārasya duḥkhabharo yena saḥ dainyaṃ dāridryaṃ duḥkhaṃ vyādhirūpaṃ tayorbharo bāhulyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Again, what is he qualified by? By the phrase beginning vidalita: he by whom the heavy burden of suffering from worldly existence has been split apart and removed. Dainya is poverty or suffering, and disease-form suffering; their bhara is abundance.

children.text: adhunā harajaṃ viśeṣayati kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ pītāmbaraḥ pītāmbaraḥ pūrvārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now he qualifies <s>haraja</s>: What is it like? It is pītāmbara, yellow-robed; the preceding meaning of pītāmbara applies.

children.text: kathaṃ yuktaḥ tamarthe spaṣṭayatyanena sūtarājenāpi catvāri vāsāṃsi dhṛtāni viprādivarṇabhedāt ||
children.translated_text: How is that fitting? He clarifies the matter: even this king <s>Sūta</s> (mercury) wears four garments according to the distinction of brāhmaṇa and the other classes.
As in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
White, red, yellow, and black are the <s>pāradas</s> (mercuries) for brāhmaṇa and the other classes.

children.text: brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāḥ śvetaraktapītakṛṣṇavastradhāriṇo jñātavyāḥ na tv eṣāṃ svarūpam iti ||
children.translated_text: The brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra varieties should be known as wearing white, red, yellow, and black garments respectively; that, however, is not their essential nature.
As in the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>:

children.text: antaḥ sunīlo bahirujjvalo yo madhyāhnasūryapratimaprakāśaḥ iti ||
children.translated_text: That which is deep blue within and bright without, shining like the midday sun...
According to tradition, the inner part is its own nature and the outer parts are its garments.
The word atha has the sense of conjunction; prasāda means clarity or favor.
Atha is used for what follows an auspicious act, for beginning, question, time, one's own authority, declaration, and conjunction.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ balijit balīn jayatīti baliścarma jarākṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Again, what is he qualified by? Balijit: it conquers the balis; bali means skin altered by old age.
Thus it has many meanings.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ nāgakṣayetyādi nā puṃsvarūpaḥ punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ gamyate 'neneti gaḥ pakṣayor gaḥ gakṣaye pakṣanāśe sati bahalarāgo bahurāgavān yaḥ sa rasaḥ tena garuḍa iva cāryate iti ||
children.translated_text: Again, what is it distinguished by? By the expression beginning with 'the destruction of nāga.' 'Nā' is in a masculine form. Again, what further is meant? 'Ga' means 'that by which one goes'; it is 'ga' with respect to the two wings. When there is a destruction of that going by the wings, the <s>rasa</s> (mercurial elixir) that then has intense color or passion is made to move by it like <s>Garuḍa</s>.

children.text: kiṃ pāradaḥ pakṣanāśe sati ākāśagamanaṃ dadātīti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intended sense is this: does <s>pārada</s> (mercury), when its wings have been destroyed, grant movement through the sky?
As in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
When killed it kills old age and death; when stupefied, it destroys diseases.

children.text: datte ca khe gatiṃ baddhaḥ ko 'nyaḥ sūtāt kriyākaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When bound, it grants movement in the sky. What other agent is there besides <s>sūta</s> (mercury)?
Thus.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ vidalitetyādiḥ pūrvārthaḥ karuṇāparatvena dainyaduḥkhahāritvaṃ sūcayati ||
children.translated_text: Again, what sort is it? The phrase beginning 'split apart' has the previous meaning; by saying that it is intent on compassion, it indicates that it removes misery and pain.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvaviśiṣṭo harajas tasmādanyaḥ karuṇāparo dayāvān kaḥ na ko 'pi yato rujaṃ śarīravyathāṃ harati ||
children.translated_text: What other being, apart from the previously described <s>harajas</s> (Śiva-born mercury), is more compassionate and merciful? There is no one, because it removes <s>ruj</s>, bodily pain.
After becoming what? After being stupefied; that is, after it has become <s>mūrchita</s> (stupefied mercury).
The definition of <s>mūrchita</s> is given in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
When <s>sūta</s> has the appearance of lampblack, having given up its dense volatility,
then the wise should know that king of <s>sūta</s> to be <s>mūrchita</s>.
Thus.

children.text: punarbandhanamanubhūya dhṛtvā muktido bhavati muktiṃ dadātīti ||
children.translated_text: Again, after undergoing and taking on binding, it becomes a giver of liberation; that is, it grants liberation.
Liberation is described as fourfold, divided into <s>sālokya</s>, <s>sārūpya</s>, <s>sāmīpya</s>, and <s>sāyujya</s>.

children.text: bandhanaṃ ca mukhyatayā dvividham avāntaravyāpāreṇa ca caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: And <s>bandhana</s> (binding) is principally twofold, while by secondary operation it is fourfold.
Now the statement of the twofold binding: it is <s>nirbījabaddha</s> (bound without seed) and <s>bījabaddha</s> (bound with seed).
<s>Nirbījabaddha</s>, as in the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>:
Mercury that has digested a quarter-part of gold and has been triturated with the addition of sulfur,
then successively heated with equal portions of sulfur, is called <s>nirbīja</s> and removes all diseases.
Thus.
Again, <s>bījabaddha</s> is as follows:
That which is prepared together with seeds made from <s>abhrasattva</s>, gold, silver, <s>arka</s>, and <s>kānta</s>,
and is then combined with sixfold sulfur powder, has still greater power even in the <s>bījabaddha</s> state.
Thus.
The statement of the secondary fourfold binding is as follows:

children.text: poṭaḥ khoṭo jalaukā ca bhasmatvaṃ ca caturvidham
children.translated_text: <s>Poṭa</s>, <s>khoṭa</s>, <s>jalaukā</s>, and the state of ash are the four kinds.
The binding of <s>sūta</s> should be known by the best physicians as fourfold.
Thus.
Their definition is given in the <s>Saṃketakalikā</s>:
<s>Poṭa</s> is the <s>parpaṭī</s>-binding, while the hardening of the paste is <s>khoṭaka</s>.

children.text: dhmāto druto bhavetkhoṭas tv āhataścūrṇatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: The <s>khoṭa</s>, when heated by blowing, becomes melted; when struck, it turns to powder.

children.text: punardhmāto drutaḥ khoṭa iti khoṭasya lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: When heated again it melts: that is <s>khoṭa</s>. This is the definition of <s>khoṭa</s>.
<s>Jalaukā</s> is the strip-binding, and ash should be like ash.
Thus.
Again, when it is well 'dead,' it makes one immortal.

children.text: sumṛta iti suḥ iti pūjāyāṃ yathā vidagdhamukhamaṇḍanabahirlāpikāyām
children.translated_text: In the word <s>sumṛta</s>, 'su' is in the sense of praise, as in the <s>Vidagdhamukhamaṇḍanabahirlāpikā</s>:

children.text: pūjāyāṃ kiṃ padaṃ proktam astanaṃ ko bibhartyuraḥ
children.translated_text: What word is stated in the sense of reverence? What does the breast bear, though it is not a breast?
What is famed as the weapon of the enemy of <s>Pralambāsura</s>?
'<s>Sunāsīra</s>' means 'venerable.'
The word 'dead' has a special meaning here.
'Dead' is as follows:

children.text: ārdratvaṃ ca ghanatvaṃ ca cāpalyaṃ gurutaijasam
children.translated_text: Moistness, density, volatility, heaviness, and fiery brilliance:
when these are not present in it, one should know that <s>sūtaka</s> to be dead mercury.
Thus.
On its being venerable, as in the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>:

children.text: abaddhasūtaṃ tu hataṃ pramādāt karoti kaṣṭaṃ prabalaṃ rasendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Unbound <s>sūta</s>, if killed through negligence, brings about intense distress, O lord of <s>rasa</s>.
Thus.

children.text: mūrchanādibandhanaparamparayā yo mṛtaḥ sa pūjyo nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: The one that has become dead through the sequence beginning with stupefaction and binding is venerable, not otherwise.
And as in the <s>Rasamañjarī</s>:

children.text: ajīrṇaṃ cāpyabījaṃ ca sūtakaṃ yastu ghātayet
children.translated_text: Whoever kills <s>sūtaka</s> that is undigested and without seed

children.text: brahmahā sa durācārī mama drohī maheśvari ||
children.translated_text: is a brahman-killer, a man of bad conduct, and a betrayer of me, O <s>Maheśvarī</s>.
Thus this meaning is appropriate.
Being intent on compassion is the nature of good people.
As follows:

children.text: chede'pi candanataruḥ surabhayati mukhaṃ kuṭhārasya iti ||
children.translated_text: Even when cut, the sandalwood tree perfumes the face of the axe.
The phrase beginning with 'gods' and so on is now explained.

children.text: tasmāt sūtarājāt anyo dvitīya pavitratara atiśayena pavitraḥ kaḥ kila śrūyate na ko 'pi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, what other than the king <s>sūta</s>, a second thing still purer and supremely purifying, is ever heard of? There is none at all.

children.text: yasmāddhetoḥ apīti niścayena asādhyaṃ rujaṃ śamayati sarvarūpānvitamasādhyaṃ divyauṣadhibhir api karmavipākenāpi sādhyate tacca kiṃviśiṣṭam asādhyaṃ suretyādiḥ surāś ca guravaś ca gāvaś ca dvijāś ca teṣāṃ yā hiṃsā hananam avamānanaṃ vātād utpanno yaḥ pāpakalāpo duṣkṛtapaṭala etasmād udbhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: For this reason it certainly pacifies even an incurable disease, one marked by every form and not curable even by divine medicines or by the ripening of karma. What is that incurable disease like? It begins with the word 'gods': it arises from a mass of sins produced by harming, killing, or insulting gods, teachers, cows, twice-born people, and the like.
The phrase beginning 'of that' is next.
By this inference the poet makes the matter accepted in common understanding.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sūtarājas tasya ko 'pyanirvacanīyaḥ sa sarvadeśīyatvena śāṃkaraḥ prādurbhāvaḥ śamayatīti duḥkhamupaśamayatīti śaṃ prasādaḥ śaṃ karotīti śaṃkaraḥ tasyāyaṃ śāṃkaraḥ duḥkhopaśamāyāyaṃ prādurbhavatīti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of that previously mentioned king <s>sūta</s> there is some indescribable manifestation belonging to <s>Śaṃkara</s>, because it is found everywhere. It pacifies, that is, alleviates suffering. 'Śam' means grace; one who makes <s>śam</s> is <s>Śaṃkara</s>; what belongs to him is <s>śāṃkara</s>. The intended meaning is that this manifestation occurs for the alleviation of suffering.
Suffering is twofold as mental affliction and disease; again, through the divisions of <s>ādhibhautika</s>, <s>ādhidaivika</s>, and <s>ādhyātmika</s>, it is threefold.

children.text: sa punarasya sūtarājasya svayaṃ sphurati prakāśata iti ||
children.translated_text: And that manifestation itself shines forth and becomes evident in this king <s>sūta</s>.

children.text: anyathā anyaprakāreṇa śāṃkaraprādurbhāvaṃ vinā pāparujaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ suragurugodvijahiṃsāpāpakalāpodbhavaṃ kathaṃ śamayati ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, without a manifestation belonging to <s>Śaṃkara</s>, how could it pacify sinful disease, leprosy, born from the mass of sins caused by harming gods, teachers, cows, and twice-born people?
Why? Because merely by shining forth it becomes an object of sight.
As in the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>:
The merit obtained by performing a hundred horse-sacrifices, by giving ten million cows, and by giving ten million lordly elephants...
A man obtains merit equal to the gift of gold and land by seeing <s>sūta</s> (mercury). Thus it says.

children.text: mūrchitabaddhamṛtasyāvasthayā trividhaṃ sūtarājasya bandhanaṃ praśaṃsati kaviḥ rasa ityādi ||
children.translated_text: The poet praises the binding of <s>Sūtarāja</s> (king Mercury), which is threefold according to the states of being stupefied, bound, and dead, with the words beginning 'rasa ...'.

children.text: bho janāḥ rasabandhaḥ pāradabandhanaṃ dhanyaḥ yasya prārambhe satataṃ nirantaraṃ karuṇā jāyata iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O people, blessed is <s>rasabandha</s> (the binding of rasa), that is, the binding of mercury; at its beginning, compassion is constantly and uninterruptedly produced. This is to be supplied.

children.text: kiṃrūpā ahaṃ govindanāmā rase siddhe sati samyagbandhanatvaṃ prāpte sati mahīṃ medinīṃ nirjarāmaraṇaṃ yathā tathā kariṣye ||
children.translated_text: Of what form is it? 'I, named <s>Govinda</s>, when the <s>rasa</s> has been perfected, that is, when proper binding has been attained, shall make the earth free from old age and death.'
Because of very close proximity, the present tense itself is used, namely the affix <s>laṭ</s>.
'Free from old age and death' is an adverbial qualifier of the action.

children.text: jarā pālityaṃ maraṇaṃ prāṇatyāga ābhyāṃ rahitaṃ yathā mahyāṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ na yuktam ||
children.translated_text: Old age is greying; death is the abandonment of the vital breath. It means 'free from these two,' since old age and death are not fitting on earth.

children.text: atra mahīpadena mahīmadhikṛtya nivasanti ye manujādayas ta eva lakṣaṇāvṛttitvāt ||
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'earth,' through secondary signification, the intended referents are precisely human beings and the like who live upon the earth.
Again, through the power of <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative alchemy), the prevention of old age is reasonable.
As in the <s>Hitopadeśa</s>:
That medicine which destroys old age and disease is <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: ādye vayasi madhye vā śuddhakāyaḥ samācared
children.translated_text: A person whose body has been purified should practice it in early age or in middle age.
Thus it says.

children.text: maraṇaniṣedhaḥ kathamauṣadhena anyauṣadhiśaktihrāsato na yuktaḥ raseśvaraśaktyādhikyād yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How can the prevention of death be effected by medicine? It is not reasonable through other medicines, because their power diminishes; but it is reasonable through the superiority of the power of <s>Raseśvara</s> (the lordly mercury).
As in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:

children.text: mṛtyorjarāviṣadharasya ca vainateya tubhyaṃ namāmi suravanditasūtarāja
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūtarāja</s>, honored by the gods, O <s>Vainateya</s> against death, old age, and the poison-bearing serpent, I bow to you.
Thus it says.
What superiority is there in the negation of old age and death? He states it with 'those who ...' and so on.
Those who are accomplished in such <s>rasa</s> are worthy of reverent salutation and praise.
The verbal root <s>vad</s> is used in the senses of salutation and praise.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā atyaktaśarīrāḥ na tyaktaṃ śarīraṃ yaiste jīvanmuktā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind are they? They are 'ones who have not abandoned the body': those by whom the body has not been abandoned. The meaning is that they are <s>jīvanmuktas</s> (liberated while living).

children.text: śarīraṃ dvividhaṃ sthūlasūkṣmabhedāt pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśātmakaṃ sthūlaṃ kośatrayātmakaṃ sūkṣmam ||
children.translated_text: The body is twofold, divided into gross and subtle: the gross is made of earth, water, fire, air, and ether, while the subtle is made of the three sheaths.
As in the sūtra:

children.text: vijñānamayaṃ manomayaṃ prāṇamayam etat kośatrayaṃ militaṃ sūkṣmaśarīramutpadyate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vijñānamaya</s>, <s>manomaya</s>, and <s>prāṇamaya</s>: when this triad of sheaths is joined together, the subtle body comes into being.
According to others, this alone is the subtle body.
And <s>rasa</s>-siddhas who have not abandoned the body are named:
<s>Manthānabhairava</s> the yogin, <s>Siddhabuddha</s>, and <s>Kanthaḍī</s>,
<s>Koraṇṭaka</s>, <s>Surānanda</s>, <s>Siddhapāda</s>, and <s>Carpaṭī</s>;
<s>Kaṇerī</s>, <s>Pūjyapāda</s>, <s>Nityanātha</s>, and <s>Nirañjana</s>,
<s>Kapālī</s>, <s>Bindunātha</s>, <s>Kākacaṇḍīśvara</s>, and <s>Gaja</s>;
<s>Āllama Prabhudeva</s>, <s>Ghoḍācolī</s>, and <s>Ṭhiṇṭhinī</s>,
<s>Bhāluki</s>, <s>Nāgadeva</s>, <s>Khaṇḍī</s>, and likewise <s>Kāpālika</s>;
these and other great siddhas, by the favor of the enjoyment of <s>rasa</s>,
having broken the staff of Time, wander through the three worlds.
Thus it says.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ tanuṃ prāptāḥ śarīraṃ grahītāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what sort are they? They have obtained a body, that is, they are takers-on of a body.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāṃ tanuṃ haragaurīsṛṣṭijāṃ haro mahādevaḥ gaurī pārvatī tayoḥ sṛṣṭiḥ sarjanaṃ maithunasaṃyogas tajjātā putrā evetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of body? One born from the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>: <s>Hara</s> is <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Gaurī</s> is <s>Pārvatī</s>; their creation, or generation, is sexual union, and those born from it are sons. This is the meaning.

children.text: punaryeṣāṃ mantragaṇāḥ kiṃkarāḥ mantrasamūhā ājñākarā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, groups of mantras are their servants: collections of mantras act according to their commands. This is the meaning.

children.text: tāvaditi sākalye yāvattāvad ityetau sākalyāvadhimānavadhāraṇeṣv iti prasādataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The word 'tāvat' denotes totality; by the rule that 'yāvat' and 'tāvat' occur in totality, limit, measure, and determination, this meaning is obtained.

children.text: idaṃ sukṛtaphalaṃ suvihitakarmaphalam idaṃ kiyat sukṛte śubhānvaye janma svatantrā dhīḥ svādhīnabuddhir ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the fruit of merit, the fruit of well-performed action. How much is this? Birth in a good lineage, and an independent intellect, that is, self-governed understanding.
The word 'api' means certainty.

children.text: sā buddhiḥ sakalamahītalatulanaphalā sakalasya niravaśeṣasya mahītalasya tulanaṃ phalaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā ||
children.translated_text: That intellect has as its fruit the weighing of the entire surface of the earth; 'entire' means without remainder, and it is so called because the weighing of the earth's surface is its fruit.

children.text: tulanam iti tulayā svatantrabuddhirūpayā sakalamahītalasya tulanaṃ bhavatyeveti yuktaṃ kimākārā kiyanmānā kaiḥ śritā kair dhṛtā ca bhūr iti jyotiṣasiddhāntavidhānād adṛṣṭāntā bhūr buddhyopalakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: It is indeed fitting that, by the scale in the form of independent intellect, the whole surface of the earth is weighed. What is its form, what is its measure, by whom is the earth inhabited, and by whom is it supported? Because of the teachings of astronomical doctrine, the earth, though without a comparable example, is apprehended by the intellect.

children.text: punaḥ sukulajanmasvatantrabuddhibhyāṃ bhūtalaṃ suvidheyaṃ pūjyaṃ jñātavyam ||
children.translated_text: Again, by birth in a good family and by independent intellect, the surface of the earth should be made amenable, honored, and known.

children.text: ekadeśagrahaṇāt sarvaṃ grāhyaṃ mahāntastokā bhūtalaṃ bahu īdṛśā mahānto yatra tiṣṭhanti tatsthānaṃ pūjyaṃ vettumaśakyatvāt sarvamiti ||
children.translated_text: Since a part is mentioned, the whole is to be understood. Great persons are few and the surface of the earth is vast; because it is impossible to know the place where such great persons reside, all of it is meant.
The connection with birth in a good family is explained with the words beginning 'bhūtala ...'.

children.text: bhūtalavidheyatāyāḥ bhūtale pṛthivīmaṇḍale yā vidheyatā sarvakarmapravīṇatā tasyā arthāḥ kāryāṇi kathaṃbhūtāḥ vividhabhogaphalāḥ vividhāśca te bhogāśca vividhabhogāḥ nānābhogāḥ phalaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The purposes of amenability on earth, that is, the works belonging to skill in every action on the earth's surface, the terrestrial sphere, are of what kind? They have various enjoyments as their fruit; because those enjoyments are diverse and manifold, they are described as having various enjoyments as their fruit.
They are the fruit, that is, in the form of fruit.
Enjoyments exist, that is, come to be, in the body.

children.text: kutaḥ yato vedāntasūtraṃ prārabdhakarmaphalabhogāyatanaṃ śarīram iti ||
children.translated_text: Why? Because the <s>Vedāntasūtra</s> says, 'The body is the seat for experiencing the fruit of already-begun karma.'
For this very reason, the body is the support of enjoyments.
The word 'aho' indicates distress or wonder.
The intended meaning is that this body is indeed the most excellent of all.
For there is the saying, 'That liberation comes when the body falls.'

children.text: sarvasādhanaṃ śarīraṃ matvābhimataṃ diśati bho janāḥ sadā sarvasmin kāle aharniśaṃ yatanīyam kiṃ kṛtvā dhanaśarīrabhogān anityān naśvarān matvā yatanīyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Having considered the body to be the means for everything, he gives the desired instruction: O people, one should always strive, at every time, day and night, after considering wealth, the body, and enjoyments to be impermanent and perishable. Thus one should strive.

children.text: kiṃ yathā śarīraṃ nityasthāyi bhavati śarīre nitye sarvaṃ nityam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is meant? Just as the body becomes permanently abiding; when the body is permanent, everything is permanent. This is the meaning.

children.text: tasya śarīrasya nityasya jñānāt sarvotkṛṣṭenānenaiva śarīraṃ nityaṃ bhaved ityavabodhāt tasyaivābhyāsācca muktir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Liberation comes from knowledge of that eternal body, from the understanding that by this very best means the body would become eternal, and from the practice of that very thing.
When what is present? When the body is stable.

children.text: manaso dharmaiḥ śarīrāśritaiḥ ṣaṅkikāraś ca dehāsthiratvam etanniṣedhatvaṃ dehasthiratvaṃ mokṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Instability of the body consists in the mind's qualities that depend on the body and in the six transformations; the negation of this is stability of the body, and that is liberation.
The teacher's statement to <s>Rāma</s> says just this:

children.text: na mokṣo nabhasaḥ pṛṣṭhe na pātāle na bhūtale
children.translated_text: Liberation is not on the back of the sky, nor in the netherworld, nor on earth.

children.text: sarvāśāsaṃkṣayaś cetaḥ śamo mokṣam itīkṣate iti ||
children.translated_text: The complete extinction of all hopes and the calming of the mind are regarded as liberation.

children.text: tasya dehasya sthairyeṇa sthirabhāvena kṛtvā rasāyanaṃ jarāvyādhināśanaṃ prati samarthaṃ kārakataram ||
children.translated_text: Through the firmness of that body, having made it stable, <s>rasāyana</s> is capable, indeed especially effective, for destroying old age and disease.
The word api means certainty, "indeed."

children.text: kiṃ sūtalohādiḥ sūtaḥ pāradaḥ lohāḥ svarṇādayo navakāḥ kṛtrimākṛtrimabhedayuktāḥ rājarītikharparīghoṣāḥ kṛtrimāḥ svarṇatāratāmranāgavaṅgalohā akṛtrimāḥ ādiśabdānmahārasā uparasāśca jñātavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: What are <s>sūta</s>, metals, and the rest? <s>Sūta</s> is mercury. The metals, beginning with gold, are nine, divided into artificial and natural kinds. <s>Rājarīti</s>, <s>kharparī</s>, and <s>ghoṣā</s> are artificial; gold, silver, copper, lead, tin, and iron are natural. By the word "and the rest," the <s>mahārasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s also should be understood.
What, then, are these? In the <s>Rasāvatāra</s> they are as follows:
<s>Hiṅgūla</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>vimala</s>, <s>acala</s>, <s>sasya</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>pakṣipati</s> are the <s>mahārasa</s>s.
<s>Sauvīra</s>, <s>gandhaka</s>, <s>śilā</s>, <s>laviraṅga</s>, <s>dhātu</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and <s>kāṅkṣī</s> are said by knowers of rasa to be the <s>uparasa</s>s.

children.text: athavā sthairyeṇa samarthe tat dehaṃ prati rasāyanaṃ kiṃ sūtalohādi ||
children.translated_text: Or, when the body has been made capable through stability, what is the <s>rasāyana</s> for that body? It is <s>sūta</s>, metals, and the rest.

children.text: sūte yadabhivyāptaṃ grāsamānena lohādi tattathoktaṃ sūte iti abhivyāpake ||
children.translated_text: The metal and so on that is fully pervaded in <s>sūta</s>, according to the measure of the swallowed portion, is described in that way; in the expression "in <s>sūta</s>," the locative denotes the pervader.
The seventh case ending is used in the sense of a locus.

children.text: taddehaṃ svayamasthiram asthirībhāvatvabhāvaṃ punar dāhyaṃ dagdhuṃ śakyaṃ punaḥ kledyam ārdrībhāvena śīrṇayituṃ śakyaṃ punaḥ śodhyaṃ śoṣayitum agnijalānilaiḥ dāhyaṃ kledyaṃ śoṣyaṃ ca śarīramityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That body itself is unstable, subject to becoming unstable; again it is burnable, capable of being burned; again it is moisturable, capable of being made to decay by wetness; and again it is dryable, capable of being dried by fire, water, and wind. Thus the body is burnable, moisturable, and dryable.

children.text: sūtalohādinā dehamanityaṃ nityaṃ bhavet ayameva yatna iti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By <s>sūta</s>, metals, and the rest, the impermanent body should become permanent. This alone is the effort intended.

children.text: pūrvaśloke sūtalohādikamuktaṃ tatrādhivyāpakādhikaraṇasya kramaṃ darśayati kāṣṭhauṣadhya ityādi ||
children.translated_text: In the preceding verse <s>sūta</s>, metals, and the rest were mentioned; with regard to that, he shows the order of the pervading locus with "woody herbs" and so on.

children.text: kāṣṭhauṣadhyaḥ kumārikādayaḥ nāge līyante tannāgaṃ vaṅge līyate tadvaṅgamapi śulbe tāmre līyate tacchulbaṃ tāre līyate tattāraṃ rūpyaṃ kanake suvarṇe līyate tatkanakaṃ sūte pārade līyate iti ||
children.translated_text: Woody herbs, such as <s>kumārikā</s>, dissolve in <s>nāga</s>, lead; that <s>nāga</s> dissolves in <s>vaṅga</s>, tin; that <s>vaṅga</s> also dissolves in <s>śulba</s>, copper; that <s>śulba</s> dissolves in <s>tāra</s>, silver; that <s>tāra</s>, silver, dissolves in <s>kanaka</s>, gold; and that <s>kanaka</s> dissolves in <s>sūta</s>, mercury.

children.text: kathaṃ līyate vidhānata ekaikena yuktaṃ samudāyenāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: How does it dissolve? According to rule, joined with each one individually and also with the aggregate.

children.text: dhātūnām arivargatvān mahārasoparasānām api yogam apiśabdāśca ||
children.translated_text: Because the metals belong to the group of antagonists, and because there is also a conjunction of the <s>mahārasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s, the words api are used.
He describes it in aggregate form with "in the supreme self" and so on.

children.text: asau eko dhātvādyantarbhūto rasarājaḥ śarīramajarāmaraṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitaṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: This one <s>rasarāja</s>, included among the metals and other substances, makes the body free from old age and death, devoid of aging and dying.

children.text: rasair mahārasoparasair antarbhūto rājate śobhate vā prakāśate iti rasarājaḥ athavā raseṣu mahārasoparaseṣu anādarībhūteṣu satsu rājata iti viśeṣārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>rasarāja</s> because, included among the rasas, <s>mahārasa</s>s, and <s>uparasa</s>s, it shines, is splendid, or becomes manifest. Or, in a special sense, it is so called because it is resplendent when the rasas, <s>mahārasa</s>s, and <s>uparasa</s>s are disregarded.

children.text: tathā ca sūtraṃ ṣaṣṭhīsaptamyau cānādare iti athavā rasānāṃ mahārasoparasadhātūnāṃ rājā teṣu mukhyatvenopadiṣṭaḥ mukhyatvenāsya grahaṇamityupalakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Accordingly there is the grammatical rule: the genitive and locative may also express disregard. Or, it is the king of the rasas, that is, of the <s>mahārasa</s>s, <s>uparasa</s>s, and metals, being taught as chief among them. Its mention as chief is an indication.
By this very term the inclusion of everything should be understood.
The word iva is used in the sense of similarity.

children.text: ātmani brahmaṇi niyataṃ niścitaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ sakalajīvānāṃ layo bhavati layo'ntarbhāvaḥ vā tasminsarve ||
children.translated_text: In the self, in <s>brahman</s>, there is the fixed dissolution of all beings, of all living creatures; dissolution means inclusion, or all are in that.

children.text: sattvā līnā eva tiṣṭhantītyātmānaḥ taṭasthasvarūpataitallakṣaṇadvayam uktam ||
children.translated_text: Since beings remain there as dissolved, that is the self; the two marks, the extrinsic and the intrinsic definition, have been stated.

children.text: tathā rasarāje'pi darśayati kāṣṭhauṣadhīdhātumahārasoparasādīnāṃ layo jñeyaḥ taṭasthalakṣaṇena layasya krama upadiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise he shows this also in the case of <s>rasarāja</s>: the dissolution of woody herbs, metals, <s>mahārasa</s>s, <s>uparasa</s>s, and the rest should be understood. By the extrinsic mark, the order of dissolution has been taught.

children.text: svarūpalakṣaṇenauṣadhīdhātumahārasoparasādayaḥ pṛthaktvena sthitā api guṇairantarbhūtā eva jñātavyāḥ yataḥ sarveṣāṃ guṇāntarbhūtaḥ sūtas tato 'nantaguṇa ācāryair upavarṇitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the intrinsic mark, herbs, metals, <s>mahārasa</s>s, <s>uparasa</s>s, and the rest, though standing separately, should still be understood as included by their qualities, because <s>sūta</s> contains the qualities of them all. Therefore the teachers describe it as possessing infinite qualities.
The secret is the similarity of the two because of the particular form of dissolution.
He states the equation of everything with "immortality" and so on.

children.text: te svātmanā ātmanā saha yogakartṛkā yogino yathā haramūrtau mahādevaśarīre līnāḥ santaḥ amṛtatvaṃ bhajante muktatvaṃ prāpnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: They, through union with their own self, are like yogins who, being dissolved in the form of <s>Hara</s>, the body of <s>Mahādeva</s>, partake of immortality and attain liberation.
<s>Amara</s> says that <s>mukti</s>, <s>kaivalya</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>śreyas</s>, <s>niḥśreyasa</s>, and <s>amṛta</s> are synonyms.

children.text: tadvattenaiva prakāreṇa rasarāje pārade kavalitagagane grāsīkṛtābhrake sati hemalohādyā līnāḥ santaḥ amṛtatvaṃ pīyūṣabhāvaṃ bhajante amarīkaraṇayogyā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: In that same way, in <s>rasarāja</s>, mercury, when "sky" has been swallowed, that is, when mica has been consumed, gold, iron, and the others, being dissolved, partake of immortality, the state of nectar, and become capable of immortalization.

children.text: hema ca lohaśca hemalohau ādyau yeṣāṃ vā hemasaṃjñako loha ādyo yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hema</s> and <s>loha</s> together are <s>hemalohau</s>; those for whom these are first are so called, or those for whom the metal called <s>hema</s> is first are so called.
When mica has been swallowed, <s>cāraṇā</s> occurs, and not otherwise.
Now he makes clear the fruit of a stable body with "stable" and so on.

children.text: pūrvoktasyaiva rasarājasyābhyāsāt sevanāddhetoḥ sthiradehaḥ pumān brahmapadaṃ prāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Because of practice, that is, use, of the very <s>rasarāja</s> described earlier, a man with a stable body attains the state of <s>brahman</s>.
The <s>brahmapada</s> (state of brahman) is of the nature of supreme bliss.
By doing what? By obtaining knowledge.
What sort of knowledge? It is furnished with the eight qualities, furnished with the eight <s>siddhis</s> (perfections) beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>.
How does one attain the <s>brahmapada</s>?

children.text: yathā punaraprathamaṃ bhavāvāsaduḥkhe saṃsāranivāsanatāpatrayātmakakaṣṭe na patatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is: so that one does not again fall into the suffering of the abode of becoming, the hardship consisting of the threefold affliction of dwelling in <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Having obtained knowledge, one attains the <s>brahmapada</s>.
How so? Because apart from knowledge there is no liberation.

children.text: anyacca kiṃ mokṣatarorbījaṃ samyagjñānaṃ kriyāsahitam iti praśnottararatnamālāyām ||
children.translated_text: And further, in the <s>Praśnottararatnamālā</s>: What is the seed of the tree of liberation? <s>samyagjñāna</s> (right knowledge) accompanied by action.
With the words beginning 'by one portion', he describes <s>brahman</s> as attainable through knowledge.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ brahma paraṃ jyotiḥ prakāśasvarūpaṃ tatparaṃ jyotir jaganti saṃsārāṇi svargamṛtyupātālādīni viṣṭabhya vyāpya sthitaṃ kena ekāṃśena anekabrahmāṇḍanāyakatvāt ekaikasmin brahmāṇḍe bahūni saṃsārāṇi vartante ata ekāṃśenetyuktaṃ punas tatparaṃ jyotīrūpam amṛtaṃ tribhiḥ pādair abhyāsasthiradehajñānasaṃjñakaiḥ sulabhaṃ sukhena labhyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of <s>brahman</s>? The supreme light, whose own nature is illumination. That supreme light stands having supported and pervaded the worlds, the realms of transmigration such as heaven, the mortal realm, and the netherworld. By what means? By one portion. Since it is lord of many <s>brahmāṇḍas</s> (cosmic eggs), and in each single <s>brahmāṇḍa</s> there are many worlds of transmigration, the phrase 'by one portion' is used. Again, that supreme, light-formed, immortal reality is easy to attain through the three <s>pādas</s> called practice, stable body, and knowledge; that is, it is obtained with ease.
First, <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice) is a cause for making the immortal easily attainable.

children.text: heturekaḥ sthiradehaś ca dvitīyo hetur jñānaṃ tṛtīyaheturmokṣe yathāvākyaṃ na viraktimātram ||
children.translated_text: One cause is practice; a stable body is the second cause, and knowledge is the third cause in liberation. According to the statement, it is not mere dispassion.
Indicating that, between the preceding and following causes, practice and knowledge, the stable body is the weightier cause, he says the words beginning 'not'.

children.text: ubhayoḥ sādhakatvāt tādṛśadehavyatiriktaṃ kathaṃcidapi kiṃcin na sidhyatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it makes both of them possible, apart from such a body nothing whatsoever is accomplished in any way; this is the meaning.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭena vyādhijarāmaraṇaduḥkhavidhureṇa vyādhirāmayaḥ jarā pālityaṃ maraṇaṃ prāṇatyāgaḥ duḥkhaṃ mohaśokādikam etair vidhuraṃ tāḍitaṃ vyadha tāḍane ityasya ghāto rūpaṃ vidhuram urapratyayāntam ||
children.translated_text: With what sort of body? One afflicted by disease, old age, death, and pain. Disease is illness; old age is greyness of hair; death is the abandonment of the vital breath; pain is delusion, grief, and so on. Vidhura means 'struck' by these; it is a form derived from the root vyadh, 'to strike', with the suffix ura.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭena kṣaṇabhaṅgureṇa kṣaṇavināśinā dehena tadbrahma cidghanānandasvarūpam upāsituṃ sevituṃ kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa śakyaṃ kuto yataḥ sūkṣmam indriyāgrāhyatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, with what sort? With a body that breaks in a moment, that perishes in a moment. With such a body, how, by what means, can that <s>brahman</s>, whose own nature is compact consciousness and bliss, be worshiped or attended upon? Why? Because it is subtle, since it cannot be grasped by the senses.

children.text: sarvopāyena śarīraṃ sthiraṃ kāryam ityāha nāmetyādi ||
children.translated_text: He says, with the words beginning 'name', that the body must be made stable by every means.

children.text: dehasiddheḥ śarīravibhūteḥ nāmāpyabhidhānamapi ko gṛhṇīyānna ko 'pītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who would even take, even utter, the name of <s>dehasiddhi</s> (perfection of the body), that bodily excellence? No one at all; this is the meaning.

children.text: kena vinā śarīreṇa śarīramantareṇa siddhirastu paraṃ tannāma kenāpi na gṛhyate śarīranāmagrahaṇamiti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Without what? Without the body, apart from the body. Let there be an attainment, but its name is not taken by anyone; the intended sense is the mention of the word 'body'.

children.text: anaśvaraṃ śarīraṃ bhavatu cet tad amalaṃ nirañjanaṃ tattvaṃ brahmāvaśyaṃ prāpyate ||
children.translated_text: If the body becomes imperishable, then that stainless, taintless reality, <s>brahman</s>, is necessarily attained.

children.text: tattattvaṃ manaso'pi na gocaraṃ cittenāpi na gamyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That reality is not even within the range of the mind; it is not reached even by thought. This is the meaning.

children.text: tarhi kena gamyam ubhayor melanam ekīkaraṇaṃ yogastenaiva prakṛtipuruṣayor ekīkaraṇenetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then by what is it reached? By the conjunction of the two, their unification; that alone is <s>yoga</s>, namely the unification of <s>prakṛti</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>. This is the meaning.

children.text: adhunā yogasya sarvakarmabhya utkṛṣṭatvaṃ darśayati yajñād ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now he shows the superiority of <s>yoga</s> over all rites with the words beginning 'than sacrifice'.

children.text: atyantaṃ śreya iti adhikatarakalyāṇaṃ sarvopadravanivāraṇātmakaṃ bhaved ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Atyantaṃ śreyaḥ means greater welfare, consisting in the removal of every misfortune; the verb 'would be' is to be supplied.

children.text: kutaḥ yajñādaśvamedhādeḥ na kevalaṃ yajñāt punardānāt dhanasyārpaṇāt pātreṣu punastapasaḥ kṛcchrātikṛcchracāndrāyapasaṃcāgnitapanādeḥ punarvedādhyayanāt vedānām ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvaṇāṃ adhyayanaṃ pāṭhākramastataḥ punardamāt vedāntānusāreṇa damastāvat bāhyendriyāṇāṃ tadvyatiriktaviṣayebhyo manasā nirvartanaṃ tadvyatiriktaṃ śravaṇādivyatiriktaṃ tataḥ punaḥ sadācārāt brāhmamuhūrtam ārabhya prātaḥsaṃgavamadhyāhnāparāhṇasāyāhnādiṣu śayanaparyantaṃ vedabodhito vidhiḥ sadācārastata iti samudāyaḥ śreyaskaro nātmasaṃvittikaraḥ punarātmasaṃvittiḥ brahmavedanaṃ yogavaśādeva syāt yogaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why? Than sacrifice, such as the <s>aśvamedha</s>; not only than sacrifice, but also than gift-giving, the offering of wealth to worthy recipients; again than austerity, such as <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>atikṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, and heating oneself amid the five fires; again than Vedic study, the study and recitation sequence of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Atharvan</s> Vedas; again than restraint. According to <s>Vedānta</s>, restraint is the withdrawal by the mind of the external senses from objects other than that, that is, other than hearing and the rest; and again than good conduct, the rule taught by the Veda beginning with the brāhma-muhūrta and continuing through morning, forenoon, midday, afternoon, evening, and so on, up to sleep. This aggregate is conducive to welfare, but it does not produce self-realization. Rather, self-realization, the knowledge of <s>brahman</s>, occurs only through the power of <s>yoga</s>; <s>yoga</s> has been stated before.

children.text: yasya jīvasya yogavaśātsaṃvittirjātā sa kīdṛśa ityāha galitetyādi ||
children.translated_text: What is the living being like in whom realization has arisen through the power of <s>yoga</s>? He says this with the words beginning 'whose many projections have dissolved'.

children.text: galitānalpavikalpa iti galito dūrībhūto 'nalpo bahutaro vikalpo mithyājñānaṃ yasya īdṛk syāt ||
children.translated_text: Galitānalpavikalpa means: one whose <s>vikalpa</s> (false conceptualization), not slight but very abundant, has melted away, has become remote. Such would he be.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛk sarvārthavivarjitaḥ sarve ca te arthāśca tair vivarjitāḥ samyagrahito bhavati kāryāṇāṃ smaraṇakaraṇayorabhāva ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, what is he like? Devoid of all objects. He is deprived of all those objects and purposes; he becomes properly grasped. The meaning is that there is no remembering or performing of actions.

children.text: punaḥ kathaṃbhūtaḥ cidānandaś cidā prakāśena ānandaḥ sukhasampattir yasya sa tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, what kind? Cidānanda: he whose bliss, the attainment of happiness, is through <s>cit</s> (consciousness), through illumination, is so called.
Blissfulness arises from a cause of illumination; from an inert cause the opposite occurs.

children.text: īdṛk saḥ sphurito'pi prakāśamāno'pi asphuritatanorjantuvargasya aprakāśaśarīrasya jīvasamūhasya kiṃ karoti pṛcchāṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: What does such a one do, even though manifest, even though shining, toward the class of creatures whose bodies are unmanifest, the multitude of living beings whose bodies do not shine? He asks a question.
Kim is used in the senses of questioning and aversion; so says <s>Prasāda</s>.

children.text: pṛcchati ca hasati ca roditi pramattavan mānavo'pi tallīna iti ||
children.translated_text: He asks, laughs, and cries; though a human being, like a madman, he is absorbed in that.
Indicating the rarity of self-realization, he says the words beginning 'the pair of eyebrows'.

children.text: yat bhrūyugamadhyagataṃ bhrūdvayāntargataṃ sat prakāśate tatra dṛṣṭiṃ nidhāya yoginaḥ paśyanti khecaryā mudrayā haṭhapradīpikāyāṃ padyam
children.translated_text: What is situated in the middle of the two eyebrows, that is, located between the two eyebrows, shines there. Fixing the gaze there, yogins see by means of the <s>Khecarī</s> mudrā. There is a verse in the <s>Haṭhapradīpikā</s>:
The tongue, moving in the reverse direction, has entered the cavity of the skull;
the gaze is set between the eyebrows. This becomes the <s>khecarī</s> mudrā.
Thus.

children.text: punaḥ śikhividyutsu vahnisaudāminīṣu nirmalaṃ sat yatprakāśate punaryat jagadbhāsi jagat saṃsāraṃ prakāśate tat cinmayaṃ prakāśapracuraṃ jyotiḥ keṣāṃcit puṇyakṛtāṃ suvihitakarmakartṝṇām unmīlati prādurbhavati na tu sarveṣāṃ yato nirmalaṃ prakāśaṃ dhyātvā vipulapuṇyena nirmalatvāya jāyate ataḥ prakāśo yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, that pure light which shines among flames and lightning, among fire and flashes of lightning, and that by which the world appears, illuminating the world of transmigration, is a conscious light, abundant in radiance. It opens forth for certain meritorious people who perform well-ordained acts, but not for everyone; for, by meditating on pure light, one is born toward purity through abundant merit. Therefore the mention of light is fitting.
Qualifying the conscious reality described earlier, he says, 'consisting solely of supreme bliss,' and so on.

children.text: tadbrahma īdṛśaṃ jñeyaṃ paramānandaikamayamiti parama utkṛṣṭo 'sāv ānandaḥ paramānandaḥ sa eva eko 'dvitīyas tātprācuryaṃ yasmiṃs tathoktaṃ punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ paramaṃ jyotiḥsvabhāvaṃ paramaṃ yajjyotiḥ tatsvabhāvaḥ svarūpaṃ yasya tad aśarīratvātsvaprakāśitvācca punaḥ avikalpaṃ mithyājñānaśūnyaṃ punarvigalitasarvakleśaṃ vigalitā viśeṣeṇa dūrīkṛtāḥ sarvakleśāḥ duḥkhāni yasmāt tat svarūpatvāt punaḥ śāntaṃ śamamayaṃ punaḥ svayaṃvedyam anyena veditum aśakyam ātmanaiva vedyaṃ tasmānnāparo'stīti bhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: That <s>brahman</s> is to be known as such: consisting solely of supreme bliss. 'Supreme' means excellent; that bliss is supreme bliss, and it alone is one, non-dual; that in which there is an abundance of it is so called. Again, of what kind is it? It is the supreme, having light as its very nature: that supreme light is the nature, the own-form, of that, because it is bodiless and self-luminous. Again, it is free from conceptual alternative, devoid of false knowledge. Again, all afflictions have melted away from it: all <s>kleśas</s>, that is, sufferings, have been especially removed from it, because this is its own nature. Again, it is peaceful, made of calm. Again, it is self-known, impossible to be known by another and knowable only by oneself, because the purport is that there is no other than it.
He states the instruction about what is to be known with 'in that,' and so forth.

children.text: tasminnādhāyeti pūrvanirūpite tasminnevātmani mana ādhāya saṃsthāpya pumān utsannakarmabandho bhavet tyaktakarmapāśaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: In 'having placed in that': having placed, that is, established, the mind in that very Self explained earlier, a man becomes one whose bondage of action has been destroyed, that is, whose fetters of action have been abandoned.

children.text: sa ihaiva janmani brahmatvaṃ prāpnotīti viśeṣaḥ brahmavid brahmaiva bhavati iti śruteḥ ||
children.translated_text: The special point is that he attains the state of <s>brahman</s> in this very birth, because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'the knower of <s>brahman</s> becomes <s>brahman</s> itself.'
That man places the mind there.

children.text: kiṃ kurvan san akhilaṃ jagat sarvasaṃsāraṃ cinmayaṃ prakāśasvarūpaṃ cidvikāraṃ paśyan avalokamāno manaścakṣuṣā kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ jagat sphurat adhyāropāpadeśena dedīpyamānam ||
children.translated_text: While doing what? While seeing the whole world, the entire world of transmigration, as conscious, as having the nature of light, as a transformation of consciousness, observing it with the mind's eye. What kind of world? Shining, blazing by way of the teaching of superimposition.
And there is the statement of the Blessed Lord:

children.text: karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever sees inaction in action, and also action in inaction,
he is wise among human beings; he is disciplined and has performed all action.
Thus.

children.text: he pārtha sa pumān manuṣyeṣu buddhimān ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Pārtha</s>, that man is wise among human beings.
By this, the general sense has been stated.

children.text: viśeṣaśca yathā rajjau sarpabhramo yathā śuktau rajatajñānaṃ yathā gandharvanagaraṃ yathā marusthale vāri tathaiva saṃsāro nāsīt nāsti na bhaviṣyatīti advaitavādānmithyaiva ||
children.translated_text: And the specific point is as follows: just as there is the mistaken perception of a snake in a rope, just as there is the cognition of silver in mother-of-pearl, just as there is a city of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, and just as there is water in a desert, in exactly the same way the world of transmigration did not exist, does not exist, and will not exist. According to the doctrine of non-duality, it is simply false.
For one whose bondage of action has been destroyed, sense-objects pass away.
Apart from the conjunction with the vital breath and the inner organ, there would be no manifestation of the senses.

children.text: tathā ca nyāyaśāstre ātmā manasā saṃyujyate mana indriyeṇa indriyamarthenetīndriyāṇāṃ vastuprāpyaprakāśakāritvaniyamād iti ||
children.translated_text: And so in the <s>Nyāyaśāstra</s>: the Self is joined with the mind, the mind with the sense faculty, and the sense faculty with the object. This is because there is a rule that the senses illuminate an object by reaching it.
For this reason, pain and pleasure do not manifest.

children.text: ātmanaḥ prakāśāt prāṇāntaḥkaraṇānāṃ prakāśaḥ prāṇāntaḥkaraṇāni tameva prakāśaṃ prāpyendriyāṇi prakāśayanti ||
children.translated_text: From the light of the Self comes the illumination of the vital breaths and the inner organs. Having obtained that very light, the vital breaths and inner organs illuminate the senses.
Therefore, both have their illumination from another.

children.text: tadvad gahanatama agrāhyamandhakāraṃ cidbhinnaṃ prakāśena prakāśitaṃ syāditi ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, the deepest, ungraspable darkness, distinct from consciousness, would be illuminated by light.
Because darkness is a negative entity, and because the senses and darkness are inert, there is a similarity between them.

children.text: adhunā antaḥkaraṇānāṃ pravṛttiṃ darśayati rāgetyādi cidbrahmasaṃsparśāditi cidbrahmaṇi prakāśasvarūpe ātmani yaḥ sparśaḥ tanniṣṭhā tato hetoḥ puruṣā rāgadveṣaviyuktāḥ snehaśatrutvavirahitāḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now he shows the activity of the inner organs with 'because of contact with attachment,' and so on. 'Because of contact with consciousness-<s>brahman</s>' means: from that cause, from contact with, that is, steadfastness in, the Self that is consciousness-<s>brahman</s> and has the nature of light, men become free from attachment and aversion, devoid of affection and hostility.

children.text: punaḥ satyaḥ ācāraḥ pravṛttidharmo yeṣāṃ te punarmṛṣārahitāḥ atyācārādyasatyavarjitā ityarthaḥ punaḥ sarvatra nirviśeṣāḥ sarvasmin mānāpamānayoḥ samāḥ tathā ca bhagavadvacanam
children.translated_text: Again, they are those whose conduct is true, whose mode of activity is <s>dharma</s>; again, they are free from falsehood, meaning devoid of untruth such as misconduct. Again, they are without distinctions everywhere, equal in honor and dishonor in every case. And there is the statement of the Blessed Lord:

children.text: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Equal toward enemy and friend, and likewise in honor and dishonor,
and so on.
Showing the attainment of liberation as contact with the Self, he says, 'they abide,' and so forth.

children.text: ye brahmabhāvamamṛtaṃ muktisārūpyatvaṃ prāptāste kṛtakṛtyāḥ kṛtasarvakāryāḥ pūrṇatāṃ prāptā ityarthaḥ punaste aṇimādiyutā aṇimādibhiryutā iha jagati tiṣṭhantīti aṇimādayo yathā
children.translated_text: Those who have obtained the immortal state of <s>brahman</s>, similarity in form to liberation, are <s>kṛtakṛtya</s>, those who have done what was to be done, meaning that they have accomplished every task and attained fullness. Again, they abide here in the world endowed with <s>aṇimā</s> and the other powers. The powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> are as follows:

children.text: aṇimā mahimā cātha laghimā garimā tathā
children.translated_text: Minuteness, greatness, then lightness, and likewise heaviness,
attainment, irresistible will, lordship, and mastery are the eight powers.
Thus.

children.text: punarvilasaddehāḥ tejaḥprāyaśarīrāḥ punaḥ sadānandāḥ kena mudā harṣeṇa sadā sarvasminkāle ānando yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ paramānande magnatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, they have shining bodies, bodies mostly made of radiance. Again, they are always blissful: by what? By joy, by gladness; they are those for whom there is bliss at all times, because they are immersed in supreme bliss.
He says that everyone should know the root of the body with 'the abode,' and so on.

children.text: ekam ajarāmaraṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitaṃ śarīraṃ vihāya tyaktvā anyat paramutkṛṣṭaṃ śreyaḥ kalyāṇasvarūpaṃ kiṃ na kim apītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having given up, that is, abandoned, a single ageless and immortal body, a body free from old age and death, what other supreme, excellent <s>śreyas</s> (highest good), whose nature is welfare, is there? The meaning is: none at all.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ śarīram āyatanaṃ vidyānāṃ vyākaraṇādicaturdaśasaṃkhyākāṅgānāṃ nivāsasthānaṃ punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ mūlaṃ dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ caturṇāṃ padārthānāṃ mūlaṃ hetuḥ dharmādayaś catvāraḥ pratītā eva ||
children.translated_text: What kind of body is it? It is an <s>āyatana</s> (abode), the dwelling place of the sciences, the fourteen branches beginning with grammar. Again, what kind is it? It is the root of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>, the four aims; it is their root, their cause. The four beginning with <s>dharma</s> are well known.

children.text: ātmano 'vekṣayā sūte sugamatvaṃ sūcayannāha pramāṇata ityādi ||
children.translated_text: In comparison with the Self, while indicating the ease of <s>sūta</s>, he says, 'from <s>pramāṇa</s>,' and so on.

children.text: yaḥ puruṣaḥ sūtakaṃ rasendraṃ na jānāti kutaḥ pramāṇataḥ pramākaraṇaṃ pramāṇaṃ pramitisādhanaṃ vā tataḥ kimbhūtāt pramāṇataḥ pratyakṣāc cakṣurindriyagrāhyarūpāt sa pumān cinmayam atisūkṣmam ātmānaṃ kathaṃ jñāsyati na katham apītyarthaḥ indriyāgocaratvāt ||
children.translated_text: The man who does not know <s>sūtaka</s>, <s>rasendra</s>, from what source? From <s>pramāṇa</s>, an instrument of valid knowledge or a means of cognition. From what sort of <s>pramāṇa</s>? From direct perception, a form grasped by the eye-sense. How will that man know the conscious, extremely subtle Self? In no way, because it is beyond the range of the senses.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭam anādivigraham ādiśca vigrahaṃ ca ādivigrahe te na vidyete yatra saḥ taṃ utpattiśarīrayorabhāvāt sthūlajñānābhāva iti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of Self is it? It is without beginning and without bodily form: that in which neither beginning nor body exists, because origination and body are absent. The intended sense is that there is no gross cognition of it.
Showing the body's instability through the divisions of age, he says, 'A child,' and so on.

children.text: ṣoḍaśavarṣa iti ṣoḍaśa varṣāṇi yasya vayasi sa ṣoḍaśābdo bāla ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the expression 'sixteen years old': one whose age is sixteen years is sixteen-year-old; the meaning is 'a child.'
In another treatise too, distinctions of age are found even within childhood.
As in the verse:
Childhood extends through the fifth year, and boyhood through the ninth;

children.text: ā ṣoḍaśācca kiśoro yauvanaṃ ca tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: adolescence extends through the sixteenth, and youth is after that.
Thus.
A child is incapable of knowledge of objects.

children.text: punaḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣebhyaḥ paraḥ viṣayarasāsvādalampaṭo bhavati viṣayāḥ śabdasparśarūparasagandhā rasāḥ śṛṅgārahāsyakaruṇaraudravīrabhayānakabībhatsādbhutaśāntāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after sixteen years, he becomes greedy for tasting the flavors of sense-objects. The sense-objects are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell; the <s>rasas</s> are the erotic, comic, pathetic, furious, heroic, terrible, disgusting, marvelous, and peaceful.

children.text: kecit śāntaṃ rasaṃ na bruvanti nirvikāratvāt eteṣām āsvādaḥ svādas tatra lampaṭo vyāsaktaḥ atha vā viṣayānantaraṃ snehastatreti ||
children.translated_text: Some do not mention the peaceful <s>rasa</s>, because it is without transformation. The tasting of these is savor, and one who is <s>lampaṭa</s> is attached to it. Or else, after 'sense-object' the sense is attachment to it.

children.text: ataḥ parato jātaviveko bhavati utpannavicāro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: After this he becomes one in whom discernment has arisen, one in whom reflection has been produced.

children.text: tadā vṛddho'kṣamaḥ paraṃ manuṣyaḥ muktiṃ kaivalyaṃ katham āpnuyāt na kathamapītyartho vayasyupaplavabhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: At that time, when he is old and incapable, how could a man attain the supreme goal, <s>mukti</s> or <s>kaivalya</s>? In no way, because disturbances occur in old age.

children.text: pūrvapadyābhiprāyaṃ vicārya muktiprāptau praśaṅkitaḥ prāhāsminn ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Having considered the intention of the preceding verse, and anticipating a question about the attainment of liberation, he says, 'in this,' and so forth.

children.text: asmin śarīre vartamāne kṣetrarūpe yeṣāṃ puṃsām ātmasaṃvedo na jātaḥ brahmajñānaṃ na jātaṃ teṣāṃ puṃsāmeva dehatyāgād ūrdhvaṃ śarīrotsargataḥ paścāt tadbrahma dūrataraṃ dūrāddūrataram ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those men, while this body, in the form of a field, exists, in whom self-awareness has not arisen, that is, <s>brahmajñāna</s> (knowledge of brahman) has not arisen, for those very men, after abandonment of the body, after casting off the body, that <s>brahman</s> is still farther away, farther than far.
Now he strengthens the previous view with 'Brahmā and the others,' and so on.

children.text: yasmin brahmādayo viṣṇurudrendrādayo brahmavido yajante saṃgatiṃ kurvanti samāpnuvantītyarthaḥ yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu atra saṃgatikaraṇam artho darśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In that with which <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and so forth, the knowers of <s>brahman</s>, unite, they perform <s>yaj</s>, that is, they enter into connection and attain it. The root <s>yaj</s> occurs in the senses of worship of a god, making connection, and giving; here the meaning 'making connection' is shown.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā prāpnuvanti divyāṃ tanuṃ paramāṃ samāśritya samprāpya tebhyo brahmādibhyo 'pyanye apare munayo nāradādayo jīvanmuktā yajante saṃgatiṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Having done what do they attain it? Having resorted to, that is, obtained, the highest divine body. Other sages too, such as <s>Nārada</s>, beyond those <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest, being <s>jīvanmuktas</s> (liberated while alive), perform <s>yaj</s>, that is, they enter into connection.

children.text: te 'pi kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ kalpāntasthāyinaḥ pralayānte'pi tiṣṭhantīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind are they also? They remain until the end of a kalpa; the sense is that they stand even at the end of dissolution.
As for <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, they certainly remain.

children.text: iti bahudhā vicāryeṣṭavastustutim āha tasmād ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Having reflected in many ways in this manner, he states a praise of the desired object with 'therefore,' and so on.

children.text: yato brahmādayo jīvanmuktāś cānye divyāṃ tanuṃ vidhāya muktiṃ prāptās tasmāddhetor yoginā yogayuktena prathamaṃ divyā tanur vidheyā dṛḍhaśarīraṃ kāryam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, and other <s>jīvanmuktas</s>, fashioned a divine body and attained liberation, therefore a yogin joined with yoga should first fashion a divine body; the meaning is that he should make the body firm.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭena yoginā jīvanmuktiṃ samīhamānena yoginā divyā tanur vidheyā ||
children.translated_text: By what kind of yogin? A divine body should be fashioned by a yogin who seeks <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while alive).
From what cause? From the conjunction of the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>.
The meaning is: from the use of <s>rasendra</s>, created by <s>Umā</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: dṛḍhaśarīreṇa vāñchitaṃ sādhyate na tv anyathā ||
children.translated_text: With a firm body the desired aim is accomplished, but not otherwise.

children.text: divyatanorhetutvād rasendrasya sādhanavidhau sādhanopadeśe sudhiyā pūjyamatinā puṃsā prathamam aṣṭādaśasaṃskārāḥ prayatnena jñātavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because <s>rasendra</s> is the cause of the divine body, in the procedure of practice, in the instruction on the means, a man of good understanding and reverent mind must first carefully learn the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (refining processes).
They are called <s>saṃskāras</s> because things are refined by them.

children.text: puṃsyapi garbhādhānādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa saṃskārā vartante ata eva saṃskārair ubhayoḥ sāmyaṃ doṣābhāvatvaṃ guṇavattvaṃ ca syāt ||
children.translated_text: For a person too there are sixteen <s>saṃskāras</s>, beginning with <s>garbhādhāna</s>. Therefore, through <s>saṃskāras</s> in both cases, there should be similarity: freedom from faults and possession of virtues.
Thus there come to be Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ saṃskārāḥ pratikarmanirmalāḥ karma karma prati nirdoṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of <s>saṃskāras</s> are they? Pure for each operation; with respect to every action, they are free from fault.
He whose fame is sustained even in the company of the nectar-eaters,
that illustrious one caused the commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s> to be made.
In two Āryā verses the enumeration of the eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> of <s>rasa</s> has been made.
Now he states the definition of the means for the <s>saṃskāras</s>.

children.text: tatra prathamoddiṣṭasya svedanasaṃskārasya sādhanaṃ spaṣṭayannāha āsurītyādi ||
children.translated_text: There, making clear the means for the first-mentioned <s>svedana-saṃskāra</s> (sweating process), he says, 'with <s>āsurī</s>,' and so forth.

children.text: sūtasya pāradasya tridinaṃ dinatrayaparimāṇaṃ yathā syāttathā mṛduvahninā svalpāgninā svedaḥ svedanaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: For <s>sūta</s>, that is, <s>pārada</s> (mercury), <s>sveda</s> or <s>svedana</s> should be performed for three days, for a period of three days, with a gentle fire, a low flame.
By what? By <s>kāñjika</s> and <s>sauvīra</s>.
Together with what? Together with <s>āsurī</s>, <s>paṭu</s>, <s>kaṭukatraya</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>ārdraka</s>, and <s>mūlaka</s>.

children.text: āsurī rājikā paṭu saindhavaṃ lavaṇaviśeṣaḥ kecitpaṭuśabdena kṣāramapi vyācakṣate kaṭukatrayaṃ śuṇṭhīmaricapippalyaḥ citrakaṃ pratītam ārdrakaṃ kandaviśeṣo nāgarahetuḥ mūlakaṃ kandaviśeṣaḥ prasiddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āsurī</s> is mustard. <s>Paṭu</s> is <s>saindhava</s>, a particular kind of salt; some also explain the word <s>paṭu</s> as alkali. <s>Kaṭukatraya</s> is dry ginger, black pepper, and long pepper. <s>Citraka</s> is well known. <s>Ārdraka</s> is a particular tuber, the source of <s>nāgara</s>. <s>Mūlaka</s> is the well-known particular tuber.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭairetaiḥ kalāṃśaiḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśaiḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśaḥ pratyekaṃ saṃyujyate ||
children.translated_text: What are these like? They are in <s>kalā</s>-parts, that is, sixteenth parts; a sixteenth part of each is to be combined separately.
This explanation is accepted by all.

children.text: atra viśeṣaḥ kāñjike sarvadhānyāmlasaṃdhānaṃ tuṣavarjye tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Here there is a special point: for <s>kāñjika</s>, one should make a sour fermentation from all grains, but without the husk.
<s>Uragā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>krāntā</s>, <s>laghuparṇī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>.
Mercury, joined with that, is steamed for three days over a gentle fire.
By means of a strong <s>dolāyantra</s>, after grinding it again and again.
Thus from the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s>.

children.text: kṣārāmlair oṣadhair vāpi dolāyantre sthitasya hi
children.translated_text: For what is placed in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, with alkaline substances, sour substances, or even herbs,
the cooking is called <s>svedana</s>; it causes the loosening of impurities.
Thus the definition.
With a liquid substance, and with the belly of the vessel half filled,
after carefully making two openings on both sides of its mouth,
one should place a rod above it and tie a packet of mercury at its middle.
Then one should steam it; this is remembered as the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
Thus the characteristic of the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
Making clear the means for the second-mentioned grinding, he says, 'with jaggery,' and so on.

children.text: etair auṣadhair dinatrayaṃ parimāṇaṃ rasasya mardanaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: With these medicines, the mercury should be ground for a measure of three days.

children.text: etaiḥ kaiḥ guḍadagdhorṇālavaṇaiḥ guḍa ikṣuvikāraḥ prasiddhaḥ dagdhorṇā dagdhā cāsau ūrṇā ceti samāsaḥ ūrṇā pratītā meṣaromanicayam ityarthaḥ lavaṇaṃ saindhavamekaṃ guḍadagdhorṇārajanī iti vā pāṭhaḥ tatra haridrā grāhyā na saindhavam ||
children.translated_text: With which ones? With jaggery, burnt wool, and salt. Jaggery is the well-known product of sugarcane. 'Burnt wool' is a compound meaning wool that has been burnt; wool is understood as a mass of sheep hair. The salt is simply <s>saindhava</s>. Or there is the reading 'jaggery, burnt wool, and <s>rajanī</s>'; in that case turmeric is to be taken, not <s>saindhava</s>.
'Measured as one-sixteenth of the mercury' means having a measure equal to one-sixteenth of the mercury.
The word 'part' is connected with each one separately.

children.text: viśeṣaścātra vastraiścaturguṇair baddhaḥ sūtaḥ sthāpyaḥ śubhe 'hani ||
children.translated_text: The special point here is this: <s>sūta</s> (mercury), bound with fourfold cloths, should be placed on an auspicious day.
In a heated mortar made of iron, copper, or stone, one should grind it only when they are hot.
Together with the prescribed herbs, with all sour substances, and also with <s>kāñjika</s>,
the grinding is called <s>mardana</s>; it is the destruction of external impurity. Thus the definition.
Here the apparatus should be understood as the one called a <s>khalva</s>, a mortar.

children.text: tallakṣaṇaṃ tu khalvayogyā śilā nīlā śyāmā snigdhā dṛḍhā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its characteristic is this: a stone suitable for a mortar is blue, dark, smooth, firm, and heavy.
It is sixteen finger-breadths high and nine finger-breadths wide. Thus.
The characteristic of a stone suitable for a mortar has been stated incidentally.

children.text: utsedhena navāṅgulaḥ khalu kalātulyāṅgulāyāmavān vistāreṇa daśāṅgulo 'tha munibhir nimnas tathaivāṅgulaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: In height it is nine finger-breadths, and it has a length in finger-breadths equal to a <s>kalā</s>; in width it is ten finger-breadths, and according to the sages its hollow is likewise measured in finger-breadths.

children.text: pālyāṃ hy aṅgulavistaraśca masṛṇo 'tīvārdhacandropamo gharṣo dvādaśakāṅgulaśca tadayaṃ khalvo mato mardane iti ||
children.translated_text: On the rim it is one finger-breadth wide, very smooth, and shaped like a half-moon; the grinding pestle is twelve finger-breadths long. This is considered the mortar for grinding. Thus.
Mercury, <s>pārada</s>, has three defects.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ malaśikhiviṣābhidhānāḥ malaśca śikhī ca viṣaṃ ca tānyevābhidhānaṃ nāma yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: What are they like? They are called <s>mala</s>, <s>śikhi</s>, and <s>viṣa</s>; that is, those whose names are precisely impurity, fire, and poison are so called.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ naisargikāḥ nisarga utpattis tatsambandhinaḥ sahajā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, what are they like? They are natural: <s>nisarga</s> means origin, and those connected with it are innate.

children.text: viśeṣaścātra malādyāḥ pañcadoṣāḥ syur bhūjādyāḥ saptakañcukāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is a special point here: the five defects beginning with <s>mala</s>, the seven coverings beginning with <s>bhūja</s>,

children.text: kuṣṭānaṣṭau rasāntaḥsthā rase te 'nantadoṣadāḥ iti rasasaṃketakalikāyām ||
children.translated_text: and the eight <s>kuṣṭhas</s> situated within mercury give endless defects in mercury. Thus in the <s>Rasasaṃketakalikā</s>.

children.text: yadyapi rasendramaṅgale pañca malādayo naisargikā doṣāḥ kathitās tathāpyatra traya eva anye dve gurutvacapalatve naisargikadoṣarūpe kuto na staḥ tribhiḥ svedanamardanamūrchanātmakaiḥ saṃskārair anivṛtteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Although in the <s>Rasendramaṅgala</s> five natural defects beginning with <s>mala</s> are taught, here there are still only three. Why are the other two, heaviness and quickness, not natural defects? Because they are not removed by the three operations consisting of steaming, grinding, and stupefying.
From the mention of the natural ones, there could also be inclusion of the adventitious ones.

children.text: atra naisargikā uktā vaikārikāḥ kuto noktāḥ vaikārikāṇāṃ bhāvābhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: Here the natural ones have been stated. Why are the adventitious ones not stated? Because the adventitious ones may or may not exist.

children.text: raso doṣatrayāvṛtaḥ prāśyamānaḥ kiṃ karoti malena maladoṣeṇa mūrchām indriyamohaṃ kurute śikhinā vahninā dāhaṃ viṣeṇa mṛtyuṃ maraṇaṃ ceti samuccaye ||
children.translated_text: What does mercury covered by the three defects do when it is consumed? Through <s>mala</s>, the impurity-defect, it causes <s>mūrchā</s>, stupefaction of the senses; through <s>śikhin</s>, fire, it causes burning; through <s>viṣa</s>, poison, it causes death. The word 'and' indicates combination.
The sense is that these must be removed.
That which, through the destruction of its own form, brings about the state of being ground into paste,
that conquered mercury is called <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s> by the learned.
That which, through the medicines prescribed for grinding, brings about the <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s> state
is said to be <s>mūrchana</s>, the destruction of the three defects. Thus.

children.text: yantram atra khalvam eva pūrvoktaṃ yat ||
children.translated_text: The apparatus here is just the mortar already mentioned.
He states <s>mūrchana</s>, the removal of the three defects, with 'house-maiden' and so on.

children.text: gṛhakanyā gṛhakumārikā malaṃ prathamaṃ doṣaṃ harati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gṛhakanyā</s>, that is, <s>gṛhakumārikā</s>, removes <s>mala</s>, the first defect.

children.text: punastriphalā trayāṇāṃ phalānāṃ samāhāraḥ triphalā agniṃ dvitīyaṃ doṣaṃ harati samāhāro yathā ekā harītakī yojyā dvau ca yojyau vibhītakau
children.translated_text: Again, <s>triphalā</s>, the collection of three fruits, removes <s>agni</s>, the second defect. The collection is as follows: one <s>harītakī</s> should be used, and two <s>vibhītakas</s> should be used,
and four <s>āmalakas</s>; this is proclaimed as <s>triphalā</s>.
Thus.

children.text: punaścitrako'gniḥ viṣaṃ tṛtīyaṃ doṣaṃ harati dūrīkarotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>citraka</s>, being fire, removes, that is, drives away, <s>viṣa</s>, the third defect.

children.text: tasmāddhetor ebhis tribhir gṛhakanyātriphalācitrakair miśritair ekīkṛtai rasaṃ sapta vārānmūrchayet vidhivanmūrchanaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: For that reason, with these three, <s>gṛhakanyā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, and <s>citraka</s>, mixed and combined, one should perform <s>mūrchana</s> (stupefying processing) on the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) seven times; one should carry out the <s>mūrchana</s> according to rule.
And here there is a special point:
The <s>mūrchana</s> of <s>rasarāja</s> (the king of rasa, mercury) must always be performed by practitioners.
First with poisons and with <s>triphalā</s>, and likewise with <s>bṛhatī</s> and secondary poisons;
with <s>karkoṭī</s>, with <s>kṣārakanda</s>, with <s>citraka</s>, and with <s>gṛhakanyā</s>;
then <s>pārada</s> (mercury) should be thoroughly triturated even with any one of these for one <s>yāma</s>.
Taking up the <s>kinnarayantra</s> apparatus, one should smear its base with an herb.
One should place the <s>sūta</s> (mercury), joined with <s>navatāra</s>, in the middle of the apparatus.

children.text: dadyād rasopari śarāvaṃ saṃdhilepaṃ dṛḍhaṃ mṛdā
children.translated_text: One should put a dish above the mercury and make a firm sealing of the joint with clay.

children.text: lavaṇena ca sampūrya dvāraṃ saṃrudhya yatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Filling it also with salt, one should carefully close the opening.
Having set it upon a stove, the wise person should kindle a blazing fire.
After one <s>yāma</s>, he should take it down and make the <s>rasa</s> cool.
Having carefully removed it from the apparatus and revived the stupefied <s>sūta</s>,

children.text: amūrchitas tadā deyaḥ kalāṃśaṃ mūrchite rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then an unstupified portion of <s>rasa</s>, amounting to a <s>kalā</s>-share, should be added to the stupefied <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: sindhūtthaṭaṅkaṇābhyāṃ ca mardayen madhusaṃyutaṃ dolāyantre tataḥ svedyaḥ kṣārāmlalavaṇaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: One should triturate it with rock-salt and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), mixed with honey; then it should be steamed in a <s>dolāyantra</s> together with alkalis, sour liquids, and salts.
After reviving it, one should thereafter perform <s>mūrchana</s> again and again on <s>raseśvara</s> (the lord of rasa, mercury).
One should make it revived again twenty-one times.
Thus in the <s>Rasasāra</s>.

children.text: sūto nāgavaṅgaparimukto bhavati nāgavaṅgābhyāṃ doṣābhyāṃ virahitaḥ pārado bhavatītyarthaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ san samutthitaḥ san ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sūta</s> becomes freed from lead and tin; the meaning is that <s>pārada</s> becomes devoid of the two defects, lead and tin. In what condition? When it has been properly revived.
That is, when it has been revived according to the correct procedure in a <s>pātana</s> apparatus, in the enclosure of two pots.

children.text: kasmāt kāñjikaṃ sauvīraṃ pūrvavarṇitaṃ tatkvāthasaṃyogād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From what? From the previously described <s>kāñjika</s> and <s>sauvīra</s>; the meaning is, through connection with their decoction.
For this is certain.

children.text: amunā virecanena uktaśodhanena sūtaḥ suviśuddho bhavet viśeṣaśuddho bhaved ityutthāpanam ||
children.translated_text: By this purging, by the purification that has been stated, the <s>sūta</s> becomes very pure, that is, especially pure; this is <s>utthāpana</s> (reviving or raising).

children.text: anena vidhinā hiṅgulasthasya sūtasyāpi utthāpanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By this method there is also <s>utthāpana</s> of the <s>sūta</s> contained in cinnabar.
Again, the restoration of its own form by procedures beginning with steaming
is called that <s>utthāpana</s>, the removal of the disorder of <s>mūrchā</s>.
