<s>Ut</s> means upward; setting upward is <s>utthāpana</s>.
Here, however, the apparatus is as follows:
It is eight <s>aṅgulas</s> in circumference and ten <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth.
It is four <s>aṅgulas</s> in elevation, with the water-reservoir one <s>aṅgula</s> below.
Into the lower vessel, the mouth of that vessel which is placed above
and whose back is sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> wide should be inserted into its opening.
On the sides, with buffalo milk, powdered <s>maṇḍūra</s>, and molasses,

children.text: vilipya śoṣayet saṃdhiṃ jalādhāre jalaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: one should smear and dry the joint; one should put water in the water-reservoir.
One should set this on the hearth; this is declared to be the <s>pātana</s> apparatus.
Thus.
Clarifying the <s>pātana-saṃskāra</s> listed as the fifth, he says, 'having made,' and so on.

children.text: tu punaḥ utthitaṃ sūtaṃ śulbapiṣṭiṃ kṛtvā śulbena tāmreṇa saha tayormelanaṃ yathā syāttathā peṣaṇaṃ vidhāya tasmin pātanayantre nipātyate karmavideti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But again, after making the revived <s>sūta</s> into a copper <s>piṣṭi</s>, that is, after grinding it in such a way that the two are combined with <s>śulba</s>, copper, it is made to descend in that <s>pātana</s> apparatus; 'by one who knows the procedure' is to be supplied.
Why? Because of suspicion of lead and tin, that is, because it is impaired by the defects of lead and tin.

children.text: tathā uktavidhānena nipatati sati pātanakarmaṇi kṛte sati śuddhaḥ sūto bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when it descends according to the stated procedure, when the <s>pātana</s> operation has been performed, the <s>sūta</s> becomes purified.

children.text: vāramityanukte granthāntare trisaptaikaviṃśativāraṃ pātanakarmaṇi kṛte sati samyak nāgavaṅgaśaṅkā naśyatīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the number of times is not stated, another text says that when the <s>pātana</s> operation has been performed three, seven, or twenty-one times, the suspicion of lead and tin is completely removed; this is the intention.
And here there is a special point concerning the <s>pātana</s> apparatus:
Two parts of purified <s>sūta</s> are combined with one part of copper.
After adding one-twentieth part of salt, one should make it into a fine <s>piṣṭi</s>.
The lower vessel is eight <s>aṅgulas</s> broad and ten <s>aṅgulas</s> long.
Below the neck, all around, it has a water-reservoir made four <s>aṅgulas</s> in size.
Its mouth enters inside the mouth of the lower vessel, with the rim of its own mouth submerged in water.
Above, a <s>ciṇṭighaṭī</s> should be placed, with a belly sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> broad.
When it is made to descend in that lower-and-upper vessel arrangement, it is freed from all defects.
<s>Rasendra</s> (the lord of rasa, mercury) becomes especially so; even this, though it has digested its morsel, should be subjected to <s>pātana</s>.

children.text: adha ūrdhvaṃ tathā tiryak pātastrividha ucyate
children.translated_text: <s>Pāta</s> is said to be threefold: downward, upward, and also sideways.

children.text: yatra tiṣṭhati sūtendro vahnis tatrānyathā jalam ||
children.translated_text: Where <s>sūtendra</s> (the lordly mercury) is situated, there is fire; elsewhere there is water.
For mercury triturated with the stated herbs and placed in the apparatus, upward, downward, or sideways,
the expulsion is called by the name <s>pātana</s>; it destroys the sheath produced by contact with tin and lead.
Thus.

children.text: ūrdhvapāte rasasyordhvagamanaṃ tatrādhaḥpātre vahniḥ jalamūrdhvapātre adhaḥpāte tu rasasyādhastādgamanaṃ bhavati yantraṃ tadeva paraṃ tu agnijalayorvyatyāsaḥ jalam atrādhaḥpātre agnirūrdhvapātre tiryakpāte tu rasastiryak patati tatraikapātrapṛṣṭhe jalam anyapātrādho vahniḥ ||
children.translated_text: In upward <s>pāta</s>, the mercury moves upward; there the fire is in the lower vessel and the water in the upper vessel. In downward <s>pāta</s>, however, the mercury moves downward; the apparatus is the same, but there is a reversal of fire and water: here the water is in the lower vessel and the fire in the upper vessel. In sideways <s>pāta</s>, the mercury falls sideways; there water is on the back of one vessel and fire beneath another vessel.
Clarifying the <s>nirodhana-saṃskāra</s> listed as the sixth, he says, 'by trituration,' and so on.

children.text: etair mardanamūrchanapātaiḥ saṃskāraviśeṣaṃ kṛtvā mandavīryatvāt kadarthito bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Having performed a special processing by means of these triturations, <s>mūrchanas</s>, and <s>pātanas</s>, it becomes debilitated because its potency is weak.

children.text: kutsitavidhānena kadarthito bhavatītyarthaḥ punaḥ sūtaḥ sṛṣṭyambujaiḥ saha mardanānantaraṃ nirodhāt mūṣādvayasampuṭe kūpikāyāṃ vā nirodhāt rundhanāt labdhāpyāyaḥ prāptabalaḥ san na ṣaṇḍhaḥ syāt na śukrarahito bhavati ||
children.translated_text: By an improper procedure it becomes damaged; this is the meaning. Again, after trituration together with <s>sṛṣṭi</s> and <s>ambuja</s>, because of confinement, because it is shut up in a capsule made from a pair of crucibles or in a flask, the <s>sūta</s>, having obtained nourishment and gained strength, does not become impotent, that is, it does not become devoid of potency.

children.text: sṛṣṭiḥ mūtraśukraśoṇitarūpā ambujaṃ lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ kamalam iti mandāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sṛṣṭi</s> consists of urine, semen, and blood. <s>Ambuja</s> means salt, rock-salt, or <s>kamala</s>, according to the dull-witted.
<s>Sṛṣṭi</s> is as follows:
The urine, semen, and blood of cows, goats, sheep, men, and women:
this is called <s>sṛṣṭi</s>, the destroyer of the defect of impotence.
Thus from the <s>Śaktyavatāra</s>.
The apparatus is as follows:
One should prepare a pair of crucibles from a lump of red rock-salt.
Having placed the <s>rasa</s> in that capsule, together with <s>navasāra</s> and lemon,
one should carefully smear the excellent joint of the capsule,
and, taking diamond-clay, should wrap it carefully with that.
After making it dry in the shade, one should then place it in a pit in the ground.
There the filling above the crucible should measure eight <s>aṅgulas</s>.
For twenty-one days one should maintain a fire of cow-dung cakes.
Day by day a fresh rock-salt crucible should be made.
One should steam it carefully and then place it in the ground.
Or else the <s>sūta</s>, combined with rock-salt, should be put inside a flask.
Then it should be placed in the ground for a period of twenty-one days.
This is called the <s>nirodhaka</s>; it produces a great opening in <s>rasa</s>.
Thus.
Clarifying the seventh-listed <s>saṃskāra</s>, he says, 'thus,' and so on.

children.text: iti pūrvoktavidhānena yantraṇādinā tadanu rodhanānantaram asau capalaścañcalo raso niyamyate karmavidā saṃniyamanaṃ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the previously stated procedure, beginning with the apparatus, and thereafter, after <s>rodhana</s>, that quick and unstable <s>rasa</s> is restrained, that is, brought under control, by one who knows the operation.

children.text: kasmāt phaṇīlaśunāmbujamārkavakarkoṭīciñcikāsvedāt phaṇī tāmbūlaṃ laśunaṃ rasonaḥ ambujaṃ lavaṇaṃ mārkavaḥ bhṛṅgarājaḥ karkoṭīti pratītā vandhyā ciñcikā amlikā etābhiḥ saha yaḥ svedaḥ yantre agnitāpaḥ tasmāt ||
children.translated_text: From what? From steaming with <s>phaṇī</s>, garlic, <s>ambuja</s>, <s>mārkava</s>, <s>karkoṭī</s>, and <s>ciñcikā</s>. <s>Phaṇī</s> is betel; <s>laśuna</s> is garlic; <s>ambuja</s> is salt; <s>mārkava</s> is <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>; <s>karkoṭī</s> is the plant known as <s>vandhyā</s>; <s>ciñcikā</s> is tamarind. The steaming together with these means the heating by fire in the apparatus.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ samyak labdhavīryaḥ prāptabalo vīryavān rasaḥ capalatvanivṛttaye niyamyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of what sort is it? Properly endowed with potency, having gained strength. The meaning is that the powerful <s>rasa</s> is restrained in order to remove its instability.

children.text: viśeṣaścātra kācakūpīṃ mṛdā lipya raso madhye vimucyate
children.translated_text: And here there is a special procedure: after smearing a glass flask with clay, the <s>rasa</s> is released into the middle.

children.text: kalāṃśaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ dattvā madhye kiṃcit pradīyate ||
children.translated_text: After adding a <s>kalā</s>-portion of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, a little is placed in the middle.
The sealing of the mouth should be made firm with diamond-clay.
After placing the flask in the ground, the cavity should be filled with <s>sitā</s>.
A fire of cow-dung cakes should be maintained for twenty-one days.
This is named the <s>niyāmaka</s>; it causes the fire to reach its limit.
For the removal of instability in one whose potency has been gained through <s>rodhana</s>,

children.text: kriyate yo rasasvedaḥ proktaṃ niyamanaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: the steaming of <s>rasa</s> that is performed is indeed called <s>niyamana</s>.
Thus.
The characteristic of the apparatus, however, is this:
It holds four <s>prasthas</s> of water and has a chamber of four <s>aṅgulas</s>.
This is called the pot-apparatus, and it is remembered as the nourishing apparatus.
Clarifying the procedure for the <s>dīpana-saṃskāra</s>, listed as the eighth, he says, 'with <s>bhū</s>, <s>khaga</s>,' and so on.

children.text: asau pūrvasaṃskṛtarasa etair auṣadhais tridinaṃ nirantaraṃ yathā syāt tathā svedena dīpitaḥ kṣutpīḍitaḥ san grāsārthī kavalābhilāṣī jāyate ||
children.translated_text: That previously processed <s>rasa</s>, when kindled by steaming continuously for three days with these medicines, becomes afflicted with hunger and desirous of a morsel.

children.text: etair oṣadhaiḥ bhūkhagaṭaṅkaṇamaricaiḥ na kevalam etaiḥ punar lavaṇāsurīśigrukāñjikaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With these medicines: <s>bhū</s>, <s>khaga</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and black pepper; not only with these, but also with salt, <s>āsurī</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>kāñjika</s>.

children.text: bhūḥ tuvarī khagaḥ kāsīsaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ maricam ūṣaṇam etaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhū</s> is <s>tuvarī</s>; <s>khaga</s> is green vitriol; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is borax; black pepper is <s>ūṣaṇa</s>; with these.

children.text: punaḥ lavaṇaṃ saindhavam āsurī rājikā śigruḥ saubhāñjanaṃ vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ kāñjikaṃ pūrvoktam amlībhūtam etaiśceti ||
children.translated_text: Again, salt is rock-salt; <s>āsurī</s> is mustard; <s>śigru</s> is <s>saubhāñjana</s>, a particular tree; and <s>kāñjika</s> is the previously mentioned fermented sour gruel. With these also.
And here there is a special procedure:
The steaming of <s>rasarāja</s> should be done with alkalis, sour substances, poisons, and liquors.
Taking a citron, one should remove the stalk and prepare it.
In its middle one should place <s>sūta</s> together with a <s>kalā</s>-portion of alkali.
Having carefully closed the opening, one should bind it inside cloth.
A <s>dolā</s>-steaming should be performed for twenty-one days.
Day by day a fresh citron should be prepared.
Licking up the metals, and oppressed by hunger,
by this very means the kindling of <s>rasarāja</s> should be performed.
For three days, or seven days, or fourteen, or twenty-one,

children.text: saṃskāraḥ sūtarāje tu kramāt kramataraṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: the <s>saṃskāra</s> for <s>sūtarāja</s> is progressively better, step by step.
Thus.

children.text: kṛtāṣṭasaṃskārasya pāradasya saṃskārāntarasiddhāṃ parīkṣām āha itītyādi ||
children.translated_text: He states the examination, established by a further <s>saṃskāra</s>, of mercury whose eight <s>saṃskāras</s> have been completed, saying 'thus,' and so on.

children.text: iti pūrvoktaprakāreṇa rasarājo dīpitaḥ san kṣudutpīḍitaḥ san viśuddho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when <s>rasarāja</s> has been kindled in the previously stated manner, and when it is afflicted by hunger, it becomes purified.

children.text: yadīdṛśo bhavati rasarājastadā cāryaḥ cāraṇakarma kāryam ||
children.translated_text: If <s>rasarāja</s> is of such a kind, then it should be made to undergo <s>cāraṇa</s>; the <s>cāraṇa</s> operation should be performed.

children.text: kīdṛk pracalitavidyullatāsahasrābhaḥ prakarṣeṇa calatyaś calanaśīlā yā vidyutastāsāṃ sahasrasyeva bhā dīptir yasya sa tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind? Having a brilliance like a thousand flashing streaks of lightning, that is, possessing a radiance like that of a thousand moving flashes of lightning.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā cāryaḥ idamagre vakṣyamāṇaṃ kiṃcit dhātūparasamahārasaratnasaṃjñakaṃ dvitīyaṃ rasarājasambandhinaṃ dattvā saṃyojyetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After doing what should it be made to undergo <s>cāraṇa</s>? After adding and combining with it a certain second substance, to be described next, connected with <s>rasarāja</s> and designated as a metal, secondary mineral, great mineral, or gem.
Anticipating the question, 'What is the second substance?', he clarifies it by saying, 'yellow,' and so on.

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ mukhaṃ vidheyam ityadhyāhāraḥ pāradasya mukhaṃ kāryamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning, 'first the mouth is to be made' is to be supplied; the meaning is that the mouth of <s>pārada</s> (mercury) is to be made.

children.text: tataścetpītakriyā bhavanti svarṇasambandhīni kāryāṇi bhavanti tadā pītaṃ svarṇaṃ deyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, if there are yellow operations, that is, operations connected with gold, then the yellow substance, gold, should be given.

children.text: śvetakriyāsu śvetaṃ deyaṃ śvetaṃ tāram ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In white operations the white substance should be given; the white substance means <s>tāra</s> (silver).
When gold, silver, and the like have been given in the mortar, the <s>rasa</s> whose mouth has been made moves and consumes.

children.text: punarnirmukho rasaḥ akṛtamukho rasaḥ khalve ghṛṣṭo gharṣitaḥ san pūrvoktaṃ carati bhakṣayati ||
children.translated_text: Again, mouthless <s>rasa</s>, that is, <s>rasa</s> whose mouth has not been made, when rubbed and ground in the mortar, consumes what was stated earlier.
With what? With the divine herbs that will be described.
As in the verse:

children.text: sāsyo rasaḥ syātpaṭuśigrututthaiḥ sarājikair vyoṣaṇakais trirātram
children.translated_text: A <s>rasa</s> with a mouth comes about from salts produced from <s>śigru</s>, together with mustard seeds and the three pungents, over three nights.
Then, when it has been ground and its body steamed, this one whose mouth is toward gold eats gold and all metals.
Thus.
And one should triturate the mouthless one with the sour group, combined according to availability.
The <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), having a mouth through conditioning, consumes mica and the rest.
The limit consisting of edible material for a given quantity of <s>sūta</s> (mercury)
is called 'so much'; that is said to be the measure of the <s>grāsa</s> (morsel).
Thus the technical definition.

Thus ends the second instruction, consisting of the purification of <s>rasa</s>, in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s> commentary called <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>, composed by <s>Caturbhuja Miśra</s>, son of <s>Miśra Maheśa</s>, the moon to the ocean of the noble <s>Kurala</s> family.
The essence of <s>Sudhākara</s>'s morsel brings happiness to <s>Padmākara</s>.
Likewise, its powers cause joy to good people.

children.text: anena padyena granthasya guṇādhikyaṃ saṃmatatvaṃ ca varṇayannāha ghanetyādi ||
children.translated_text: With this verse, while describing the great excellence and accepted authority of the work, he says, beginning with 'ghana.'
Men of such a kind are indeed miserly.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ ghanarahitabījacāraṇasamprāptadalādidravyakṛtakṛtyāḥ ghanenābhrakeṇa rahitaṃ varjitaṃ yad bījacāraṇam anyadhātvādīnāṃ bījakavalanaṃ tena yatprāptaṃ dalādidravyaṃ pattrarañjanavarṇavṛddhitārakṛṣṭī melāpakādikaṃ vastu tena ye kṛtakṛtyāḥ pūrṇāḥ ātmānaṃ manyante ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind? Those who, having accomplished their purpose with leaf and similar substances obtained through <s>bīja-cāraṇa</s> devoid of <s>ghana</s>, that is, without mica, think themselves fulfilled; by <s>bīja-cāraṇa</s> is meant the swallowing of seed, such as other metals, and through it are obtained leaf and similar materials, things such as coloring of leaves, increase of color, extraction of silver, and alloying.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ samudraṃ prāpya ratnākaraṃ labdhvā varāṭikālābhasaṃtuṣṭāḥ kapardikālābhena saṃtuṣṭiṃ prāptaḥ daridrabhāvāditi bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of misers? Those who, after reaching the ocean, a mine of jewels, are satisfied with obtaining cowries; the sense is that, because of poverty, they have become satisfied with the gain of cowries.

children.text: tathā evaṃvidhāḥ kṛpaṇā idaṃ śāstraṃ ratnākararūpaṃ bahuratnaṃ prāpya dalādidravyeṇa kṛtakṛtyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, such misers, after obtaining this treatise, which is like a jewel-mine and full of many jewels, regard themselves as fulfilled by leaf and similar substances.

children.text: śāstrasamudrayor guṇaratnaiḥ sāmyaṃ varāṭikādalādirdravyayoḥ sāmyaṃ tucchatayā yata ubhāv api nikṛṣṭāv eva ||
children.translated_text: The treatise and the ocean are alike in possessing jewels of excellence; cowries and leaf-like substances are alike in triviality, since both are certainly low-grade.

For this treatise gives much, since it grants <s>mudrikā-vedha</s>, <s>sparśa-vedha</s>, <s>dhūma-vedha</s>, <s>śabda-vedha</s>, <s>dhāmya-vedha</s>, <s>adhāmya-dhātu-vedha</s>, and other forms of transmuting penetration.

children.text: punaratra granthe guṇādhikyaśataṃ ca varṇayannāhānye ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Again, while describing a hundredfold abundance of merits here in the work, he says, beginning with 'others.'
The word 'again' has the sense of non-primary and qualifying usage; this is the clarification.
Here it is used as a further qualification.
Others, greater than the former ones, exist.

children.text: kiṃ kurvantaḥ parāmṛtaṃ labdhavantaḥ santa amarā jātā maraṇarahitā jīvanmuktā jātā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Doing what? Having obtained the supreme nectar, they became immortal, that is, free from death and liberated while living.

children.text: paraṃ ca tadamṛtaṃ ceti samāsaḥ mokṣam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The compound means 'that which is both supreme and nectar'; it means liberation.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā lakṣmīkarirājakaustubhādīni avadhīrya avahelanaṃ vidhāya lakṣmīrharipriyā karirāja airāvata indravāraṇaḥ kaustubho harermaṇiḥ ityādīni caturdaśaratnāni ||
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having disregarded and treated with contempt <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the king of elephants, <s>Kaustubha</s>, and the rest: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, beloved of <s>Hari</s>; the elephant-king <s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Indra</s>'s elephant; <s>Kaustubha</s>, <s>Hari</s>'s jewel; and the other fourteen jewels.

children.text: satām ayameva svabhāvaḥ daridrāṇāṃ kṛpaṇānāṃ pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: This alone is the nature of good people; the poor and miserly are as stated before.
For this very reason this treatise is a touchstone for misers and great men.
Because it is most excellent, he states the means for <s>gagana-grāsa</s> (the swallowing of mica), beginning with 'alkali.'
'The appetite of <s>rasarāja</s> (the king of rasa, mercury) arises' is to be supplied.

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā kṣārauṣadhipaṭvamlaiḥ kṣārauṣadhayo 'himārādayaḥ paṭu saindhavam amlam amlavetasādi etaiḥ kṣudutpattir bhaved ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By means of what? By alkaline herbs, salts, and sour substances: the alkaline herbs are <s>ahimāra</s> and the rest; <s>paṭu</s> is rock-salt; sour substance is <s>amlavetasa</s> and the like. The meaning is that by these the arising of appetite occurs.
The alkaline herbs are as follows:
<s>Ahimāra</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, together with <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>,
and <s>snuhi</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>karavīra</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>kṣīrakanda</s>;
<s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>tumbā</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and <s>agnimanthaka</s>;

children.text: karīraṃ citrakaṃ śigruṃ varuṇaṃ vetasaṃ vaṭam ||
children.translated_text: <s>karīra</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>varuṇa</s>, <s>vetasa</s>, and <s>vaṭa</s>;
<s>paṭolī</s>, <s>arjuna</s>, <s>kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, <s>kadalī</s>, and <s>vajrakandaka</s>;

children.text: aśvatthaṃ sūraṇaṃ jālīṃ dahet kandān anekaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>sūraṇa</s>, and <s>jālī</s>; one should burn many tubers.
One should burn all these by internal smoke, and likewise <s>devadālī</s>.
This group is proclaimed under the name 'medicinal alkalis.'
Thus.
The sour group is as follows:
<s>Amlavetasa</s>, <s>jambīra</s>, <s>lakuca</s>, and <s>bījapūraka</s>,

children.text: cāṅgerī caṇakāmlaṃ ca nāraṅgaṃ tittiḍī tathā ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>cāṅgerī</s>, sour chickpea, <s>nāraṅga</s>, and <s>tittiḍī</s>.
Also <s>ambaṣṭhā</s>, <s>karamarda</s>, <s>kapittha</s>, <s>karaṇa</s>, and the like;
or the sour group may be combined with five sour substances; it is so proclaimed.
Among all of them, sour chickpea alone is praised,
or <s>amlavetasa</s> alone is the very best among all.
Thus.

children.text: ityetaiḥ kṣārauṣadhipaṭvamlaiḥ kṣudbodho bhavet rāgabandhane ca bhavetāṃ rāgo rañjanaṃ bandhanaṃ pūrvam upavarṇitam ||
children.translated_text: By these alkaline herbs, salts, and sour substances the awakening of appetite occurs; and coloring and binding also occur. <s>Rāga</s> means coloring, and <s>bandhana</s> has been described earlier.

children.text: kuto hetoḥ etaiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ karaṇarūpaiḥ svedāt ||
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because of steaming by these previously stated procedures.
The word "again" is used as a qualifier.

children.text: pakṣacchedaḥ rasapakṣāpakartanaṃ yathā sthiro bhavati dravyatvaṃ guṇavattvaṃ vā gaganamabhrakaṃ vinā na bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pakṣaccheda</s> is the cutting away of the side or support of <s>rasa</s>; the meaning is that, just as it becomes stable, substantiality or the possession of qualities does not occur without <s>gagana</s>, that is, mica.
He states its substantiality by means of mica, in passages such as "digested with mica."
When it lacks strength and has only very slight awakening, impotence occurs.
For example:
Because of coldness, absence of trituration, and digestion of impure metal,
or because too much <s>viḍa</s> is given, it consumes what is digested and passes into an undigested state.
Because of excessive fire, lack of nourishment, and absence of <s>krāmaṇa</s>,

children.text: ityetā vikriyā jñeyā aṣṭabhiḥ ṣaṇḍhatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: these transformations should be known; through the eight causes it falls into impotence.
Thus.

children.text: ato raso'ṣṭasaṃskārānantaram abhrakajīrṇaḥ kartavyaḥ yato'bhrakajīrṇaṃ balavān bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, after the eight <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>rasa</s> should be made digested with mica, because what is digested with mica becomes powerful.

children.text: abhrakajīrṇe grāsanyāye na jāritaṃ yasmin sa tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the case of <s>abhrakajīrṇa</s>, according to the rule of the morsel, that in which the mica has not been digested is spoken of in this way.

children.text: tasyābhrajāraṇāyogyasya rasasya cāraṇe kevalakavalane ete proktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the <s>cāraṇa</s>, the mere swallowing, of that <s>rasa</s> which is not fit for mica-digestion, these procedures are taught.

children.text: ete ke saṃdhānavāsanauṣadhinirmukhasamukhā eva mahāyogāḥ mahaddravyatvakārakāḥ saṃdhānaṃ sarvadhānyānām aṣṭauṣadhyādīnāṃ ca saṃdhānaṃ yathā sarvadhānyāni nikṣipya āranālaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: What are these? They are the great operations called <s>saṃdhāna</s>, <s>vāsanauṣadhi</s>, <s>nirmukha</s>, and <s>samukha</s>, which produce great substantiality. <s>Saṃdhāna</s> is the combining of all grains and of the eight herbs and the like; for example, after placing all the grains, one should make <s>āranāla</s>.
One should put into it herbs furnished with leaves and roots.
With <s>kṣitikāsīsa</s>, sea-salt, rock-salt, the three pungents, and mustard-seed,
one should prepare that mixture and keep it warm for seven days.
And, together with that <s>āranāla</s>, one should ferment it in a copper vessel.
This is <s>saṃdhāna</s> for the purpose of <s>abhraka-cāraṇa</s>.
The <s>vāsanauṣadhi</s> herbs are as follows:
The class of herbs should be understood just as it is stated in the treatises.

children.text: jalajaṃ sthalajaṃ caiva samyak jñātvā tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Having properly distinguished the aquatic and the terrestrial, one should carry out the operation.

children.text: jalajā utpalī padmā sthalajā ca prasāriṇī
children.translated_text: The aquatic plants are <s>utpalī</s> and <s>padmā</s>; the terrestrial ones are <s>prasāriṇī</s>,
<s>jālinī</s>, <s>abhracandrā</s>, <s>citraparṇī</s>, and <s>triparṇikā</s>,
also <s>rasacandraukasa</s>, and likewise <s>jalamūlaka</s>,
<s>samaṅgā</s>, <s>vāribhūtā</s>, and water-born <s>apāmārga</s>.
<s>ajamārī</s>, <s>upāmbu</s>, <s>kumbhikā</s>, and <s>jalapippalī</s>,
<s>jalapūrvā</s>, <s>ambusītā</s>, and likewise <s>kumārī</s> and <s>nāginī</s>.
<s>sitajaṅghā</s> and <s>svara</s>, and likewise <s>sarpa</s> and <s>sugandhikā</s>,
<s>vṛddhā</s> and <s>bṛhatī</s>; similarly <s>mūrti</s> and <s>mārjārapādikā</s>.
Likewise <s>jalacakorī</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, and <s>ahilocanā</s>,

children.text: jayāṃvica varāhī ca apattrā īśvarī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>jayāṃvica</s>, <s>varāhī</s>, <s>apattrā</s>, and <s>īśvarī</s> as well.
<s>kurkurī</s> and <s>halinī</s>, also <s>bṛhatī</s> and <s>vajrakandaka</s>,

children.text: musalī vanamālā ca vidārī mohinī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>musalī</s>, <s>vanamālā</s>, <s>vidārī</s>, and likewise <s>mohinī</s>.

children.text: māṇḍūkī lavaṇā caiva ugrā ca uttamā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>māṇḍūkī</s> and <s>lavaṇā</s>, also <s>ugrā</s> and <s>uttamā</s>,
<s>śikhipādī</s>, <s>kapotī</s>, <s>nandinī</s>, and <s>vṛścikālikā</s>,

children.text: haṃsapādī śikhā caiva sārivā vāyasī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>haṃsapādī</s> and <s>śikhā</s>, also <s>sārivā</s> and <s>vāyasī</s>,
<s>dantī</s> and <s>gojihvikā</s>, also <s>garuḍī</s> and <s>hemapuṣpikā</s>.
<s>samaṅgā</s> and the aquatic plant, also <s>māṃsī</s> and <s>pāṣāṇabhedikā</s>,
<s>alambuṣā</s>, <s>meghanādā</s>, <s>śukanādā</s>, and <s>kapotikī</s>.

children.text: kṣīrikā tulasī dhānyā meṣikā ca vanārjakā
children.translated_text: <s>kṣīrikā</s>, <s>tulasī</s>, <s>dhānyā</s>, <s>meṣikā</s>, and <s>vanārjakā</s>,
<s>vārāhī</s>, <s>caṇakāyāsī</s>, and likewise <s>aparājitā</s>.
This group of sixty-four herbs has indeed been proclaimed.
By the application of the sixth and eighth groups one should not bring about the state.
Thus.
This group of herbs is also to be employed in <s>saṃdhāna</s>.

children.text: saṃdhānaṃ ca vāsanauṣadhayaśca tābhiḥ kṛtvā ye nirmukhasamukhā eva yogāḥ akṛtamukhakṛtamukhā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the operation with <s>saṃdhāna</s> and the <s>vāsanauṣadhi</s> herbs, the preparations that are <s>nirmukha</s> and <s>samukha</s> are precisely those with an unmade mouth and a made mouth.
As the method of <s>abhraka-cāraṇa</s> in the <s>nirmukha</s> mode, he states the passage beginning "niścandrika."

children.text: hi niścitaṃ yadgaganamabhrakaṃ niścandrikaṃ candrarahitaṃ bhavati vajrasaṃjñakam ityarthaḥ tadgaganaṃ rucirair nirdoṣair manoramair vividhaiḥ kṣārāmlair bhāvitaṃ plāvitaṃ kāryaṃ kṣārā yavakṣārasvarjikṣāraṭaṅkaṇakṣārādayo 'mlā amlavetasajambīrādyāḥ pūrvoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For, certainly, the <s>gagana</s>, that is, mica, which is <s>niścandrika</s>, devoid of moon-like lustre, meaning what is called <s>vajra</s>, should be treated and soaked with various attractive, faultless, pleasing alkalis and acids. The alkalis are <s>yavakṣāra</s>, <s>svarjikṣāra</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇakṣāra</s>, and so on; the acids are <s>amlavetasa</s>, <s>jambīra</s>, and the like, as stated earlier.

children.text: nanu kṣārā rucirāḥ kathaṃ bhavanti ucyate yathā sarjikācūrṇabhāgaikaṃ viṃśadbhāgaṃ jalasya ca ||
children.translated_text: But how can alkalis be attractive? The answer is: one part of powdered <s>sarjikā</s> and twenty parts of water

children.text: tāvatkvāthyaṃ kṣiped bhāṇḍe yāvatphenaṃ sitaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: should be boiled in a vessel until white foam appears.

children.text: kṣīṇe kṣīṇe jalaṃ dattvā śvetaphenaṃ ca gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: As the water is repeatedly diminished, more water should be added, and the white foam should be collected.
Then it should be dissolved by the <s>ḍekayantra</s> through the application of fire.
The dissolving should be done twenty-one times, combined with urine.
This, called <s>svarjikākṣāra</s>, is considered supreme for dissolving.
Thus the special procedure.
In this way the alkalis become extremely excellent, well-cooked, and cooling.

children.text: punaḥ sṛṣṭitrayanīrakaṇātumbarurasamarditaṃ go'jāvinārīṇāṃ mūtraṃ śukraṃ ca śoṇitaṃ sṛṣṭitrayaṃ nīrakaṇā jalapippalī paṭuriti loke tumburu pratītaṃ jalakaṇā ca tumbaruśca anayo rasaḥ sṛṣṭitrayaṃ ca jalakaṇātumbarurasaśca tābhyāṃ mardanaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Again, trituration should be done with the three products of generation, with <s>nīrakaṇā</s>, and with <s>tumburu</s> juice. The three products of generation are urine, semen, and blood from cow, goat, sheep, and woman. <s>Nīrakaṇā</s> is <s>jalapippalī</s>, known in common speech as <s>paṭu</s>; <s>tumburu</s> is well known. Thus the rubbing is to be done with the three products of generation and with the juice of <s>jalakaṇā</s> and <s>tumburu</s>.

children.text: rasaḥ pāradaḥ nirmukho'pi evaṃvidhaṃ gaganaṃ carati grāsīkaroti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> means <s>pārada</s>, mercury. Even when <s>nirmukha</s>, it consumes such <s>gagana</s> and makes it into a morsel.
The procedure is found in another treatise:
The three milks, the water of <s>kumārī</s>, <s>gaṅgāputra</s>, and the three urines,
with the shoot of the banyan and goat's blood: mica well triturated with these,
and fired a hundred times, becomes like a ruby.

children.text: niścandrikaṃ mṛtaṃ tv abhraṃ vṛddhadehe rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: Dead mica that is <s>niścandrika</s> is a rejuvenant in an aged body.
It destroys the intoxication and pride of passion; it is praised for those whose virility has been impaired.
Thus.
He states another procedure, beginning with "yava," and so on.

children.text: punarabhrakaṃ yavaciñcikāmbupuṭitaṃ kāryaṃ yavaciñcikā pratītā yavaciñciketi loke tasyā ambudravaḥ tena puṭitam ātapayogena bhāvitam ||
children.translated_text: Again, the mica should be made treated with the water of <s>yavaciñcikā</s>. <s>Yavaciñcikā</s> is well known, being called <s>yavaciñcikā</s> in common speech; its watery liquid is meant. Treated with that, it is impregnated by exposure to the sun.

children.text: punastanmūlaśatāvarīgadākulitaṃ kāryaṃ tasyā yavaciñcikāyā mūlaṃ tanmūlaṃ śatāvarī śatapād gadaḥ kuṣṭhaḥ etair ākulaṃ vyāptaṃ pariplutam ||
children.translated_text: Again, it should be made saturated with its root, <s>śatāvarī</s>, and <s>gada</s>. Its root means the root of that <s>yavaciñcikā</s>; <s>śatāvarī</s> is <s>śatapād</s>; <s>gada</s> is <s>kuṣṭha</s>. With these it is filled, pervaded, and soaked.
When fresh medicinal plants are unavailable, this is the rule, as follows:
When the fresh juices are unobtainable, one should take the dry substance,
cook it in eight times as much water, and take it when one quarter remains.
Thus.

children.text: punar ghanaravaśigrupunarnavarasabhāvitaṃ kāryaṃ ghanaravas taṇḍulīyakaḥ śigru saubhāñjanaṃ suhijanā iti loke punarnavā varṣābhūḥ pratītā eteṣāṃ rasena bhāvitaṃ pariplutam ātapayogena śoṣyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, it should be made impregnated with the juices of <s>ghanarava</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>. <s>Ghanarava</s> is <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s>; <s>śigru</s> is <s>saubhāñjana</s>, called <s>suhijanā</s> in common speech; <s>punarnavā</s> is <s>varṣābhū</s>, and is well known. The meaning is that it is impregnated and soaked with the juice of these and then dried by exposure to the sun.
Mica prepared in this way is consumed by <s>rasa</s>.
In the <s>nirmukha</s> procedure, the word <s>bhāvanā</s> should be understood as meaning one hundred times, because this agrees with another treatise.
Here there is a special point.
Having ground it in the juice of <s>somavallī</s>, one should give it three <s>puṭas</s>,
and with the juice of <s>somavallī</s> itself one should impregnate it seven times.
One should place it in an earthen vessel, combined with <s>rasa</s>.
One should grind the root of <s>śarapuṅkhā</s> with cow's milk,
and mix <s>sūta</s> with the paste; the <s>gagana</s> then moves below and above it.
One should set it in the heat of the sun; when without a mouth, it consumes it at once.

children.text: jāyate piṣṭikā śīghraṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: A <s>piṣṭikā</s> is quickly produced; no doubt should be entertained here.
Thus.
And another procedure:
Having taken the juice of <s>tilaparṇī</s>, one should impregnate <s>gagana</s> with it.
By trituration a <s>piṣṭi</s> is produced; no doubt should be entertained here.
Thus.
And another procedure:
One should repeatedly quench lead in the extract of <s>muṇḍī</s>.

children.text: tenābhrakaṃ tu saṃyojya bhūyo bhūyaḥ paṭe dahet ||
children.translated_text: Having combined mica with that, one should burn it again and again on cloth.
With each of the roots of <s>citraka</s> and fresh ginger, seven times each,
the powdered sulfur and mica should be carefully soaked.
Mixed with lead and the juice of <s>muṇḍī</s>, and impregnated with the sour juice of <s>rasaluṅga</s>,
it should be added as a sixteenth part; in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, the <s>rasa</s> will consume it.
Thus the <s>nirmukha-cāraṇa</s>.
He states the <s>samukha-cāraṇa</s>, beginning with "<s>sarjī</s>," and so on.
<s>Āranāla</s> is the <s>kāñjika</s> that was mentioned in the steaming procedure.
"In an <s>arka</s> vessel" means in a copper vessel.
For three days, for that long, one should make it ferment.

children.text: kīdṛgvidham āranālaṃ sarjīkṣitikhagaṭaṅkaṇalavaṇānvitaṃ sarjī pratītā sājīti loke kṣitiḥ sphaṭikā khagaḥ kāsīsaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ sohāgā iti loke lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ tadabhāve lavaṇāṣṭakeṣu yatra yallabhyaṃ tadeva yojyaṃ lavaṇoddeśaḥ
children.translated_text: What sort of <s>āranāla</s>? It is furnished with <s>sarjī</s>, <s>kṣiti</s>, <s>khaga</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and salt. <s>Sarjī</s> is well known, called <s>sājī</s> in common speech; <s>kṣiti</s> is alum; <s>khaga</s> is green vitriol; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s>, called <s>sohāgā</s> in common speech; salt is rock salt. In its absence, whichever of the eight salts is available should be used. The enumeration of salts is:

children.text: saindhavaṃ rucakaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ viḍaṃ sāmudram audbhidam
children.translated_text: Rock salt, <s>rucaka</s>, black salt, <s>viḍa</s>, sea salt, and <s>audbhida</s>,
<s>romaka</s> and <s>pāṃśuja</s>: these are called the eight salts.
Thus it should be made furnished with these, that is, mixed with them.

children.text: tadāranālaṃ gaganādikabhāvane abhrakādiplāvane śastaṃ pradhānam abhrakādikā agre vakṣyamāṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>āranāla</s> is excellent and principal for impregnating <s>gagana</s> and the rest, and for soaking mica and the rest. "Mica and the rest" are those to be stated later.

children.text: nirmukhā samukhā ceti dvividhā cāraṇā matā nirmukhā cāraṇā proktā bījādhānena bhāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Cāraṇa</s> is considered twofold, <s>nirmukha</s> and <s>samukha</s>. <s>Nirmukha-cāraṇa</s> has been stated by way of depositing the seed in a measured portion.

children.text: śuddhaṃ svarṇaṃ ca rūpyaṃ ca bījam ityabhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Purified gold and silver are called the seed.
The introduction of seed in a sixty-fourth part is called the mouth.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte raso grāsalolupo mukhavān bhavet
children.translated_text: When this has been done, <s>rasa</s> becomes furnished with a mouth and greedy for morsels.
It becomes capable of eating even hard metals.

children.text: iyaṃ hi samukhā proktā cāraṇā varavārttikaiḥ
children.translated_text: This is declared to be <s>samukha-cāraṇa</s> by the best alchemical authorities.
Thus.

children.text: abhrakādyapadhātūnāṃ nirmukhacāraṇaṃ hemādidhātūnāṃ samukhacāraṇam iti viveko jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The distinction should be understood as follows: for inferior metals such as mica there is <s>nirmukha-cāraṇa</s>, while for metals such as gold there is <s>samukha-cāraṇa</s>.

children.text: rasāyane śarīrakārye nāgavaṅgau na cāraṇīyau kiṃtu svarṇādikaṃ bījaṃ cāraṇīyam iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>rasāyana</s>, when the aim concerns the body, lead and tin should not be subjected to <s>cāraṇa</s>; rather, seed such as gold should be subjected to <s>cāraṇa</s>. This is the sense.
By the word "and the rest," he states the special application of lead and tin, beginning with "in that," and so on.

children.text: tasmin pūrvoktasaṃdhāne śuddhaṃ nirmalīkṛtaṃ nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ pradrāvya jalarūpaṃ vidhāya vahniyogāt iti śeṣaḥ niṣecayet niṣekaḥ kartavyaḥ vā tatraiva saṃdhāne vaṅgaṃ raṅgaṃ pradrāvya niṣecayet ||
children.translated_text: In that previously mentioned fermented liquid, one should melt purified and cleansed lead, that is, <s>sīsaka</s>, make it liquid like water by the application of fire, as must be supplied, and quench it; or, in that very fermented liquid, one should melt tin, that is, <s>raṅga</s>, and quench it.
How many times? One hundred times; the meaning is, a full hundred times.

children.text: tadvaṅgaṃ tāravidhau rūpyavidhāne yojyaṃ rasena saha militaṃ kāryam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That tin should be used in the procedure for silver, that is, in the operation concerning silver; it should be made mixed together with <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: āsyām āryāyāṃ svarṇādhikāre'nuktamapi nāgaṃ granthāntarāt samāyojyam iti viśeṣārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this <s>āryā</s> verse, although lead is not mentioned in the section on gold, it should nevertheless be supplied from another treatise; this is the special meaning.

children.text: tannāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca rasāyane śarīrasiddhinimittaṃ na yojyamiti yato nāgavaṅgaprabhavāv aupādhikau doṣau galabandhagulmadau kathitau etannāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca grāsārthe yojyamiti yuktaṃ yata etenāntargatenānyadapi grāhyaṃ dravyaṃ grasatīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That lead and tin should not be used in <s>rasāyana</s> for the purpose of bodily perfection, because the adventitious defects produced from lead and tin are said to cause throat obstruction and <s>gulma</s>. It is proper that this lead and tin be used for the sake of a morsel, because when it has entered within, the <s>rasa</s> consumes other material as well. This is the sense.
A special point concerning tin:

children.text: khurakaṃ miśrakaṃ ceti dvividhaṃ vaṅgam ucyate
children.translated_text: Tin is said to be of two kinds, <s>khuraka</s> and <s>miśraka</s>.

children.text: khurakaṃ guṇataḥ śreṣṭhaṃ miśrakaṃ na rase hitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khuraka</s> is superior in its qualities; <s>miśraka</s> is not beneficial for <s>rasa</s>.
Thus the suitable one should be taken for work with silver.
Clarifying the sequence beginning with <s>gagana</s> and the rest, he says, beginning with "<s>gagana</s>," and so on.

children.text: anena pūrvoktasaṃdhānena sarvaṃ sakalaṃ bhāvyaṃ bhāvitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: By this previously stated preparation, one should make everything, the whole set of materials, <s>bhāvya</s>, that is, impregnated or processed.
What is meant by 'everything'? Powders of <s>gagana</s> (mica), <s>rasa</s>, <s>uparasa</s>, <s>amṛtaloha</s>, metals, <s>rasāyana</s> substances, and so on.

children.text: gaganamabhrakaṃ vajrasaṃjñikaṃ rasā mahārasā hiṅgulasvarṇamākṣikarūpyamākṣikaśilājatucapalacumbakavaikrāntakharparagairikasphaṭikakāsīsasaṃjñakā amṛtaṃ viṣaṃ vā amṛtalohā na mṛtā amṛtā amṛtāśca te lohāś ca dhāvata iti rasāḥ pūrvoktāḥ āyasā lohās teṣāṃ saṃyogajāni yāni cūrṇāni kalkāni śulbābhrādīni ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gagana</s> is <s>abhraka</s> (mica), also known as <s>vajra</s>. The <s>rasas</s> are the <s>mahārasas</s> called <s>hiṅgula</s>, <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>, <s>rūpyamākṣika</s>, <s>śilājatu</s>, <s>capala</s>, <s>cumbaka</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>kharpara</s>, <s>gairika</s>, <s>sphaṭika</s>, and <s>kāsīsa</s>. <s>Amṛta</s> is either poison; <s>amṛtalohas</s> are metals that are not dead, but living. The previously mentioned substances are called <s>rasas</s> because they flow; <s>āyasas</s> are metals. The powders and pastes born from combinations of these, such as copper and mica, are meant.
By the word 'and so on,' the <s>uparasas</s> too are included.

children.text: na kevalametānyeva saṃdhānena bhāvyāni kiṃtvanyad api yat kiṃcic cāraṇāvastu cāraṇayogyaṃ dravyaratnādikaṃ tadapyetena saṃdhānena bhāvyaṃ cāraṇārtham ||
children.translated_text: Not only these substances are to be processed with the preparation, but anything else that is a material for <s>cāraṇā</s>, any substance such as gems that is fit for <s>cāraṇā</s>, is also to be processed with this preparation for the sake of <s>cāraṇā</s>.
He states the particular rule concerning gold and silver with the words 'at first,' and so on.

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ hemnaḥ svarṇasya piṣṭīṃ khalve mṛditāṃ vakṣyamāṇena iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that, that is, next, the <s>piṣṭi</s> (paste) of gold, pounded in a mortar, is to be used by the method that will be stated; this is to be supplied.
The <s>rasa</s> acts upon that <s>piṣṭi</s>.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā piṣṭīṃ dadyāt ādau prathamataḥ sūteśvare gaganamabhrakaṃ dattvā ||
children.translated_text: What should one do before adding the <s>piṣṭi</s>? First, one should add <s>gagana</s>, namely mica, to <s>sūteśvara</s> (lordly mercury).
The rule for gold has been shown.
In an operation involving gold, one should add gold alone; in an operation involving silver, silver alone.
A special point concerning gold:
Gold is said to be fivefold: natural, innate, and fire-born;
this threefold gold should be employed when it is of sixteen <s>varṇas</s>.
That which is mine-born and that which is produced by alchemical transmutation, made into good leaf and purified,
is endowed with fourteen <s>varṇas</s> and removes the diseases of human beings.
Thus.
There is also a special point concerning silver:

children.text: kailāse sahajaṃ rūpyaṃ khanijaṃ kṛtrimaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Silver is innate on <s>Kailāsa</s>, and likewise mine-born and artificial;

children.text: vyutkrameṇa guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ nāgottīrṇe rase hitam ||
children.translated_text: in reverse order, it is superior in qualities and is beneficial in mercury extracted from lead.
Thus.
Silver too, of the previously stated grade, should be subjected to <s>cāraṇā</s>.
He states the vessel and medicines for grinding the <s>piṣṭi</s> with the words 'in small portions,' and so on.

children.text: abhrahemalohādīni abhramabhrakaṃ pratītaṃ hema kanakaṃ tadeva lohaḥ abhrakaṃ ca hemalohaśca tāv ādī yasya tat ||
children.translated_text: 'Mica, gold, metals, and so on' means this: <s>abhra</s> is the well-known mica; <s>hema</s> is gold; that itself is a metal. The compound refers to a substance beginning with mica and gold-metal.

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ dravyaṃ kṣitikhagavetasabījapūrāmlaiḥ kṣitiśca khagaś ca vetasaṃ ca bījapūraś ca kṣitikhagabījapūrāḥ bījapūro mātuluṅgaḥ teṣāṃ trayāṇāmamlāḥ tair mṛditaṃ gharṣitaṃ sat rasendraś carati ||
children.translated_text: A substance of this sort, once it has been ground and rubbed with the acids of <s>kṣiti</s>, <s>khaga</s>, <s>vetasa</s>, and <s>bījapūra</s>, is acted upon by <s>rasendra</s> (lordly mercury). Here <s>bījapūra</s> means citron, and the sour liquids of those three are meant.
What should one do before grinding it? One should add it in <s>truṭi</s>-sized, very small portions.
In what? In a <s>sāra</s> mortar.
That is, in just such a <s>sāra</s>, a mortar made from the essence of the sharp class of metal.
A special point concerning <s>sāra</s>:

children.text: muṇḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tathā kāntaṃ bhedāstasya trayodaśa
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍa</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>kānta</s>: its divisions are thirteen.

children.text: mṛdu kuṇṭhaṃ ca kaḍāraṃ trividhaṃ muṇḍamucyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛdu</s>, <s>kuṇṭha</s>, and <s>kaḍāra</s>; <s>muṇḍa</s> is said to be threefold.

children.text: kharasāraṃ ca hannālaṃ tārāvartaṃ viḍaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kharasāra</s>, <s>hannāla</s>, <s>tārāvarta</s>, and <s>viḍa</s>,
together with <s>kālaloha</s> and that called <s>gaja</s>; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is said to be sixfold.

children.text: kāntaṃ lohaṃ caturdhoktaṃ romakaṃ bhrāmakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> iron is declared to be fourfold: <s>romaka</s> and <s>bhrāmaka</s>,
<s>cumbaka</s> and <s>drāvaka</s>; their qualities increase successively.
Thus.
The mortar is as follows:
A mortar, made of stone and the like, without cracks, should have a two-<s>aṅgula</s> bowl.

children.text: aṣṭāṅgulāvaṭī kāryā dīrghā vā vartulā tathā ||
children.translated_text: Its cavity should be eight <s>aṅgulas</s>, either long or round.
The pestle should be twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> long and four <s>aṅgulas</s> thick.
The mouth should be made round, resembling the interior of a mirror.
Thus.
In 'made of stone and the like,' one should understand stone, iron, and <s>arka</s>.
He states the measure for the <s>cāraṇā</s> of metals and the like with the words 'with mouth,' and so on.

children.text: iti pūrvoktaṃ pattrābhrakam uktaṃ pattrābhrakacāraṇam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The previously stated leaf-mica is meant; that is, the <s>cāraṇā</s> of leaf-mica.

children.text: samukhaṃ mukhasahitaṃ cāraṇaṃ bhavatu vātha nirmukhaṃ mukhavarjitaṃ cāraṇaṃ bhavatu ubhayatrāpi tulyaṃ samānaṃ sūtaṃ cārayet dhātvādīniti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether the <s>cāraṇā</s> is <s>samukha</s>, with a mouth, or <s>nirmukha</s>, without a mouth, in both cases one should feed an equal amount of <s>sūta</s>; 'metals and the like' is to be supplied.

children.text: atra vikalpo dviguṇaṃ sūtād dviguṇitaṃ cārayed vā caturguṇitaṃ sūtāccaturguṇitaṃ vā aṣṭaguṇaṃ sūtādaṣṭaguṇitaṃ vā ṣoḍaśaguṇaṃ sūtāt ṣoḍaśaguṇitaṃ vā dvātriṃśatāguṇitaṃ sūtād dvātriṃśadguṇitaṃ cārayet ||
children.translated_text: Here there is an option: one may feed twice the amount of the <s>sūta</s>, or four times the amount of the <s>sūta</s>, or eight times the amount of the <s>sūta</s>, or sixteen times the amount of the <s>sūta</s>, or thirty-two times the amount of the <s>sūta</s>.

children.text: tena vidhānena pūrvoktena vidhānena truṭiśo dattvetyādinā ||
children.translated_text: By that method, namely the method stated before beginning with 'adding in small portions.'

children.text: cāraṇā trilakṣaṇā bhavati trīṇi lakṣaṇāni cihnāni yasyāṃ sā tathoktā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Cāraṇā</s> has three marks, that is, it is said to possess three distinguishing signs.

children.text: kathaṃ grāsaḥ abhrakasya grāsanaṃ nirmukhatvena samukhatvena vāparā piṣṭī rasenābhrāder melanaṃ punargarbho rasasya garbhe rasarūpaṃ gaganaṃ tiṣṭhatīti ||
children.translated_text: How? <s>Grāsa</s> is the swallowing of mica, whether without a mouth or with a mouth. Another is <s>piṣṭi</s>, the union of mica and the other substances with <s>rasa</s>. Again there is <s>garbha</s>, because <s>gagana</s> in the form of <s>rasa</s> remains in the womb of the <s>rasa</s>.
Because of the syntactic connection across the two verses, this is a pair of verses.

children.text: iti gaganādigrāsapramāṇaṃ kathitam atha cāraṇāvidhānamāha dolanavidhinetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Thus the measure of the swallowing of <s>gagana</s> and the other substances has been stated. Now he states the procedure of <s>cāraṇā</s> with the words 'by the swinging procedure,' and so on.

children.text: gaganamabhrakaṃ yair auṣadhaiḥ piṣṭaṃ peṣitaṃ bhavati tair evauṣadhair nālpamānair bahumānair nānāvidhabhaṅgasaṃskṛtaṃ kuryāditi śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mica, with whatever medicines it has been ground and pulverized, should be prepared with those same medicines, not in small quantities but in large quantities, by many kinds of <s>bhaṅga</s>; this is to be supplied.

children.text: nānāvidhā anekaprakārā ye bhaṅgās taraṃgā āgamābdhijātās taiḥ saṃskṛtam upaskṛtam ||
children.translated_text: It should be processed and refined by the many kinds of <s>bhaṅgas</s>, waves or procedures, that arise from the ocean of tradition.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ gaganaṃ māraṇavidhinā pañcatvavidhānena uddiṣṭam uddeśitam
children.translated_text: What sort of <s>gagana</s>? That which has been prescribed by the method of killing, that is, by the procedure of reducing it to the condition of the five elements.

children.text: evaṃvidham api gaganaṃ dolanavidhinā cāraṇāyāṃ yojyamiti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sense is that even such <s>gagana</s> (mica) should be applied to <s>cāraṇā</s> (feeding) by the swinging procedure.
Now he states the opinion of those of little understanding with the words beginning "others."

children.text: anye mahadbhyo 'pare tucchamatayas tucchā stokā matirbuddhiryeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ alpabuddhaya iti yāvat ||
children.translated_text: "Others," that is, people distinct from the great ones, are of petty mind: their mind, their intellect, is petty and slight; they are so called. In short, they are of little intelligence.

children.text: rasaṃ jīrṇaṃ jāraṇasaṃskāropapannaṃ rasaṃ manyante iti ||
children.translated_text: They regard <s>rasa</s> (mercury) as "digested," that is, as mercury furnished with the refining process called <s>jāraṇa</s>.

children.text: kiṃ gandhakaniṣpiṣṭiśulbapiṣṭirajo gandhakena yā niṣpiṣṭiḥ piṣṭībhūtā śulbena yā piṣṭiḥ piṣṭībhūtā tāmrapiṣṭītyarthaḥ gandhakaniṣpiṣṭiśca śulbapiṣṭiśca tayoryadrajaḥ pāṃśuḥ gandhakapiṣṭī yathā
children.translated_text: What is the powder of sulphur-triturated paste and copper paste? The trituration made with sulphur is <s>gandhakaniṣpiṣṭi</s>; the paste made with copper, namely a paste-form, is <s>śulbapiṣṭi</s>, that is, copper paste. The powder, the dust, of those two, the sulphur paste and the copper paste, is as follows:
The powder of sulphur-stone, together with the juice of chickpea,
one should impregnate seven times, and also seven times with the blood of a woman.
Then one should place one <s>pala</s> of purified mercury in a potsherd,
and add the treated sulphur, combined with a human lump.
With heat even in a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swinging apparatus), a paste forms at once.
Thus.
In just this way copper paste also arises.
What kind of powder of sulphur-triturated paste and copper paste is meant? That which is produced by the swinging procedure, that is, generated by the arrangement of a swing-apparatus.
The sense is that what has been said in that way is not coherent.
Showing <s>vāsanāmukhacāraṇa</s>, a feeding with a perfuming mouth, as included within <s>samukhacāraṇa</s>, feeding with a mouth, he says the words beginning "with oils."

children.text: rasarājaḥ pārado hāṭakatārādi svarṇarūpyādi dhātudravyaṃ kṛtrimākṛtrimātmakanavasaṃkhyākaṃ pūrvamuktaṃ carati bhakṣati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasarāja</s>, the king of <s>rasa</s>, namely mercury, consumes the metal substances such as gold and silver, the ninefold set, artificial and non-artificial, previously mentioned.
By what means? Through the <s>golaka</s>-mouth.
And <s>golaka</s> is a particular kind of mouth; by that he means by means of a ball of <s>viḍa</s>.
When does this occur? When <s>rasa</s> has been heated with oil and the other substances.

children.text: tailam ādiḥ yeṣāṃ te tailādikās tailavasāmūtraśukrapuṣpāḥ etaistapto yo rasa uṣṇatvaṃ nīto yo 'sau pāradastasmin satyevaṃ ghanamabhrakaṃ carati rasendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The substances beginning with oil are oils, fats, urine, semen, and menstrual fluid; when the <s>rasa</s>, the mercury that has been brought to heat by these, is present in this way, <s>rasendra</s> consumes dense <s>abhra</s>, mica.
Again, with the nine substances beginning with gold made into morsels and swallowed, it comes to the state of a lump, that is, it attains compactness.
The oils are as follows:
Oil produced from <s>kaṅguṇī</s>, <s>tumbinī</s>, <s>ghoṣā</s>, <s>karañja</s>, and <s>śrīphala</s>,
and from <s>kaṭuvātāri</s>, <s>siddhārtha</s>, <s>somarājī</s>, and <s>vibhītaka</s>;
from flaxseed, from <s>mahākālī</s>, from neem, and also from sesame.
<s>Apāmārga</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>tumburu</s> are also included as substances.
Oil arises from the fruits of <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>unmatta</s>, and <s>bhallāta</s>.
Thus.
Fat is as follows:
The fat of goats, camels, donkeys, and rams, and likewise the fat of a buffalo.
Thus.
The urines, menstrual fluids, and semen are as follows:
The urines of elephants, young camels, she-buffaloes, donkeys, and horses;

children.text: striyaḥ puṃsas tathā mūtraṃ puṣpaṃ vīryaṃ ca yojayet
children.translated_text: one should apply the urine of a woman and also of a man, together with menstrual fluid and semen.
Thus.
With that intention in view, he states another opinion with the words beginning "others."

children.text: eke uktavidhānena cāraṇāṃ kurvanti anye apare rasaṃ pāradaṃ svacchaṃ kṛtvā svedanādyaṣṭasaṃskāropasaṃskṛtaṃ vidhāya vā hiṅgulotthaṃ ghanam abhrakaṃ cārayanti abhrakasya cāraṇāṃ kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Some perform <s>cāraṇā</s> by the stated procedure; others, having made the <s>rasa</s>, mercury, clear, or having prepared it by the eight processes beginning with sweating, or using mercury produced from <s>hiṅgula</s>, cause dense <s>abhra</s>, mica, to be consumed; they perform the <s>cāraṇā</s> of mica.

children.text: kena śukapicchamukhena śukapicchaṃ saṃdhānaviśeṣaḥ mukhaṃ viśeṣo yeṣāṃ saṃdhānānāṃ tena ||
children.translated_text: By what means? Through the <s>śukapiccha</s>-mouth. <s>Śukapiccha</s>, "parrot-feather," is a particular kind of compounding medium, and the mouth belongs to that particular class of compounding media.

children.text: kva sati cārayanti āśitagrāse sati bhuktakavale sati punaś cāryam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When do they cause it to be consumed? When a swallowed morsel is present, that is, after a mouthful has been eaten, it should again be fed.

children.text: kena siddhopadeśavidhinā siddhā rasasiddhā nityanāthavīranāthādayaḥ pūrvoktāḥ teṣāṃ ya upadeśavidhis tena ||
children.translated_text: By what means? By the instructional procedure of the perfected ones: the <s>rasa</s>-adepts, such as <s>Nityanātha</s> and <s>Vīranātha</s>, mentioned earlier. The procedure of their instruction is meant.

children.text: na śuṣkeṇa saṃdhānenārdrībhāvāt nīrasatāṃ prāptena punaścāraṇā na syāt ||
children.translated_text: It should not be done with a dry compounding medium; because moistening is required, once it has become devoid of juice there would be no further <s>cāraṇā</s>.
<s>Śukapiccha</s> is as follows:
Ashes and alkalis that are very dry, alkalis and salts as well,
one should stir together with the acidic group and place in a copper vessel.
Until it has the appearance of a parrot's feather, one should impregnate mica with that.
The mercury swallows it at that very moment; the <s>golaka</s> is prescribed.
Thus.
With a view to another opinion, he states a different procedure with the words beginning "or else."

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ vidhānaṃ kuryāt athavā pakṣāntare idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: One should perform the procedure previously stated; or else, in an alternative case, one should perform this procedure that is about to be stated.

children.text: mākṣikagaganamiti mākṣikena yuktaṃ gaganam abhrakaṃ samabhāgaṃ dvayaṃ tulyabhāgaṃ puṭitaṃ bhāvitaṃ yat paṭu saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ śāstrāntarasāmyād amlavargeṇa puṭitaṃ tena yutaṃ militaṃ sat pakvaṃ vahnipuṭitaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Mākṣika</s>-<s>gagana</s>" means mica joined with <s>mākṣika</s>. The two, in equal parts, are to be roasted and impregnated. The sharp salt is rock-salt; in agreement with another treatise it is to be roasted with the acidic group. When the mixture is joined with that salt, it should be cooked, that is, subjected to a fire-roasting; this is to be supplied.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā lohapātre muṇḍādibhājane prakṣipya madhye sthāpya ||
children.translated_text: After doing what? After putting it into an iron vessel, a vessel of <s>muṇḍa</s> iron and the like, and placing it in the middle.

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ kṛṣṇābhraṃ svedāntarvahnitāpamadhye rasaḥ pāradaś carati grasati mākṣikasaṃyogāt kṣipram iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This kind of black mica is consumed, that is, swallowed, by <s>rasa</s>, mercury, amid the heat of fire after the sweating process; because of its conjunction with <s>mākṣika</s>, this happens quickly. This is the sense.
He states the instructional procedure with the words beginning "that."

children.text: yenopadeśena gandhābhrakapraveśanaṃ gandhapāṣāṇasaṃyogād yadabhrapraveśena bhavati abhrasya pāradāntaḥpraveśo bhavati tamupadeśamahaṃ kavir vakṣyāmi kathayiṣye ||
children.translated_text: By whatever instruction the entry of sulphur and mica occurs, that is, by which, through conjunction with sulphur-stone and through the entry of mica, the entry of mica into mercury occurs, I, the poet, shall state and explain that instruction.
Because of extreme proximity, the present tense alone is used; the transmitted text here contains a corrupt sign.
"But" means "again."

children.text: pakṣachinnaśca raso rasarasāyanayor yogyaḥ rase jvarādiroganāśake jvarāṅkuśādau rasāyane ca jarāvyādhināśane prayoge yogyaḥ samarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>pakṣachinna</s> <s>rasa</s> is fit for both <s>rasa</s> medicine and <s>rasāyana</s>: it is capable in a <s>rasa</s> preparation that destroys fevers and other diseases, such as <s>Jvarāṅkuśa</s>, and also in a <s>rasāyana</s> application that destroys old age and disease.
As in the <s>Mañjarī</s>:
When it has been killed, it serves for purification of the body; when stupefied, for the destruction of disease.
In some diseases one uses ash of <s>rasa</s> (mercury); in some cases, for bodily purposes, the stupefied form is used.
When it has been bound by the two, one should employ it according to the operation seen in the śāstra.
Thus.
The sense is this: through the introduction of <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) and <s>abhraka</s> (mica), it becomes wing-clipped and motionless.
Specifying <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), he says, 'king of <s>rasa</s>,' and so on.
In the binding of <s>rasa</s>, that is, in the binding of mercury, <s>gandhaka</s> is in every way the most excellent binder.

children.text: kuto yataḥ sūtakapakṣacchedī gandhakaḥ sūtasya pāradasya pakṣau chinatti ||
children.translated_text: Why? Because <s>gandhaka</s> cuts off the wings of <s>sūtaka</s>, that is, of mercury.

children.text: punaḥ kuto rasarājarāgadāyī rasarājaḥ pāradaḥ tasya rāgaṃ rañjanaṃ dadātīti ||
children.translated_text: Again, why? Because it gives color to the king of <s>rasa</s>: the king of <s>rasa</s> is mercury, and it gives color, or dyeing, to it.

children.text: punaḥ kuto bījānāṃ pākajāraṇasamarthaḥ pākaśca jāraṇaṃ ca pākajāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: Again, why? Because it is capable of the cooking and digestion of the <s>bīja</s> substances; cooking and digestion together are meant by 'cooking-digestion.'
He states how the cutting off of the wings of <s>rasa</s> is to be done by <s>gandhaka</s> and <s>abhraka</s>, with the words 'having given,' and so on.

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ khalve lohārkāśmamaye gandhakaṃ truṭiśo dattvā alpamātraṃ vāraṃ vāraṃ gandharasau dattvā tāvanmardanīyaṃ yāvat sā piṣṭikā ekaśarīratā bhavati kajjaliketi vyaktārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: First, in a mortar made of iron, <s>arka</s>-stone, or stone, one should add <s>gandhaka</s> in <s>truṭi</s>-sized portions, that is, in small amounts, again and again; after adding <s>gandha</s> and <s>rasa</s>, one should grind until that paste becomes of one body. This is plainly called <s>kajjalikā</s>.

children.text: tadanu tatpaścāt rasagandhakapiṣṭīkaraṇānantaraṃ tatra rasagandhakapiṣṭyā gaganam abhrakaṃ samabhāganiyojitaṃ gandharasābhyāṃ tulyāṃśaṃ militaṃ kāryam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thereafter, that is, after making a paste of <s>rasa</s> and <s>gandhaka</s>, <s>gagana</s>, meaning <s>abhraka</s> (mica), is to be added there in an equal portion; the sense is that it should be combined with <s>gandha</s> and <s>rasa</s> in equal shares.

children.text: kayā kṛtvā drutabalivasayā drutā dravībhūtā yā balivasā bhekamatsyakarkaṭaśiśumārāṇāṃ tailarūpā śarīrajātā tayā ||
children.translated_text: With what? With liquefied <s>balivasā</s>: that is, the melted fat, in the form of oil, produced from the bodies of frogs, fish, crabs, and <s>śiśumāra</s>.
The intended meaning is that, after adding an equal portion of <s>abhraka</s>, grinding should be done with <s>balivasā</s>.
<s>Balivasā</s> is as follows:
the fat that comes from frog and fish, or else the fat of a crab;

children.text: bhāvyam ebhiḥ kramād gandhaṃ śiśumāravasāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: one should impregnate <s>gandha</s> successively with these, or also with the fat of <s>śiśumāra</s>.
Any one among these is <s>balivasā</s>, a true binder of <s>sūta</s> (mercury),
and it also produces coloring, according to the procedure of the jewel crucible.
This, called <s>balivasā</s>, binds <s>sūtaka</s> in an instant.
Thus.
The meaning is that one should make a paste of <s>rasa</s>, <s>gandha</s>, and <s>abhra</s>.

children.text: sā pūrvoktā rasagandhābhrapiṣṭir athetyanantaraṃ dīpikāyantre 'dhaḥpātane raso nirmuktamalas tyaktadoṣo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: That previously mentioned paste of <s>rasa</s>, <s>gandha</s>, and <s>abhra</s>, then, immediately afterward, in a <s>dīpikā</s> apparatus by downward distillation, becomes <s>rasa</s> freed from impurity and rid of defects.
When it is free from impurity in that way, it becomes one whose wings have been cut off.

children.text: kābhyām abhragandhābhyām abhraṃ ca gandhaśca abhragandhau tābhyāṃ gandhakāntaḥ saṃyogāt sukhaṃ rasābhrapiṣṭirbhavet yato gandhako dvaṃdvamelanasamarthaḥ kiṃ punarbalivasayeti tṛtīyaślokārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By what two? By <s>abhra</s> and <s>gandha</s>: <s>abhra</s> and <s>gandha</s> together are <s>abhragandhau</s>. Because of union ending in <s>gandhaka</s>, a paste of <s>rasa</s> and <s>abhra</s> is easily produced, since <s>gandhaka</s> is capable of joining a pair; how much more so with <s>balivasā</s>. This is the meaning of the third verse.
It is a connected set of verses.
He states the form of the previously processed <s>rasa</s> and the accomplishment of another operation with the words 'ash,' and so on.
And again.
Then, because of the downward distillation, the <s>rasa</s> becomes ash-like, resembling ash.

children.text: sa ca bhasmākāro rasaḥ hemnā svarṇena sārdham ubhayamelane yujyate karmavidā iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that ash-like <s>rasa</s> is fit to be joined with <s>hema</s>, gold; 'by one who knows the operation' is to be supplied.

children.text: athavā samuccaye avyayo rekārthasambandhāt pakṣāntare ca ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the indeclinable 'athavā' has an aggregative sense; and, because of connection with the syllable 're', there is another alternative as well.

children.text: athavā hemnā saha pūrvarasavidhānena gandhapiṣṭiṃ kuryāt athavā drutagandhakasya dravībhūtagandhakasya madhye paktvā vahniyogena supakvaṃ kṛtvā rasaṃ piṣṭivat rasahemagandhapiṣṭiṃ kuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, with gold, one should make a <s>gandha-piṣṭi</s> according to the previous method of <s>rasa</s>; or, after cooking the <s>rasa</s> in the midst of melted <s>gandhaka</s>, making it well cooked through the application of fire, one should make a paste of <s>rasa</s>, gold, and <s>gandha</s>, like a <s>piṣṭi</s>.
He states the procedure for joining the previously indicated pair with the words 'that,' and so on.
And again.

children.text: sā pūrvoktā hemapiṣṭiḥ rasahemagandhakṛtaretasoḥ sambandhaḥ sadātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That previously mentioned gold paste is the lasting conjunction of the essence produced by <s>rasa</s>, gold, and <s>gandha</s>.

children.text: hemnā militā yā piṣṭimelanaviśet sā hemapiṣṭī bhūyaḥ punaḥ gandhake vipacyate yuktyā pākaḥ kāryaḥ pūrvavad gandhake ||
children.translated_text: The paste-mixture joined with gold is that gold paste; it is again cooked in <s>gandhaka</s>. The cooking should be done skillfully in <s>gandhaka</s>, as before.

children.text: ittham uktavidhānena hemnā saha sūtaḥ pārado milati granthimeti kva sati dvaṃdve sati ubhayasaṃyoge sati ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by the stated procedure, <s>sūta</s>, mercury, unites with gold and reaches a knot when the pair exists, that is, when there is a union of the two.

children.text: tathoktavidhānena dvaṃdve milati sati tatkālād alpakālato mriyate pañcatvamupayāti ||
children.translated_text: When the pair has been joined by the stated procedure, it dies at that very time, or after a short time.
The sense is that it becomes dead when a small further operation has been performed.
Thus ends the procedure for cutting the wings.

children.text: etāvatā rasapakṣakartanena nālaṃ bhavitavyamityāha itare ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Having said so much, he says that merely cutting the wings of <s>rasa</s> should not be considered sufficient, with the words 'others,' and so on.

children.text: ye puruṣā iti uktavidhānena pakṣacchedaṃ rasapakṣāpakartanaṃ vāñchanti punaḥ dvaṃdve rasamāraṇaṃ dvaṃdvena pūrvoktena rasahemagandhakena kṛtvā yadrasamāraṇaṃ tanna vāñchanti punarbījānāmapi raktābhrahemarasakādīnāmapi pākaṃ vahniyogena supakvakaraṇaṃ na vāñchanti te puruṣāḥ pūrvaṃ pakṣacchedaṃ jñātvā hṛṣyanti harṣayuktā bhavanti pakṣacchedaṃ vinānyakāryasiddhiṃ jñātvetyarthas tadanu ca kāryāsiddhau tapyanti paritāpayuktā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those men who desire wing-cutting, that is, the cutting off of the wings of <s>rasa</s>, by the procedure just stated, but do not desire the killing of <s>rasa</s> in the pair, that killing of <s>rasa</s> accomplished by the previously mentioned <s>rasa</s>, gold, and <s>gandhaka</s>, and who also do not desire the cooking, by the application of fire, of <s>bīja</s> substances such as red <s>abhra</s>, gold, and <s>rasaka</s>, rejoice at first after learning wing-cutting, thinking that the other operation can be accomplished on the basis of wing-cutting alone; but afterward, when the operation fails, they are distressed.
Having indicated the <s>cāraṇa</s> of <s>gagana</s> (mica), he praises another processing operation with the words 'in this way,' and so on.

children.text: mayā granthakartrā asmin śāstre karmaṇyati saṃvādī prakāraḥ agrimaprakaraṇe sattvaniṣkāsanarūpaḥ nirdiśyate nirdeśaḥ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: By me, the author of the treatise, in this śāstra and its operation, an especially coherent method, taking the form of the extraction of <s>sattva</s> in the following section, is being indicated.
It is perceived and is refined by those who know refinement; therefore it is compatible.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā itthamuktaprakāreṇa anekairdoṣaiḥ anekakaṣṭaiḥ bahuśramairbahvāyāsairgaganacāraṇaṃ matvā abhrakacāraṇaṃ jñātvā ||
children.translated_text: Having done what? In the manner thus stated, having understood the <s>cāraṇā</s> of <s>gagana</s>, that is, the <s>cāraṇā</s> of mica, as involving many faults, many difficulties, much labor, and much exertion.
The sense is that, after the <s>cāraṇā</s> of <s>gagana</s>, another, superior procedure is being taught.
Showing another procedure, he says, 'ungraspable,' and so on.

children.text: evaṃvidho harajo yāvadyonau abhrake na viśati na milati yāvadbandhaṃ bandhanaṃ kuto bhajate prāpnoti na kuto'pi yonāv apraviśati sati na bandhanamāpnotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So long as such <s>haraja</s> does not enter, that is, unite with, the <s>yoni</s>, namely mica, how can it attain bondage? The meaning is that, if it has not entered any <s>yoni</s>, it does not attain binding.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭo harajaḥ agrāhyaḥ haraḥ kathamapi na gṛhyate 'navayavatvāt harajas tadguṇa eva kāraṇānurūpaṃ kāryamiti nyāyāt
children.translated_text: What kind of <s>haraja</s> is it? It is ungraspable: <s>Hara</s> is not grasped in any way, because he has no limbs; <s>haraja</s> has that same quality, according to the maxim that the effect conforms to the cause.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭo nirlepaḥ vaikārikair doṣaguṇairna lipyata iti doṣaguṇanivṛtteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, what kind is it? It is stainless: it is not smeared by modified faults and qualities, because faults and qualities have ceased.

children.text: punaḥ sūkṣmagatiḥ sūkṣmā gatir gamanaṃ pravartanaṃ vā yasya saḥ dhūmarūpāvalokanatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, it has subtle movement: it is one whose motion, going, or activity is subtle, since it is observed in the form of smoke.
Again, it is pervasive, because it pervades the body, metals, and so on.

children.text: punarakṣayaḥ na kṣayo yasyetyakṣayaḥ sarvadā bhāvarūpatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, it is imperishable: that which has no decay is imperishable, because it always has the nature of being.

children.text: punarjīvaḥ ajīve prakāśatvābhāvaḥ svatvaṃ vihāya malinopādhikatvānnirupādhāv upādhisampattiriti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, it is living: in what is lifeless there is an absence of manifestation. The intended sense is that, after it has abandoned its own nature and become conditioned by a defiled adjunct, there is the acquisition of adjuncts in what is without adjuncts.
For there is the Vedānta statement: beginningless ignorance has that as its support and that as its object.

Thus ends the third illumination, consisting of the <s>cāraṇā</s> of mica-leaf with a mouth, included within the method beginning with mouthless <s>vāsanā</s>, in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s> commentary <s>Mugdhāvabodhinī</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Caturbhuja</s>, son of <s>Maheśa</s> and nectar of the ocean of the <s>Kurala</s> lineage.

children.text: adhunābhrasattvacāraṇaṃ tatra pītakarmaṇi gaganavarṇabhedānāha kṛṣṇa ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Now comes the <s>cāraṇā</s> of mica-essence. There, in the yellow operation, he states the distinctions in the colors of <s>gagana</s> with 'black,' and so on.

children.text: kṛṣṇo ghano rakto ghanaḥ pīto ghanaśceti trividhaḥ pātitasattvaḥ pātitaṃ sattvaṃ yasyeti samāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Black dense, red dense, and yellow dense: thus the one whose essence has been extracted is threefold; the compound means 'that whose essence has been extracted.'
A <s>vajrī</s> of this sort is to be employed in the yellow operation, that is, in work involving gold.

children.text: vajriṇo lakṣaṇaṃ dhmāto'pi haṭhāgnau saṃyojito 'pi yaḥ sthūlatārakārahito bhavati sthūlāśca tāstārakāśca tābhī rahitaḥ dalasamuccayarūpāḥ sthūlatārakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The characteristic of <s>vajrin</s> is this: even when heated, even when placed in a violent fire, it is free from large star-like flakes; the large star-like flakes are accumulations of layers.

children.text: anukto'pi śvetavarṇo ghanaḥ śvetakarmaṇi yojyaḥ granthāntarasāmyād ayam abhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Although not explicitly mentioned, dense white mica is to be used in the white operation, because this agrees with another treatise; this is the intended sense.

children.text: yathā granthāntare raktaṃ pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ śastaṃ hemakriyāsu gaganaṃ hi ||
children.translated_text: As another treatise says: red, yellow, and black <s>gagana</s> are commended in operations involving gold;

children.text: tārakriyāsu śuklaṃ rasāyane sarvameva tu śreṣṭham iti ||
children.translated_text: white is commended in operations involving silver, but in <s>rasāyana</s> all of it is best. Thus.

children.text: abhre 'pi vṛttikṛdviśeṣamāha kadācid girijā devī haraṃ dṛṣṭvā manoharam ||
children.translated_text: With regard to mica too, the commentator states a special tradition: Once the goddess <s>Girijā</s>, seeing <s>Hara</s> charming,
at that time he released seed; from that arose white mica.

children.text: śvetaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tadbhūmisaṃgamāt
children.translated_text: Through contact with that ground it became white, red, yellow, and black,

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajrābhraṃ ca caturvidham ||
children.translated_text: and it is fourfold: <s>pināka</s>, <s>dardura</s>, <s>nāga</s>, and <s>vajrābhra</s>.
When heated in fire, <s>pināka</s> readily throws off a mass of flakes.
<s>Nāga</s> makes a hissing sound, while <s>dardura</s> sounds like a frog.

children.text: caturthaṃ khecaraṃ vajraṃ naivāgnau vikṛtiṃ bhajet
children.translated_text: The fourth, the sky-moving <s>vajra</s>, undergoes no alteration at all in fire.
Therefore <s>vajrābhraka</s> is best, conquering disease, old age, and death. Thus.

children.text: cāraṇāyām abhrapattre vaiṣamyaṃ sattve ca sugamatvaṃ sūcayannāha niścandrikam ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Indicating the unevenness of mica-leaf in <s>cāraṇā</s> and the ease with respect to the essence, he says, 'without moonlight,' and so on.

children.text: ihāsmin cāraṇāsaṃskāre niścandrikaṃ gaganaṃ tārakārahitam abhraṃ vāsanābhiḥ pūrvoktābhir vāsanauṣadhibhiḥ śatadhā śataprakāraṃ vāsitaṃ mathitam api rasendraḥ pāradas tadapi bahuśramaiḥ saṃskṛtamapyabhraṃ na carati grāsīkaroti ||
children.translated_text: In this process of <s>cāraṇā</s>, <s>rasendra</s>, that is, mercury, does not consume as a mouthful <s>gagana</s>, namely mica, that is <s>niścandrika</s>, without star-like glitter, even if it has been scented a hundred ways with the previously mentioned <s>vāsanā</s> medicines and churned, and even if that mica has been refined with much labor.

children.text: atra cāraṇe sattvaṃ yatnataḥ prayatnāt kathaṃ prabhavet kathamapi samarthībhavet sattvaṃ yatnataḥ samarthībhavedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this <s>cāraṇā</s>, how can the essence become effective through effort? The meaning is that the essence can become effective through effort.
Because the essence is easier and has superior qualities, he praises it with 'having left aside,' and so on.

children.text: abhrasattvamekaṃ muktvā tyaktvā anyo 'paro rasapakṣāpakartanasamartho na pāradapakṣacchettā na tena sattvena sukhaṃ yathā syāttathā rasaḥ pārado niyamyate pāradasya niyamanaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ badhyate ca bandhanaṃ prāpyate raso baddho bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Apart from mica-essence alone, there is no other thing capable of cutting the wings of <s>rasa</s>; by that essence, <s>rasa</s>, namely mercury, is restrained with ease, and is also bound, that is, mercury becomes bound.

children.text: kimbhūtaḥ san niyamanaṃ bandhanaṃ ca pnoti niruddhaprasaraḥ san niruddha ārundhittaḥ prasaraḥ prasaraṇaṃ prakṛṣṭena gamanaṃ yasya tādṛśaḥ san ||
children.translated_text: In what condition does it attain restraint and binding? While its spreading has been checked: it is one whose extension, whose expansive movement, has been obstructed and stopped.
Showing the qualification for binding <s>rasa</s>, he says, 'wing-cutting,' and so on.

children.text: yo vādī abhrasattvagrasanena vinā pakṣacchedam kṛtvā pakṣāpakartanam avidhāya rasabandhaṃ kartuṃ pāradabandhanaṃ vidhātum īhate ceṣṭate sa vādī na kiṃtu jaḍa evam apaṇḍita iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The practitioner who, without the swallowing of mica-essence, desires to bind <s>rasa</s>, that is, to effect the binding of mercury, by doing 'wing-cutting' while not performing the cutting off of the wings, is not a true practitioner, but merely dull and unlearned; this is the sense.

children.text: kaḥ kṛtvā rasabandhanaṃ kartumīhate bījaiḥ raktābhrahemarasakair ityādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having done what does he desire to bind <s>rasa</s>? With seeds such as red mica, <s>hemarasaka</s>, and the like.
The indeclinable word 'eva' excludes other substances.

children.text: pakṣacchedanaṃ kṛtvā bandhanaṃ kāryamayaṃ vidhiḥ anyathā tv avidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After cutting the wings, the binding is to be carried out; this is the proper rule. Otherwise, it is an improper procedure.

children.text: avidher dṛṣṭāntamāha yathā ajitendriyo lampaṭaḥ pumān mokṣaṃ vāñchati ||
children.translated_text: He gives an example of improper procedure: just as an uncontrolled, wanton man desires liberation.
Thus there is similarity between one whose senses are uncontrolled and one who is dull.
He states the marks of <s>pārada</s> (mercury) whose wings have been cut, with the words beginning 'not,' and so on.

children.text: evaṃvidhaḥ pāradaḥ sūto yaḥ sa pakṣacchinnaḥ pakṣau chinnau cheditau yasyeti samāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s>, that is, mercury, of this sort is wing-cut: 'one whose two wings have been cut or severed' is the compound analysis.

children.text: sa kaḥ yo nādhaḥ patati adhaḥpātane kṛte ūrdhvato 'dhobhāgo na patati punaradhobhāgata ūrdhvapātane kṛte ūrdhvaṃ na yāti anudgārī acañcalo bhavet yantre svastha eva tiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is it like? When made to fall downward, it does not fall below, that is, its lower part does not drop from above; and when made to rise upward again from below, it does not go upward. It should be non-eruptive and motionless, meaning that it remains steady in the apparatus.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ abhrajīrṇaḥ abhrakaṃ jīrṇaṃ niḥśeṣatām āptaṃ yasmin rasa iti samāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what sort is it? It is one in which <s>abhra</s> has been digested: the compound means 'a <s>rasa</s> in which mica has been digested and brought to complete disappearance.'

children.text: grāsamātreṇa pakṣacchedo na jāyate yāvanna cāritamabhrakaṃ jaratīti dhvanyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The implied meaning is that the cutting of the wings does not occur merely by swallowing a mouthful, so long as the treated mica has not been digested.
That <s>sūta</s> is wing-cut.

children.text: vajrābhraṃ vihāya pinākanāgabhekāḥ satvamocane'samarthā iti darśayannāha śvetetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Showing that, apart from <s>vajrābhra</s>, the kinds called <s>Pināka</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, and <s>Bheka</s> are unable to release essence, he says 'white,' and so on.

children.text: ye dhmātāḥ sthūlatārakārahitāḥ pattracayena varjitā raktapītakṛṣṇāḥ kathitāḥ pūrvaṃ varṇitāste śvetādicaturvarṇā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Those which, when smelted, are without large star-like particles, devoid of layers of leaf, and have previously been described as red, yellow, and black, become four-colored, beginning with white.
