children.text: trayāṇāṃ raktapītakṛṣṇavarṇābhrāṇāṃ cet śvetavarṇa ādau yujyate tadā caturvarṇā bhavantītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that if the white color is added first to the three micas colored red, yellow, and black, then they become four-colored.

children.text: teṣāṃ caturvarṇānāṃ madhye yo vajrī vajrasaṃjñako ghanaḥ sa satvaṃ muñcati dhmātaḥ san satvaṃ tyajati nānye ||
children.translated_text: Among those four-colored varieties, the dense one called <s>vajrī</s> releases <s>sattva</s>: when it is smelted, it gives up its essence; the others do not.

children.text: apare pinākanāgabhekāhvayāḥ dhmātāḥ santaḥ kācatāṃ yānti kācākāratvam āpnuvanti na ca sattvanirgama iti ||
children.translated_text: The others, called <s>Pināka</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, and <s>Bheka</s>, when smelted, become glass; they assume a glass-like form, and no essence issues forth.

children.text: sasattvabalavatvābhyām utkṛṣṭatvād vajrābhraṃ punaḥ praśaṃsati sitetyādi ||
children.translated_text: Because <s>vajrābhra</s> is excellent owing to its possession of essence and strength, he again praises it with the words beginning 'white,' and so on.

children.text: loke saṃsāre ye kecit ghanā udāhṛtāḥ kathitāste alpabalāḥ alpaṃ balaṃ yeṣu te tathoktāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the world, whatever dense micas are mentioned are of little strength, that is, they have little power in them.

children.text: niḥsattvāḥ satvavarjitāḥ dhmāteṣu teṣu satvābhāva ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are without <s>sattva</s>, devoid of essence; the meaning is that there is no essence in them when they are smelted.

children.text: te ke ghanāḥ sitaraktāsitapītāḥ śvetaraktakṛṣṇapītavarṇāḥ nānye varṇāḥ santīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Which dense micas are they? Those of white, red, black, and yellow color; the sense is that there are no other colors.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ caturvarṇānāṃ madhye vajrī vajrasaṃjñakaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ pradhānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among all four colors, <s>vajrī</s>, the one known as <s>vajra</s>, is the best and foremost.
He states the mica that should be given, with the words 'even in <s>sūta</s>,' and so on.

children.text: rasāyanināṃ rasāyanaṃ jarāvyādhividhvaṃsibheṣajaṃ vidyate yeṣāṃ yeṣu vā te rasāyaninaḥ teṣāṃ paraṃ pradhānaṃ satvamabhrasatvaṃ parikīrtitaṃ saṃkathitaṃ yathā granthāntare
children.translated_text: For <s>rasāyanins</s>, those who possess or employ <s>rasāyana</s>, the medicine that destroys old age and disease, the supreme and foremost essence is declared to be the essence of mica, as in another treatise:
A wise man who partakes of <s>sattva</s>, after having performed purification, obtains the arresting of age.
Thus.

children.text: abhrasatvaṃ sūte'pi pārade'pi paramamutkṛṣṭaṃ pakṣacchedanasamarthaṃ baladaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: The essence of mica is supreme even in <s>sūta</s>, that is, even in mercury; it is excellent, capable of cutting the wings, and strength-giving.

children.text: punastrividhaṃ gaganam abhakṣyam abhojyaṃ rasāyanināṃ sūte'pi ||
children.translated_text: Again, the threefold <s>gagana</s>, mica, is not to be eaten, not to be consumed, by <s>rasāyanins</s>, nor even in <s>sūta</s>.

children.text: kiṃ tattrividham ekaṃ kācaṃ vahnau dhamanātkācākāratāṃ nītaṃ dvitīyaṃ kiṭṭaṃ yaddhamanātkiṭṭasvarūpaṃ prāptaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pattrarajaḥ patrāṇāṃ samāhitaṃ yadrajas tadevaṃ trividham abhakṣyaṃ sadoṣatvāt ||
children.translated_text: What is that threefold kind? The first is glass, made to assume a glass-like form by blowing in the fire; the second is slag, that which has reached the form of slag through blowing; the third is leaf-dust, the collected dust of the leaves. This threefold kind is inedible because it is defective.
Showing the procedure for the falling of <s>sattva</s>, he says 'it releases,' and so on.

children.text: ghanas tṛṇasāravikārakaiḥ svinnaḥ tṛṇameva sāro yeṣāṃ te tṛṇasārāḥ teṣāṃ ye vikārakā viśeṣās tair auṣadhaiḥ sūryāvartakādibhiḥ kṛtvā svinnau vahnau dhmāto ghanaḥ satvaṃ muñcati sattvapātaṃ vidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: A dense mica, steamed with modifications of grass-essence, namely with medicines such as <s>sūryāvartaka</s> and the rest, and then smelted in the fire, releases <s>sattva</s>; it brings about the falling of the essence.

children.text: punaḥ kācaṃ kiṭṭaṃ ca parihṛtya sattvaṃ patitakācakiṭṭayuktaṃ yadā bhavati tadā prayatnena grāhyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, after rejecting glass and slag, when the fallen <s>sattva</s> is mixed with glass and slag that have fallen with it, it should then be carefully collected; this is the meaning.
Now he states another special procedure with the words beginning 'it should be steamed.'

children.text: svedyo ghanaḥ pūrvoktaistṛṇasāravikāraiḥ sveditamabhraṃ svedavidhiruktaḥ punarghanasya piṇḍaṃ baddhvā kaiḥ saha māhiṣadadhidugdhamūtraśakṛdājyaiḥ kṛtvā mahiṣyā idaṃ māhiṣaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ yaddadhi dugdhaṃ mūtraṃ śakṛdviṣṭhā ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ caitaiḥ piṇḍaṃ baddhvā ||
children.translated_text: The dense mica is to be steamed. Mica steamed with the previously mentioned modifications of grass-essence has had its steaming procedure stated. Then, having made a lump of the dense mica, with what should it be made? With buffalo curd, milk, urine, dung, and ghee: 'buffalo' means belonging to a buffalo cow, and with such curd, milk, urine, dung, and ghee, a lump should be made.
The word 'and then' has the sense of conjunction.

children.text: pañcagavyaiḥ gavāṃ dugdhadadhimūtraśakṛdājyaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ kāryaḥ piṇḍaṃ baddhvetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be combined with the five cow-products, namely cow's milk, curd, urine, dung, and ghee; the meaning is that the lump should be made with them.

children.text: etatpiṇḍaṃ lohanibhaṃ muṇḍaprabhaṃ sattvaṃ pātayati pūrvasaṃbadhāt ghanasya ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: This lump causes an iron-like, <s>muṇḍa</s>-like shining <s>sattva</s> to fall; from the previous connection, 'of the dense mica' is to be supplied.

children.text: sūryātapapītarasā iti sūryātape savitṛgharme pītāḥ śoṣitā rasā dravā yaiḥ evaṃvidhā dhātavo dhmātāḥ santaḥ svalpaṃ īṣanmātraṃ sattvaṃ muñcanti tyajanti ||
children.translated_text: 'Whose juices have been drunk by the heat of the sun' means metals whose liquids have been drunk, that is, dried, in sunlight, in the heat of the sun. Such metals, when smelted, release only a little, a mere trace, of <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: punasta eva sūryātapapītarasā dhātavaḥ svasthānasthāḥ svakīyaṃ yatsthānaṃ draveṇa sthānapiṇḍaṃ rūpaṃ tasmin tiṣṭhantīti evaṃvidhāḥ santo bahalaṃ bhūyiṣṭhaṃ satvaṃ muñcanti dravantītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, those very metals whose juices have been drunk by the heat of the sun, when they remain in their own place, that is, in their own mass-like form made by the liquid, release abundant, very plentiful <s>sattva</s>; the meaning is that they melt.

In the phrase 'whose juices have been drunk by the heat of the sun,' whose juices are meant? Those of melting medicines such as <s>sūryāvartaka</s>, plantain, <s>vandhyā</s>, <s>karkoṭakī</s>, and the rest.
He states the marks of a fallen <s>sattva</s> with the words 'very deep,' and so on.

children.text: megho ghano bahugambhīraṃ yathā syāttathā dhmātaḥ san suvarṇadhārābhiḥ śobhanavarṇadhārābhiḥ vā suvarṇavat kanakavat varṇo yāsāṃ tābhiḥ nirmalatvāt prakāśakatvācca varṣati dhārāpātaṃ vidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>megha</s>, that is, the <s>ghana</s>, when blown so as to become very deep, pours down streams, whether streams of gold or streams of fine color, or streams whose color is like gold, because of their purity and brightness.

children.text: kathaṃbhūtaṃ devamukhatulyaṃ vahninā tulyaṃ samaṃ amalaṃ nirmalaṃ haritapītaraktādidhūmarahitatvāt patitaṃ satvaṃ tathā vindyāt ghanasyetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind is it? One should know the fallen <s>sattva</s> of <s>ghana</s> to be like a god's face, equal to fire, stainless and pure, because it is free from green, yellow, red, and similar smoke.
Likewise, in another treatise:
By the fierce fire of the bellows, in a blazing fire with great flames,
when it has become exceedingly kindled, the coals, O learned ones, come to exhaustion.
Again, if not otherwise, the wise man should do this two or three times on the top,
when the fire has become blazing, with pure flames and great strength.

children.text: patitaṃ tu tadā vindyāt tatsattvaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then one should know that that <s>sattva</s> has fallen; there is no doubt about this.
But the fallen matter should be separated, free from slag and charcoal.

children.text: nirguṇaṃ lakṣayitvā tu punar dhāmyo yathāvatā
children.translated_text: After recognizing it as lacking good qualities, it should again be blown properly.
When blown twice or thrice in this way, it releases the <s>sattva</s> completely.
Showing the increase of quality in the <s>sattva</s> from its combination with <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, he says 'with <s>mākṣika</s>,' and so on.

children.text: gagane bhavaṃ gaganaṃ aṇpratyayāntaṃ ṇito vā iti sūtreṇa na vṛddhiḥ gaganaṃ abhrasatvam ||
children.translated_text: That which is produced in <s>gagana</s> is <s>gagana</s>; it ends in the suffix <s>aṇ</s>. By the rule '<s>ṇito vā</s>' there is no <s>vṛddhi</s>. Here <s>gagana</s> means <s>abhra-sattva</s>, the essence of mica.

children.text: mākṣike bhavaṃ mākṣikaṃ mākṣikasatvaṃ tena sahitaṃ pūrvasatvaṃ cet dhmātaṃ tadubhayasatvaṃ mukhapradaṃ bhavati rasasya iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the previous <s>sattva</s>, together with <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, the essence of pyrite, is blown, that combined <s>sattva</s> becomes <s>mukha-prada</s>, giver of a mouth, for the <s>rasa</s>; this is to be supplied.
The compound means 'it gives a mouth in an eminent way.'

children.text: tadanu ca tatpaścācca nāgair vaṅgaiḥ sahitaṃ pūrvaṃ yadgaganaṃ abhrasatvaṃ mukhapradamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that, and subsequently, the previous <s>gagana</s>, that is, <s>abhra-sattva</s>, together with <s>nāga</s> and <s>vaṅga</s>, is <s>mukha-prada</s>, giver of a mouth.

children.text: vā sukhapradaṃ iti pāṭhaḥ asmin yoge bahukleśaṃ vihāya sukhena cāraṇaṃ bhavatīti vikalpārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or there is the reading <s>sukha-prada</s>, giver of ease: in this operation, after much trouble is avoided, <s>cāraṇā</s> takes place easily. This is the alternative meaning.
He states <s>mākṣika-sattva</s> as primary with the words 'with <s>mākṣika</s>,' and so on.

children.text: sūtakaḥ pārado ghanasatvaṃ abhrasatvaṃ nikhilaṃ samastaṃ carati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūtaka</s>, mercury, acts upon all <s>ghana-sattva</s>, that is, all <s>abhra-sattva</s>.

children.text: kasmāt mākṣikasatve yogāt mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ tatsatve yo yogastasmāt ||
children.translated_text: Why? Because of its conjunction with <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>; <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite, and the conjunction is with its <s>sattva</s>.
<s>Niyatam</s> means certainly.

children.text: mākṣikasattvayogād ghanasattvaṃ carati raso garbhadrāvī garbhe drāvayati sattvaṃ dravarūpaṃ vidhatte yaḥ sa tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through conjunction with <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, the <s>ghana-sattva</s> is acted upon; the <s>rasa</s> is <s>garbha-drāvin</s>, one that melts the <s>sattva</s> in its womb and makes it liquid.
The meaning is that <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>abhra-sattva</s> remain in molten form inside the belly of the <s>sūta</s>.

children.text: evamamunā vidhānena saha sūtakaḥ pārado rajyate rāgavān bhavati badhyate baddhaśca bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this procedure, along with it, <s>sūtaka</s>, mercury, is colored, that is, becomes possessed of color, and is bound; that is, it becomes fixed.
After the combination with <s>mākṣika</s>, another procedure is described with the words '<s>sattva</s>,' and so on.

children.text: ghanasyābhrasya satvaṃ tathā kāntaṃ lohaviśeṣaṃ tālakayuktaṃ tālakena haritālena yuktaṃ surundhitaṃ dhmātaṃ sat trayamapi satvarūpaṃ bhavati yadaikavāradhamanena satvaṃ na milati tathā punardvistrivelābhir dhamanaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> of <s>ghana</s>, namely mica, and likewise <s>kānta</s>, a particular kind of iron, joined with <s>tālaka</s>, that is, orpiment, and well enclosed and blown, all three become <s>sattva</s>-like. If the <s>sattva</s> is not obtained by a single blowing, then blowing should again be done two or three times.

children.text: samabhāgatālakayojanaṃ ghanasatvamākṣikasatvayogadrāvaṇāddhamitādatyarthaṃ tatsatvaṃ rakhe pārade bandhakāri bhavati paramamutkṛṣṭaṃ bandhanapradaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The addition of an equal part of <s>tālaka</s>, when the <s>ghana-sattva</s> has been greatly melted and blown through union with <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, makes that <s>sattva</s> a binder in <s>rasa</s>, mercury; it becomes an excellent giver of fixation.
The sense is that, through the <s>cāraṇā</s> of that <s>sattva</s>, the <s>rasa</s> obtains fixation.
The mark of <s>kānta</s> is as follows:

children.text: pātre yasmin praviśati jale tailabindurna sarpet hiṅgurgandhaṃ visṛjati nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbakalkaḥ
children.translated_text: In a vessel in which, when it is placed in water, a drop of oil does not spread, and in which asafoetida gives off its own smell and neem paste its bitterness,

children.text: pāke dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākāratāṃ naiva bhūmau kāntaṃ lohaṃ viduriti ca tallakṣaṇoktaṃ na cānyat
children.translated_text: and in which, during cooking, milk assumes a peak-like form and not on the ground: that, and no other, is known as <s>kānta</s> iron, according to the stated marks.
Thus.
He states the preparation of the alloy of <s>kānta</s> and <s>abhra-sattva</s> with the words 'iron,' and so on.
The word <s>ca</s>, 'and,' has the sense of conjunction.

children.text: lohaṃ pūrvoktalakṣaṇaṃ muṇḍādikaṃ abhrasatvaṃ ca tālakasamabhāgasāritaṃ tālakasya samabhāgena pūrvavidhānena mukhādinā yatsāritaṃ ekaśarīratāṃ nītaṃ sṛ gatāvityasya dhāto rūpaṃ sāritaṃ pramilitam ityarthaḥ evaṃvidhaṃ kāntābhrasatvālaṃ rasaścarati ||
children.translated_text: Iron, marked as previously described, such as <s>muṇḍa</s> and the rest, and <s>abhra-sattva</s>, processed with an equal part of <s>tālaka</s>; that is, brought into one body by the previous method beginning with <s>mukha</s>. The word <s>sārita</s> is a form from the root <s>sṛ</s>, 'to go'; it means mixed together. <s>Rasa</s> acts upon such a <s>kānta-abhra-sattva</s> alloy.

children.text: ca punaḥ aṅgulimṛditaṃ aṅgulinā marditaṃ tat kāntābhrasatvālaṃ garbhe rasodare dravati tatsvarūpatvena milati ||
children.translated_text: And again, that <s>kānta-abhra-sattva</s> alloy, rubbed with a finger, melts in the womb, in the belly of the <s>rasa</s>, and unites with it as its own form.
Why? Because of connection with <s>abhiṣava</s>; <s>abhiṣava</s> means close rubbing or trituration, and this occurs through connection with that.

children.text: lohasya trayo daśabhedānāṃ madhyāt kenāpi bhedena sahayogaḥ kārya iti lohaśabdena dhvanitam ||
children.translated_text: By the word <s>loha</s>, it is suggested that a combination should be made with any one of the thirteen kinds of iron.
Having stated the combination with iron, he states the combination with <s>vaṅga</s> with the words '<s>vaṅga</s>,' and so on.

children.text: atha lohakathanānantaraṃ vaṅgaṃ khurasaṃjñakaṃ abhrakaṃ ca etaddvayaṃ tālakaṣaḍbhāgasāritaṃ tālakasya ṣaḍaṃśena ekaśarīratāṃ nītaṃ tatsvarūpaṃ rasaścarati ||
children.translated_text: Now, after the statement about iron, <s>vaṅga</s>, known as <s>khura</s>, and <s>abhraka</s>: these two, processed with a sixth part of <s>tālaka</s> and brought into one body, are acted upon by <s>rasa</s> in that form.

children.text: kasmāt abhiṣavayogāt abhiṣavaḥ saṃmardanaṃ tadyogāt ṣuñ abhiṣave ityasya dhāto rūpaṃ abhiṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why? Because of connection with <s>abhiṣava</s>; <s>abhiṣava</s> is close rubbing or trituration. The word <s>abhiṣava</s> is a form from the root <s>ṣuñ</s> in the sense of pressing or extracting.
Again, the <s>rasa</s> acts upon it and unites with it.

children.text: cāritaṃ yat taddravati taddrutaṃ rase vrajati pṛthaktvāt saṃ milati nātrasandehaḥ niḥ saṃdigdhamiva ||
children.translated_text: What has been subjected to <s>cāraṇā</s> melts; when melted, it enters the <s>rasa</s>. Since it had been separate, it then fully unites with it. There is no doubt here; it is quite certain.

children.text: vaṅgasya laghudravitvāt ṣaḍaṃśayogastālakasya yuktaḥ lohajāteḥ kāṭhiṇyāt samabhāgatvaṃ uditam ||
children.translated_text: Because <s>vaṅga</s> is easily liquefied, the addition of one sixth part of <s>tālaka</s> is proper; because the class of iron is hard, equal parts have been stated.
He states the procedure for <s>abhra-sattva</s> with the words 'abundant,' and so on.

children.text: vaṭakīkṛtaṃ ca tanmṛtaṃ ca gaganaṃ tathoktaṃ na vaṭako vaṭakaḥ kriyata iti vaṭakīkṛtaṃ atra abhūtatadbhāve cviḥpratyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The expression means the <s>gagana</s>, namely mica, which has been made into pellets and calcined. It is called 'made into a pellet' because a pellet is made, not because there is no pellet; here the suffix <s>cvi</s> is used in the sense of becoming what it was not before.

children.text: pañcabhirniculapuṭaiḥ pañcasaṃkhyābhirvetasavṛkṣadravabhāvanābhir bhāvitaṃ yanmṛtagaganaṃ mṛtābhraṃ vaṭakīkṛtaṃ satsatvaṃ patati taddrāvakauṣadhayogaṃ vidhāya vahninā vidhamanāditi śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The calcined <s>gagana</s>, that is, calcined mica, which has been made into pellets and treated by five <s>nicula-puṭas</s>, meaning five applications with the liquid of the cane-like <s>vetasa</s> tree, releases <s>sattva</s>. The remaining sense is: after preparing the combination of melting medicines, it is blown by fire.

children.text: kiyanmānaṃ satvaṃ patati bahalaṃ bahu anyavidheradhikam ||
children.translated_text: How much <s>sattva</s> falls? Abundant, much, more than by the other procedure.

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ svarṇavarṇaṃ pītaśvetaṃ prakāśākhyaṃ punarnirañjanaṃ nirmalaṃ kiṭṭarahitaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: What is it like? It is gold-colored, yellow-white, called bright, and moreover spotless, pure, and free from slag.
In this <s>sattva</s> there is no glassy slag.
This is the most excellent procedure, superior to the previously stated abundant falling of <s>sattva</s>; that is the meaning.
He states the procedure for making only <s>sattva</s> undergo <s>cāraṇā</s> with the words 'that,' and so on.

children.text: tatastadabhrasatvapātanavidheranantaraṃ tadevābhrasatvaṃ cūrṇīkṛtya kalkaṃ vidhāya kṣārāmlairbhāvitaṃ kuryāt kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ amlā jambīrādayaḥ tairbahuśo bahuvāraṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that, immediately after the procedure for causing that <s>abhra-sattva</s> to fall, that very <s>abhra-sattva</s> should be powdered, made into a paste, and treated with alkalis and acids. The alkalis are <s>svarjikā</s> and the like; the acids are citron and the like. The meaning is that it should be heated many times, repeatedly, by the heat-puṭa with those substances.

children.text: punaḥ sṛṣṭitrayanīrakaṇātumbururasamarditaṃ sṛṣṭiḥ pūrvoktā tattrayaṃ mūtraśukraśoṇitamiti nīrakaṇā jalapippalī tumbaru pratītaṃ eteṣāṃ rasena marditaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Again it should be rubbed with the juices of the three generative fluids, <s>nīrakaṇā</s>, and <s>tumburu</s>. The generative fluids are those previously mentioned, namely urine, semen, and blood. <s>Nīrakaṇā</s> is water-pepper; <s>tumburu</s> is well known. It should be rubbed with the juice of these.

children.text: abhrasattvamevaṃ kṛtaṃ sat carati grasati rasaḥ ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>abhra-sattva</s> has been prepared in this way, it moves in, that is, it is consumed; 'by <s>rasa</s>' is to be supplied.
Now he discusses copper-mica with the words 'dense,' and so on.

children.text: ghanasatvaśulbamākṣikasamabhāganiyojitaṃ ghanasatvam abhrasatvaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ samabhāgena tulyabhāgena niyojitaṃ prayuktaṃ tanmilitaṃ sat śulbābhraṃ kathitam ||
children.translated_text: Dense <s>sattva</s>, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s> are applied in equal parts: dense <s>sattva</s> is <s>abhra-sattva</s>, copper is <s>tāmra</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite. When they are applied in equal measure, in equal parts, and have become combined, that is called copper-mica.
Here he states what kind of copper should be used.
There are two coppers, <s>mleccha</s> and <s>Nepāla</s>; in <s>rasa</s> work, <s>Nepāla</s> is the best.
It withstands blows from the hammer, is smooth, has red plates, is stainless, and is soft.
But the <s>mleccha</s> type, when washed, is black, rough yet oily, and unable to withstand hammering.
Mixed with lead and iron, it is not the best in operations with <s>rasa</s>.
Thus; therefore the Nepalese one should be taken, that is the meaning.

children.text: tacchulvābhraṃ rasaḥ kṣipraṃ carati punaḥ kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ tacchulbaṃ jīryati jāraṇamāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> quickly acts upon that copper-mica; moreover that copper is quickly, that is, rapidly, digested and reaches <s>jāraṇa</s>.
Here the combination with <s>mākṣika</s> is for the purpose of joining copper and <s>abhra-sattva</s>, and because it is pleasing to <s>rasa</s>; such is the idea.
He states the procedure for the <s>cāraṇā</s> of copper-mica with the words 'thus,' and so on.

children.text: iti pūrvoktaṃ tāpyaśulbasahitaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ nepālasaṃjñakaṃ tābhyāṃ sahitaṃ miśritaṃ ghanasatvaṃ taptalohakhalvake mṛditaṃ kāryaṃ mardanīyaṃ kaiḥ kṛtvā kāñjikavetasajambīrabījapūrāmlaiḥ kāñjikamuktavidhānaṃ sauvīraṃ vetasaṃ cukraṃ jambīraṃ prasiddhaṃ bījapūro mātuluṅgaḥ eteṣāmamlaiḥ dravarūpaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The previously described dense <s>sattva</s>, along with <s>tāpya</s> and copper, should be ground in a heated iron mortar. <s>Tāpya</s> is gold-pyrite, and the copper is the kind called Nepalese; mixed with those two, the dense <s>sattva</s> is to be worked and ground. With what? With the acids of rice-gruel, <s>vetasa</s>, citron, and <s>bījapūra</s>: rice-gruel is the previously described <s>sauvīra</s>, <s>vetasa</s> is <s>cukra</s>, citron is well known, and <s>bījapūra</s> is citron-fruit. The liquid acidic forms of these are meant.
Then <s>rasendra</s>, mercury, acts upon and consumes the copper-mica.

children.text: lohakhalvasya kathanāt taptakhalvake mardanaṃ kuryāditi tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because an iron mortar is mentioned, the intended meaning is that grinding should be done in a heated mortar.
He states another method with the words 'thus,' and so on.

children.text: iti pūrvoktalakṣaṇaṃ tīkṣṇaśulbanāgaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tāmraṃ nāgaṃ ca etattrayaṃ mākṣikayuktaṃ svarṇamākṣikayutaṃ samaṃ tulyabhāgaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: The three substances with the previously stated characteristics, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, copper, and lead, should be made equal, in equal parts, together with <s>mākṣika</s>, that is, with gold-pyrite.

children.text: tatkṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ taiḥ sarvaiḥ piṣṭīstambhena khoṭabhasma kāryam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>khoṭa</s> made from them should be turned into <s>khoṭa</s>-ash by the fixation of the paste with all those substances.

children.text: puṭavidhinā vahnipuṭavidhānena tatkṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ bhasma kāryaṃ punaḥ tadbhasma satve nirvyūḍhaṃ nirvāhitaṃ sat satvarañjakaṃ bhavati khasatve abhrasatve rāgadāyi bhavati rañjitaṃ tatsatvaṃ rasarañjakaṃ bhavediti ||
children.translated_text: By the <s>puṭa</s> procedure, that is, by the procedure of fire-heating, the <s>khoṭa</s> made from them should be reduced to ash. Then, when that ash has been led into the <s>sattva</s> and carried through, it becomes a colorant of <s>sattva</s>; it gives color to <s>kha-sattva</s>, namely <s>abhra-sattva</s>. That colored <s>sattva</s> becomes a colorant of <s>rasa</s>.
He states the <s>cāraṇā</s> of colored dense <s>sattva</s> with the words 'it should be made to act,' and so on.

children.text: tadvidhaṃ pūrvarañjitaṃ ghanasatvam abhrasatvaṃ ca ghanaṃ kevalaghanodbhavaṃ satvaṃ arañjitaṃ rase pārade cāryaṃ grāsagrasanamānenaitad abhrasatvaṃ rase saṃyojyam ||
children.translated_text: That kind of previously colored dense <s>sattva</s>, namely <s>abhra-sattva</s>, and also dense <s>sattva</s> produced from dense mica alone, though uncolored, should be made to act in <s>rasa</s>, mercury. This <s>abhra-sattva</s> should be combined with <s>rasa</s> in the measure of the swallowed morsel.

children.text: vā satve sarvabījaṃ sarvaṃ rāgadāyi dravyaṃ saṃyojya nirvāhyaṃ nirvāhitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Or, all seed, that is, every color-giving substance, should be combined with the <s>sattva</s> and carried through.

children.text: kutaḥ dvandvasaṃkarataḥ dvandvānāṃ saṃkaro melāpaḥ saṅkaro'vakara ityamaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why? Because of the mixing of pairs. The mixing of pairs is their union; <s>saṅkara</s> means mixture, according to <s>Amara</s>.

children.text: nirvāhyaṃ iti vaha prāpaṇe ityasya rūpaṃ pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nirvāhya</s>, 'to be carried through,' is the form of the root <s>vah</s>, 'to carry or cause to reach,' as before.
<s>Niravyayam</s> has the sense of certainty; <s>nir</s> is used for certainty and negation, according to <s>Amara</s>.
Now, concerning the <s>cāraṇā</s> of <s>rasa</s>, he states what should be known with the words '<s>abhraka</s>,' and so on.

children.text: yo vādī rasakartā ādau prathamaṃ abhracāraṇaṃ na jānāti yathā raso'bhrakaṃ carati grasati punaḥ tatpaścāt garbhadruticāraṇaṃ yadrasagarbhe drutaṃ dravarūpaṃ tiṣṭhatyabhrādikaṃ tasya cāraṇaṃ grasanaṃ punarante hemnaḥ svarṇasya cāraṇaṃ grasanaṃ na jānāti sa vṛthaiva mithyaiva arthakṣayaṃ dhananāśaṃ kurute kāryasiddherabhāvāt ||
children.translated_text: A practitioner of <s>rasa</s> who, at the outset, does not know <s>abhra-cāraṇa</s>, the feeding of mica, namely how <s>rasa</s> takes in and consumes mica, and after that does not know <s>garbha-druti-cāraṇa</s>, the feeding and consuming of mica and the like when it remains melted and liquid in the womb of the <s>rasa</s>, and finally does not know the feeding and consuming of <s>hema</s>, gold, merely wastes his property, indeed destroys his wealth, because the desired operation is not accomplished.
The sense is that only one who knows everything should undertake an operation with <s>rasa</s>.
He states the secret of the morsel with the words beginning '<s>gagana</s>'.

children.text: ahaṃ śrīmadgovindabhagavatpūjyapādācāryaḥ ekamadvitīyaṃ gaganagrāsarahasyaṃ abhrakakavalane grāsakautukaṃ vakṣyāmi kathayāmi ||
children.translated_text: I, the revered teacher <s>Govindabhagavatpūjyapāda</s>, shall explain the one, non-dual secret of the morsel of <s>gagana</s>, the wonder involved in swallowing mica.

children.text: kasmāt ghanārkasaṃyogāt ghanaṃ abhrakasatvaṃ arkastāmraṃ etayoḥ saṃyogaḥ tasmāt ubhayasatvakṛtakhoṭaṃ cāryam ||
children.translated_text: Because of the conjunction of <s>ghana</s> and <s>arka</s>, that is, of mica essence and copper, a <s>khoṭa</s> made from the essences of both should be fed.
The word '<s>atha</s>' indicates an alternative position.

children.text: abhrasatvasya yasya dhāto rūpaṃ tena saha yasya dhātorvā saṃyogo bhavati dvandvabhāvāt saṅkarataḥ tatsaṃyuktamabhidhānaṃ bhavati yathā śulvābhraṃ nāgābhraṃ vaṅgābhraṃ mākṣikābhraṃ hemābhram iti evaṃ sarvatra saṃyogānnāmaniṣpattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the form of some metal is joined with the <s>sattva</s> of mica, or when there is conjunction with some other metal, because of duality and mixture the name is formed as a compound with that joined element, as in '<s>śulvābhra</s>', '<s>nāgābhra</s>', '<s>vaṅgābhra</s>', '<s>mākṣikābhra</s>', and '<s>hemābhra</s>'. Thus everywhere the name arises from conjunction.

children.text: grastasya drāvaṇaṃ garbhe garbhadrutirudāhṛtā bahireva dravīkṛtya ghanasatvādikaṃ khalu
children.translated_text: The melting, in the womb, of what has been swallowed is called <s>garbha-druti</s>. But after melting <s>ghana-sattva</s> and the like outside,
that melting for the purpose of digesting <s>rasendra</s> is called <s>bāhya-druti</s>, external liquefaction.
Heated by the rays of speech, satisfy the water-lily of <s>Janaka</s>,
and long illumine the water-lilies rising from ponds with radiance.
Now he states the praise of <s>garbha-druti</s> and <s>bāhya-druti</s> with the words beginning '<s>yadi</s>'.

children.text: yadi ced ghanasatvam abhrasatvaṃ garbhe pāradasyāntarna patati dravatvaṃ nāpnoti vā bījāni śulbābhrādīni pāradasyodare no dravanti na rasarūpā bhavanti ca punaḥ bāhyadrutir na yujyate cedevaṃ na syāttarhi iha asyāṃ kriyāyāṃ prāptāyāṃ satyāṃ sūto rasaḥ kathaṃ badhyate anyathā na ko'pyupāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>ghana-sattva</s>, the essence of mica, does not fall inside, in the womb of mercury, or does not attain liquidity, or if the seeds such as <s>śulvābhra</s> and the rest do not melt in the belly of mercury and become of the nature of <s>rasa</s>, and again if <s>bāhya-druti</s> is not applicable, then, when this operation has been reached, how can <s>sūta</s>, mercury, be bound? Otherwise there is no means at all.
Showing the superiority of <s>garbha-druti</s>, he says with the words beginning '<s>garbha</s>'.

children.text: cīrṇo 'pi grāsaḥ cāraṇatāṃ prāpto 'pi kavalaḥ yadi garbhadrutyā rahito bhavet rasasyodare rasarūpakaraṇavarjito bhavet tadā ekatāṃ na yāti rasarūpo na bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Even a consumed morsel, even a lump that has undergone <s>cāraṇā</s>, if it is without <s>garbha-druti</s>, that is, if it has not been transformed into the nature of <s>rasa</s> in the belly of the <s>rasa</s>, then it does not reach unity and does not become <s>rasa</s> in form.

children.text: punarekībhāvena vinā grāso na jīryate jāraṇatvaṃ nāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Again, without becoming one, the morsel is not digested; it does not attain the state of <s>jāraṇa</s>.

children.text: tena hetunā garbhadrutipūrvikā jāraṇā kāryā rasabandhe jāraṇaṃ heturiti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason, digestion should be performed after <s>garbha-druti</s>; the sense is that <s>jāraṇa</s>, digestion, is the cause in the binding of <s>rasa</s>.
He states what must first be done in digestion with the words beginning '<s>bījānām</s>'.

children.text: bījānāṃ śulbābhrādīnāṃ ko'pyanirvacanīyaḥ saṃskāro garbhe drutikārakaḥ prathamaṃ kartavyaḥ saṃskriyata iti saṃskāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the seeds, such as <s>śulvābhra</s> and the rest, some indescribable preparation that produces melting in the womb must first be done; it is called <s>saṃskāra</s> because the material is prepared.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ tādṛśaḥ taiḥ bījaiḥ sadṛśaḥ yathā bījāni śaktimanti santi tathā saṃskāro 'pi śaktimān kartavya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind is it? Such a one, similar to those seeds: just as the seeds possess potency, so too the preparation must be made potent. This is the meaning.
By what should the preparation be done? By the sour group, beginning with citron and the like.

children.text: yena saṃskāreṇa rasarājasya garbhe rasodare bījāni dhātūpadhātujātāni śulbābhrādīni dravantītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that preparation the seeds, born from metals and secondary metals, such as <s>śulvābhra</s> and the rest, melt in the womb of <s>rasarāja</s>, in the belly of <s>rasa</s>. This is the meaning.
He states the praise of the gold-seed with the words beginning '<s>sama</s>'.

children.text: samamākṣikakṛtavāpaṃ samabhāgaṃ tulyāṃśaṃ hemnā yanmākṣikaṃ tasya kṛtvā vāpo vāraṃ vāram ākṣepo 'gniyogād yasmin tathoktaṃ punastaddhema samamākṣikasatvasaṃyutaṃ hemnā samaṃ tulyaṃ yanmākṣikasatvaṃ tena saṃyutaṃ kṛtakhoṭaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having made a repeated casting of <s>mākṣika</s> equal in portion to the gold, that is, with equal shares, again and again through the use of fire, one should then make that gold, joined with <s>mākṣika-sattva</s> equal to the gold, into a <s>khoṭa</s>.
That gold in the form of a <s>khoṭa</s> melts in the womb, inside the mercury.
Again, that melted gold is digested and reaches the condition of having been digested.

children.text: taddhema jaritaṃ sat sūtaṃ raseśvaraṃ badhnāti ||
children.translated_text: When that gold has been digested, it binds <s>sūta</s>, the lord of <s>rasa</s>.
In any other manner <s>sūta</s> does not obtain binding.

children.text: mākṣikasya vāpo hemno varṇotkarṣaprada iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sense is that the casting of <s>mākṣika</s> gives excellence of color to the gold.
He states the excellence of quality in <s>rasa</s> from the feeding of <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, with the words beginning '<s>mākṣika-sattva</s>'.

children.text: mākṣikasatvaṃ vahnyauṣadhayogadrutaṃ yaddhemamākṣikasāraṃ hemnā kanakena saha sūte pārade pūrvaṃ yadgutaṃ punaḥ pādādikajāritaṃ pādādikavibhāgena pādārdhasatvena niḥśeṣatāmāptaṃ sat ayaṃ sūtaḥ tārāriṣṭaṃ tāraṃ rūpyādi ariṣṭaṃ śubhaṃ varakanakaṃ kurute pūrṇavarṇamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, namely the essence of gold-pyrite melted through the combination of fire and medicines, which has first been swallowed in <s>sūta</s>, mercury, together with <s>hema</s>, gold, and then digested in quarter portions and the like until nothing remains: this <s>sūta</s> turns silver and other auspicious metals into excellent gold of full color.

children.text: kena vidhānena pattralepanena patraṃ kaṇṭakabhedi tatra yo'sau lepaḥ vahniyogāditi śeṣaḥ tena ||
children.translated_text: By what procedure? By smearing a leaf: that is, by the application, through the use of fire, of a paste on a leaf thin enough to be pierced by a thorn.
The meaning is clear: when gold has been digested with <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, gold is produced by smearing a silver leaf.
He states the definition of <s>garbha-druti</s> with the words beginning '<s>sama</s>'.

children.text: yadi grāsaḥ samarasatāṃ yāto bhavedrasatulyarūpatāṃ prāpto bhavet punarvastrādgalito bhavet caturguṇaśvetavastrānniḥsṛto bhavet punastulanāyāṃ tulākarmaṇi yadādhiko'pi syāttadā garbhe pāradasyāntar druto grāso jñātavyaḥ garbhadruto raso veditavya iti vyaktārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the <s>grāsa</s> has reached sameness, that is, has attained a form equal to <s>rasa</s>; again, if it has fallen from the cloth, that is, has passed out through fourfold white cloth; and if, when weighed on the balance, it is even heavier, then the <s>grāsa</s>, melted inside the womb of mercury, is to be known. The <s>rasa</s> is to be understood as womb-melted. This is the clear meaning.

children.text: punarasau raso drutvā dravarūpaṃ śīghraṃ prāpto jīryati dhātūnapi vidhāneneti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, that <s>rasa</s>, after melting and quickly attaining liquid form, digests even metals by the proper procedure; this is to be supplied.
He states the excellence of <s>mākṣika-sattva</s> with the words 'not,' and so on.

children.text: mākṣikasatvena vinā svarṇamākṣikasāram antareṇa hema kanakaṃ vā tāraṃ rūpyaṃ na dravati ||
children.translated_text: Without <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, that is, apart from the essence of gold-pyrite, gold, or silver, does not melt.

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā viḍaiḥ kṛtvā śaṅkhacūrṇārkakṣārādikṛtapiṇḍaiḥ kṛtvā granthāntare ca
children.translated_text: By means of what? By means of <s>viḍa</s>s, lumps made with conch-powder, <s>arka</s>-alkali, and the like. And in another treatise:
With salts, alkalis, subsidiary minerals, and these acidic substances, it is considered a <s>viḍa</s>.

children.text: same garbhe tu saṃsthāpyo hyanenaiva dravībhavet
children.translated_text: It should be placed in the same womb; by this alone it will become melted.
Thus.

children.text: na kevalaṃ biḍaiḥ kiṃtu kṣārairapi na kṣāraiḥ svarjikāyavakṣāraṭaṅkaṇādyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It does not melt only by <s>viḍa</s>s; nor even by alkalis such as <s>svarjikā</s>, <s>yavakṣāra</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and the rest.

children.text: na kevalaṃ kṣāraiḥ kiṃtu snehairapi na snehāni yathā
children.translated_text: It does not melt only by alkalis; nor even by oils. The oils are as follows:
Oil arising from <s>kaṅguṇika</s>, free from defect, from <s>karañja</s>, and from <s>śrīphala</s>,
from <s>kaṭu</s>, <s>vātāri</s>, <s>siddhārtha</s>, <s>somarājī</s>, and <s>vibhītaka</s>,
from flaxseed, <s>mahākāla</s>, neem, and sesame likewise,
and the group consisting of <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>dantī</s>, and <s>tumbara</s>,
and oil produced from the fruits of <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>unmatta</s>, and <s>bhallāta</s>.
Thus.
It does not melt even with oils.
But through <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, melting in the womb arises.
With what special kind of <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>? With red, that is, with the red group.
Kept for three days, that is, for a period of three days, placed within the red group.
The red group is as follows:

children.text: dāḍimaṃ kiṃśukaṃ caiva bandhūkaṃ ca kusumbhakam
children.translated_text: Pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, <s>bandhūka</s>, and <s>kusumbhaka</s>,
together with equal <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, beginning with turmeric, and combined with lac juice,
joined with red sandalwood: this is proclaimed as the red group.
Thus.
He states the procedure for the apparatus for digesting gold with the words 'salt,' and so on.

children.text: prathamaṃ lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ devīsvarasaplutaṃ kuryāt brāhmīsvakīyarasena saṃmiśraṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: First one should make the salt, <s>saindhava</s>, moistened with <s>devī</s>-juice; that is, one should mix it with <s>brāhmī</s>'s own juice.

children.text: punar brāhmīrasaplutaṃ lavaṇaṃ ca ahipatraṃ tāmbūlidalaṃ tacca dvayaṃ śilayā vitatagrāveṇa cūrṇitaṃ peṣitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then the salt moistened with <s>brāhmī</s>-juice and the <s>ahipatra</s>, the betel leaf, those two, should be crushed with a stone, that is, ground with a broad stone slab.
Then this should be placed in an iron vessel, a vessel made of iron.

children.text: etat sthāpitaṃ dravyaṃ puṭatritayāt tripuṭakaraṇādagnisaṃyogena sumṛtaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: This deposited substance, after three <s>puṭa</s>s, by the action of fire through three firings, becomes well calcined.

children.text: tasya devīsvarasaplutasya sumṛtasaindhavasya mukhādhārā sphuṭavikaṭakaṭorikā pātrī kāryā mukhameva ādhāro yasyāḥ sā evaṃvidhā sphuṭā prakaṭā vikaṭā viparītā adhomukhetyarthaḥ sā kaṭorikā vihitā kāryā ayaḥpātrasya ||
children.translated_text: From that well-calcined <s>saindhava</s>, moistened with <s>devī</s>-juice, a bowl should be made as a mouth-support for the iron vessel: a manifest, broad, inverted bowl. 'Whose mouth is its support' means that it is clear, broad, reversed, in other words downward-facing; such a bowl should be prepared.

children.text: tasyāḥ kaṭorikāyā upari ūrdhvabhāge eṣā kaṭorikā ādeyā sthāpyā ||
children.translated_text: On top of that bowl, in its upper part, this bowl is to be set in place.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā aṅgulotsedhā aṅgula utsedhaḥ parimāṇaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā ||
children.translated_text: What kind is it? One finger high, that is, one whose measure of elevation is a finger.
Again, what kind? Depressed by half a finger, that is, with its middle sunk to the measure of half a finger.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭā vihitachidratritayā vihitāni kṛtāni chidratritayāni yasyāṃ sā evaṃvidhā śastā ca saṃtulavihitachidratritayā ||
children.translated_text: Again, what kind? Furnished with three made holes, that is, with three holes made in it; and it is recommended when the three holes are made evenly.
Four fingers high: the bowl in the upper part above that is intended to be raised to the measure of four fingers.

children.text: punaśchidreṣu triṣu śalākā yojyā lohaśalākāḥ kṣepyāḥ punastatrāpi chidreṣu hemapatrāṇi kaṇṭakavedhīni kanakapatrāṇi yojyānīti ||
children.translated_text: Then rods should be fitted into the three holes, that is, iron rods should be inserted; and there too, on the holes, gold leaves, pierced by spikes, should be placed.

children.text: evaṃvidhe pūrvaṃ nirmite yantre hemapatrāṇi sthāpya vidhūpyante ||
children.translated_text: In such an apparatus, previously constructed in this way, the gold leaves are placed and fumigated.

children.text: tato'gniṃ pradīpayet yantrādhastād yantrādhobhāge vahniṃ prajvālayet tadā tāni hemapatrāṇi kṛṣṇāni śyāmavarṇāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Then one should kindle the fire; one should light the fire below the apparatus, beneath the apparatus. Then those gold leaves become black, dark-colored.

children.text: kasmāt dhūmopalepamātrāt dhūmaścāsāvupalepaśca dhūmopalepas tanmātrāt tatpramāṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Why? Merely from a coating of smoke: the smoke itself is a coating, and the mere measure of that smoke-coating is meant.
With the same medicine with which the fumigation has been explained, a coating should be applied to the leaves.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃbhūtāni hemapatrāṇi rasendro jarati agnitāpitāni santi vahniyogāttaptāni kṛtāni ||
children.translated_text: Again, what kind are the gold leaves that <s>rasendra</s> digests? They have been heated by fire, made hot through contact with fire.
This digestion of gold has been stated.
Thus, by five verses, there is a <s>kulaka</s>.
Now he states the digestion of silver with the words 'by that,' and so on.

children.text: tenaiva vidhinā pūrvapidhānena tārapatraṃ rūpyadalaṃ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ śyāmalaprabhaṃ jāyate ||
children.translated_text: By that same procedure, by the previously stated method, the silver leaf, the sheet of silver, becomes black in color, dark in luster.

children.text: kena saṃsvedya yantrayogena saṃsvedaḥ prabalāgnis tasyedaṃ sambandhi yadyantraṃ yasya yo yogastena ||
children.translated_text: By what? By being heated through an apparatus-procedure: the heating is a strong fire, and the apparatus connected with it is that to which the procedure belongs.

children.text: tattārapatraṃ punaḥ garbhe rasodare dravati jalatvamāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: That silver leaf again melts in the womb, in the belly of the <s>rasa</s>, and reaches liquidity.

children.text: punastasmin yantre dravati caśabdāt rasendrastatpatraṃ jarati tārakṛṣṇīti ||
children.translated_text: Again, when it melts in that apparatus, and, by the word 'and,' <s>rasendra</s> digests that leaf; this is the blackening of silver.
Now he states another procedure with the words 'or else,' and so on.
The word 'or else' has the sense of addition, because it is fixed on the same meaning.

children.text: balinā gandhena saha vaṅgaṃ yantrayogena kṛṣṇaṃ jāyeta ||
children.translated_text: Together with powerful <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) would become black through the apparatus-procedure.

children.text: kevalaṃ vaṅgaṃ punarnāgābhidhānena saha nāgavidhānamapyevaṃ syāditi vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tin alone, again, together with what is called <s>nāga</s> (lead): the procedure for <s>nāga</s> would also be the same. This is clear.

children.text: nāgābhidhāneneti nāganāmnā ākhyāhve abhidhānaṃ ca nāmadheyaṃ ca nāma ca ityamaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'By the designation <s>nāga</s>' means 'by the name <s>nāga</s>': <s>ākhyā</s>, <s>āhva</s>, <s>abhidhāna</s>, <s>nāmadheya</s>, and <s>nāman</s> all mean 'name,' according to <s>Amara</s>.

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ vaṅgaṃ vā nāgaṃ vā hemāhvaṃ hemapatraṃ vā tāraṃ tārapatraṃ vā etatsarvaṃ balinā kṛṣṇaṃ jāyeta mṛtaṃ ca sarvaṃ garbhe rasāntare dravati nātra saṃdehaḥ asaṃdigdhamidamuktam ||
children.translated_text: Thus this whole substance, whether <s>vaṅga</s>, <s>nāga</s>, what is called <s>hema</s>, <s>hemapatra</s>, <s>tāra</s>, or <s>tārapatra</s>, becomes black through <s>balin</s> and is killed; and all of it melts in the womb, in another <s>rasa</s>. There is no doubt here; this has been stated without uncertainty.
By the word <s>ca</s>, 'and,' it is also said to be consumed; it reaches complete exhaustion.
He states another procedure with the words '<s>rasakam</s>,' and so on.

children.text: rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ balinā gandhena saha yuktaṃ sat militaṃ sat samabhāgena iti śeṣaḥ kena kṛtvā pūrvoktavidhānayogena pūrvoktaṃ yadvidhānaṃ yantrādikaṃ tasya yo'sau yogastena kṛtvā tāvadbhṛśamatyarthaṃ pakvaṃ kāryaṃ yāvadaśarīratāṃ yāti taccūrṇaṃ garbhe rasodare dravati garbhadrutirbhavati caśabdājjarati ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s>, that is, <s>kharparika</s>, when joined and combined with <s>balin</s>, namely sulphur, in an equal part, this being supplied, should be cooked very intensely and thoroughly by the previously stated method, that is, by the application of the previously stated apparatus and the rest, until it becomes bodiless. That powder melts in the womb, in the belly of <s>rasa</s>, and becomes <s>garbha-druti</s>; by the word <s>ca</s>, it is also consumed.
He states another method with the words '<s>vyūḍha</s>,' and so on.
<s>Atha</s> means 'after that.'

children.text: gandhakāśmā gandhapāṣāṇaḥ śataguṇasaṃkhyaṃ yathā syāttathā uttame hemni pūrṇavarṇe vyūḍho nirvāhyaḥ tadgandhavyūḍhaṃ hema sūte pārade piṣṭirbhavati hi niścitaṃ garbhe rasāntardravati garbhadrutir bhavatītyatravismayo ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhakāśman</s> is <s>gandha-pāṣāṇa</s>, sulphur-stone. It should be caused to pass into excellent gold, gold of full color, in a hundredfold quantity. That gold into which the sulphur has been introduced certainly becomes a paste in <s>sūta</s>, mercury; it melts inside the womb, inside the <s>rasa</s>, and becomes <s>garbha-druti</s>. Here there is no wonder.
He states another method with the words '<s>athavā</s>,' and so on.

children.text: athaveti samuccaye rasakavaraṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kharparikaṃ śuddhahemni pūrṇavarṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt śataguṇanirvāhaḥ kāryaḥ ekaguṇasvarṇe śataguṇanirvāha iti yuktaṃ evaṃ kṛte sati varabījaṃ śreṣṭhabījaṃ bhavati tadbījaṃ garbhe rasodare dravati garbhe drutirbhavati rasendre pārade śīghraṃ avilambitaṃ jarati ca niḥśeṣatām āpnoti vidhānena iti śeṣaḥ atra dravaṇe jaraṇe ca na sandehaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>athavā</s> has the sense of conjunction. The best <s>rasaka</s>, excellent <s>kharparika</s>, should be introduced a hundred times into purified gold of full color; a hundredfold carrying-through is to be done. The proper rule is that there is a hundredfold carrying-through into gold of one part. When this has been done, it becomes an excellent seed. That seed melts in the womb, in the belly of <s>rasa</s>, and becomes molten in the womb; and in <s>rasendra</s>, mercury, it is quickly, without delay, consumed and reaches complete exhaustion, by the procedure, this being supplied. There is no doubt here about either melting or consumption.
With reference to the previous matter, he states another method with the words '<s>athavā</s>,' and so on.

children.text: tālakasatvaṃ haritālasāraṃ śataguṇaṃ śataguṇitaṃ hemni kanake nirvyūḍhaṃ andhamūṣāyāṃ vā prakāśamūṣāyāṃ vahniyogena iti śeṣaḥ tālakasatvasya hemni nirvāhaḥ kārya iti vyaktiḥ tacca tat sattvaṃ kevalaṃ vā śilayā manaḥśilayā sārdhaṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ kāryaṃ taddhema garbhe rasodare dravati atha rasendro rasarājaḥ drutaṃ jarati vidhāneneti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> of <s>tālaka</s>, the essence of orpiment, made a hundredfold, should be introduced into <s>hema</s>, gold, in a closed crucible or an open crucible, by the application of fire, this being supplied. The meaning is that the <s>sattva</s> of <s>tālaka</s> should be carried into gold. And that <s>sattva</s>, either by itself or together with <s>śilā</s>, realgar, should be introduced. That gold melts in the womb, in the belly of <s>rasa</s>. Then <s>rasendra</s>, the king <s>rasa</s>, is quickly consumed, by the procedure.
Now he states another procedure with the words '<s>rasa</s>,' and so on.

children.text: rasadaradābhrakatāpyamiti rasaḥ pāradaḥ darado hiṅgulaḥ abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ vimalā rukmamākṣikaṃ mṛtaṃ yacchulbaṃ tāmraṃ loho muṇḍādiśca eteṣāṃ rasādīnāṃ rasaparpaṭīvat parpaṭikā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: In '<s>rasa-darada-abhraka-tāpya</s>,' <s>rasa</s> is mercury, <s>darada</s> is cinnabar, <s>abhraka</s> is mica, which is well known, <s>tāpya</s> is gold pyrite, <s>vimalā</s> is copper pyrite, and the killed <s>śulba</s> is copper, while <s>loha</s> is <s>muṇḍa</s> and the other irons. From these, beginning with <s>rasa</s>, a thin sheet, like a <s>rasa-parpaṭī</s>, should be made.

children.text: tayā yutaṃ nāgaṃ punaḥ kaṅkuṣṭhaśilāyutaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ haritapītavarṇo viṣaharapāṣāṇajātiḥ śilā manohvā tābhyāṃ yutaṃ miśritaṃ yannāgaṃ sīsakaḥ snuhyarkadugdhapiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ snuhī sehuṇḍaḥ arkaḥ prasiddho viṭapī tayordugdhena piṣṭaṃ pāṃśubhūtaṃ mṛtaṃ yannāgaṃ kukkuṭapuṭavidhāneneti śeṣaḥ etadapi bījaṃ siddhaṃ garbhe dravati ca pūrvasaṃbandhāt ||
children.translated_text: The <s>nāga</s>, lead, joined with that and again joined with <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and <s>śilā</s> should be prepared. <s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is a yellow-green class of poison-destroying stone, and <s>śilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>, realgar. The <s>nāga</s>, lead, mixed with those two should be ground with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>; <s>snuhī</s> is <s>sehuṇḍa</s>, and <s>arka</s> is the well-known tree. The <s>nāga</s>, killed and reduced to powder by being ground with the milks of those two, by the procedure of a <s>kukkuṭa-puṭa</s>, this being supplied, is also a perfected seed and melts in the womb, from the previous connection.
Now he states the procedure for a <s>vaṅga</s>-seed with the words '<s>abhraka</s>,' and so on.

children.text: ciñcākṣāravimiśraṃ yadvaṅgaṃ amlikākṣārayuktaṃ vaṅgaṃ abhrakatālakaśaṅkharasasahitaṃ abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ śaṅkhaṃ kambugrīvaṃ rasaḥ pāradaḥ etaiścaturbhiḥ sahitaṃ yathā syāttathā punaḥ punaḥ vāraṃ vāraṃ nirutthaṃ yāvat tāvatpuṭitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: The <s>vaṅga</s> that is mixed with tamarind alkali, that is, tin joined with sour alkali, and furnished with <s>abhraka</s>, <s>tālaka</s>, <s>śaṅkha</s>, and <s>rasa</s>--mica, orpiment, conch-shell, and mercury--should be heated again and again, time after time, until it becomes without rising.

children.text: etadauṣadhasyāṃśabhāgena saha puṭanādvaṅgaṃ nirjīvatāṃ yāti pañcatvamāpnoti etadapi bījaṃ siddhaṃ garbhadrāvaṇe jāraṇārthe ca pūrvasaṃbandhāt ||
children.translated_text: Because of the heating together with one part of this medicine, the <s>vaṅga</s> becomes lifeless and reaches dissolution. This too is a perfected seed for melting in the womb and for the purpose of consumption, from the previous connection.
He says that this medicine is the cause for <s>nāga</s> and <s>vaṅga</s> with the words '<s>vidhinā</s>,' and so on.

children.text: anena vidhinā uktavidhānena nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ puṭitaṃ sat mriyate mṛtaṃ bhavatīti vāmunā vidhānenaiva nirutthatāṃ gataṃ aśarīratāṃ prāptaṃ vaṅgaṃ sarvakarmasu cāraṇajāraṇabhakṣaṇādikāryeṣu niyujyate rasajñairiti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this method, by the stated procedure, <s>nāga</s>, lead, when heated, is killed, or becomes killed; and by this very procedure <s>vaṅga</s>, tin, having become without rising and having attained bodilessness, is employed by those who know <s>rasa</s> in all operations, such as <s>cāraṇa</s>, <s>jāraṇa</s>, and eating, this being supplied.

children.text: nāgavaṅgamāraṇam ekavidham evoktam atas tadbhakṣaṇādiṣu parasparaṃ guṇādhikayogyaṃ natu jāraṇādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: The killing of <s>nāga</s> and <s>vaṅga</s> has been stated as one single kind. Therefore, in such matters as their eating, there is a mutual suitability according to superiority of qualities, but not in such matters as <s>jāraṇa</s>.
He states the procedure for the consumption of <s>nāga</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, <s>śulba</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> with the words '<s>mṛta-nāgam</s>,' and so on.

children.text: mṛtanāgamiti mṛtaṃ nirjīvatāṃ gataṃ yannāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tathānena vidhānena mṛtaṃ vaṅgaṃ tathā mṛtaṃ nirutthatāṃ gataṃ varaśulbaṃ tāmraṃ tathā ca mṛtaṃ tīkṣṇam arivargeṇeti śeṣaḥ eṣāṃ madhye ekaikaṃ nāgaṃ vā vaṅgaṃ vā śulbaṃ vā tīkṣṇaṃ vā pṛthaktvena hemavare pūrṇavarṇe svarṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ hemnaḥ śataguṇanirvāhitaṃ kuryāt tatsiddhaṃ garbhe rasodare dravati caśabdājjarati ca ||
children.translated_text: "Dead <s>nāga</s>" means <s>nāga</s>, lead, which has died, that is, has reached a lifeless state. In the same way, by this procedure, dead <s>vaṅga</s>, tin, and likewise excellent <s>śulba</s>, copper, which is dead, that is, has reached a state from which it does not rise again, and likewise dead <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, iron, should be understood as treated with the enemy-group. Among these, each single one, whether <s>nāga</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, <s>śulba</s>, or <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, separately, should make excellent gold, gold of full color, carried through a hundred times the quantity of gold. When that is accomplished, it melts in the womb, in the belly of the <s>rasa</s>; and, by the word "and," it also digests.
Showing the power of the great seed, he says "of equal womb," and so on.

children.text: ihāsmiñśāstre vidhinā śāstroktarītyā yāni bījānyuktāni tāni kartavyāni sāmānyeneti bhāvaḥ paraṃ garbhadrutyarthaṃ ayaṃ vārttikendro yogaḥ vārttāsu kuśalā vārtikāḥ śāstropadeśarahitā ityarthaḥ atra bhāvādyarthe ikpratyayaḥ teṣu vārtikeṣu indraḥ pravaro yogaḥ tathānenaiva prakāreṇa ekamataścāyaṃ śāstropadeśikānāṃ śāstropadeśarahitānāṃ ca abhimata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, in this treatise, the seeds that have been stated according to rule, that is, in the manner taught by the treatise, are to be prepared; this is the general sense. But for the sake of womb-melting this is the chief procedure among the <s>vārtikas</s>. <s>Vārtikas</s> are those skilled in practical arts, meaning those without instruction from the treatise; here the suffix <s>ik</s> is used in the sense of state or condition. Among those <s>vārtikas</s>, this procedure is the <s>indra</s>, the foremost. Thus, in this very manner, it is approved both by those who possess instruction from the treatise and by those who lack instruction from the treatise.
He states the procedure for melting the seed in the belly of the <s>rasa</s> with "or else," and so on.
The word "or else" has the sense of conjunction.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ dīrghatamamūṣāyantrasya talabhāge piṣṭī rasendrabījayor nirmitā piṣṭikā ca punaḥ sudṛḍhā yathā syāttathā lagnā kartavyā ||
children.translated_text: Above, at the lower part of the apparatus of the very long crucible, a <s>piṣṭī</s>, a small paste-ball made from <s>rasendra</s> and the seed, should again be fixed very firmly.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā kharparasyārdhe mṛnmayapātrasya khaṇḍārdhe khaṇḍaikadeśa ityarthaḥ dīrghatamāṃ adhobhāgamukhīṃ adhobhāge mukhaṃ yasyāḥ sā tathoktā tāṃ dattvā ||
children.translated_text: After doing what? Having placed a very long one on half of a <s>kharpara</s>, that is, on half of an earthen vessel, meaning on one part of a fragment, with its mouth turned downward, that is, having its opening in the lower part.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃ kṛtvā gandhakadhūmaṃ dattvā vā stokaṃ stokaṃ alpamalpaṃ tālakadhūmaṃ dattvā vā śilāhvarasakasya śilāhvā manaḥśilā rasakaḥ kharparaḥ cakavad bhāvasamāsaḥ tasya dhūmaṃ dattvā ||
children.translated_text: Again, after doing what? Having applied smoke of sulfur, or having applied, little by little, a small amount of smoke of <s>tālaka</s>, or having applied smoke of <s>śilāhva-rasaka</s>. <s>Śilāhvā</s> is realgar, and <s>rasaka</s> is <s>kharpara</s>; the compound is like <s>cakavat</s>, a compound in the sense of becoming, and means the smoke of that.

children.text: punastatkharparaṃ adhomukhamukhāṃ ca mṛdā liptāṃ mṛdveṣṭitāṃ karīṣāgnau dhmāpayet karīṣavahnāvityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then that <s>kharpara</s>, together with the downward-facing mouth, plastered with clay, that is, wrapped in clay, should be blown in a fire of cow-dung cakes, meaning in a cow-dung fire.

children.text: evaṃ adhomukhāṃ kharparaṃ ca dattvā daityendraṃ balināmānaṃ prastāvādgandhakaṃ tadanu tatkaraṇapaścād dāhayet ||
children.translated_text: When, in this way, the downward-facing <s>kharpara</s> has been placed, then the lord of the demons, named <s>Bali</s>, here by context sulfur, should afterward be burned, after that operation.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte sati rasendramilitaṃ yadbījaṃ tadgarbhe rasendrāntardravati ||
children.translated_text: When this has been done, the seed joined with <s>rasendra</s> melts in the womb, inside the <s>rasendra</s>.

children.text: punarbījasahito rasendro 'dhike dāhe sati mriyata ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, when there is excessive burning, the <s>rasendra</s> together with the seed dies; this is the meaning.
Because it is connected with three verses, this is a single qualified construction.
Now, for the sake of digesting gold, he states a <s>biḍa</s> with "sulfur," and so on.

children.text: gandhakatālakaśailā iti gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ śailaḥ śilājatuḥ dvaṃdvaḥ samāsaḥ tena tathoktāḥ samabhāgāḥ kāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Sulfur, <s>tālaka</s>, and <s>śaila</s>": sulfur is well known, <s>tālaka</s> is orpiment, and <s>śaila</s> is bitumen; this is a copulative compound. These, so named, should be made in equal parts.

children.text: punaḥ sauvīrakaṃ śuklāñjanaṃ rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ gairikaṃ dhātugairikaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ atraikavadbhāvasamāsaḥ tattathoktaṃ samabhāgaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>sauvīraka</s>, white collyrium, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>kharparika</s>, <s>gairika</s>, mineral ochre, and <s>darada</s>, cinnabar: here there is a compound with singular sense. What is so called should be made in equal part.

children.text: punaḥ kṣārāmlalavaṇāni kṣārā yavakṣārādayaḥ amlaṃ jambīrādi lavaṇāni saindhavādīni etānyapi samabhāgāni ||
children.translated_text: Again, alkalis, acids, and salts: the alkalis are barley-alkali and the like, the acid is citron and the like, and the salts are rock salt and the rest. These too are to be in equal parts.

children.text: kaiḥ saha mākṣikavaikrāntavimalasamabhāgaiḥ saha mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ vimalaṃ rukmamākṣikaṃ etāni samabhāgāni tairbiḍa ucyate sarvaiḥ samabhāgaiḥ sumarditair biḍaḥ kārya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with what? Together with equal parts of <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>vimala</s>. <s>Mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite; <s>vaikrānta</s> is dust born from diamond-ground; <s>vimala</s> is golden pyrite. With these equal parts, it is called <s>biḍa</s>; the meaning is that <s>biḍa</s> should be made from all of them in equal parts, well triturated.

children.text: biḍayogādyathā bījaṃ garbhe dravati tathāha kṛtvetyādi ||
children.translated_text: How the seed melts in the womb through the application of the <s>biḍa</s> is stated with "having made," and so on.

children.text: pūrvoktā yā piṣṭī tāmanenaivoktabiḍayogena tapte khalve taptasaṃbandhāllohamaye tripuṭaiḥ karīṣāgnyātmakair mṛditā gharṣitā sati anenaiva ca veṣṭitā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: The previously mentioned <s>piṣṭī</s>, when rubbed, that is, ground, in a heated mortar by means of triple pellets consisting of cow-dung fire, in connection with heat, should be wrapped with this very <s>biḍa</s> procedure just described.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā suvarṇapiṣṭīṃ kanakapiṣṭīṃ vā anyasyāpi dhātoḥ suvarṇapiṣṭīṃ śobhanavarṇāṃ piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: After doing what? After making a gold <s>piṣṭī</s>, or a golden <s>piṣṭī</s> of another metal also, a <s>piṣṭī</s> of beautiful color.

children.text: khalve mṛditā satī tathā tenaiva prakāreṇa natvanyaprakāreṇa garbhe rasodare dravati salilarūpā tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: When it has been rubbed in a mortar, then, in that very way and not in another way, it melts in the womb, in the belly of the <s>rasa</s>, and remains in the form of liquid.
Now he states the womb-melting of <s>vaikrānta</s> with "red," and so on.

children.text: vaikrāntabhasma vajrabhūmijaṃ rajas tadudbhavaṃ bhasma rakte raktagaṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ śatavāraṃ nirvāhitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>-ash, the dust born from diamond-ground, the ash produced from that, should be carried through in the red group a hundred times.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ netrahitaṃ netrahitaśabdena maṇitvaṃ darśitaṃ maṇayo netrahitā iti ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind? "Beneficial to the eyes." By the expression "beneficial to the eyes," its gem-nature is indicated, for gems are beneficial to the eyes.

children.text: vimalaṃ rūpyamākṣikaṃ śvetavarṇaṃ yanmākṣikaṃ raktagaṇe śatanirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s>, silver-pyrite, the white-colored <s>mākṣika</s>, should be carried through in the red group a hundred times.

children.text: tadubhayaṃ vaikrāntaṃ vimalaṃ ca raktaśatanirvyūḍhaṃ sat raso grāsavidhānaṃ vihāya samaṃ grasati kavalayati stadgrasitaṃ garbhe rasāntardravati jarati ca iti caśabdārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those two, <s>vaikrānta</s> and <s>vimala</s>, when carried through a hundred times in the red group, are swallowed equally by the <s>rasa</s>, abandoning the ordinary procedure for taking a mouthful; it gulps them down. Having been swallowed by it, they melt in the womb, inside the <s>rasa</s>, and also digest; this is the meaning of the word "and."
Showing the superiority of the red group, he says "which," and so on.

children.text: ye kecidviḍayogā atra granthāntareṣvapi ca kathitāḥ tathā kṣārāmlalavaṇāni kathitāni kṣārā yavakṣārādayaḥ atha ca vṛkṣauṣadhisamudbhavāḥ amlā jambīrādayaḥ amlavṛkṣaśākasamudbhavāśca yānyetāni kathitāni ca punarye dīptavargāḥ kathitā dīptikarā yogā abhihitāḥ te sarve biḍakṣārāmlalavaṇadīptavargāḥ śatanirvyūḍhā garbhadrutikārakāḥ garbhe rasodare drutaṃ dravarūpaṃ kurvanti dhātumaṇiratnādīnīti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>biḍa</s>-recipes have been stated here and also in other treatises, and likewise the alkalis, acids, and salts that have been stated: the alkalis are barley-alkali and the like, and those produced from trees and herbs; the acids are citron and the like, and those produced from acid trees and greens. And again, those groups called the <s>dīpta</s>-class, the recipes that produce ignition, have been described. All these, the <s>biḍa</s>, alkalis, acids, salts, and <s>dīpta</s>-class, when carried through a hundred times, produce <s>garbha-druti</s>; that is, they make metals, minerals, gems, and the like become quickly liquid, in liquid form, in the womb, in the belly of <s>rasa</s>.
He states the rule of equal and other proportions in the case of a hundredfold carrying-through and the like, with the words beginning '<s>śata</s>'.

children.text: śatanirvyūḍha iti śatavāraṃ nirvāhite raktagaṇe iti śeṣaḥ samaṃ tulyaṃ grasati rasa iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Carried through a hundred times' means, in the red group carried through a hundred times; the remainder is, '<s>rasa</s> swallows an equal amount.'

children.text: punaḥ pañcasaptativyūḍhe sati pādonaṃ caturthāṃśavarjitaṃ samagraṃ grasatīti ||
children.translated_text: Again, when it has been carried through seventy-five times, it swallows the whole less a quarter, that is, with the fourth part excluded.
Again, when it has been carried through fifty times, it swallows half of that, that is, half of the equal amount.
Again, when it is twenty-fivefold, it swallows a quarter, that is, a fourth part.

children.text: nyūnādhike nirvyūḍhe sati nyūnādhikāṃśo jñeya iti viśeṣārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the carrying-through is less or more, the proportion is to be understood as less or more; this is the special point.
He states the sequence for a lesser carrying-through with the words beginning 'an eighth'.

children.text: tu punastadardhe sārdhadvādaśake nirvyūḍhe sati aṣṭāṃśaṃ tadardhe ṣaḍvāranirvyūḍhe sati ṣoḍaśāṃśamiti punastasyārdhe trivāranirvyūḍhe sati dvātriṃśadaṃśaṃ tadardhanirvyūḍhe ekadvivāranirvyūḍhe sati catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśaṃ raso grasatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But again, when it has been carried through half of that, twelve and a half times, <s>rasa</s> swallows an eighth. When it has been carried through half of that, six times, it swallows a sixteenth. Again, when it has been carried through half of that, three times, it swallows a thirty-second part. When it has been carried through half of that, once or twice, it swallows a sixty-fourth part; this is the meaning.
When <s>garbha-druti</s> has occurred, he states what should be done, with the words beginning '<s>iti</s>'.

children.text: ityuktavidhānena gaditāṃ kathitāṃ garbhadrutiṃ jñātvā tapte khalvatale lohamaye karīṣāgninā uṣṇatāṃ nīte mṛditāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Knowing the <s>garbha-druti</s> that has been declared, that is, stated, according to the prescribed method, one should make it rubbed on the heated surface of a mortar, an iron one, brought to heat by a fire of cow-dung cakes.

children.text: kena abhiṣavayogena abhiṣavaḥ saṃmardanaṃ tasya yogena na kevalamanena amlavargeṇa ca jambīrādinā na kevalamanenāpi svedanavidhinā ca svedanavidhiḥ svedanasaṃskāroktatvānnātrābhihitaḥ jāraṇahetoriti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By what means? By the method of <s>abhiṣava</s>; <s>abhiṣava</s> is thorough trituration, and the method belongs to that. Not by this alone, but also with the acid group, citron and the like; and not by this alone either, but also by the heating method. The heating method, since it has been stated in the heating preparation, is not described here. The remainder is, 'for the sake of <s>jāraṇa</s>'.
Showing the earlier equipment for rubbing and heating, he says, with the words beginning 'having known'.

children.text: bījabalābalamardanayogaṃ kṛtaṃ jñātvā bījānāṃ dhātūpadhātuyogajanitānāṃ balābale nyūnādhike yo'sau mardanayogastameva kṛtaṃ jñātvā viditvā rasarāje svedavidhānaṃ kuryāt vā puṭaṃ vahniyogaṃ kuryāt vā yantraṃ vihitarasakarma kuryāt vihitaṃ kṛtaṃ rasasya karma saṃskārarūpaṃ yatra tathoktaṃ garbhayantrādikamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having known that the rubbing-method has been made according to the strength and weakness of the seed, that is, having understood that very rubbing-method, greater or lesser, according to the strength and weakness of seeds produced from combinations of metals and secondary metals, one should perform the heating procedure on <s>rasarāja</s>, or one should perform a <s>puṭa</s>, an application of fire, or one should use an apparatus, a prescribed operation for <s>rasa</s>. This means an apparatus such as a womb-apparatus in which the operation of <s>rasa</s>, in the form of preparation, has been prescribed and performed.
Because the operation of <s>sūta</s> is difficult to understand, he praises the teacher's feet, with the words beginning '<s>sūta</s>'.

children.text: yathā yena prakāreṇa sūtavaraṃ pāradaḥ lakṣayate jñāyate karmakṛteti śeṣaḥ punaryathā bījaṃ upekṣatāṃ na yāti samyak milati tadvattenaiva prakāreṇa gurupādanirdiṣṭaṃ karma ācāryavaryadarśitaṃ pūjyaṃ saṃskārarūpaṃ vidhinā ācāryoktavidhānena kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In whatever way the excellent <s>sūta</s>, mercury, is recognized, the remainder being 'as fit for work,' and again in whatever way the seed does not pass into neglect but combines properly, in just that way one should perform the venerable operation, in the form of preparation, indicated by the teacher's feet and shown by the best of teachers, according to the rule taught by the teacher.
The characteristics of the teacher's feet:
He should know the distinctions of all śāstras and be skilled in the operation of <s>rasa</s>.
One furnished with such characteristics should be a teacher of <s>rasavidyā</s>.
Thus.
Thus ends the section on <s>jāraṇa</s> through <s>garbha-druti</s>.
Praising external melting, he says, with the words beginning '<s>bāhya-druti</s>'.
Melting is said to be of two kinds: <s>garbha-druti</s> and <s>bāhya-druti</s>.
<s>Garbha-druti</s> has been stated before; <s>bāhya-druti</s> is now being explained.
Of what kind is it? Extremely pure, very stainless.

children.text: eṣā ca punaḥ keṣāṃcideva siddhānāṃ sphurati siddhā rasavidyāpāragā nityanāthādayaḥ teṣāṃ te jānantīti ||
children.translated_text: And this, again, appears only to certain perfected ones. The perfected ones are those who have crossed to the far shore of <s>rasavidyā</s>, such as <s>Nityanātha</s>; it is they who know it.
Because it is hard to obtain, <s>bāhya-druti</s> is rare here.

children.text: tebhyaḥ samyak jñātvā tathā tenaiva siddhodeśavidhānena drutayo bāhyadrutayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having properly learned it from them, and in that very manner, according to the instruction-method of the perfected ones, there are meltings, namely external meltings.
Now he states the digestion of <s>nāga</s>, with the words beginning '<s>vara-nāga</s>'.

children.text: varanāgaṃ śreṣṭhajāti sīsakaṃ jāraṇayogyaṃ rasarājaṃ uktasaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaṃ pāradaṃ bījavaraṃ hemabījaṃ etattrayaṃ sāritaṃ militaṃ kāryaṃ punargandhakaśilālasahitaṃ gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ śilā manaḥśilā ālaṃ haritālaṃ dvandvastāni taiḥ sahitaṃ ca kāryaṃ etat sarvaṣaṭkaṃ dīpavartitaḥ prajvālitadīpavartiyogāt nirnāgaṃ nāgavarjitaṃ bhavati nāgaṃ jaratītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Excellent <s>nāga</s>, that is, lead of the best type fit for digestion; <s>rasarāja</s>, mercury prepared by the stated preparations; and the best seed, a gold seed: these three should be made combined and joined. Again, it should be made together with sulfur, <s>śilā</s>, and <s>āla</s>: sulfur is well known, <s>śilā</s> is realgar, and <s>āla</s> is orpiment. These form a copulative group, and it should be made together with them. This whole group of six, through the application of a kindled lamp-wick, becomes without <s>nāga</s>, devoid of lead; the meaning is that it digests the lead.

children.text: yathā nirṇāgaṃ syāttathā vidhānam āha baddhvetyādi ||
children.translated_text: He states the procedure by which it becomes leadless, with the words beginning 'having tied'.

children.text: tatpūrvoktaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ sudṛḍhe vastre nūtane vastre atropaśleṣike 'dhikaraṇe saptamī poṭalikāyāṃ baddhvā punastaile tilodbhave tatṣaṭkaṃ magnaṃ nimajjitaṃ kṛtvā tadadhaḥ śikhīkṛto dīpo'vadhāryaḥ na śikhī śikhāyuktaḥ kṛtaḥ śikhīkṛtaḥ śikhāvānityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The previously mentioned group of six should be tied in a very firm cloth, a new cloth. Here the locative in 'in the pouch' is used with reference to the receptacle. Having tied it in a small bundle, then one should immerse that group of six in oil produced from sesame. Below it, a lamp made into a flame should be fixed. It is not merely 'flaming' as an adjective; 'made into a flame' means made furnished with a flame, that is, flame-bearing.

children.text: anena vidhinā kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ nirnāgaṃ syāditi ||
children.translated_text: By this method it quickly, swiftly, becomes without <s>nāga</s>.
He states the procedure for making it leadless, with the words beginning 'having made'.

children.text: tu punaḥ dīrghāṃ gostanākārāṃ sudṛḍhāṃ nirvraṇavajropamāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā tāṃ mūṣāṃ prati śilālacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā śilā manohvā ālaṃ haritālaṃ etayoścūrṇaṃ paścātsūtaṃ pūrvoktaṃ pāradaṃ kṣiptvā tato'nantaraṃ śilācūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā tāmeva rasasaṃyuktāṃ mūṣāṃ bhasmagartāyāṃ bhasmanā yuktā yā gartā tasyāṃ dhmātaṃ kuryāt punastāvadbhasmanā ācchādya yāvatsvāṅgaśītalaṃ svayameva śītalaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, having made a long, cow-teat-shaped, very firm crucible, free of cracks and like a thunderbolt, one should put powder of <s>śilā</s> into that crucible. <s>Śilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>, and <s>āla</s> is <s>haritāla</s>; after the powder of these two, one should put in <s>sūta</s>, the previously mentioned mercury, and after that powder of <s>śilā</s>. Then that same crucible, joined with <s>rasa</s>, should be blown in an ash-pit, that is, in a pit filled with ash. It should again be covered with ash until it becomes cold in its own body, that is, cold of itself.

children.text: tatra tasyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ sakalaṃ samastaṃ nāgaṃ subhakṣitaṃ jīrṇatāṃ gataṃ jñātvā sūtaṃ ākṛṣya uddhārya nirnāgakaraṇavidhānam etat ||
children.translated_text: There, in that crucible, when one knows that all the <s>nāga</s> has been well eaten and has reached digestion, one should draw out and remove the <s>sūta</s>. This is the procedure for making it free from <s>nāga</s>.
He states what is to be done after making it free from <s>nāga</s>, with the words "having known," and so on.

children.text: nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ truṭitaṃ buddhvā punarapi nāgaṃ dahyāt pūrvoktavidhānena pārade iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having understood that the <s>nāga</s>, lead, has split apart, one should again burn the <s>nāga</s> by the previously stated procedure, in mercury; this last phrase is to be supplied.
One should do it in just such a way that the <s>nāga</s> becomes threefold.

children.text: paścātsūtaṃ śuddhaṃ kṛtvā pāradaṃ nirnāgaṃ vidhāya tadanu nāgajāraṇānantaraṃ bījavaraṃ pūrvoktaṃ yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Afterward, having purified the <s>sūta</s> and made the mercury free from <s>nāga</s>, then, after the digestion of <s>nāga</s>, one should apply the excellent seed mentioned before.
Now he states the combination with <s>tāra</s>, with the words "or else," and so on.
The word "or else" indicates another procedure.

children.text: tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ sūtam iti tāraṃ rūpyaṃ vaṅgaṃ khurakaṃ sūtaṃ saṃskṛtapāradaṃ etattritayaṃ saṃsārya melanaṃ vidhāya vaṅgaparihīnaṃ kuryāt tathā tenaiva vidhānena tālasya yo'sau yogastena yantrayogena ca dīrghamūṣāyogena ca nirvaṅgaṃ vaṅgavivarjitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In "<s>tāra</s>, <s>vaṅga</s>, and <s>sūta</s>," <s>tāra</s> is silver, <s>vaṅga</s> is <s>khuraka</s>, tin, and <s>sūta</s> is processed mercury. Having brought this triad together and made a union, one should make it free from <s>vaṅga</s>. Likewise, by that very procedure, by the apparatus-procedure connected with the operation of <s>tāla</s> and by the procedure of the long crucible, one should make it free from <s>vaṅga</s>, devoid of tin.
He states another procedure with the words "or else," and so on.

children.text: athavā tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ vaṭakākāraṃ taile tilodbhave pakvaṃ kuryāt nūnaṃ niścitaṃ tadvaṭakaṃ tathā pakvaṃ kuryādyathā nirvaṅgaṃ jāyate vahniyogena iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else, one should make <s>tāra</s> and <s>vaṅga</s> into the form of pellets and cook them in oil produced from sesame. Certainly that pellet should be cooked in such a way that, by the application of fire, it becomes free from <s>vaṅga</s>; this is to be supplied.
He states another procedure with the words "<s>piṣṭī</s>," and so on.

children.text: bījavareṇaiva pūrvakanakabījenaiva sāritaṃ militaṃ sat piṣṭīstambhaṃ khoṭastambhaṃ kṛtvā tadanu tatpaścāt athaveti prakārāntaraṃ darśayati tu punaḥ baddharasena khoṭabaddharasena sahitaṃ surañjitaṃ śobhanavidhānena varṇavṛddhīkṛtaṃ bījaṃ svarṇabījaṃ saṃyutaṃ kuryāt yoga eva kārya iti dvividhānam uktam ||
children.translated_text: When it has been made to flow or has been mixed with the excellent seed alone, that is, with the previously mentioned gold-seed, one should make a <s>piṣṭī-stambha</s>, a <s>khoṭa-stambha</s>. After that, with the word "or else," he shows another method: again, together with bound <s>rasa</s>, that is, with <s>khoṭa</s>-bound <s>rasa</s>, one should combine the well-colored seed, the gold-seed whose color has been increased by an excellent procedure. Thus two procedures have been stated as the operation to be performed.
And he states something else with the words "sulfur," and so on.

children.text: gandhakanihitaṃ gandhake nihitaṃ sthāpitaṃ sūtaṃ ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā sūtaṃ madhyasthaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Placed in sulfur" means <s>sūta</s> placed and set in sulfur. The meaning is that, after putting sulfur above and below, one should make the <s>sūta</s> stand in the middle.

children.text: ca punarevaṃvidhaṃ sūtaṃ śṛṅkhalāyāṃ śṛṅkhalīkaraṇayoge nihitānihitaṃ yannihitaṃ tadanihitam ajāritaṃ kāryaṃ nihitānihitasaṃyogāt śṛṅkhaleyaṃ nūnaṃ niścitaṃ yojitanirvyūḍharase pūrvaṃ yojitaṃ paścānnirvāhitaṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ yatra tattasminnevaṃvidharase garbhadrutiḥ pāradasyodare bījāni dravanti ||
children.translated_text: And again, <s>sūta</s> of this kind, placed in a chain, that is, in the operation of making a chain, should be made "placed and not placed": what is placed should be made not placed, undigested. From the conjunction of what is placed and not placed, this chain is certainly formed. In <s>rasa</s> in which the <s>rasa</s> has first been joined and afterward carried through, that is, completed, <s>garbha-druti</s> occurs: the seeds melt in the belly of the mercury.
He states digestion by the <s>piṣṭī</s> procedure with the words "of <s>sūtaka</s>," and so on.

children.text: tu punaḥ rasendrake garbhe rasendrakṛto yo'sau garbhastasmin bījaṃ kṛtvā vidhinā piṣṭīrvidheyā sā piṣṭī mṛditā kāryā kasmāt abhiṣavayogāt saṃmardanayogāt kena saha sūtakabhasmavareṇa saha sūtakasya yadbhasmavaraṃ tena sā piṣṭī garbhe dravati caśabdājjarati ca ||
children.translated_text: Again, when a seed has been placed in the womb of <s>rasendraka</s>, that is, in the womb made by <s>rasendra</s>, <s>piṣṭīs</s> should be prepared by the rule. That <s>piṣṭī</s> should be rubbed. Why? Because of the operation of <s>abhiṣava</s>, the operation of trituration. With what? Together with the excellent ash of <s>sūtaka</s>. With that excellent ash of <s>sūtaka</s>, that <s>piṣṭī</s> melts in the womb and, by the word "and," also digests.
He states the procedure for the excellent seed with the words "leaf-mica," and so on.

children.text: patrābhrakamiti abhrakasya patrāṇi vābhrakasya satvaṃ punaḥ kāṃkṣī saurāṣṭrī kāntamākṣikaṃ kāntaścumbakaḥ mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ eteṣāṃ dvandva ekatvaṃ punaretat nirguṇḍīgṛhakanyācāṅgerīpalāśaśākaiḥ puṭitaṃ nirguṇḍī sephālikā gṛhakanyā kumārī cāṅgerī amlaśākaḥ palāśo brahmavṛkṣaḥ śāko vṛkṣaviśeṣaḥ eteṣāṃ dvandvasamāsaḥ eteṣāṃ rasaṃ gṛhītvā pūrvauṣadhapuṭitaṃ kuryāt gharme iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Leaf-mica" means the leaves of mica, or else the essence of mica. Again, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, that is, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, and <s>kānta-mākṣika</s>: <s>kānta</s> is magnet, and <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-pyrite. These are in a copulative compound with singular sense. Again, this should be calcined with the vegetables <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>gṛhakanyā</s>, <s>cāṅgerī</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and <s>śāka</s>. <s>Nirguṇḍī</s> is <s>sephālikā</s>; <s>gṛhakanyā</s> is aloe; <s>cāṅgerī</s> is a sour green; <s>palāśa</s> is the <s>brahma-vṛkṣa</s>; and <s>śāka</s> is a particular tree. These are in a copulative compound. Taking the juice of these, one should calcine the previously mentioned medicines with it, in the heat; this last phrase is to be supplied.

children.text: tadauṣadhaṃ puṭitaṃ kṛtvā punastatpuṭitamauṣadhaṃ tatpādaśeṣaṃ caturthāṃśaṃ lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ dattvā haṇḍikāpākena haṇḍikāyāṃ mṛdbhājane yaḥ pākastena pācitaṃ vahnau puṭitaṃ tāvatkuryād yāvat sindūrasaṃprabhaṃ sindūratulyavarṇaṃ bhavati ||
