children.translated_text: Having calcined that medicine, one should again take that calcined medicine, add rock salt equal to one fourth of what remains of it, and cook it by the cooking of a pot, that is, by cooking in an earthen vessel. It should be cooked and calcined in the fire until it has a cinnabar-like appearance, a color like cinnabar.

children.text: kathaṃ pācitaṃ kuryāt sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā ekaikaṃ śatavyūḍhamiti ||
children.translated_text: How should it be cooked? In such a way that it becomes very firm: each one is to be carried through a hundred times.

children.text: pūrvoktānāṃ sindūrīkṛtānām uparasānām adharāt ekaikaṃ ekaṃ ekaṃ pṛthaktvena śatavyūḍhaṃ śatavāraṃ vāhitaṃ bījavaraṃ jāyate kanake iti śeṣaḥ tadbījaṃ rasendrasya garbhe dravati caśabdāt kṣipraṃ śīghraṃ jarati ca ||
children.translated_text: From beneath the previously mentioned secondary minerals that have been made cinnabar-colored, each one separately, one by one, carried through a hundred times, becomes an excellent seed, in gold; this last phrase is to be supplied. That seed melts in the womb of <s>rasendra</s> and, by the word "and," quickly, rapidly, digests as well.

children.text: kathaṃ aṅgulyā anāmikayā yo 'bhiṣavayogaḥ saṃmardanayogasteneti viśeṣakam ||
children.translated_text: How? By the operation of <s>abhiṣava</s>, that is, by the operation of trituration, with the ring finger; this is a qualifying detail.

children.text: nāgena bījakaraṇamāha ujjvalahemavare svarṇaśreṣṭhe āvartye samyagdrute nāgaṃ śuddhasīsakaṃ āvartyaṃ pradrāvyaṃ kiṃ kṛtvā samaṃ svarṇasamabhāgakṣepaṃ kṣiptvā punarnāgopari triguṇaśilāprativāpaṃ triguṇā yā śilā tasyā nirvāpaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: He states the making of a seed with <s>nāga</s>: in excellent bright gold, that is, in the best gold, when it has been melted and properly liquefied, <s>nāga</s>, purified lead, is to be melted and liquefied. Having done what? Having thrown in an equal addition, equal in part to the gold, then over the <s>nāga</s> one should perform a threefold application of <s>śilā</s>, that is, a quenching with three times as much <s>śilā</s>.
<s>Śilā</s> means <s>manaḥśilā</s>, realgar.

children.text: tatsiddhaṃ ahibījaṃ nāgayogena bījaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ rasavidbhiḥ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That, when perfected, is <s>ahi-bīja</s>; the seed produced by the conjunction with <s>nāga</s> is so designated by those who know <s>rasa</s>. This is to be supplied.
Now he states the seed produced by conjunction with <s>vaṅga</s>, beginning with '<s>vaṅgam</s>.'

children.text: tena pūrvoktena vidhinā vidhānena tu punaḥ hemavare pūrvavarṇite vaṅgaṃ kṣepya tālavāpena haritālanikṣepeṇa nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt vā tāre āvartye vaṅgaṃ nikṣipya nirvyūḍhaṃ nirvāhitaṃ sadbījavaraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: By that previously stated method and procedure, again, into excellent gold, the previously described gold of full color, <s>vaṅga</s> should be cast, and by an application of <s>tāla</s>, that is, by adding <s>haritāla</s>, it should be made carried-through. Or, when <s>tāra</s>, silver, has been melted, <s>vaṅga</s> should be added, and, when carried-through and brought to completion, it becomes an excellent good seed.

children.text: kasmāt truṭitasaṃyogāt truṭitaṃ bhavati tathā bījavaramiti vaṅgabījaṃ tat pūrvavat dravati jarati ca ||
children.translated_text: Why? Because of the connection with what is broken off: it becomes broken off, and likewise it becomes an excellent seed. That <s>vaṅga</s>-seed, like the preceding one, both melts and is digested.
He states praise of the seed called gold, beginning with '<s>yaḥ</s>.'

children.text: bhujaṅgāt sīsakāt niḥsṛtaḥ bhujaṅgaśilāvāpena kṣayaṃ nītvā yaḥ pṛthagbhūtaḥ sa rasakesarīvajrapañjaraḥ kathitaḥ rasa eva kesarī siṃhaḥ tadarthaṃ vajrapañjaraḥ vajreṇa vyadhitaḥ pañjaro'tidṛḍhatvāt siṃharakṣaṇasamartha ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which has emerged from <s>bhujaṅga</s>, that is, from lead, and which, by an application of <s>bhujaṅga-śilā</s>, has been brought to diminution and made separate, is called the diamond cage for the lion of <s>rasa</s>. <s>Rasa</s> itself is the lion, and for its sake there is a diamond cage; because it is a cage pierced with diamond and extremely firm, it is capable of guarding the lion. This is the meaning.

children.text: punarviśeṣeṇocyate ayaṃ vajrapañjaro na kiṃtu ayaṃ rasāṅkuśaḥ raso gajarūpaḥ tasyāṅkuśaḥ vaśīkaraṇasamarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again this is said more specifically: this is not merely a diamond cage, but this is the goad for <s>rasa</s>. <s>Rasa</s> is in the form of an elephant, and this is its goad, capable of bringing it under control.
The word '<s>nāma</s>' is used in the sense of supposition.
'Renowned' means proclaimed.

children.text: kasmāt kuṭilāt kimapi vastuharaṇāt kuṭilo vakro bhavati duṣṭasvabhāva eva anena hemnā nāgaharaṇaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: From what? From the crooked one, because it takes away some object. '<s>Kuṭila</s>' means bent, and indeed evil by nature. By means of this gold the removal of <s>nāga</s> has been accomplished.

children.text: kathaṃbhūtāt kuṭilāt phaṇī bhujaṅgaḥ hema svarṇaṃ tayorguṇā vidyante yasmin evaṃvidhāt kuṭilādeśo yuktaḥ aṅkuśo'pi vakro bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: What sort of crooked thing is it? It is such a crooked thing as possesses the qualities of <s>phaṇin</s>, the serpent, and of <s>hema</s>, gold. From such a crooked thing the designation is appropriate, for a goad too is curved.
Here there is the figure of speech called delusion, because in the gold-seed a delusive perception of a diamond cage and an elephant goad has arisen.
He states the making of this seed into <s>piṣṭī</s>, beginning with '<s>evam</s>.'

children.text: evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa vidhinārthād upadeśena pakvaṃ yadbījavaraṃ tathā pūrvasaṃskṛtaḥ sūtarāṭ pāradaḥ amlena jambīrādinā saṃsvedyaḥ svedākhyo vidhiḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this procedure, that is, by the teaching, the excellent seed that has been cooked, and likewise <s>sūtarāj</s>, mercury, previously processed, should be steamed with an acid such as citron; the procedure called steaming is to be performed.

children.text: atra kimavadhistatkartavyo yāvat ślakṣṇā spaṣṭā piṣṭī ekaśarīratā bhavet rasabījayoriti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Up to what limit should that be done here? Until a smooth, clear <s>piṣṭī</s>, a single-bodied state, comes into being for the <s>rasa</s> and the seed. This is to be supplied.
He states another procedure with '<s>tailena</s>' and so on.

children.text: tena pūrvoktena vidhinā vadhavidhānena tilatailena svinnā sveditā satī piṣṭirbhavati vahnāviti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that previously stated method, by the killing procedure, when it has been steamed with sesame oil, it becomes a <s>piṣṭī</s>; 'in fire' is to be supplied.
With '<s>athavā</s>' he shows another procedure.

children.text: śilayā dṛṣanmayayā nighṛṣṭabījaṃ nighṛṣṭaṃ gharṣitaṃ yadbījaṃ nāgākhyaṃ tat sūteneti śeṣaḥ akhilaṃ samastaṃ yathā syāttathā piṣṭirbhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: The seed called <s>nāga</s>, which has been rubbed and ground with <s>śilā</s> on a stone slab, becomes entirely, completely, a <s>piṣṭī</s> with <s>sūta</s>, mercury. This is to be supplied.
He states how the pellet should be cooked, beginning with '<s>pākaḥ</s>.'

children.text: vaṭakavidhinā māṣavaṭakavidhinā tailayogena pākaḥ kartavyaḥ vahnau pācanaṃ vidheyamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Cooking should be done according to the pellet-procedure, that is, the procedure for a <s>māṣa</s>-pellet, with the application of oil; the meaning is that cooking over fire is to be performed.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā krāmaṇapiṇḍe kṣiptvā biḍapiṇḍamadhye sthāpya ca punarmāṣair annaviśeṣair dṛḍhapiṇḍatvaṃ syāt māṣacūrṇaveṣṭitaṃ krāmaṇapiṇḍaṃ dṛḍhaṃ bhavediti vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having placed it in a <s>krāmaṇa</s>-lump and set it in the middle of a <s>biḍa</s>-lump. And by means of <s>māṣa</s>, a particular grain, it should become a firm lump; the explanation is that the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-lump wrapped in <s>māṣa</s>-flour becomes firm.
He states its procedure, beginning with '<s>mṛdu</s>.'

children.text: māṣacūrṇitajātaṃ krāmaṇapiṇḍaṃ tāvat supakvaṃ kartavyaṃ yāvaddagdhaṃ na bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The <s>krāmaṇa</s>-lump made from ground <s>māṣa</s> should be made well cooked only so long as it is not burned.

children.text: kena supakvaṃ mṛdvagninā komalavahninā puṭaḥ tatpiṇḍataḥ śeṣaṃ śiṣṭaṃ taṃ nirmalapāradaṃ ākṛṣya gṛhītvā piṇḍamanyasmin piṇḍe tathā pūrvaprakāreṇa pācyamiti ||
children.translated_text: By what is it well cooked? By a gentle fire, a soft fire. A <s>puṭa</s> is meant. Having drawn out and taken the remaining pure mercury from that lump, the lump should be cooked in another lump in the same previous manner.
And he states another method, beginning with '<s>athavā</s>.'
'<s>Athavā</s>' introduces another procedure.

children.text: punarapi piṣṭīrdolātapte auṣadhapiṇḍe dolayottapte uṣṇatāṃ nīte krāmaṇauṣadhānāṃ piṇḍe kṣepya madhye sthāpya kasyopari kharpare mṛnmayapātropari ||
children.translated_text: Again, the <s>piṣṭī</s> should be placed in a medicinal lump heated in a <s>dolā</s>, that is, in a lump of <s>krāmaṇa</s>-medicines brought to heat by a <s>dolā</s>, and set in the middle, on top of what? On a <s>kharpara</s>, an earthen vessel.

children.text: kena vidhinā pūrvoktena tailena vā amleneti ||
children.translated_text: By what procedure? By the previously stated one, either with oil or with acid.

children.text: kiyatkālaṃ yāvadgarbhe rasodare piṣṭī dravati tāvadbiḍāntare piṇḍāntare kṣepyeti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For how long? Until the <s>piṣṭī</s> melts in the womb, in the belly of the <s>rasa</s>. The intended meaning is that until then it should be placed inside another <s>biḍa</s>, another lump.
And he states another point, beginning with '<s>evam</s>.'

children.text: evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa garbhe rasodare jarati niḥśeṣatvaṃ rasodare prāpnoti ca punargarbhadrutyā rahitaṃ draveṇa varjitaṃ bījavaraṃ biḍairjarati drutabījamāraṇasamartho biḍa ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this procedure, it is digested in the womb, in the belly of the <s>rasa</s>, and reaches complete exhaustion in the belly of the <s>rasa</s>. And the excellent seed, lacking womb-melting and devoid of liquid, is digested by <s>biḍa</s>s; the meaning is that <s>biḍa</s> is capable of killing the molten seed.
The measure of a swallowed liquid, by conjunction with <s>biḍa</s>, apparatuses, and the like,
is called <s>jāraṇa</s>; its procedures exist in tens of millions.
'Procedures of the apparatuses' is to be supplied.
But the divisions of <s>jāraṇa</s> are:
making the morsel circulate, melting it in the womb, and also digesting it;
<s>jāraṇa</s> has been taught as threefold by the excellent practical experts.
Thus.
He states the <s>jāraṇa</s> that consists of womb-melting, beginning with '<s>grāsam</s>.'

children.text: pūrvoktaprakāreṇa grāsaṃ kavalaṃ yathāsaṃkhyaṃ cārayitvā punargarbhadrutiṃ kṛtvā tatastadanantaraṃ tadgarbhadrutaṃ sūtaṃ bhūrje bhūrjavṛkṣatvakpuṭake sthāpayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having, by the method stated before, caused it to take in the <s>grāsa</s>, the mouthful, in due order, and again having made <s>garbha-druti</s> (melting in the womb), then immediately afterward one should place that <s>sūta</s> (mercury), melted in the womb, in <s>bhūrja</s>, that is, in a packet of birch-tree bark. This is the meaning.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭe bhūrje lavaṇakṣārāmlasudhāsurabhimūtreṇa kṛtalepe lavaṇāni saindhavādīni kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ amlo jambīrādiḥ sudhā śukticūrṇaṃ surabhī dhenustanmūtraṃ etena yogena kṛtvā kṛto lepo yasmin ||
children.translated_text: In what sort of <s>bhūrja</s>? In one smeared with salt, alkali, acid, lime, and cow urine. The salts are rock salt and the like; the alkalis are <s>svarjikā</s> and the like; the acid is citron and the like; lime is powdered oyster shell; <s>surabhī</s> is a cow, and its urine is meant. A coating has been made on it with this mixture.
The meaning is that the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) endowed with internal melting is to be placed there.
He states the procedure for <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion) with the words beginning <s>dṛḍha</s>.

children.text: dṛḍhavastrabāhyabaddhe iti dṛḍhaṃ nūtanaṃ ghanaṃ ca yadvastraṃ tena bāhye sarvato baddhe saṃyate pūrvoktena dolāsvedena dolāyantravidhinā yaḥ svedastaṃ kṛtvā grāsaṃ rasāntardrutaṃ kavalaṃ jārayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dṛḍha-vastra-bāhya-baddhe</s> means: bound and tied all around on the outside with a strong, new, and dense cloth. Having performed the previously mentioned <s>dolā-sveda</s>, the steaming by the method of the <s>dolā-yantra</s>, one should digest the <s>grāsa</s>, the mouthful melted inside the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: kutra kumbhe kalaśe kiṃviśiṣṭe sauvīreṇārdhapūrṇe sauvīreṇa svedanasaṃskāroditakāñjikena kṛtvā ardhapūrṇe ||
children.translated_text: Where is this done? In a <s>kumbha</s>, a pot. Of what kind? Half-filled with <s>sauvīra</s>, that is, half-filled with the fermented sour gruel called <s>kāñjika</s>, which was prescribed for the steaming operation.
<s>Athavā</s> introduces another procedure.

children.text: sakṣāramūtrakaiḥ saha kṣāraḥ svarjikādibhiḥ vartante yāni mūtrāṇi go'jāvinārīṇāmiti śeṣaḥ etaiḥ ardhabhṛte kumbhe jārayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with alkaline urines: the urines in which alkalis such as <s>svarjikā</s> are present are meant, namely those of cow, goat, sheep, and woman. With these one should digest it in a half-filled pot. This is the meaning.
Now, in the digestion of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), he states the number of days with the words beginning <s>amunā</s>.

children.text: amunā krameṇeti uktaprakāreṇa tribhistribhirdivasaiḥ tribhiḥ saṃkhyākairdivasaiḥ grāse jāte anyagrāsaḥ kriyate garbhadrutagrāsaḥ kriyate garbhadrutagrāsaḥ tridivasairjaratīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Amunā krameṇa</s> means 'by the stated procedure.' Every three days, that is, at intervals of three days, when one <s>grāsa</s> has been completed, another <s>grāsa</s> is made, a <s>garbha-druta-grāsa</s> is made. The sense is that a mouthful melted in the womb digests in three days.

children.text: atheti tridinasvedānantaraṃ jīrṇasya rasasya lakṣaṇaṃ jñeyaṃ grāso jīrṇo na veti jñātavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Atha</s> means after the three days of steaming. The sign of the digested <s>rasa</s> should be known; one should determine whether the <s>grāsa</s> has been digested or not.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā yantrāddolikābhidhānād uddhṛtya yantrād bahir gṛhītveti ||
children.translated_text: After doing what? Having lifted it from the apparatus called the <s>dolikā</s>, that is, having taken it out of the apparatus.
He states the removal of impurity from the <s>rasa</s> with the words beginning <s>uddhṛta</s>.

children.text: uddhṛtamātramiti yantrād bahir gṛhītamātraṃ tatpātre bhājane mṛnmaye kāñjikena prakṣālya ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uddhṛta-mātram</s> means as soon as it has been taken out of the apparatus. It should be washed with <s>kāñjika</s> in that vessel, an earthen dish.

children.text: punar ato rasātsamalaṃ malasaṃyutaṃ kāñjikaṃ haraṇīyaṃ bahiḥ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Then from this <s>rasa</s> the <s>kāñjika</s> that is <s>samala</s>, mixed with impurity, should be removed, that is, taken out.

children.text: kena kṛtvā vastrayogena vastre kṣiptaṃ sat tadeva tiṣṭhati na kāñjikam ||
children.translated_text: By what means? By the use of cloth: when it has been placed in a cloth, only the <s>rasa</s> remains there, not the <s>kāñjika</s>.
He also states that very procedure with the words beginning <s>tadanu</s>.

children.text: tadanu vastrayogānantaraṃ sukhoṣṇe pātre asau rasaḥ saṃmardyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that, after the use of the cloth, this <s>rasa</s> should be rubbed in a pleasantly warm vessel.

children.text: kathaṃ yathā na hīyate nāśaṃ nāpnuyāt atyauṣṇyāt vā kāṃsyatāmranāgavaṅgakanakatārapātrāt vā dṛḍhakaraghātād raso hīna eva syāt ato'sau pāradas tāvan saṃmardyo yāvallagnakāñjikaṃ rasasaṃsargasauvīraṃ śuṣyati niḥśeṣatāṃ yātītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How? In such a way that it is not diminished, that it does not come to destruction. Because of excessive heat, or because of a vessel of bronze, copper, lead, tin, gold, or silver, or because of a hard blow from the hand, the <s>rasa</s> would indeed become diminished. Therefore that <s>pārada</s> (mercury) should be rubbed only until the adhering <s>kāñjika</s>, the <s>sauvīra</s> in contact with the <s>rasa</s>, dries up and is completely gone. This is the meaning.
He also states that very procedure with the words beginning <s>ittham</s>.

children.text: itthaṃ amunā prakāreṇa karamardanataḥ hastatalamardanataḥ sunirmalībhūto malarahitaḥ śoṣitajalo rasaścaturguṇena vastreṇa kṛtvā pānasyopari pīḍyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this method, the <s>rasa</s>, having become very pure through rubbing by hand, free of impurity and dried of water, should be pressed through a fourfold cloth over a drinking vessel.
He states the sign of a digested <s>grāsa</s> with the words beginning <s>yadi</s>.

children.text: tadā pārado jīrṇagrāso jñeyaḥ jīrṇo niḥśeṣatvamāpanno grāso yasmin sa tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>pārada</s> is to be known as having a digested <s>grāsa</s>: it is called so because the <s>grāsa</s> in it has been digested and brought to complete exhaustion.

children.text: yadi sakalaḥ sarvaḥ vastrātparigalitaḥ caturguṇavastrāt cyuto bhavati pātre iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If all of it, the whole, has filtered through the cloth, has passed through the fourfold cloth, then it is in the vessel; this is supplied.

children.text: punaryadi grāsena saha ekatāṃ yātaḥ san militaḥ san raso daṇḍadharo na bhavati sthirarūpo na syāt tadā jīrṇagrāso jñātavya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, if the <s>rasa</s>, having become one with the <s>grāsa</s>, having become mixed with it, does not become <s>daṇḍa-dhara</s>, that is, does not have a firm rod-like form, then it should be understood as having a digested <s>grāsa</s>. This is the meaning.
He states the sign of undigested <s>rasa</s> with the words beginning <s>grāsāt</s>.

children.text: grāsāt kavalasaṃyogāt ajīrṇapiṣṭīṃ ajīrṇā aparipakvā yā piṣṭī pūrvoktalakṣaṇā tāṃ sūtāt rasāt yantre pātanakarmocite pātayet ||
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>grāsa</s>, from contact with the mouthful, one should make the undigested <s>piṣṭī</s>, the uncooked paste with the previously stated characteristics, fall away from the <s>sūta</s>, the <s>rasa</s>, in an apparatus suited to the operation of <s>pātana</s>.

children.text: evaṃ grāsātpṛthakkṛtya patitaḥ svastho nirmalo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having been separated from the <s>grāsa</s> and made to fall, it becomes healthy and pure.

children.text: punargrāsaḥ pakvo vahnitale dattvā pakvaḥ kṛtastaṃ rasendro jaratīti ||
children.translated_text: Again, the <s>grāsa</s>, cooked by placing it over the fire, is digested by <s>rasendra</s> (the lordly mercury).
He states the use of apparatus and the rest for the digestion of the <s>grāsa</s> with the words beginning <s>dolāyām</s>.

children.text: yathākrameṇaiva catuḥṣaṣṭyādinaiva catvāro grāsā dolāyāṃ jāryāḥ śeṣā grāsāścatvāraḥ asaṃkhyā vā kacchapayantre jalayantre ca jāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the proper order, beginning with the one-sixty-fourth part, four <s>grāsas</s> are to be digested in the <s>dolā</s>. The remaining <s>grāsas</s>, four in number or else not numerically fixed, are to be digested in the <s>kacchapa-yantra</s> and the water apparatus.
Why are the remaining ones four? Because in other treatises there are only eight <s>grāsas</s>.

children.text: jāraṇe kimavadhiḥ yāvaddviguṇādikaṃ jarati pāradāddviguṇitaṃ ādiśabdena dviguṇānnyūnaṃ na kāryaṃ adhikamadhikaṃ ca bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: What is the limit in digestion? Until it digests twice as much and more. It should not be made less than twice the quantity of the <s>pārada</s>; by the word <s>ādi</s>, let it be more and more.

children.text: śaktyavatare'ṣṭau bṛhacchāstre kvacid aṣṭau grāsā uktāḥ kvacidviṃśatigrāsā iti ||
children.translated_text: When capacity permits, in the larger treatise eight <s>grāsas</s> are mentioned in some places, and in some places twenty <s>grāsas</s>.
Showing that the number of <s>grāsas</s> is not specified, he says the words beginning <s>na</s>.

children.text: atrāsmin śāstre ādau prathamaṃ grāsapramāṇaniyamaḥ kartuṃ na śakyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, in this treatise, at the outset no rule for the measure of the <s>grāsa</s> can be made.

children.text: yataḥ kāraṇāt gaganamabhraṃ sarvāṅgaṃ na grasate rasa iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the reason that the <s>rasa</s>, mercury, does not swallow <s>gagana</s>, mica, in all its parts; this is supplied.
The meaning is that the <s>gagana</s>, the mica, swallowed in all its parts, must be known only by its signs.
He states the condition of the <s>rasa</s> when the <s>grāsa</s> begins with a one-sixty-fourth part, with the words beginning <s>yadi</s>.

children.text: yadi cedrasaḥ catuḥṣaṣṭyaṃśān pramāṇato grāsaṃ grasati hi niścitaṃ tadā daṇḍaṃ dhārayet vastrānna kṣaratītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, then, the <s>rasa</s> certainly consumes a <s>grāsa</s> measuring sixty-fourth parts, then it should retain the form of a rod; that is, it does not drip from the cloth.

children.text: punaścatvāriṃśadbhāgapraveśato rasodare iti śeṣaḥ tadā pāyasākāraḥ kvathitadugdhākāro bhavet nibiḍatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, when there is entry of a fortieth part into the belly of the <s>rasa</s>, this being supplied, then it becomes like <s>pāyasa</s>, like boiled milk, because of its compactness.
He states that very point with the words “it becomes,” and so on.

children.text: viṃśadbhāgāt triṃśadbhāgasya jāraṇato jalaukākāro bhavet rasa ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the digestion of a thirtieth part from a twentieth part, it becomes like a leech; “the <s>rasa</s>” is to be supplied.

children.text: punaḥ viṃśatyā viṃśadbhāgajāraṇena avipluṣo bhaved āsanānna calati ||
children.translated_text: Again, with twenty, by the digestion of a twentieth part, it becomes <s>avipluṣa</s>: it does not move from its seat.

children.text: punaḥ ṣoḍaśāṃśāt ṣoḍaśāṃśabhāgajāraṇataḥ chedī bhavet kṣurikādibhiḥ chede kṛte pṛthaktvamāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Again, from a sixteenth part, because of the digestion of a sixteenth-part measure, it becomes divisible: when a cut is made with razors and the like, it attains separateness.
Therefore, above a sixteenth part the <s>grāsa</s> is hard to digest.
And he states that with the words “by five,” and so on.

children.text: evaṃ uktaprakāreṇa punargarbhadrāve nipuṇaḥ rasodare abhradhātvādīnāṃ drutikaraṇe pravīṇaḥ pumān kalāṃśena grāsaṃ yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the stated manner, a man again skilled in <s>garbhadrāva</s>, expert in making a liquefaction of mica-essence and other minerals in the belly of <s>rasa</s>, should apply the <s>grāsa</s> by a <s>kalā</s>-fraction.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā pañcabhiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ grāsaiścāru yathā syāttathā ghanasatvamādau jārayitvā pañcabhirgrāsair ghanasatvajāraṇānantaraṃ ṣoḍaśabhāgena bījaṃ jārayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After first digesting the dense essence beautifully with the five previously stated <s>grāsas</s>, the meaning is that, after the digestion of the dense essence by five <s>grāsas</s>, one should digest the seed by a sixteenth part.
He states the marks of <s>rasa</s> that has digested mica with the words “smoky,” and so on.

children.text: abhrajīrṇarasa evaṃvidho bhavati abhraṃ jīrṇaṃ yasmin sa tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> that has digested mica is of this sort; that in which mica has been digested is so called.

children.text: vahniyogāt prathamaṃ dhūmro dhūmrābho bhavati punaściṭiciṭiśabdo bhavati tato maṇḍūkagatirbhavati punastathā tena prakāreṇa dhṛte sati sakampo bhavati punarvahnau niṣkampaḥ svastho bhavati abhrasatvadrutasya lakṣaṇamiti ||
children.translated_text: Through contact with fire, at first it becomes smoky, having a smoky appearance. Then there is a crackling sound; after that there is frog-like movement. Again, when it is held in that same manner, it trembles; then in the fire it is motionless and steady. This is the mark of liquefied mica-essence.
He states that very point with the words “tawny,” and so on.
Again, <s>rasa</s> of this sort should be known as having digested mica.

children.text: kīdṛśaḥ kapilaḥ varṇataḥ nirudgārī sthirabhāvaḥ punaḥ sa raso vipluṣabhāvaṃ cañcalatvaṃ muñcate ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind? It is tawny in color, without emission, and stable in condition. Again, that <s>rasa</s> gives up the state of <s>vipluṣa</s>, that is, restlessness.

children.text: punarniṣkampaḥ svasthaḥ punargatirahitaḥ pakṣacchinnaḥ iti lakṣaṇānyabhrajīrṇasya bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Again, it is motionless and steady; again, it is without movement, as if its wings were cut. These are the marks of mica-digested <s>rasa</s>.
He describes the <s>kacchapa-yantra</s> with the words “water,” and so on.

children.text: jalapūrṇapātramadhye iti jalapūrṇaṃ yatpātraṃ tasya madhye suvistīrṇaṃ sundarāyataṃ ghaṭakharparaṃ kumbhakhaṇḍaṃ dattvā tadupari kharparopari biḍamadhyagataḥ sūtaḥ sthāpyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of a vessel filled with water, that is, in the middle of a water-filled vessel, after placing a very broad and well-extended potsherd, a fragment of a jar, the <s>sūta</s> situated in the middle of the <s>biḍa</s> should be placed on top of it, on top of the potsherd.

children.text: kutra kuḍye mṛdā vinirmite viśālamukhe laghulohakaṭorikayā atilaghvī yā lohasya muṇḍādeḥ kaṭorikā pātraviśeṣaḥ tayā viḍāvṛtaṃ sūtaṃ ācchādya ā samantāt saṃrudhya ||
children.translated_text: Where? In a clay-made enclosure with a broad mouth. Covering the <s>sūta</s>, which is covered with <s>biḍa</s>, with a very small iron bowl, a small vessel made of iron such as <s>muṇḍa</s>, one should close it up all around.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭayā kṛtapaṭamṛtsandhilepayā kṛtaḥ paṭamṛdbhyāṃ sandherlepo rodho yasyāḥ sā tayā ||
children.translated_text: With what kind of bowl? With one whose joint has been plastered with cloth and clay, that is, whose seam has been sealed and blocked by cloth and clay.

children.text: punastatkuḍyāntargataghaṭakharparaṃ aṅgāraiḥ pūrṇaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ karīṣatuṣamiśraiḥ karīṣo gomayasya cūrṇaṃ tuṣāḥ śālyāderdhānyasya tair miśritairiti ||
children.translated_text: Then the potsherd situated inside that enclosure is filled with embers. With what kind? With embers mixed with cow-dung powder and husks; <s>karīṣa</s> is the powder of cow-dung, and <s>tuṣa</s> means the husks of rice and other grain.
He states what is prescribed in the <s>kacchapa-yantra</s> with the words “from steaming,” and so on.

children.text: kacchapayantrastho raso jarati grāsaṃ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> situated in the <s>kacchapa-yantra</s> digests the <s>grāsa</s>, this being supplied.
From what cause? From steaming, that is, from being heated all around in the fire.

children.text: na kevalaṃ svedanato mardanataśca viḍādinā ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Not only from steaming, but also from trituration with <s>biḍa</s> and the like; this is to be supplied.

children.text: tato 'gnibalenaiva sarvalohānāṃ svarṇādīnāṃ asminnantarāle garbhadrutirbhavati atrāgnibalameva mukhyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Then, by the strength of the fire alone, <s>garbhadruti</s> of all metals, gold and the rest, takes place in this interval. Here the strength of fire itself is primary.
He states the twofold procedure in <s>jāraṇa</s> with the words “thus,” and so on.

children.text: evamamunā prakāreṇa kacchapayantre nidhāya jīryati grāsaṃ rasa iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this procedure, after placing it in the <s>kacchapa-yantra</s>, the <s>rasa</s> digests the <s>grāsa</s>; this is to be supplied.

children.text: yathā raso na kṣayati kṣayaṃ nāpnoti tathā kāryo vidhiḥ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The procedure should be carried out in such a way that the <s>rasa</s> is not depleted and does not come to loss; this is to be supplied.
The intention is to protect the support of the operation.

children.text: punaḥ kṣārabiḍaiḥ kṣayameti nāśamāpnoti grāsa ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, by alkaline <s>biḍas</s> the <s>grāsa</s> comes to loss, that is, is destroyed; this is to be supplied.

children.text: punaḥ sa rasa uparasairgandhādibhiḥ grāsaṃ utprāvalyena girati gilatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, that <s>rasa</s> swallows the <s>grāsa</s> with secondary minerals such as sulphur, with great force; that is, it gulps it down.
With alkalis, acids, sulphur and the other substances, with urines, and also with sharp salts,
for the sake of digesting the <s>rasa</s>’s <s>grāsa</s>, that is called <s>biḍa</s>.
This is the definition.
By the word <s>biḍa</s>, a lump is meant.
He states the ease of <s>jāraṇa</s> by means of <s>biḍas</s> with the words “the mouthful,” and so on.

children.text: grāsaṃ na muñcati ca punastam evānyagrāsaṃ na vāñchati bhūyaḥ punaḥ bhuktavibhuktimātrāt kāṃścidguṇān nityaṃ bhajati dadhāti grāsagrasanamātrāt guṇaṃ karotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It does not release the <s>grāsa</s>, and again it does not desire another <s>grāsa</s> besides that one. Merely from eating and digesting repeatedly, it constantly takes on certain qualities; the meaning is that, merely by swallowing the <s>grāsa</s>, it produces a quality.
For the reason that, when it is done with <s>biḍas</s> having the characteristics to be stated below, the <s>grāsa</s> is digested; this is the meaning.

children.text: kutaḥ pracurakevalavahniyogāt pracura udagro yaḥ kevalavahniyogaḥ śuddhāgniyogastasmāt ||
children.translated_text: From what cause? From abundant use of fire alone, that is, from the abundant and intense application of pure fire alone.
With what kind? With very dense, compact ones.

children.text: yato biḍāḥ śreṣṭhās tasmādviḍair eva jāraṇā syāt sugamatvāditi bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since <s>biḍas</s> are excellent, <s>jāraṇa</s> should therefore be done by <s>biḍas</s> alone, because it is easy; this is the intention.
He states the preparation of <s>biḍa</s> with the words “sauvarcala,” and so on.

children.text: tāmradalānyapi jārayati buddhimān iti śeṣaḥ svarṇabījādīnāṃ kā katheti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A wise man digests even copper leaves; what need is there to speak of gold-seeds and the like? This is the intention.
By means of what? By means of <s>biḍas</s>.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭair biḍaiḥ sauvarcalakaṭukatrayakāṃkṣīkāsīsagandhakaiḥ sauvarcalaṃ rucakaṃ kaṭutrayaṃ śuṇṭhīmaricapippalyātmakaṃ kākṣī saurāṣṭrī kāsīsaṃ puṣpakāsīsaṃ gandhakaṃ lelitakaṃ etānyauṣadhāni yeṣu viḍeṣu santi te tathoktāḥ taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With what sort of <s>biḍa</s>s? With those containing <s>sauvarcala</s>, the three pungents, <s>kākṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and sulfur. <s>Sauvarcala</s> is <s>rucaka</s>; the three pungents consist of dry ginger, black pepper, and long pepper; <s>kākṣī</s> is <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>; <s>kāsīsa</s> is <s>puṣpakāsīsa</s>; sulfur is <s>lelitaka</s>. These medicines are present in the <s>biḍa</s>s so described; by means of them.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ śigro rasaśatabhāvyaiḥ śigroḥ saubhāñjanasya rasena śatavāraṃ bhāvyāḥ ye biḍāstaiḥ evaṃ niṣpannairviḍairniścitaṃ jāraṇā syāditi bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what sort? Those to be impregnated a hundred times with the juice of <s>śigru</s>. The <s>biḍa</s>s are to be treated a hundred times with the juice of <s>śigru</s>, that is, <s>saubhāñjana</s>. With <s>biḍa</s>s thus prepared, <s>jāraṇa</s> certainly takes place; this is the meaning.
He states another <s>biḍa</s>, beginning with '<s>sarva</s>.'

children.text: sarvāṅgadagdhamūlakabhasma pratigālitamiti sarvāṅgena mūlatvakpatrapuṣpaphalena saha dagdhaṃ bhasmatāṃ prāptaṃ yanmūlakakandaṃ tadbhasma surabhimūtreṇa gojalena gālitaṃ kāryaṃ kṣāro grāhya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The ash of mūlaka burned in all its parts and filtered' means this: the bulb of <s>mūlaka</s>, burned together with all its parts, namely root, bark, leaf, flower, and fruit, and reduced to ash, should be filtered with cow urine, the liquid of the cow. The meaning is that the alkali is to be taken.

children.text: punarbalivasayā balamukhyā yā jalaukā maṇḍūkādīnāṃ vasā yathā ca
children.translated_text: Again, with <s>balivasā</s>: this means the fat of strong creatures, especially leeches, frogs, and the like, as follows:
The fat of a frog and a fish, or else the fat of a rooster,
with these one should in sequence impregnate the sulfur, or also with the fat of a <s>śiśumāra</s>.

children.text: ekā balivasā samyak sūtasya bandhinī param
children.translated_text: A single properly prepared <s>balivasā</s> is supreme for binding <s>sūta</s>.
And it also produces coloring, according to the procedure of the jewel-crucible.
Thus.

children.text: balivasayā śataṃ śatavāraṃ kṣārabhūtaṃ bhasma bhāvyaṃ punaḥ tacchatabhāvyam auṣadhaṃ tatkṣaṇataḥ tatkālato hema svarṇaṃ jāryate raso grāsabhūtaṃ hema jaratīti biḍayogāditi bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With <s>balivasā</s> the ash that has become alkali is to be impregnated a hundred times. Again, by that medicine so impregnated a hundred times, gold is digested immediately, at that very time. The intended sense is that, through the combination with <s>biḍa</s>, the <s>rasa</s> digests the gold that has become its mouthful.
Now he states particular alkali-producing trees, shrubs, and herbs, beginning with '<s>kadalī</s>.'

children.text: yathālābhaṃ lābham anatikramya eṣāṃ kṣāraḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their alkali should be prepared according to availability, without going beyond what is obtained.

children.text: te ke kadalīpalāśatilaniculakanakasuradālivāstukairaṇḍāḥ kadalī rambhā palāśo brahmavṛkṣaḥ tilāḥ pratītāḥ niculo vetasavṛkṣaḥ kanako dhattūraḥ suradālī devadālī vāstukaṃ kṣāraśākaṃ eraṇḍo vātāriḥ ete kṣārasaṃbhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Which are they? <s>Kadalī</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, sesame, <s>nicula</s>, <s>kanaka</s>, <s>suradālī</s>, <s>vāstuka</s>, and castor. <s>Kadalī</s> is plantain; <s>palāśa</s> is the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>; sesame is well known; <s>nicula</s> is the cane tree; <s>kanaka</s> is dhattūra; <s>suradālī</s> is devadālī; <s>vāstuka</s> is an alkaline vegetable; castor is <s>vātāri</s>. These are sources of alkali.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā ete varṣābhūvṛṣamokṣakasahitāḥ varṣābhūḥ punarnavā vṛṣo vāsakaḥ mokṣako mokhāvṛkṣa iti pratītaḥ etaiḥ saṃyutā ityuddeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of what sort are these? They are accompanied by <s>varṣābhū</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s>, and <s>mokṣaka</s>: <s>varṣābhū</s> is <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>vṛṣa</s> is <s>vāsaka</s>, and <s>mokṣaka</s> is known as the <s>mokhā</s> tree. The statement is that they are combined with these.
He states the procedure for making alkali, beginning with '<s>ānīya</s>.'
First, having brought the alkali trees mentioned before, having taken them from a forest tract,

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭān kusumaphalaśiphātvakpalāśairupetān kusumāni prasūnāni pratītāni śiphā mūlaṃ tvaktvacā pravālā nūtanapallavāḥ etaiḥ pañcāṅgāhvayair upetān saṃyutān ||
children.translated_text: of what sort? Provided with flowers, fruits, roots, bark, and shoots. Flowers are blossoms and are well known; <s>śiphā</s> means root; <s>tvak</s> is bark; <s>palāśa</s> means fresh sprouts. They are furnished with these, called the five parts.
Having made them into pieces, that is, into many fragments,

children.text: na kevalaṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ vipulataraśilāpiṣṭagātrātiśuṣkān kṛtvā vipulatarā ativistīrṇā yā śilā tasyāṃ piṣṭāni gātrāṇi yeṣāṃ te'śuṣkā nirasāḥ tānevaṃvidhān kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: and not merely into pieces: having made their bodies, ground on a very broad stone, exceedingly dry. That is, having made them such that their limbs have been ground on an extensive stone and are dry, without sap.

children.text: punastāneva ca tilānāṃ kāṇḍairnālaiḥ saha dagdhvā ||
children.translated_text: Then, having burned those very things together with sesame stalks and stems,

children.text: punaḥ karisurabhihayāmbhobhiḥ hastigo'śvānāṃ mūtrairāsrāvya āplutya tadbhasma tyaktvā vastrair jalaṃ grāhyamiti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: again one should moisten and drench that ash with the urines of elephant, cow, and horse. After discarding the ash, the liquid should be taken through cloths; this is to be supplied.

children.text: tajjalaṃ mṛduśikhini komalāgnau pacet kena vaṃśapākena vaṃśānāṃ samavahnitvāt ||
children.translated_text: That liquid should be cooked over a gentle flame, a soft fire. With what? By cooking with bamboo fuel, because bamboos give an even fire.
He states the sign that the alkali-liquid has been cooked, beginning with '<s>tad</s>.'

children.text: tajjalaṃ kṣārapānīyaṃ śuṣyamāṇaṃ sat niścitaṃ yadā sabāṣpabudbudān vidhatte saha bāṣpeṇa jalātyayadhūmena vartante ye budbudāstān tadā kṣāro niṣpanno jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that liquid, the alkaline water, while drying up, certainly produces bubbles with vapor, bubbles accompanied by steam, the smoke that marks the passing away of the water, then the alkali should be known to be completed.

children.text: punastadā tryūṣaṇaṃ śuṇṭhīmaricapippalyaḥ hiṅgu rāmaṭhaṃ gandhakaṃ lelītakaṃ punaḥ kṣāratrayaṃ sarjikāyavāgrajaṭaṅkaṇāhvayaṃ lavaṇāni ṣaṭ saindhavādīni bhūḥ tuvarī khagaṃ kāsīsaṃ etāni kṣipet etatkṣāreṇārdreṇa saha miśraṃ kāryamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should add <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, namely dry ginger, black pepper, and long pepper; asafoetida; <s>rāmaṭha</s>; sulfur, that is, <s>lelītaka</s>; again the three alkalis called <s>sarjikā</s>, <s>yavāgraja</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>; the six salts beginning with rock salt; <s>bhū</s>, that is, <s>tuvarī</s>; and <s>khaga</s>, that is, <s>kāsīsa</s>. The meaning is that these are to be mixed together with this moist alkali.

children.text: tathā ca dravyāṇi tryūṣaṇādīni saṃmiśrya ekīkṛtya nivṛtya ca saṃmardya śastrakaṭorikāpuṭe lohamayapātrasaṃpuṭe vyavasthitaṃ saptadināni dhānyagataṃ kasyaciddhānyasya madhyagataṃ sthāpayet kutra bhūtale pṛthivyā āsthāne tato'nantaraṃ tatsiddhaṃ rasajāraṇādikaṃ prati prayojyaṃ etadbiḍarūpaṃ rasajāraṇādiṣu praśastamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And so, having combined the substances beginning with <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> and made them one, and having repeatedly pounded them, one should place the mixture in a lidded iron vessel, an iron container, and keep it for seven days within grain, in the middle of some grain, on the ground, in a place on the earth. After that, once accomplished, it is to be used for the digestion of <s>rasa</s> and the like. The meaning is that this, in the form of <s>biḍa</s>, is excellent for the digestion of <s>rasa</s> and similar operations.
He states the alkali procedure for <s>jāraṇa</s>, beginning with '<s>jambīra</s>.'

children.text: kṣārā uktavṛkṣodbhavāḥ nitarām atiśayena garbhadrutijāraṇe rasāntargrāsajāraṇe śastā utkṛṣṭā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: The alkalis produced from the trees already stated are very, indeed exceedingly, effective for melting in the womb and digestion, that is, for digesting a mouthful inside the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: kutaḥ jambīrabījapūrakacāṅgerīvetasāmlasaṃyogāt jambīraḥ pratītaḥ bījapūrako mātuluṅgaḥ cāṅgerī amlapatrikā vetasāmlaṃ cukrakaṃ eṣāṃ yo rasastasya saṃyogāt etairbhāvitāḥ kṣārā biḍavatkāryakarā iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why? Because of conjunction with the acids of <s>jambīra</s>, <s>bījapūraka</s>, <s>cāṅgerī</s>, and cane-sour juice. <s>Jambīra</s> is well known; <s>bījapūraka</s> is citron; <s>cāṅgerī</s> is the sour-leaved plant; <s>vetasāmla</s> is <s>cukraka</s>. The sense is that alkalis impregnated with their juice act like <s>biḍa</s>.
He states the application of <s>biḍa</s> to <s>rasa</s>, beginning with '<s>biḍam</s>.'

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ sūtasya rasasyāṣṭamāṃśena pūrvanirmitaṃ viḍaṃ adharottaraṃ adha uparibhāgaṃ ca dattvā evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa jāraṇaṃ kuryāt punaḥ kramyate aneneti kramo biḍarūpaḥ tatkramaḥ paraṃparā tasmāt agniṃ vivardhayet karmakṛt ityadhyāhāraḥ vāraṃvāraṃ biḍasaṃprayogādagnirvardhate ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning, first, having placed the previously prepared <s>biḍa</s> with one-eighth part of the <s>sūta</s>, that is, of the <s>rasa</s>, below and above, on the lower and upper parts, one should perform <s>jāraṇa</s> in this way, by this procedure. Again, that by which one proceeds is a <s>krama</s>, and it has the form of <s>biḍa</s>; its sequence is a succession. Therefore the practitioner should increase the fire. By repeated application of <s>biḍa</s>, the fire increases.
That moon shines in the sky with brightness when the cloud has disappeared;
in the same way, here too, by relying on that, it is distinguished among human beings.
By the <s>jāraṇa</s> of well-prepared <s>biḍa</s>, metals, and the like, in the case of <s>rasa</s>,
the production of yellow and other colors is called <s>rañjana</s> (coloring).
Thus the definition.
He states the particular shade of mica with the words beginning '<s>jīrṇābhraka</s>.'

children.text: rasendro yadā jīrṇābhro bhavati tadā ghanānurūpiṇīṃ jīrṇābhrasamavarṇāṃ chāyāṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: When <s>rasendra</s> has become one in which mica is digested, then it displays a shade corresponding to the cloudlike substance, the same color as the digested mica.

children.text: kṛṣṇe jīrṇe kṛṣṇāṃ rakte'bhre jīrṇe raktāṃ pīte pītāṃ tathā site śubhre sitāṃ evaṃ caturvidhāṃ chāyāṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: When black mica is digested it displays a black shade; when red mica is digested, a red one; with yellow, a yellow one; and likewise with white, bright mica, a white one. Thus it displays a fourfold shade.

children.text: punardvayostrayāṇāṃ vā caturṇāṃ saṃkare melāpe sati dvitricaturṇām anurūpiṇīṃ chāyāṃ darśayatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, when there is a mixture, a combination, of two, three, or four of them, it displays a shade corresponding to those two, three, or four. This is the meaning.
He states the specific color produced through the conjunction of mica, with the words beginning '<s>kṛṣṇa</s>.'

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakeṇa jīrṇena raso balavān bhavet tu punaḥ asitarāgaiḥ kṛṣṇarāgairyujyate ||
children.translated_text: With black mica digested in it, the <s>rasa</s> becomes powerful, and moreover it is joined with dark colors, with black tints.

children.text: tathā śvetena śvetai rāgair yujyate raktena raktaiḥ pītena pītaiḥ kapilāgnerdivyasyāpi sarvasyādarśanarūpaṃ kṣayakarasya balairdravyāṇāṃ tādṛśo varṇo rasavarṇato varṇakovidairjñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, with white it is joined with white colors; with red, with red colors; and with yellow, with yellow colors. Experts in color should understand such a color of the substances, according to the color of the <s>rasa</s>, even in the case of tawny, fiery, bright, and other substances whose forms are not all plainly visible and whose powers cause reduction.
He states praise of colored <s>rasa</s>, with the words beginning '<s>atha</s>.'

children.text: athānantaraṃ rasaḥ rasendro yadā vakṣyamāṇaiḥ śvetādibhiḥ rāgaiḥ rajyate tadā nijakarme varṇaṃ svakīyameva svābhāvikaṃ rūpaṃ na jahāti na tyajati punastaireva rāgaiḥ nirṇikto raktaḥ san rañjanaṃ kurute rāgadāyī bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: Now, thereafter, when the <s>rasa</s>, <s>rasendra</s>, is colored by the white and other colors that will be described, then in its own operation it does not abandon its color, its own natural form. Again, being tinged and colored by those very colors, it performs coloring; that is, it becomes a giver of color.

children.text: tathā no rakto na rañjanaṃ kurute avidyamānatvānniṣedhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, if it is not colored, it does not perform coloring; the negation is because the coloring is absent.
He states the rule for <s>rasa</s> when mica-essence and the like are combined with it, with the words beginning '<s>balam</s>.'
Strength resides in mica-essence; that is, through union with mica-essence the <s>rasa</s> obtains strength.

children.text: punastīkṣṇe lohabhede jāraṇarāgā jāraṇena tīkṣṇasthā rāgāḥ pratiṣṭhitā bhavantītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, in <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, a kind of iron, the colors connected with <s>jāraṇa</s> are established; that is, by <s>jāraṇa</s> the colors residing in <s>tīkṣṇa</s> become fixed.

children.text: sāraṇamatha nāgavaṅgābhyām iti nāgavaṅgābhyāṃ duḥsaraṇaṃ sāraṇadravyaṃ sarata iti ||
children.translated_text: As for '<s>sāraṇa</s> with lead and tin,' by lead and tin there is a difficult-to-move <s>sāraṇa</s> substance; it is so called because it moves or makes movement possible.
He states that <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is the cause of everything, with the words beginning '<s>krāmati</s>.'

children.text: tīkṣṇena lohabhedena rasaḥ krāmati krāmaṇaṃ vidadhāti punas tīkṣṇena kṛtvā grāsaḥ kṣaṇādalpakālato jīryate jāraṇam āpnoti punarhemnaḥ suvarṇasya yonirutpattisthānaṃ tīkṣṇamasti punaḥ rāgān rañjanabhāvān tīkṣṇena kṛtvā raso gṛhṇāti svasmin rāgān dadhātītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, a kind of iron, the <s>rasa</s> advances and effects penetration. Again, when <s>tīkṣṇa</s> has been used, the morsel is digested in a moment, in a short time, and attains <s>jāraṇa</s>. Again, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is the womb, the place of origin, of gold. And again, through <s>tīkṣṇa</s> the <s>rasa</s> takes on colors and coloring states; it holds colors within itself. This is the meaning.
He states the superior qualities of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> through conjunction with cinnabar, with the words beginning '<s>tad api</s>.'

children.text: api niścayena tat tīkṣṇaṃ daradena hiṅgulena hataṃ māritaṃ vā mākṣikena svarṇamākṣikena ravisahitaṃ tāmrasaṃyutaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ hataṃ māritaṃ punarvāsanayā vāsanauṣadhena vāsitaṃ paribhāvitaṃ ghanavad abhravat cāryaṃ jāryaṃ ca satvābhravat nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: Indeed, that <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, killed or incinerated with <s>darada</s>, that is, cinnabar, or else <s>tīkṣṇa</s> killed with <s>mākṣika</s>, namely gold-mākṣika, and accompanied by <s>ravi</s>, that is, copper, and again impregnated and treated with a perfuming drug, is to be made to consume and to be digested like <s>ghana</s>, like mica, and like mica-essence, and not otherwise.
He states these substances as comparable to <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, with the words beginning '<s>kānta</s>.'

children.text: rasarañjane rasendre rāgakarmaṇi kāntaṃ cumbakapāṣāṇotthaṃ lohaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ veti samuccaye tīkṣṇaṃ lohabhedo vā kāñcīṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ vā vajrasasyakādīnāṃ vajrasasyakāvādiryeṣāṃ te teṣāṃ hīrakacapalādīnāṃ ekatamaṃ tanmadhyādekatamaṃ sarvaṃ vā atrābhīṣṭaśabdasya pratyekaṃ saṃbandhaḥ hīrakādīni ratnāni sasyakādyā upadhātavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For coloring <s>rasa</s>, for the color-operation in <s>rasendra</s>, <s>kānta</s>, the iron produced from lodestone, is best; or, with the sense of inclusion, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, a kind of iron, or <s>kāñcī</s>, or gold-mākṣika, or one among diamond, <s>sasyaka</s>, and similar substances, that is, one among diamond, <s>capala</s>, and the like. The word 'desired' is connected separately with each item. Diamond and the rest are gems; <s>sasyaka</s> and the rest are secondary metals.

children.text: vā rasarañjane ayameva saṃkaraḥ sarveṣāṃ kāntādīnāṃ melāpaḥ sarvatrābhīṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, in the coloring of <s>rasa</s>, this very mixture, the combination of all substances such as <s>kānta</s>, is desired everywhere.
He states what will be described in relation to each particular transformation, with the words beginning '<s>balam</s>.'
The knowers of metals, the physicians of <s>rasa</s>, declare this.

children.text: iti kiṃ kuṭile balaṃ abhyadhikaṃ sarvādhikaṃ punastīkṣṇe'bhyadhiko rāgaḥ rañjanaṃ tu punaḥ pannage nāge'bhyadhikaṃ snehaḥ snigdhatvaṃ tu punaḥ rāgasnehabalāni trīṇyevoktāni kamale tāmre kuṭilatīkṣṇapannagānāṃ jāraṇādrase yathā balarāgasnehā bhavanti tathaikatāmrajāraṇāt trayo bhavantītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is meant? In <s>kuṭila</s> there is greater strength, indeed the greatest; again, in <s>tīkṣṇa</s> there is greater color. Coloring, however, and again unctuousness, are greater in <s>pannaga</s>, that is, lead. Thus the three, color, unctuousness, and strength, have been stated. In lotus-like copper, just as strength, color, and unctuousness arise in <s>rasa</s> from the digestion of <s>kuṭila</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>pannaga</s>, so from the digestion of copper alone all three arise. This is the meaning.
He states the means for binding <s>rasa</s>, with the words beginning '<s>sarvaiḥ</s>.'

children.text: biḍayogena pūrvoktena jīrṇo jāraṇamāpanno rasarājo bandhamupayāti bandhanamādatte ||
children.translated_text: The king of <s>rasa</s>, having been digested, having attained <s>jāraṇa</s>, by means of the previously stated conjunction with <s>biḍa</s>, attains binding; it takes on fixation.

children.text: kaiḥ saha jīrṇaḥ ebhiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ sarvair lohairdhātubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With what has it been digested? With all these previously mentioned irons or metals.
Of what kind? Killed by <s>mākṣika</s>, incinerated with gold-mākṣika.
And again of what kind? Melted, liquefied, in the womb, in the belly of the <s>rasa</s>.
He states the procedure for the killing of the metals that are going to be mentioned, beginning with '<s>tālaka</s>.'

children.text: vaṅgaśastrādīn vaṅgaṃ trapuṣaṃ śastraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ te ādiryeṣāṃ te tān ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Vaṅga-śastra</s> and the rest' means those whose first members are <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), <s>trapuṣa</s> (tin), and <s>śastra</s>, the sharp metal.

children.text: kābhiḥ saha puṭo vahet tālakadaradaśilābhiḥ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ śilā manaḥśilā tābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With what should one carry out the <s>puṭa</s> (closed heating)? With <s>tālaka</s>, <s>darada</s>, and <s>śilā</s>: <s>tālaka</s> is yellow orpiment, <s>darada</s> is cinnabar, and <s>śilā</s> is realgar; with these.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭābhiḥ snehakṣārāmlalavaṇasahitābhiḥ snehaḥ tailaṃ kaṅguṇitumbinyādīnāṃ kṣāraḥ svarjikādiḥ amlaṃ jambīrādi lavaṇāni saindhavādīni etaiḥ sahitābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of these substances? They are accompanied by oils, alkalis, acids, and salts: oil is that of <s>kaṅguṇī</s>, <s>tumbinī</s>, and the like; alkali is <s>svarjikā</s> and the like; acid is citron and the like; and the salts are rock salt and the like. They are accompanied by these.

children.text: ekadhātuto dvādaśāṃśād ārabhya yāvatsamakadviguṇatriguṇabhāgāḥ samāpyante tāvatpuṭo vahediti vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The explanation is this: beginning from a twelfth part relative to one metal and continuing until equal, double, and triple portions are completed, one should carry out the <s>puṭa</s> heating.
He states what is to be done with a metal that has been heated in the <s>puṭa</s>, beginning with '<s>rakta</s>.'

children.text: uktadhāturgarbhitaṃ rasaṃ raktasnehaniṣekaiḥ rakto raktavargaḥ snehaḥ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ anayorniṣekāḥ siñcanāni taiḥ śeṣaṃ dhātuvarjitaṃ kuryāt iyaṃ rasasya kṛṣṭiḥ rasasya guṇākarṣaṇaṃ punariyaṃ kṛṣṭiḥ rasendraṃ indragopanibhaṃ kurute atiriktavarṇaṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: One should make the previously stated metal leave the <s>rasa</s> in which it has been placed by sprinklings of red substances and oils. '<s>Rakta</s>' is the red group; oil is that of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the like; the sprinklings are pourings with these two. One should leave the residue without the metal. This is the <s>kṛṣṭi</s> of <s>rasa</s>, the drawing out of the qualities of the <s>rasa</s>. Again, this <s>kṛṣṭi</s> makes <s>rasendra</s> like an indragopa insect; it gives it an exceedingly red color.

children.text: kutaḥ cāraṇajāraṇamātrāt punaḥ puṭitadhātūnāṃ cāraṇaṃ ca jāraṇaṃ jīrṇaṃkaraṇaṃ ca tanmātrāt vā cāraṇasya dravyasya jāraṇaṃ tanmātrāt ubhayoḥ pakṣayoreka evārthaḥ paramuktiviśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why? Merely from <s>cāraṇa</s> and <s>jāraṇa</s>: that is, from the <s>cāraṇa</s> of the metals heated again in the <s>puṭa</s> and from <s>jāraṇa</s>, making them digested; or from the <s>jāraṇa</s> of the substance used for <s>cāraṇa</s> alone. In both interpretations the meaning is the same; only the manner of statement differs.
He states the praise of copper as the chief material, beginning with '<s>athavā</s>.'

children.text: athaveti vidhānāntare kevalaṃ śuddhaṃ vānyasaṃyogena varjitaṃ amalaṃ jātapūrvaśodhanaṃ triguṇaṃ cīrṇajīrṇaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ pūrvaṃ cīrṇaṃ cāraṇamāptaṃ paścājjīrṇaṃ jāraṇamāpannaṃ evaṃbhūtaṃ tāmraṃ sūtaṃ lākṣārasasannibhaṃ alaktakaprabhaṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Athavā</s>' introduces another procedure. The meaning is that one should make copper, either entirely pure and free from combination with another substance or spotless because it has already undergone purification, undergo <s>cāraṇa</s> and <s>jāraṇa</s> to three times the quantity: first <s>cīrṇa</s>, having obtained <s>cāraṇa</s>, and afterward <s>jīrṇa</s>, having obtained <s>jāraṇa</s>. Copper in this condition makes the <s>sūta</s> resemble lac-dye, with the lustre of red lac.
He states another procedure, beginning with '<s>rakta</s>.'

children.text: raktagaṇena dāḍimakiṃśukabandhūkādinā pūrvoktena galitaṃ yat paśujalaṃ gomūtraṃ tena bhāvitā yās tāpyagandhakamanaḥśilās tāsāṃ madhyād ekena tāpyena svarṇamākṣikena vā gandhakena vā śilayā vāpitamṛtaṃ sat kamalaṃ tāmraṃ rasaṃ rañjayati rāgaṃ dadātītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the red group previously mentioned, such as pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and <s>bandhūka</s>, there is strained animal water, namely cow urine. <s>Tāpya</s>, sulphur, and realgar, prepared with that, are meant. When the dead <s>kamala</s>, copper, has been impregnated with one from among these, either <s>tāpya</s>, that is gold-pyrites, sulphur, or <s>śilā</s>, it colors the <s>rasa</s>; that is, it gives it redness.
He states the sulphur and the other substances that are authorized for coloration.

children.text: tatra gandhakaḥ kīdṛśaṃ rāgaṃ dadāti tatsvarūpamāha bāhya ityādi ||
children.translated_text: There he explains what kind of coloration sulphur gives, describing its nature with the words beginning '<s>bāhya</s>.'

children.text: gandhakarāgo bāhyo bahirbhavaḥ punarmanaḥśilātāle manaḥśilā manohvā tālaṃ haritālaṃ tāvubhe vilulitarāge cañcalarāge punar mākṣikasatvarasakau svarṇamākṣikasatvakharparikau dvāveva rañjane rasarāge śastau gandhakamanaḥśilātālebhyaḥ pradhānau atyadhikāvityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The color produced by sulphur is external, arising on the outside. Again, realgar and orpiment, that is <s>manaḥśilā</s>, also called <s>manohvā</s>, and <s>tāla</s>, yellow orpiment, both have an unstable color, a wavering color. But the essences of <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>rasaka</s>, namely gold-pyrites essence and calamine, these two alone are praised for coloring, for the color of <s>rasa</s>; they are chief, far superior to sulphur, realgar, and orpiment. This is the meaning.
He states what is to be done with the two chief substances, copper and calamine, beginning with '<s>kramavṛttau</s>.'

children.text: kramavṛttau ravirasakau saṃśuddhau viśeṣavidhānena śodhitau vā uttamajātīyau mūkamūṣikādhmātau andhamūṣāyāṃ dhmātau vahniyogīkṛtau kāryau etattriguṇaṃ yathā syāttathā cīrṇo jīrṇaśca sūtaḥ hemanibho jāyate etena cāraṇamāpannaḥ paścāttenaiva jāraṇām āpanno rasaḥ svarṇaprabho bhavedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>ravi</s> and <s>rasaka</s>, copper and calamine, used in due sequence, should be thoroughly purified, or purified by a special procedure, or of the best kind, and should be smelted in a closed crucible, heated in a blind crucible and brought into contact with fire. When the <s>sūta</s> has undergone <s>cāraṇa</s> and then <s>jāraṇa</s> so that this is threefold, it becomes like gold. The meaning is that <s>rasa</s> which has first obtained <s>cāraṇa</s> and then, by that very material, has obtained <s>jāraṇa</s>, becomes golden in appearance.
He states the use of mica, beginning with '<s>atha</s>.'

children.text: atha rasakayogānantaraṃ kṛṣṇavarṇābhrakacūrṇaṃ śyāmavarṇābhrakarajaḥ tathā ravirasakavidhānena kharparakeṇa sahitaṃ puṭitaṃ sat sakalaṃ samastaṃ raktaṃ bhavet tadraktabhūtamabhraṃ triguṇaṃ yathā syāttathā cīrṇaḥ cāraṇamāpannas tato jīrṇo jāraṇamāpannaśca san sūto hemadrutisannibhaḥ svarṇadravasadṛśo bhaved ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, after the procedure with <s>rasaka</s>, black-colored mica powder, that is dark-colored mica dust, when heated in a <s>puṭa</s> together with calamine according to the procedure for copper and <s>rasaka</s>, becomes entirely red. That mica, once red, when it has undergone <s>cāraṇa</s> three times and then has become <s>jīrṇa</s>, having obtained <s>jāraṇa</s>, makes <s>sūta</s> resemble molten gold, that is, like liquid gold. This is the meaning.
Now he states the killing of gold, beginning with '<s>triguṇena</s>.'

children.text: tu punaḥ triguṇena mākṣikeṇa svarṇatriguṇitena tāpyena yatkanakaṃ mṛtaṃ tatkanakaṃ indragopako varṣākālīno raktavarṇo jīvaviśeṣaḥ tadvannibhā dīptiryasya tadindragopanibhaṃ bhavatīti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, gold killed with three times as much <s>mākṣika</s>, that is with <s>tāpya</s> three times the quantity of the gold, has a brilliance like an indragopa insect, a red creature of the rainy season; the remainder is to be supplied: it becomes like an indragopa.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ kanakaṃ mṛtaṃ rasakatālayutaṃ rasakaṃ kharparaṃ tālaṃ haritālaṃ tābhyāṃ yutaṃ miśritaṃ sat yanmṛtaṃ pañcatvamāptamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of killed gold? Gold killed while joined with <s>rasaka</s> and <s>tāla</s>: <s>rasaka</s> is calamine and <s>tāla</s> is yellow orpiment. The meaning is that it has been mixed with these two and, being killed, has reached the state of death.

children.text: punaḥ paṭusahitaṃ lavaṇamiśritaṃ punar haṇḍikayā bhājanena pakvaṃ vahnipuṭitaṃ tadapi pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: Again, when combined with <s>paṭu</s>, that is mixed with salt, and then cooked in a pot, heated by fire, it too is as before.

children.text: mṛtakanakacūrṇaṃ sūtavare pārade triguṇaṃ cīrṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ cāritaṃ jāritaṃ ca sat sūto drutahemanibho bhavet galitasvarṇaprabha ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the powder of killed gold has been made <s>cīrṇa</s> and <s>jīrṇa</s> in excellent <s>sūta</s>, mercury, in a quantity three times as great, that is when it has been subjected to <s>cāraṇa</s> and <s>jāraṇa</s>, the <s>sūta</s> becomes like molten gold, with the lustre of melted gold. This is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ rañjito rasaḥ sarvalohāni dhātūni kṛtrimākṛtrimāni navavidhāni rañjati svarṇarūpāṇi karotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> colored in this way colors all metals, the artificial and the natural metals, the nine kinds; that is, it makes them have the form of gold.
He states the progressively greater excellence of all metallic essences, beginning with '<s>patra</s>.'

children.text: patrādaṣṭaguṇaṃ satvaṃ abhrapatre jīrṇe sati rase yo guṇastasmādaṣṭaguṇo guṇastatsatve ityarthaḥ punaḥ sattvāt drutistaddravarūpā aṣṭaguṇā punardruter bījaṃ dhātūparasasaṃyogajanitaṃ pūrvopavarṇitaṃ tadaṣṭaguṇaṃ tataḥ sarvotkṛṣṭatvādbījaṃ jārayennatvanyat ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sattva</s> is eight times the leaf: when the mica leaf has been digested, the quality that exists in the <s>rasa</s> is eightfold in its <s>sattva</s>; this is the meaning. Again, from the <s>sattva</s> comes <s>druti</s>, that liquid form, eightfold; and again, from the <s>druti</s> comes the <s>bīja</s>, produced by the conjunction of metals, secondary minerals, and <s>rasa</s>, already described before. That is eightfold. Therefore, because the <s>bīja</s> is superior to all, one should digest the <s>bīja</s>, not anything else.
It is like the moon in radiance and like the sun in brilliance.
It is also like the maker of night and day, and it does not dwell together with the wicked.
When, by a special quenching, its color becomes like that,
soft and fit for varied processing, that is called <s>bīja</s>.
Thus ends the definition.
He praises the <s>bīja</s>, beginning with '<s>iti</s>.'

children.text: ityuktavidhānena rakto'pi rasendro bījena vinā karmakṛnna bhavati bījenaiva karmakārī syādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the procedure thus stated, even when <s>rasendra</s> has become red, it does not perform its operation without <s>bīja</s>; it becomes capable of acting only through <s>bīja</s>. This is the meaning.

children.text: tadbījaṃ dvividhaṃ dviprakāraṃ pītasitaṃ ekaṃ pītaṃ aparaṃ sitaṃ śvetaṃ svarṇarūpyakriyāyogyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>bīja</s> is twofold, of two kinds, yellow and white: one is yellow, the other white, suitable for operations involving gold and silver. This is the meaning.

children.text: tadbījaṃ siddhaṃ sarvalakṣaṇopetaṃ rase pārade niyojyaṃ nāsiddhamiti ||
children.translated_text: That <s>bīja</s>, when perfected and endowed with all the marks, should be applied to <s>rasa</s>, mercury; not an unperfected one.
Beginning with '<s>tasya</s>.'

children.text: tasya bījasya viśuddhiḥ śodhanaṃ bahudhā bahuprakāraiḥ kṛtvā rasoparasadhātūnāṃ bahuvidhatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Its purification, that is, the cleansing of that <s>bīja</s>, should be done in many ways, because <s>rasa</s>s, secondary minerals, and metals are of many kinds.

children.text: kaiḥ kṛtvā gaganarasalohacūrṇaiḥ gaganamabhraṃ rasā vaikrāntādayo'ṣṭau vakṣyamāṇāḥ uparasā gandhakādayaḥ lohā dhātavaḥ teṣāṃ cūrṇāni taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With what? With powders of <s>gagana</s>, <s>rasa</s>, and metal: <s>gagana</s> is mica; the <s>rasa</s>s are the eight beginning with <s>vaikrānta</s> that will be stated; the secondary minerals are those beginning with sulfur; the metals are the <s>dhātu</s>s. With their powders, then.

children.text: ca punaḥ tair gaganarasoparasalohacūrṇair aśuddhaiḥ śuddhivarjitaistadbījaṃ na śudhyate śuddhihīnaṃ syāt kāraṇānurūpaṃ kāryamitinyāyāt ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, with those powders of <s>gagana</s>, <s>rasa</s>, secondary minerals, and metals when they are impure, devoid of purification, that <s>bīja</s> is not purified; it remains without purity, according to the maxim that the effect conforms to its cause.
He states the effect of impure <s>bīja</s>, beginning with '<s>yaḥ</s>.'

children.text: punarviśeṣeṇa yaḥ saṃskārakṛdetairgaganādyair aśuddhaiḥ kṛtvā rasasya karma kurute tasya puruṣasya rasaḥ pārado 'vyāpako 'saraṇaśīlo bhavet pataṅgī ūrdhvagāmī ca bhavet yantrasyādhobhāge na tiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, in particular, the person who performs the processing and carries out the operation of <s>rasa</s> with these impure substances beginning with <s>gagana</s>: his <s>rasa</s>, mercury, becomes non-pervasive and not disposed to move; it also becomes upward-flying, meaning that it does not remain in the lower part of the apparatus.

children.text: ete vakṣyamāṇā aṣṭau rasāḥ rasasaṃjñakāḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: These following eight are to be regarded as <s>rasa</s>s, substances bearing the name <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: ete ke vaikrāntakāntasasyakamākṣikavimalādridaradarasakāś ceti vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ kāntaṃ cumbakotthaṃ sasyakaṃ capalaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ vimalā raupyamākṣikaṃ adri śilājatu daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ rasakaḥ kharparikaḥ ete rasasaṃjñikā jñeyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Which are they? <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, <s>adri</s>, <s>darada</s>, and <s>rasaka</s>. <s>Vaikrānta</s> is a mineral born in diamond-ground; <s>kānta</s> is produced from magnet; <s>sasyaka</s> is <s>capala</s>; <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>; <s>vimalā</s> is silver pyrite; <s>adri</s> is <s>śilājatu</s>; <s>darada</s> is cinnabar; and <s>rasaka</s> is <s>kharparika</s>. These should be known as substances bearing the name <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: tathā eṣāṃ satvāni sārāṇi rasāyanāni jarāvyādhināśanāni syuriti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise their <s>sattva</s>s, their essences, are <s>rasāyana</s>s, elixirs that destroy old age and disease.
He names the substances called <s>uparasa</s>, beginning with '<s>gandhaka</s>.'
The following are to be called <s>uparasa</s>s.

children.text: kimidaṃ gandhakagairikaśilālakṣitikhecaram iti gandhakaṃ pratītaṃ gairikaṃ dhātugairikaṃ śilā manohvā ālaṃ haritālaṃ kṣitiḥ sphaṭikā khecaraṃ kāsīsaṃ etat sarvamiti ca punaḥ añjanaṃ nīlāñjanaṃ punaḥ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ ityaṣṭau uparasasaṃjñakā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What are they? Sulfur, red ochre, <s>śilā</s>, <s>āla</s>, <s>kṣiti</s>, and <s>khecara</s>: sulfur is well known; red ochre is mineral ochre; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>; <s>āla</s> is orpiment; <s>kṣiti</s> is crystal; <s>khecara</s> is green vitriol. All this is meant. And again there is collyrium, namely blue collyrium; and again <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>viraṅga</s>. These eight are called <s>uparasa</s>s. This is the meaning.
<s>Śikhi</s> and <s>śaśin</s>, namely gold and silver, are called the noble metals, that is, they bear the designation noble metal.
He names those called base metals, beginning with '<s>tāmra</s>.'

children.text: tāmrāratīkṣṇakāntābhrasatvalohānīti tāmraṃ nepālakaṃ āraṃ rājarītiḥ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ kāntaṃ cumbakodbhavaṃ abhrasatvaṃ gaganasāraṃ lohaṃ muṇḍaṃ etānīti punarvaṅganāgau ete pūtisaṃjñakāḥ kathitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The metals copper, <s>āra</s>, steel, magnet, mica-essence, and iron: copper is <s>nepālaka</s>; <s>āra</s> is <s>rājarīti</s>; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is steel; <s>kānta</s> is produced from magnet; mica-essence is the essence of <s>gagana</s>; <s>loha</s> is wrought iron. These, and again tin and lead, are said to be called <s>pūti</s> metals.
For those called <s>pūti</s> metals, purification, the proper removal of impurities, is to be performed.
He names the categories of salts and alkalis, beginning with '<s>sauvarcala</s>.'

children.text: etāni vakṣyamāṇāni lavaṇasaṃjñānyāhuḥ ācāryāḥ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The teachers say that the following are called salts; this is to be supplied.

children.text: kāni sauvarcalasaindhavakacūlikasāmudraromakabiḍānīti sauvarcalaṃ rucakaṃ saindhavaṃ maṇikamanthāhvayaṃ cūlikaṃ kācalavaṇaṃ sāmudraṃ kṣārābdhijaṃ romakaṃ pratītaṃ biḍaṃ lavaṇaviśeṣaḥ etānīti ||
children.translated_text: Which ones? <s>Sauvarcala</s>, rock salt, <s>kacūlika</s>, sea salt, <s>romaka</s>, and <s>biḍa</s>: <s>sauvarcala</s> is <s>rucaka</s>; rock salt is known as <s>maṇikamantha</s>; <s>cūlika</s> is glass-salt; sea salt is born from the alkaline ocean; <s>romaka</s> is well known; and <s>biḍa</s> is a particular kind of salt. These are meant.

children.text: punaḥ svarjī sarjikā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ yavakṣāraḥ pratītaḥ ete kṣārāḥ kṣārasaṃjñikāḥ rasakarmaṇi ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>svarjī</s>, <s>sarjikā</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>saubhāgya</s>, and the well-known <s>yavakṣāra</s>: these are alkalis, substances bearing the name alkali, in the operation of <s>rasa</s>; this is to be supplied.
He states the group that has dissolving power and is purifying, beginning with '<s>sūryāvarta</s>.'

children.text: sūryaṃ prati āvartako bhramaṇaṃ yasyetyevaṃvidhaḥ kadalī rambhā vandhyā phalarahitā karkoṭī kośātakī jālinī suradālī devadālī śigruḥ saubhāñjanaṃ vajrakando vadasūraṇakandaḥ nīrakaṇā jalapippalī kākamācī vāyasī iti gaṇaḥ śodhanadrāvaṇayogya iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūryāvarta</s>, so called because it turns toward the sun; <s>kadalī</s>, the plantain; <s>rambhā</s>; the barren one, fruitless; <s>karkoṭī</s>; <s>kośātakī</s>; <s>jālinī</s>; <s>suradālī</s>, <s>devadālī</s>; <s>śigru</s>; <s>saubhāñjana</s>; <s>vajrakanda</s>, that is, the tuber called <s>sūraṇa</s>; <s>nīrakaṇā</s>, water-pepper; and <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>vāyasī</s>: this group is suitable for purification and dissolution.
He states the procedure for purification and dissolution by the purifying and dissolving substances, beginning with '<s>āsām</s>.'

children.text: āsāṃ pūrvauṣadhīnāṃ madhyāt ekarasena ekasyā rasena rasoparasā vaikrāntādayo'ṣṭau rasāḥ gandhakādayo 'ṣṭāvuparasāḥ bahuśo'nekavāraṃ bhāvitā gharmapuṭitāḥ kāryāḥ punarlavaṇakṣārāmlabhāvitāśca lavaṇāni sauvarcalādīni ṣaṭ kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ amlā jambīrādayaḥ tairbahuvāraṃ bhāvitās tīvragharmapuṭitā rasoparasāḥ śudhyanti doṣavarjitā bhavanti punaste dhmātāḥ santaḥ satvāni svīyasārāṇi muñcanti tyajantīti ||
children.translated_text: Among these previously mentioned plants, the <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s should be repeatedly, many times, impregnated with a single juice, the juice of one of them: the eight <s>rasa</s>s beginning with <s>vaikrānta</s>, and the eight <s>uparasa</s>s beginning with sulfur, are to be treated with heating. Again they should be impregnated with salts, alkalis, and acids: the salts are the six beginning with <s>sauvarcala</s>, the alkalis are those beginning with <s>svarjikā</s>, and the acids are those beginning with citron. The <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s, when repeatedly impregnated with these and treated with strong heating, are purified and become free from defects. Then, when they are smelted, they release, that is, abandon, their <s>sattva</s>s, their own essences.
He states the purification of the <s>rasa</s>s in sequence, beginning with '<s>svinna</s>'.

children.text: sakṣārāmlairvaikrāntakaṃ svinnaṃ dolābhidhānena sveditaṃ kuryāt tat svinnaṃ vaikrāntaṃ haṭhāt prābalyāt dhmātaṃ sat dravati sāraṃ muñcati drutamātraṃ satvanirgamamātrameva śudhyati pūrvasaṃbandhāt dravati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrāntaka</s> should be made boiled together with alkalis and acids, that is, steamed by the procedure called <s>dolā</s>. That boiled <s>vaikrānta</s>, when smelted forcefully, through intensity, melts and releases its essence. As soon as it has melted, at the very moment when the <s>sattva</s> emerges, it is purified. Because of the preceding connection, it melts.
He states that, beginning with '<s>sasyaka</s>'.
<s>Sasyaka</s> too, and <s>capala</s> too, should be thoroughly impregnated with the red group, such as pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and <s>bandhūka</s>.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ sneharāgasaṃsiktaṃ snehaḥ kaṅguṇitumbunyādīnāṃ rāgo raktavarṇadravaḥ tābhyāṃ vahnau taptaṃ sasyakaṃ saṃsiktaṃ secitamiti ghṛtaiḥ saṃsiktaṃ komalaṃ bhāvanāyogyaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Of what sort? Saturated with oil and red dye: the oil is that of <s>kaṅguṇī</s>, <s>tumbunī</s>, and the like, and the dye is a red-colored liquid. With those two, <s>sasyaka</s> heated in fire should be sprinkled, meaning sprinkled with ghee; it becomes soft and fit for impregnation.
With how many repetitions should it be thoroughly impregnated? With seven, that is, seven in number.
After this it is applied in the operation, such as for <s>bīja</s> and the like.
He states that, beginning with '<s>kṣāraiḥ</s>'.

children.text: vimalaṃ raupyamākṣikaṃ ādau prathamaṃ kṣāraiḥ svarjikādibhiḥ snehaistailaiḥ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ bhāvitaṃ kuryāt paścādamlena jambīrādinā bhāvitaṃ kuryāt evaṃvidhaṃ kṛtaṃ sat śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vimala</s>, namely silver pyrite, should first be impregnated with alkalis such as <s>svarjikā</s> and with oils, the oils of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the like. Afterwards it should be impregnated with an acid such as citron. When it has been prepared in this way, it is purified.

children.text: tathā tenaiva vidhinā rasakaṃ kharparakaṃ śudhyati daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ caivaṃ mākṣikamapyeva śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, by that same procedure, <s>rasaka</s>, namely <s>kharparaka</s>, is purified; <s>darada</s>, that is, cinnabar, is also purified in this way, and <s>mākṣika</s> too is purified in just this way.
He states the purification of gold and silver, beginning with '<s>tanuḥ</s>'.
On the passage beginning with '<s>lavaṇa</s>'.

children.text: lavaṇāni sauvarcalādīni kṣārāḥ svarjikādayaḥ amlāḥ jambīrādayaḥ ravirarkaḥ snuhī sudhā tayoḥ kṣīrāṇi etaiḥ tanurapi sūkṣmamapi patraṃ dalaṃ sāralohākhyayoḥ iti śeṣaḥ liptaṃ dhmātaṃ sat bahuśo'nekavāraṃ nirguṇḍīrase saṃsiktaṃ śephālīdrave siñcitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: The salts are those beginning with <s>sauvarcala</s>; the alkalis are those beginning with <s>svarjikā</s>; the acids are those beginning with citron; <s>ravi</s> is <s>arka</s>; <s>snuhī</s> is <s>sudhā</s>; and their milks are meant. With these, even a thin leaf, a fine sheet, of those called noble metals should be smeared and smelted. Then it should be repeatedly, many times, sprinkled in the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, that is, drenched in the liquid of <s>śephālī</s>.

children.text: tarhi svarṇaṃ rūpyaṃ ca raktaṃ āraktachaviyutaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ caśabdācchudhyati ||
children.translated_text: Then gold and silver become red, meaning endowed with a reddish luster; and from the word 'and' it is understood that they are purified.
He states the purification of base metals, beginning with '<s>śudhyati</s>'.

children.text: nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ nirguṇḍīrasasekaiḥ śephālīrasaṃsecanaiḥ śudhyati nirdoṣo bhavati vaṅgaśca śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s>, lead, is purified by sprinklings with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice, by drenchings with <s>śephālī</s> juice; it becomes free from defects. And <s>vaṅga</s>, tin, is also purified.

children.text: evaṃ raviṇā tāmreṇa saha ghoṣo'pi kāṃsyamapi śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, together with <s>ravi</s>, copper, <s>ghoṣa</s>, that is, bronze, is also purified.

children.text: kativāraṃ secanaiḥ munibhiḥ saptasaṃkhyākaiḥ tanmūlarajaḥ nirguṇḍīśiphācūrṇaṃ tatpravāpaiḥ galiteṣu nāgavaṅgaravighoṣeṣu rajo nikṣepaṇaiśca catvāraḥ śudhyantīti ||
children.translated_text: With how many sprinklings? With seven, the number of sages. Its root-powder means powder of the root of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>; by throwings in of that, and by castings of the powder into melted lead, tin, copper, and bronze, the four are purified.
He states that, beginning with '<s>raktagaṇa</s>'.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ sārākhyaṃ raktagaṇagalitapaśujalabhāvitaṃ puṭitaṃ sat raktagaṇena saha galitaṃ militaṃ yat paśujalaṃ gomūtraṃ tena bhāvitaṃ tato vahnipuṭitaṃ sat rajyate rāgamāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tīkṣṇa</s>, called <s>sāra</s>, when treated by heat after being impregnated with animal liquid melted together with the red group, becomes colored. That is, it is impregnated with animal liquid, namely cow's urine, which has been melted and mixed with the red group; then, after being treated in a fire-pit, it takes on color.

children.text: punastīkṣṇaṃ kadalīśikhirasabhāvitapuṭitaṃ vā rambhācitrakarasabhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ tato vahnipuṭitaṃ ca sat tribhirvāraiḥ śudhyatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, when impregnated and heat-treated with the juice of plantain shoots, or when impregnated with the juices of <s>rambhā</s> and <s>citraka</s>, treated with heat, and then treated in a fire-pit, is purified by three repetitions. This is the meaning.
He states, in general terms, the purification and killing of all metals, beginning with '<s>sarva</s>'.

children.text: sarvo loho dhātuvargaḥ śudhyati mṛtaśca bhavati punaḥ rajyati ca ||
children.translated_text: Every metal, the class of metals, is purified, becomes killed, and again becomes colored.

children.text: kena bhṛśaṃ atyarthaṃ yathā syāttathā mākṣikadaradena tāpyahiṅgulena kṛtvā yo vāpaḥ galiteṣu loheṣu mākṣikadaradaprakṣepaṇaṃ tasmāt suragopasaṃnibha indragopasadṛśaḥ sarvo loho bhavet ||
children.translated_text: By what means? By a very strong casting with <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>darada</s>, that is, with <s>tāpya</s> and cinnabar: the casting is the throwing of <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>darada</s> into melted metals. From that, every metal becomes like <s>suragopa</s>, like an <s>indragopa</s> insect.

children.text: vā śulbaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣikadaradavāpena suragopasannibhaṃ syāt vā gandhena gandhakavāpena mṛtamapyeva syādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or copper, by the casting of <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>darada</s>, becomes like <s>suragopa</s>; or, by the casting of sulfur, even when killed it becomes just so. This is the meaning.
It has constantly given happiness to the purified, and likewise to the wicked.
For those whose selves are impure, it is a maker of suffering, death, and also anger.
He praises the <s>sattva</s>s of those bearing the name <s>rasa</s>, beginning with '<s>vaikrāntam</s>'.

children.text: vaikrāntakāntasasyakamākṣikavimalādayaḥ śuddhā api dvandve na milanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, and the others, even when purified, do not combine in a pair.

children.text: vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ sasyakaścapalaḥ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ vimalā raupyamākṣikam ityādayo gandhakādayaścoparasaṃjñakā na milanti ekaśarīratāṃ nāpnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> is the mineral from diamond-ground; <s>kānta</s> is magnet; <s>sasyaka</s> is <s>capala</s>; <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>; <s>vimalā</s> is silver pyrite; and the others, together with sulfur and the rest called <s>uparasa</s>s, do not combine, that is, they do not attain a single body.
In what context? In <s>dvandva</s>, the union of the two.

children.text: punastān śuddhānapi rasaḥ sūto na grasati ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>rasa</s>, mercury, does not consume them, even though they are purified.
He states the predominance of <s>vaikrānta</s>, beginning with '<s>nāga</s>'.
<s>Vaikrāntaka</s> having this set of characteristics should be known.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ nāganāsikābhidhānaṃ nāgānāṃ phaṇināṃ nāsikā eva abhidhānaṃ saṃjñā yasya tat ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind is it? It bears the name <s>Nāganāsikā</s>: that is, its designation or name is literally the nose of nāgas, serpents.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ candrodakaṃ candramasaḥ sambandhi yadudakaṃ balaṃ tasmādevāmṛtaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what kind is it? It is <s>candrodaka</s>: the water connected with the moon is strength, and from that alone comes <s>amṛta</s>.

children.text: āptakāṭhinyaṃ prāptaṃ kāṭhinyaṃ yena pūrvametacca mṛdūtpannamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It has attained hardness, that by which hardness has been acquired. Previously, however, this had arisen soft; this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ rasavaikrāntaṃ rasasaṃjñakaṃ vaikrāntaṃ rasaṃ sūtaṃ badhnāti ||
children.translated_text: Such <s>rasavaikrānta</s>, the <s>vaikrānta</s> called a <s>rasa</s>, binds <s>rasa</s>, namely <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
By what means? By its own <s>sattva</s>, its own essence.
