He states the form of <s>vaikrānta</s>, beginning with the words '<s>nānā</s>'.

children.text: pūrvamupavarṇitaṃ vaikrāntaṃ nānāvidhasaṃsthānamasti nānāvidhamanekaprakāraṃ saṃsthānaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yasya tat saṃsthānaṃ vyañjanaṃ liṅgaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cihnamākṛtiḥ iti mādhavanidānaṃ sitāsitaraktapītavarṇatvān nānāvidhasaṃsthānam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The previously described <s>vaikrānta</s> has many kinds of configuration: that whose configuration, mark, is of many kinds. Configuration means indication, sign, mark, emblem, or shape, as in the <s>Mādhavanidāna</s>. Because it may be white, black, red, or yellow in color, it is said to have many kinds of configuration; this is the meaning.

children.text: punarnirjaraśikhariśikharasambhūtaṃ nirjarāṇāṃ devānāṃ yaḥ śikharī parvatastasya śikharaṃ śṛṅgaṃ tatra sambhūtam utpannam ||
children.translated_text: Again, it is produced on the summit of the mountain of the immortals: it arises on the summit, the peak, of that mountain belonging to the immortals, the gods.

children.text: nānāvidhasaṃsthānaṃ kutaḥ dhārodambhasi dhārābhirudanta unmattamambho yatra samaye tasmin varṣākāle śailodakaṃ śilāsaṃbandhi yadudakaṃ jalaṃ tat prāpya śreṣṭhaṃ tadaśma vaikrāntābhidhānaṃ nānāvarṇaṃ bhavati yataḥ śilodakasya nānāvidhatvam ||
children.translated_text: Why does it have many kinds of configuration? In the rainy season, when water is stirred up by streams, the excellent stone named <s>vaikrānta</s>, having obtained mountain water, that is, water connected with rock, becomes many-colored, because rock water is itself of many kinds.
He states the extraction of the <s>sattva</s> of <s>vaikrānta</s>, beginning with '<s>bhastre</s>'.

children.text: tadvaikrāntaṃ pañcamāhiṣasubaddhaṃ dadhidugdhājyamūtraśakṛdbhiḥ pañcasaṃkhyākair māhiṣaiḥ saha subaddhaṃ piṇḍākṛti kṛtaṃ sat bhastrādvayena khallayugmena haṭhato balāt dhmātavyam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>vaikrānta</s>, thoroughly combined with the five buffalo products, namely curd, milk, ghee, urine, and dung, and made into a lump, should be blown forcefully with two bellows and a pair of mortars.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā daśāṃśasarjikapaṭuṭaṅkaṇaguñjikākṣārān dattvā daśāṃśavibhāgena sarjikālavaṇasaubhāgyaraktikāyavakṣārān piṣṭavaikrānte kṣepyetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After doing what? After adding alkalis consisting of one-tenth parts of <s>sarjikā</s>, salt, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>guñjikā</s>, and <s>yavakṣāra</s>; that is, they should be put into the ground <s>vaikrānta</s> in a tenth-part proportion.
When it has been blown, what happens? He states this with the words beginning '<s>tad</s>'.
It releases <s>sattva</s>, its essence, in the form of sparks, like particles of fire.
Then that <s>sattva</s> becomes hard; that is, it is made hard.

children.text: tatsatvaṃ ākārato muktānikaraprāyaṃ mauktikarāśisadṛśaṃ syāt evaṃvidhaṃ satvaṃ kācaṃ adhivarjya dūrīkṛtya tat nirmalaṃ grāhyamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>sattva</s> should be like a cluster of pearls in shape, resembling a heap of pearls. Having removed the glassy slag and set it aside, that pure <s>sattva</s> should be taken; this is the meaning.
This is a pair of verses.
He states the use of the <s>sattva</s> of <s>vaikrānta</s>, beginning with '<s>rasa</s>'.

children.text: tadrasavaikrāntakaṃ sattvaṃ hemnā samaṃ svarṇena samabhāgaṃ dvandvānvitaṃ sat dvandvamelāpakauṣadhasahitaṃ sat evamamunā vidhānena milati rase iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>sattva</s> of <s>rasavaikrāntaka</s>, equal in measure to gold and joined with <s>dvandva</s>, that is, accompanied by the drugs that unite the pair, combines with <s>rasa</s> by this procedure; the words 'with <s>rasa</s>' are to be supplied.

children.text: punastena satvena saha ghanasatvamabhrasāraṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ nirvāhitaṃ sat tenobhayasatvasaṃyogena rasaḥ sūto bandhamupayāti bandhanamāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>ghana-sattva</s>, the essence of mica, has been fully processed together with that <s>sattva</s>, through the conjunction of both essences <s>rasa</s>, mercury, comes to binding and attains fixation.
He states the procedure for extracting <s>sattva</s>, beginning with '<s>vajra</s>'.

children.text: dṛḍhāṅgārair iti dṛḍhakathanāt khadirādīnāṃ pūrvoktatvādbhastrādvayena ca dhmātā satī vajrābhrakāntasasyakamākṣikaprabhṛtisakaladhātūnāṃ vajrasaṃjñakaṃ yadabhraṃ tadvajrābhraṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ sasyakaṃ capalā mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ itiprabhṛtayaḥ sakaladhātavaḥ sarvoparasāsteṣāṃ piṇḍī satvaṃ pātayati ||
children.translated_text: Since firm charcoal has been specified, and since woods such as khadira have been mentioned earlier, the lump of all the metals and secondary minerals, such as <s>vajrābhra</s>, the mica called adamantine, <s>kānta</s> (magnet), <s>sasyaka</s> or <s>capalā</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s>, namely gold-mākṣika, when blown with two bellows, causes its <s>sattva</s> to fall.
He praises the <s>sattva</s> of <s>mākṣika</s> because of its power, beginning with '<s>hitvā</s>'.

children.text: mākṣikasatvaṃ tāpyasāraṃ hitvā tyaktvā anyeṣāṃ rasoparasānāṃ śaktiḥ sāmarthyaṃ nāsti ||
children.translated_text: Apart from the <s>sattva</s> of <s>mākṣika</s>, the essence of <s>tāpya</s>, the other <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s have no power.

children.text: kiṃbhūtā śaktiḥ lohaghnīti lohān hantīti vigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of power? It is <s>lohaghnī</s>, metal-destroying: the analysis is 'it destroys metals'.

children.text: punastāvatsattvaṃ na patati yāvadbhastrā ante satvasamīpe na āhrīyeta na prāpyeta tasmādalpenāgninā satvāpravṛttirityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>sattva</s> does not fall until the bellows are brought right up to the end, near the <s>sattva</s>. Therefore, with a small fire there is no activity of the <s>sattva</s>; this is the meaning.
Having set aside the <s>sattva</s> of <s>mākṣika</s>, he states the activity of other <s>sattva</s>s, beginning with '<s>raktam</s>'.

children.text: raktaṃ lohitaṃ nāgasamaṃ sīsakatulyaṃ mṛdu komalaṃ evaṃvidhaṃ satvaṃ yasmāddhetor mākṣikāt patati tāpyāt nirgacchati tadvattasmāddhetor vā tasmādvidhānataḥ gandhāśmano gandhakasya yatnena mṛdubhāvaṃ kāryaṃ yathā gandhako'pi mṛdurbhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since a red, blood-colored, lead-like, soft and tender <s>sattva</s> falls from <s>mākṣika</s>, that is, comes forth from <s>tāpya</s>, therefore, for that reason or by that procedure, the softening of <s>gandhāśman</s>, sulfur, should be carefully effected, so that the sulfur too becomes soft; this is the meaning.
He states the procedure for the <s>sattva</s> of <s>mākṣika</s>, beginning with '<s>lavaṇa</s>'.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ lavaṇāmlena lavaṇaṃ mukhyatvāt granthāntarasāmyācca saindhavaṃ amlo jambīrādiḥ tena marditaṃ punaramlena jambīrādinā vidhinā uktarītyā puṭitaṃ vahnau pratāpitaṃ sat muñcati pūrvaślokasaṃbandhāt sattvaṃ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>, that is <s>tāpya</s>, ground with salt and acid, where the salt, because it is principal and because of agreement with other treatises, is rock salt, and the acid is citron and the like, and then, by the stated method, calcined in a closed heating with an acid such as citron and heated in fire, releases its <s>sattva</s>, as supplied from the preceding verse.
The <s>sattva</s> that has fallen in this way should be taken.
With salt and acid, sulfur too becomes soft.

children.text: tu punaḥ soṣṇe āyasapātre vahnau tāpite lohapātre piṣṭikā bhavati raktavarṇarajorūpety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, in an iron vessel that is hot, that is, heated in the fire, it becomes a <s>piṣṭikā</s>, meaning a red-colored powdery substance.
He states the extraction of <s>sattva</s> from <s>tuttha</s> and the other substances, beginning with '<s>tuttha</s>'.

children.text: tutthāt tutthaṃ śikhigrīvaṃ tasmāt tāpyajasamamiti mākṣikasatvavat mākṣikasatvavidhānenāsya satvapāta ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From <s>tuttha</s> comes <s>tuttha</s>-essence, peacock-neck in color; therefore it is said to be like that produced from <s>tāpya</s>. The meaning is that its <s>sattva-pāta</s> (extraction of essence) is like the essence of <s>mākṣika</s>, by the procedure for <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>.

children.text: samasṛṣṭaṃ samaṃ tāpyena tulyaṃ varṇamārdavābhyāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ kathitamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Samasṛṣṭa</s>' means equal, formed like <s>tāpya</s> in color and softness; that is, it is said to be the same.
<s>Tutthaka-sattva</s> of this kind falls out, that is, is extracted.

children.text: abhraketyādi abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ vaikrāntaṃ rasavaikrāntaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ itiprabhṛtīnām ityādīnāṃ tattvaṃ patrasatvapātanayoge lohanibhaṃ muṇḍavarṇam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Beginning with '<s>abhraka</s>': mica is well known; <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>rasa-vaikrānta</s>, and <s>kānta</s>, magnet, and so forth. In the procedure for extracting leaf-essence from these and the like, their essence is like iron, of the color of wrought iron. This is the meaning.
Again he states another procedure for <s>mākṣika</s>, beginning with '<s>strī</s>'.

children.text: tāpyaṃ strīvajrīdugdhabhāvitaṃ strī nārī vajrī sehuṇḍaḥ tayordugdhaṃ tena bhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: One should make <s>tāpya</s> impregnated with the milk or latex of <s>strī</s> and <s>vajrī</s>: <s>strī</s> is <s>nārī</s>, and <s>vajrī</s> is <s>sehuṇḍa</s>. It is to be impregnated with the milk of those two and heated in a warm <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: punareraṇḍasnehena śataṃ śatavāraṃ bhāvitaṃ ca kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Again one should make it impregnated with castor oil one hundred times.

children.text: tato vāraistribhireva dhmātaṃ sat haimaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ tasyedaṃ haimaṃ satvaṃ śulbasamaṃ tāmranibhaṃ bhavati rañjakaṃ rase rāgadāyī syātkanake'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: After that, when smelted only three times, the golden essence, that is, the essence of gold-pyrites, becomes like copper, resembling copper. It colors; it gives redness to <s>rasa</s>, and also to gold.
He states another method, beginning with '<s>kadalī</s>'.

children.text: tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ kadalīrasaśatabhāvitamadhvairaṇḍatailaparipakvam iti prathamaṃ rambhādraveṇa śatavāraṃ bhāvitaṃ paścāt madhvairaṇḍatailābhyāṃ saha paripakvaṃ samyak pācitaṃ sat satvaṃ muñcati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s>, namely <s>mākṣika</s>, impregnated one hundred times with plantain juice and cooked with honey and castor oil: first it is impregnated a hundred times with the liquid of <s>rambhā</s>, the plantain, and afterward it is well cooked together with honey and castor oil. In that condition it releases its <s>sattva</s>.
By what means? By three heatings, that is, by smelting three times.
In the same way <s>rasaka</s>, calamine, also releases its <s>sattva</s>.
For the extraction of <s>sattva</s>, he states the lump-mixture, beginning with '<s>ūrṇā</s>'.

children.text: ūrṇā iti ūrṇā meṣaroma ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ guḍaḥ pratītaḥ puro gugguluḥ lākṣā jatu sarjaraso rālaḥ etaiḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ sarvadhātubhiḥ rasoparasairvā svarṇādibhiḥ saha piṣṭaiḥ peṣitaiḥ punaḥ chāgīkṣīreṇa ajāpayasā kṛtā yā piṇḍī sā satvavidhau satvapātanakarmaṇi śastā pradhānā ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Ūrṇā</s>' means wool, the hair of sheep; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s>; jaggery is well known; <s>pura</s> is guggul; <s>lākṣā</s> is lac; <s>jatu</s> is lac-resin; and <s>sarja-rasa</s> is <s>rāla</s>. A lump made from these, ground together with all metals, <s>rasa</s>s or <s>uparasa</s>s, such as gold and the rest, and then made with goat's milk, is praised, that is, is excellent, for the procedure of <s>sattva</s>, the operation of extracting essence.
It certainly extracts the <s>sattva</s>, the essence, of metals, <s>rasa</s>s, and <s>uparasa</s>s.
He states another procedure, beginning with '<s>cūrṇita</s>'.

children.text: cūrṇitasatvasamānaṃ cūrṇitaṃ piṣṭaṃ yat satvaṃ sāraṃ tatsamānaṃ viśuddhatvāt satvasamānaṃ dhāturasoparasacūrṇaṃ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Cūrṇita-sattva-samāna</s>' means powder of metals, <s>rasa</s>s, and <s>uparasa</s>s that is equal to <s>sattva</s>: what has been powdered and ground, the essence or core, is equal to <s>sattva</s> because of its purity. This is to be supplied.

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ viśuddhaṃ cūrṇaṃ ādareṇa prītyā ādau saṃgṛhya ṭaṅkaṇapalasaptayutaṃ kuryāt saubhāgyasya palaiḥ saptasaṃkhyākaiḥ sahitaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having first taken such pure powder with care and satisfaction, one should make it joined with seven <s>pala</s>s of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>; that is, one should make it combined with seven <s>pala</s>s of <s>saubhāgya</s>.

children.text: viśuddhe cūrṇe triṃśatpale saptapalaṃ saubhāgyaṃ yojyaṃ evaṃ ṭaṅkaṇavidhānena ca punaḥ guñjāpalatritayena raktikāpalatritayaparimāṇena yojitaṃ kuryād iti ||
children.translated_text: To thirty <s>pala</s>s of purified powder, seven <s>pala</s>s of <s>saubhāgya</s> should be added. Then, according to the procedure with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, it should again be made joined with three <s>pala</s>s of <s>guñjā</s>, that is, with a measure of three <s>pala</s>s of <s>raktikā</s>.

children.text: tilacūrṇakakiṭṭapalaiḥ tilaṃ pratītaṃ teṣāṃ cūrṇakaṃ kiṭṭaṃ muṇḍādīnāṃ malaṃ tayoḥ palaiḥ palamānairgodhūmabaddhapiṇḍī bahuśo bahuvāraṃ gopañcakabhāvitaṃ gavāṃ kṣīrājyadadhimūtraviṭkena bhāvitā kiṃ kṛtvā matsyair āloḍya matsyaiḥ kṣudrajalacarair āloḍya saṃmiśryetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With <s>pala</s>-measures of sesame powder and slag: sesame is well known; its powder, and slag, the impurity of wrought iron and the like, are meant. A wheat-bound lump made with <s>pala</s>-measures of these is to be impregnated many times with <s>gopañcaka</s>, the five products of the cow, namely milk, ghee, curds, urine, and dung. After doing what? After stirring it with fish, that is, after mixing it with small aquatic fish.

children.text: koṣṭhake koṣṭhikāyantre dhamanavidhinā utkṣipyotkṣipya dhamanena bhastrānalena tat satvaṃ patati pūrvasaṃbandhāt tāpyādīnāṃ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the furnace, in the furnace-apparatus, by the method of blowing, by blowing again and again with the fire of the bellows, that <s>sattva</s> falls out. From the previous connection, the <s>sattva</s> of <s>tāpya</s> and the rest is to be supplied.
And again the mica-essence, the core from mica, flows together.

children.text: tathaivoktavidhānena sarvāṇi samastāni satvāni sārāṇi patanti anuktānāṃ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, by the stated method, all essences, all cores, fall out; this is to be supplied for those not explicitly mentioned.
He was well-conducted, one whose undertakings were rightly begun, intelligent, and a revealer of true knowledge;
and he was a knower of wealth and <s>dharma</s> (normative order), charming, possessing the excellences of graceful speech.
At the beginning he gives praise of the golden essence, beginning with '<s>svīkṛtya</s>'.

children.text: haimaṃ svarṇamākṣikasatvaṃ saṃmiliti kiṃkṛtvā sarvalohaguṇān sarvaloheṣu samastadhātuṣu saṃmilitā miśritāḥ ye guṇās tān gṛhītvā tathā rase praviśati yathā gaṅgā sarvā nadyaḥ saritaḥ svīkṛtya aṅgīkṛtya jaladhau samudre praviśati ||
children.translated_text: The golden essence, the essence of gold-pyrites, having gathered together the qualities of all metals, that is, having taken up the qualities that are mixed in all metals, enters <s>rasa</s>, just as the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, having received all rivers, enters the ocean.
He states the section on <s>tāpya-sattva</s>, beginning with '<s>jīryati</s>'.

children.text: tat haimaṃ tāpyasatvaṃ śulbe tāmre milati sati sattvaṃ jīryati jāraṇatvamāpnoti rase iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That golden <s>tāpya-sattva</s>, when mixed with copper, is digested, that is, attains the state of <s>jāraṇa</s>, in <s>rasa</s>; this is to be supplied.

children.text: tasmin satve śulbe milati sati kiṭṭatāṃ yāti lohamalasadṛśaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: When copper is mixed into that <s>sattva</s>, it goes to the state of slag; it becomes like the impurity of metal.

children.text: prathamaṃ tatsatvaṃ kariṇā nāgena saha hemakriyāsu svarṇakāryeṣu nirvyūḍhaṃ rase nirvāhitaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: First, that <s>sattva</s> should be carried through in <s>rasa</s> together with <s>nāga</s>, lead, for operations involving gold; that is, it should be made effective in gold-work.

children.text: punastrapuṇā vaṅgena saha tārakriyāsu rūpyakāryeṣu nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt nāgavaṅgau sarvatra pītasitakāryeṣu praśastāvityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, it should be carried through together with <s>trapu</s>, tin, for operations involving <s>tāra</s>, silver. Lead and tin are praised everywhere for yellow and white operations respectively. This is the meaning.
He states the combination for mica-essence, beginning with '<s>ghana-sattva</s>'.

children.text: khalu niścaye vākyālaṅkāre vā ghanasatvam abhrasāraṃ raviṇā tāmreṇa saha rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane dvaṃdvakaṃ ghanasatvatāmraṃ yojyaṃ punaḥ raktagaṇapātabhāvitagirijatumākṣikagairikadaradaiḥ raktagaṇasya yaḥ pātaḥ pātanaṃ nikṣepo vā tena bhāvitāni gharmapuṭitāni girijatumākṣikagairikadaradāni girijatu śilājatu mākṣikaṃ pratītaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ etairbījaśeṣaṃ kuryād ityāgāmiślokājjñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Here <s>khalu</s> may express certainty, or it may be merely an ornament of the sentence. For <s>rasāyana</s>, the destruction of old age and disease, <s>ghanasatva</s>, the essence of mica, also called <s>abhrasāra</s>, should be combined with <s>ravi</s>, copper; the compound is <s>ghanasatvatāmra</s>, mica-essence with copper. Again, from the forthcoming verse, "one should make the remainder as <s>bīja</s>," it is to be understood that this is to be done with <s>girijatu</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, red ochre, and <s>darada</s>, which have been impregnated by the application of the red group. The application of the red group means either pouring it on or depositing it, and the <s>girijatu</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, red ochre, and <s>darada</s> have been so impregnated and heated in a sweat-pit. <s>Girijatu</s> is <s>śilājatu</s>; <s>mākṣika</s> is well known; <s>darada</s> is cinnabar.
He states another procedure, beginning with "<s>mṛdula</s>."

children.text: mṛdulaṃ nepālasaṃjñikaṃ tāmraṃ kāntaṃ lohajāti ghanasatvamabhrasāraṃ punarmṛtaṃ nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ lohajāti kanakaṃ hema etattrayaṃ bījaṃ śulbāditrayaṃ ca bījasaṃjñakaṃ daradaśilātālamākṣikairvāpāt daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ śilā manohvā tālaṃ haritālaṃ etaiḥ kṛtvā vāpaḥ vahnitapte parikṣepaḥ tasmāt bījaśeṣaṃ kurvīta ubhayorbīje abhrasatvahemnaḥ śeṣe kuryādityarthaḥ vā evaṃ kṛte yaccheṣaṃ tiṣṭhati tadbījamiti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛdula</s>, called <s>Nepāla</s>, is copper; <s>kānta</s> is a type of iron; <s>ghanasatva</s> is mica-essence. Again, killed <s>nāga</s> is lead; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is a type of iron; and <s>kanaka</s> is gold. These three are the <s>bīja</s>, and the group of three beginning with copper is also known as <s>bīja</s>. With <s>darada</s>, <s>śilā</s>, <s>tāla</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s> one should make an application: <s>darada</s> is cinnabar, <s>śilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>, and <s>tāla</s> is yellow orpiment. The application is the throwing in while the substance is heated by fire. From that one should make the remainder as <s>bīja</s>; that is, one should leave the two <s>bīja</s>s, mica-essence and gold. Or, when this has been done, whatever remains is called the <s>bīja</s>.
He states another procedure, beginning with "killed <s>nāga</s>."

children.text: mayannāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tanmṛtanāgaṃ ca mṛtaṃ yadvaṅgaṃ raktagaṇāvāpamṛtaṃ ca yacchulvaṃ vā ghanasatvatārakanakaṃ ghanasatvamabhrasāraṃ tāraṃ rūpyaṃ kanakaṃ hema etannadugaṇasarvaṃ vā pratyekaṃ pṛthak giriṇā śilājatunā saha dhmātaṃ kuryāt adhikaśodhanaiḥ daradaśilātālairvāpāt bījaśeṣaṃ kuryāditi pūrvasaṃbandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Killed <s>nāga</s>, that is lead, and killed tin, and copper that has been killed by application of the red group, or the whole group consisting of mica-essence, silver, and gold, namely <s>ghanasatva</s> or mica-essence, <s>tāra</s> or silver, and <s>kanaka</s> or gold, or each one separately, should be smelted together with <s>giri</s>, <s>śilājatu</s>. Through further purifications one should make the remainder as <s>bīja</s> by applying <s>darada</s>, <s>śilā</s>, and <s>tāla</s>; this is connected with the preceding instruction.
The red group is pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and the like; or the yellow group, as follows:
<s>Kiṃśuka</s>, <s>karṇikāra</s>, and likewise the two kinds of turmeric:
"This is declared to be the yellow class in the operation of the king of <s>rasa</s>."

children.text: vā mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ vā rājāvartaṃ rājavarto lājavarada iti bhāṣāyāṃ atha vimalaṃ tāramākṣikaṃ ityekatamaṃ sarvameva vā gairikakunaṭīkṣitigandhakakhagaiḥ gairikaṃ pratītaṃ kunaṭī manohvā kṣitiḥ sphaṭakī gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ khagaḥ kāsīsaṃ etairiti ||
children.translated_text: Or <s>mākṣika</s>, that is <s>tāpya</s>; or <s>rājāvarta</s>, which in the vernacular is called <s>lājavarda</s>; or then <s>vimala</s>, silver-pyrites; either one of these, or indeed all of them, together with red ochre, <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>kṣiti</s>, sulfur, and <s>khaga</s>. Red ochre is well known; <s>kunaṭī</s> is <s>manohvā</s>; <s>kṣiti</s> is alum; sulfur is well known; and <s>khaga</s> is green vitriol. With these, then.

children.text: etaiḥ pūrvoktaireva rase nirvyūḍhe raso rāgādi rañjanādi gṛhṇāti ādiśabdāt sāraṇaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ punarbandham upayāti bandhanamāpnoti punaḥ mṛtalohoparasādyaiḥ mṛtāśca te lohāśca dhātavaśca ta eva uparasā gandhakādyāḥ ādyaśabdāt rasā api tairnirvyūḍhaiḥ kṛtvā śṛṅkhalābījaṃ uttarottaraṃ rañjakaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s> has been processed with these same substances previously stated, <s>rasa</s> takes on coloration and the like, namely dyeing and so forth; by the word "and so forth" <s>sāraṇa</s> too is to be understood. Again it obtains binding, that is, becomes bound. Further, by being processed with killed metals and secondary minerals and the like, namely metals that have been killed and are themselves metals and minerals, together with secondary minerals such as sulfur and, by the word "and the like," <s>rasa</s>s also, it becomes a chained <s>bīja</s>, each subsequent one acting as a colorant for the next.

children.text: rasalohairiti rasā vaikrāntādayo lohā dhātavaḥ pratītās tair nirvyūḍhaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ advandvākhyaiḥ ekātmaiḥ saṃkarairvā sarvaiḥ saṃkaro'vakare ityamaraḥ evaṃ niṣpanne bījaṃ jāraṇayogyaṃ sadityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the phrase "with <s>rasa</s>s and metals," the <s>rasa</s>s are those such as <s>vaikrānta</s>, and the metals are the well-known metals. The <s>bīja</s> processed with them is of what sort? It is called <s>advandva</s>, either single in nature or compounded with all of them; <s>Amara</s> says that <s>saṃkara</s> means mixture. When thus produced, the <s>bīja</s> is fit for <s>jāraṇa</s>.
He states another special procedure, beginning with "<s>bīja</s>."
This produced <s>bīja</s> should be sprinkled into the red group.

children.text: punastena raktagaṇena kṛtavāpaṃ kṛto vāpo yasmin tat ||
children.translated_text: Then it should be made to receive an application with that red group, that is, it should be something in which an application has been made.

children.text: punastadbījaṃ cāritajāritamātraṃ pūrvaṃ ca paścāt jāritaṃ santaṃ sūtaṃ rañjayati rāgaṃ prāpayati badhnāti ceti ||
children.translated_text: Again, when that <s>bīja</s> has merely undergone <s>cāraṇa</s> and <s>jāraṇa</s>, having first been made to undergo <s>cāraṇa</s> and afterward <s>jāraṇa</s>, it colors the <s>sūta</s>, bringing it to coloration, and also binds it.
He states this, beginning with "<s>rakta</s>."

children.text: raktasneha iti raktagaṇo dāḍimakiṃśukādikaḥ snehaḥ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ etairviśodhitāḥ paścānmṛtā ye dhātavo rasādayaśca rasoparasāstaiḥ sarveṣāṃ bījānāṃ pūrvoktānāṃ vāpaṃ kuru rase iti śeṣaḥ vā rakte raktavarṇe snehe snehavarge niṣekaṃ ca vidhānadvayamidam ||
children.translated_text: In the expression "red unctuous substance," the red group consists of pomegranate, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and the like, and the unctuous substances are those such as <s>kaṅguṇī</s>. With metals that have been purified by these and then killed, and with <s>rasa</s>s and secondary minerals, make the application of all the previously mentioned <s>bīja</s>s; "in the <s>rasa</s>" is to be supplied. Or else there are two procedures here: sprinkling in a red-colored unctuous substance, that is, in the class of unctuous substances, and application.

children.text: pītakriyāyāṃ bījānyuktāni atha śvetakriyāyāṃ bījānyāha vaṅgetyādi ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bīja</s>s for the yellow operation have been stated. Now he states the <s>bīja</s>s for the white operation, beginning with "tin."

children.text: vaṅgābhramiti vaṅgaṃ raṅgaṃ abhraṃ gaganaṃ ete bījahetave iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Tin and mica" means tin, called <s>raṅga</s>, and mica, called <s>gagana</s>; these are for the sake of <s>bīja</s>, as is to be supplied.

children.text: punarabhratāraṃ abhraṃ gaganaṃ tāraṃ rūpyaṃ iti ca sitaṃ śvetaṃ yacchailamalaṃ śilājatu tena āhatau samyak mṛtau sitavaṅgau tāraraṅgau kāryau punaḥ raktaṃ hema sitaṃ tāraṃ tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ tābhyāṃ hataṃ māritaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, mica and silver, namely mica or <s>gagana</s> and <s>tāra</s> or silver, are to be used. Tin and silver, both white, should be properly struck and killed with white mountain exudate, that is <s>śilājatu</s>. Again, red gold, white silver, and <s>tāpya</s>, that is <s>mākṣika</s>, should be struck by those two and killed.

children.text: punastāraṃ rūpyaṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ vaṅgaṃ cābhraṃ ca yatra tadevaṃvidhaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then one should make silver, that is <s>tāra</s>, so processed, and also tin and mica, in such a state.
The meaning is that all this is to be applied to <s>rasa</s> in the silver operations.
He states that mica-essence is primary in the <s>bīja</s>, beginning with "<s>nirvāhaṇa</s>."
What is this for? For the pacification of all faults, that is, for the destruction of all faults in metals and the like.

children.text: evamamunā prakāreṇa yathā dhātunirvāhaṇavidhistathā bījānāṃ rase nirvāhaṇaṃ kuryāt sarvabījanirvāhaṇe abhrakasatvaṃ prathamaṃ nirvāhyamiti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this procedure, just as there is a method for processing metals, so one should perform the processing of the <s>bīja</s>s in <s>rasa</s>. It should be known that in the processing of all <s>bīja</s>s, mica-essence must first be processed.
He states the rule for processing, beginning with "goat."

children.text: evaṃvidhāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā dhātunirvāhaṇaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After making such a crucible, one should perform the processing of the metals; this is to be supplied.

children.text: kiṃbhūtāṃ chāgāsthibhasmanirmitamūṣāmiti chāgo bastastasyāsthīni tadbhasmanā nirmitā kṛtā yā mūṣā tām ||
children.translated_text: What kind of crucible? The crucible made from the ashes of goat bones: a <s>chāga</s> is a goat, its bones are used, and the crucible made or fashioned with their ashes is meant.
Again, of what kind? It is shaped like a bowl and resembles a cow's udder.
Again, what is its special quality? It has dense perforations, that is, compact holes.

children.text: punaḥ ṭaṅkaṇaviṣaguñjākṛtalepāṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ viṣaṃ saktukaṃ guñjā raktikā tābhiḥ kṛto lepo yasyāṃ sā tām ||
children.translated_text: Again, it has a coating made from <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, poison, and <s>guñjā</s>: <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s> (borax), the poison is <s>saktuka</s>, and <s>guñjā</s> is <s>raktikā</s>; it is the crucible on which a coating has been made with these.
The meaning is that such a crucible is to be used in the operation of joining leaves, that is, in the joining of metal sheets.
By the play of words he makes the world imitate nectar.
If that which is itself manhood is only somewhat dependent on the two tongues of nectar, there is no fault in this.
Now he states the method for the operation of <s>dvandva</s> (pairing or conjunction), beginning with '<s>yāvat</s>'.
The word '<s>yāvat</s>' is used in the sense of a limit, 'so long as' or 'until'.

children.text: lohāni hemādīni nāgāṅgatayā bhujaṅgaśarīratayā na milanti sugamatvena ekaśarīratāṃ nāpnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: The metals, beginning with gold, do not combine as the body of a serpent, that is, as one serpent-body; they do not readily attain the state of a single body.

children.text: keṣu sarvasattveṣu abhrādīnāṃ sāreṣu sattvasya kāṭhinyādvinopāyaṃ naikatāṃ yānti lohāni ||
children.translated_text: In which things? In all <s>sattva</s>s, the essences beginning with mica. Because of the hardness of the <s>sattva</s>, the metals do not become one without a method.
Therefore, until then, <s>rasa</s> does not move through the whole body.

children.text: kena kṛtvā satveṣu lohāni milanti dvandvayogena daradādinā vā guḍapuraṭaṅkaṇādineti ||
children.translated_text: By what means do metals combine in the <s>sattva</s>s? By <s>dvandva-yoga</s>, either with <s>darada</s> and the like, or with molasses, <s>pura</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and so on.
He states the procedure for joining <s>sattva</s>, beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>'.
'Metal' means gold and the like.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ sasyakaṃ capalā daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ etena catuṣkeṇa vā ebhyo 'nyatamenoktarasoparasena vāpitaṃ sudhmātaṃ śobhanayuktyā dhmātaṃ ca sat niviḍabhāvaṃ saṃtyajati sattve saṃmilati ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>; <s>rasaka</s> is <s>kharparika</s>; <s>sasyaka</s> is <s>capalā</s>; and <s>darada</s> is <s>hiṅgula</s>. When metal has been impregnated and well smelted with this set of four, or with any one of these stated <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s, and has been smelted by a proper method, it gives up its compact condition and combines with the <s>sattva</s>.
He states another procedure, beginning with '<s>guḍa</s>'.

children.text: idaṃ dvaṃdvitaṃ dvaṃdvīkṛtaṃ lohaṃ sattvena militaṃ rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane yojyam ||
children.translated_text: This joined, <s>dvandva</s>-made metal, combined with <s>sattva</s>, is to be used in <s>rasāyana</s>, the destruction of old age and disease.
By what <s>dvandva</s>-joining substances has it been made into <s>dvandva</s>? He says this beginning with '<s>guḍa</s>'.

children.text: guḍaḥ pratītaḥ puro gugguluḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ lākṣā jatu sarjaraso rālā etaiḥ dhātakīsamāyuktaiḥ dhātakī pratītā tatsamāyuktaiḥ punaḥ strīstanyena nārīdugdhena piṣṭairmarditaiḥ etairdvandvamelāpakaiḥ kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Guḍa</s> is well known; <s>pura</s> is guggul; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s>; <s>lākṣā</s> is lac; and <s>sarjarasa</s> is resin. With these, joined with <s>dhātakī</s>, which is well known, and again ground and triturated with woman's milk, that is, female milk, one performs the joining agents of <s>dvandva</s>.

children.text: sarve dvandveṣu satvaṃ prati dvandveṣu milanti ekībhavanti lohāni iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In all the <s>dvandva</s>s, the <s>sattva</s>s combine in relation to each <s>dvandva</s>; the words 'the metals' are to be supplied: the metals become one.
With which things? With wool and the others.

children.text: ūrṇā pratītā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ girijatu śilājatu karṇākṣimalaṃ manuṣyasya indragopako jīvaviśeṣaḥ karkaṭakaścakulīraḥ syātkulīraḥ karkaṭakaḥ ityamaraḥ etaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wool is well known; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s>; <s>girijatu</s> is <s>śilājatu</s>; ear and eye dirt means that of a human being; <s>indragopaka</s> is a particular living creature; and <s>karkaṭaka</s> is a crab, for the lexicon says, '<s>cakulīra</s> is <s>kulīra</s>, and <s>kulīra</s> is <s>karkaṭaka</s>'. With these.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaiḥ nārīpayasā strīdugdhena piṣṭaiḥ kalkitaiḥ trayo'pi dvandvamelāpakayogā iti ||
children.translated_text: Of what special kind? Ground with the milk of a woman, that is, made into paste with female milk. Thus there are three <s>dvandva</s>-joining formulae.
He states another procedure, beginning with '<s>rasa</s>'.

children.text: evamuktavidhānena rasavaikrāntakaṃ dvandvānvitaṃ svakīyadvandvasahitaṃ milati pṛthagbhāvaṃ tyajati ||
children.translated_text: By the procedure thus stated, <s>rasavaikrāntaka</s>, accompanied by <s>dvandva</s>, that is, together with its own <s>dvandva</s>, combines and gives up separateness.
Together with what? With gold.

children.text: tadrasavaikrāntasattvaṃ hemnā saha nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt tena rasavaikrāntasattvahemayogena raso bandhamupayāti baddho bhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: One should make that <s>rasavaikrānta-sattva</s> drawn out or blended with gold. Through that conjunction of <s>rasavaikrānta-sattva</s> and gold, <s>rasa</s> enters into bondage; it becomes bound.
Now he states another special procedure, beginning with '<s>śastam</s>'.
A <s>bīja</s> of this kind is excellent. Where? In every <s>dvandva</s>.
Again, when made with these, the <s>bīja</s> should be excellent.

children.text: kaiḥ girijatulelītakendragopādyaiḥ girijatu śilājatu lelītako gandhakaḥ indragopaḥ surendragopo jīvaviśeṣaḥ ete ādyā yeṣāṃ taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With which substances? With <s>girijatu</s>, <s>lelītaka</s>, <s>indragopa</s>, and the rest: <s>girijatu</s> is <s>śilājatu</s>, <s>lelītaka</s> is sulphur, and <s>indragopa</s>, also called <s>surendragopa</s>, is a particular living creature. These and similar substances are meant.

children.text: na kevalametair mahiṣīkarṇamalādyaiśca mahiṣyāḥ karṇayormala ādyo yeṣāṃ te ādyaśabdānnāsākṣimalaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Not only with these, but also with substances beginning with buffalo-ear dirt: the dirt from a buffalo cow's ears is first among them; by the word 'and the rest' nose and eye dirt are also included.

children.text: punaṣṭaṅkaṇālaviṣaiḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ ālaṃ haritālaṃ viṣaṃ kandajaṃ etaiḥ piṣṭairdvandvamelāpaḥ syāditi punaḥ saṃbandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>āla</s>, and poison: <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s>, <s>āla</s> is yellow orpiment, and the poison is of tuber-origin. Ground with these, the joining of <s>dvandva</s> occurs; this connection is to be supplied again.
He states another procedure, beginning with '<s>madhu</s>'.

children.text: etaiḥ pūrvoktair yogaiḥ madhusahitaiḥ kṣaudrayutaiḥ tārābhraṃ rūpyagaganaṃ milati ||
children.translated_text: With these previously stated formulae, when they are accompanied by honey, that is, joined with honey, <s>tārābhra</s>, silver-mica, combines.

children.text: ca punastāpyakanakaṃ mākṣikasvarṇaṃ idaṃ dvandvaṃ ca milati ||
children.translated_text: And again <s>tāpya-kanaka</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>-gold, this <s>dvandva</s> too combines.

children.text: na kevalaṃ pūrvoktayogair milati punaretair eraṇḍatailaṭaṅkaṇakaṅkuṣṭhaśilendragopaiśca eraṇḍatailaṃ vātārisnehaḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ śilā manohvā indragopako jīvaviśeṣaḥ etaiśca madhusahitaiḥ kṛtvā dvandvaṃ milatītyavaśyam ||
children.translated_text: It combines not only by the previously stated formulae, but also by these: castor oil, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>śilā</s>, and <s>indragopa</s>; castor oil is the oil hostile to wind, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s>, <s>śilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>, and <s>indragopaka</s> is a particular living creature. With these also, accompanied by honey, the <s>dvandva</s> certainly combines.
He states that procedure, beginning with '<s>sūtena</s>'.

children.text: prathamaṃ sūtena rasena saha śuddhakanakaṃ niṣpiṣya saṃmardya punaḥ samābhrayojitaṃ kṛtvā samaṃ ca tadabhraṃ ca tena yojitaṃ kṛtvā paścātpādena caturthāṃśavibhāgena pūrvoktadvandvānyatamakaṃ kalpyaṃ pūrvoktadvandvam eraṇḍatailādikaṃ girijatvādikaṃ ca tebhyo 'nyatamakaṃ dvandvaṃ yojyamiti ||
children.translated_text: First one should grind and thoroughly triturate purified gold together with <s>sūta</s>, that is, <s>rasa</s>. Then, after combining it with an equal quantity of mica, that is, after joining it with an equal amount of that mica, afterward one should prepare one from among the previously stated <s>dvandva</s>s in a quarter part. The meaning is that one should add any one <s>dvandva</s> from among the previously stated <s>dvandva</s>s, such as those beginning with castor oil or those beginning with <s>girijatu</s>.
He states another procedure, beginning with '<s>rasa</s>'.

children.text: rasoparasasya vaikrāntagandhakādermadhye śuddhamākṣikaṃ nirdoṣaṃ tāpyaṃ hemno dviguṇaṃ kanakāddviguṇitaṃ dattvā dviguṇamākṣikayutaṃ hema dattvetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among the <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s, such as <s>vaikrānta</s> and sulfur, pure <s>mākṣika</s>, faultless <s>tāpya</s>, should be given in twice the amount of gold; that is, gold combined with twice as much <s>mākṣika</s> is to be given.

children.text: etadrasoparasādikaṃ kākamācyā vāyasyāḥ svarasena mṛdnīyāt mardanaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: These substances, beginning with the <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s, should be ground with the fresh juice of <s>kākamācī</s>, also called <s>vāyasī</s>; one should perform trituration.
And with the bulb of the plantain; that is, also with the bulb of the banana plant.
This preceding medicine should be made into a lump, spherical in shape.
By this procedure <s>hemābhra</s>, gold-mica, and <s>hematāpya</s>, gold-<s>tāpya</s>, combine.
Where? In a diamond-crucible.
Thus he says:
Three parts of clay, two parts of hemp refuse, and one part of burnt husk-stone and the like,
together with half a part of slag, well broken up: with these one should indeed make a diamond-crucible for the extraction of <s>sattva</s>.
So it says.

children.text: evam amunā vidhinā raviśaśitīkṣṇaiḥ saha ravistāmraṃ śaśī rūpyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ lohajātiḥ etaiḥ sārdhaṃ gaganādisatvāni abhrādīnāṃ sārāṇi milantīti yugmam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by this procedure, the essences of mica and the like combine with <s>ravi</s>, <s>śaśin</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s>: <s>ravi</s> is copper, <s>śaśin</s> is silver, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is a class of iron. The essences of mica and the rest combine with these; this is a pair of verses.
He states the topic of the <s>sattva</s> of mica with the words beginning '<s>saṃkara</s>'.
The procedure for mixed <s>bīja</s>s too is to be carried out; that is, this is an instruction about what must be done.

children.text: ityādi pūrvoktaṃ tu punaḥ gaganasatvayogena abhrakasattvena sārdhaṃ mākṣīkayogād anyaṃ yojyaṃ abhrasatvena saha mākṣīkaṃ na syāditi vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: What was stated earlier is again to be joined with the <s>sattva</s> of mica, through the conjunction of <s>gagana-sattva</s>; because of the conjunction with <s>mākṣika</s>, another substance should be combined. The point is that <s>mākṣika</s> is not to be absent when there is mica-<s>sattva</s>.
This begins with '<s>kānta</s>' and so on.

children.text: mākṣikeṇa mṛtaṃ yannāgaṃ tālaṃ haritālaṃ śilā manohvā ca tattathā pūrvoktakalkasahitaṃ yatkalkaṃ rasoparasādīnāṃ tena sahitaṃ yuktaṃ kāntamukhaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Lead killed by <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>tāla</s>, that is yellow orpiment, and <s>śilā</s>, namely <s>manohvā</s>, should likewise be joined with the previously stated paste. That paste consists of the <s>rasa</s>s, <s>uparasa</s>s, and the like. It is to be furnished with a <s>kānta</s>-base, as follows:
In the absence of the <s>sattva</s> of mica, one should supply the <s>sattva</s> of <s>kānta</s>.
Or, if the <s>sattva</s> of <s>kānta</s> is absent, one should supply <s>tīkṣṇa</s>-iron.
So it says.

children.text: madhuni mādhava eva madhuvrataḥ prakurute mudito madhuraṃ ravam
children.translated_text: Only in the spring does the delighted bee make a sweet sound.

children.text: vararavo'pi satāṃ ca samāgamaṃ śabalatā kimupaiti na cārutām ||
children.translated_text: Even a fine sound, through association with good people, surely attains a charming variegation.
Among the mixed <s>bīja</s>s he states those called <s>mahābīja</s>, beginning with '<s>mākṣika</s>'.

children.text: etattrikaṃ mahābījaṃ kimetat mākṣīkakāntatīkṣṇaṃ mākṣīkakāntaśulbaṃ tīkṣṇābhrakaṃ ca mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ lohajātir abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ etattritayaṃ bījaṃ mahābījaṃ etattritrimukhaṃ pratyekaṃ mahāsaṃjñam ||
children.translated_text: This triad is <s>mahābīja</s>. What is it? <s>Mākṣika-kānta-tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>mākṣika-kānta-śulba</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇa-abhraka-mākṣika</s>. Here <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>, <s>kānta</s> is magnetite, <s>śulba</s> is copper, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is a class of iron, and <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s>, mica. This threefold group is the <s>bīja</s> called <s>mahābīja</s>; each of its three forms individually has the designation 'great'.
The special point here is this:
I shall declare the cooking of the <s>bīja</s> for the sake of the digestion of <s>rasa</s>.
This sequence of rules is purified by a <s>bīja</s> that has been evenly digested.
So it says.
And, in a secondary sense, each individual substance is intended by the designation <s>bīja</s>.
He states that with the words beginning '<s>mākṣika</s>'.

children.text: mākṣīkakāntaśulbaṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ etadapi mahābījaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika-kānta-śulba</s>: <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>, <s>kānta</s> is magnetite, and <s>śulba</s> is copper. This too should be understood as <s>mahābīja</s>.

children.text: punaḥ śulbābhrakamākṣīkaṃ punaḥ kāntābhrakamākṣīkaṃ kāntaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ tathā tāpyakaśulbābhrakaṃ etadapi ca mahābījaṃ jñeyamiti ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>śulba-abhraka-mākṣika</s>; again, <s>kānta-abhraka-mākṣika</s>, where <s>kānta</s> is magnet-stone, <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s>, mica, and <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>; and likewise <s>tāpya-śulba-abhraka</s>. These too should be understood as <s>mahābīja</s>.
He states that with the words beginning '<s>mākṣika</s>'.

children.text: mākṣīkatīkṣṇaśulbaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāralohajātiḥ śulbaṃ tāmram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika-tīkṣṇa-śulba</s>: <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is a class of hard iron, and <s>śulba</s> is copper.

children.text: punastīkṣṇaśulbābhrakaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ abhrakaṃ gaganam ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>tīkṣṇa-śulba-abhraka</s>: <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is hard iron, <s>śulba</s> is copper, and <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s>, mica.

children.text: punarmākṣīkakāntakanakaṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ kāntaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ kanakaṃ svarṇam ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>mākṣika-kānta-kanaka</s>: <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>, <s>kānta</s> is magnet-stone, and <s>kanaka</s> is gold.

children.text: punaḥ kanakāruṇamākṣikaṃ kanakaṃ svarṇaṃ aruṇaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣikaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ ceti catuṣṭayaṃ mahābījaṃ pravarabījam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>kanaka-aruṇa-mākṣika</s>: <s>kanaka</s> is gold, <s>aruṇa</s> is copper, and <s>mākṣika</s> is gold-<s>mākṣika</s>. Thus this group of four is <s>mahābīja</s>, meaning an excellent <s>bīja</s>.
Each of the four individually has the designation <s>mahābīja</s>.
He states that with '<s>mākṣika-tīkṣṇa-tāra</s>'.

children.text: mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ tāraṃ rūpyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is hard iron, and <s>tāra</s> is silver.

children.text: punastārāruṇamākṣikaṃ evamuktavidhānena idamapi tāraṃ rūpyaṃ aruṇaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyam ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>tāra-aruṇa-mākṣika</s>: according to the procedure just stated, this too consists of <s>tāra</s>, silver, <s>aruṇa</s>, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>tāpya</s>.

children.text: punaḥ kānte cumbake'bhivyāpake adhikaraṇe śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ yat prayuktam ||
children.translated_text: Again, in the case where <s>kānta</s>, magnetite, is the pervading basis, <s>śulba</s>, copper, and <s>tāpya</s>, gold-<s>mākṣika</s>, are used.
The word '<s>api</s>' means certainly.

children.text: śulbābhratāpyakāñcanaṃ vā śulbaṃ tāmraṃ abhraṃ gaganaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ kāñcanaṃ hema etaccatuṣṭayamapi mahābījaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Or <s>śulba-abhraka-tāpya-kāñcana</s>: <s>śulba</s> is copper, <s>abhra</s> is <s>gagana</s>, mica, <s>tāpya</s> is gold-<s>mākṣika</s>, and <s>kāñcana</s> is gold. This fourfold group too should be understood as <s>mahābīja</s>.
The connection with the designation <s>mahābīja</s> applies to each separately; this is the clarification.
He states that with '<s>kānta-indu-sasya-tāpya</s>'.

children.text: kāntaṃ kāntapāṣāṇaṃ industāraṃ sasyaṃ capalā tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> is magnet-stone, <s>indu</s> is <s>tāra</s>, silver, <s>sasya</s> is <s>capalā</s>, and <s>tāpya</s> is gold-<s>mākṣika</s>.

children.text: punaḥ kāntābhrakatīkṣṇamākṣikaṃ tathā hemābhraśulbatāpyaṃ punarhemābhrakaśulbamākṣikaṃ vā hema kanakaṃ abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ mākṣīkaṃ tāpyaṃ etaccatuṣṭayamapi mahābījaṃ jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>kānta-abhraka-tīkṣṇa-mākṣika</s>; likewise <s>hema-abhraka-śulba-tāpya</s>; or again <s>hema-abhraka-śulba-mākṣika</s>. Here <s>hema</s> is <s>kanaka</s>, gold, <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s>, mica, <s>śulba</s> is copper, and <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>. This fourfold group too should be understood as <s>mahābīja</s>.
The implied meaning is that each individual substance too has the designation <s>bīja</s>.
He states that with the words beginning '<s>kānta</s>'.

children.text: kāntābhraśulbatāpyaṃ kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ abhrakaṃ gaganaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ ityapi mahābījam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta-abhraka-śulba-tāpya</s>: <s>kānta</s> is magnetite, <s>abhraka</s> is <s>gagana</s>, mica, <s>śulba</s> is copper, and <s>tāpya</s> is <s>mākṣika</s>. This too is <s>mahābīja</s>.

children.text: eteṣāṃ mahābījānāṃ cet saṃkarabījaṃ pratyekaṃ dravyasya bījasaṃjñā sā tarhi catuḥṣaṣṭipramāṇā syādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If, among these <s>mahābīja</s>s, there is a mixed <s>bīja</s> and each individual substance has the designation <s>bīja</s>, then its number would be sixty-four; this is the meaning.
He states the procedure for the <s>bīja</s>, beginning with "of all."

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ sarveṣāṃ bījānāṃ yathoktaṃ saṃyogaṃ catuḥṣaṣṭīnāṃ uktasaṃjñānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ saṃyogaṃ ekatrīkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā yadekatrīkṛtaṃ vahnau drāvitaṃ bhavati tatsarvaṃ śatavāpyaṃ bījaṃ siddhaṃ prayatnena syāditi śabdārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The literal meaning is this: first, after making the prescribed conjunction of all the <s>bīja</s>s, that is, after gathering together the sixty-four substances with the stated names, everything so gathered together, when melted in fire, becomes the accomplished <s>bīja</s> called <s>śatavāpya</s>, provided it is done carefully.
He states the causes in the binding of <s>sūta</s>, beginning with "not."

children.text: yadi garbhe rasodare ghanasattvaṃ abhrakasāraṃ na patati na prāpnoti vā garbhe bījāni asminnadhyāye abhihitāni mākṣikakāntaśulbādīni yāvanno dravanti ca punarbāhyadrutistasyā yogo rase drutimelanaṃ na syāt tattasmāddhetoḥ sūta ihāsyāṃ kriyāyāmasatyāṃ kathaṃ badhyate ghanatvaṃ dhatte ||
children.translated_text: If <s>ghanasattva</s>, the essence of mica, does not fall, or is not obtained, in the womb, that is, in the belly of <s>rasa</s>, and if the <s>bīja</s>s described in this chapter, such as <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and copper, do not melt in the womb, and furthermore if the conjunction of external liquefaction with it, the mixing of that liquefaction into <s>rasa</s>, does not take place, then, for that reason, how can <s>sūta</s> be bound in this operation and take on solidity?
The intention is that <s>sūta</s> is certainly bound by internal liquefaction and external liquefaction.

children.text: śaradi śāradamegho varṣati varṣāsu vārṣiko vārdaḥ
children.translated_text: In autumn the autumnal cloud rains; in the rainy season the rainy-season cloud gives water.
In the springtime the cuckoo, nourished by others and possessing excellent speed, constantly shines.
He states what results from the digestion of <s>bīja</s>, beginning with "equal."

children.text: samaṃ sūtatulyaṃ adhiśabdād aparimitaṃ samādadhikaṃ yajjīrṇaṃ jāraṇamāptaṃ bījaṃ niṣpannabījaṃ tenaiva jīrṇena bījena saha āvartatā kāryā āvarta iti āvartaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bīja</s> that has been digested in an amount equal to <s>sūta</s>, and, by the word <s>adhi</s>, even in an unlimited amount beyond equal, and has obtained <s>jāraṇa</s>, is the perfected <s>bīja</s>. With that same digested <s>bīja</s>, repeated melting is to be performed; this repeated melting is called <s>āvarta</s>.

children.text: kiṃ tat yasmādvidhānāddhema kanakaṃ jāyate khalu niścayena tatkaraṇaṃ tasya vidhānasya karaṇam ||
children.translated_text: What is that? It is the carrying out of the procedure by which gold, <s>hema</s> or <s>kanaka</s>, is certainly produced.

children.text: samādijīrṇasya sūtasya rūpyādiṣu prayogātkanakaṃ bhavediti vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sense is that gold will arise when <s>sūta</s> digested in an equal or greater amount is applied to silver and the like.
He states the procedure for killing <s>sūta</s>, beginning with "having melted."
"In a <s>śastrapātra</s>" means in a vessel made of sharp metal; the seventh case is used in the sense of the supporting receptacle.

children.text: gandhapādena gandhasya turyāṃśavibhāgena sūtakaṃ dadyāt tatpātroparibhāge dattaṃ pradrāvya vahninā iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should place <s>sūtaka</s> with a quarter part of sulfur, that is, with a fourth part of <s>gandha</s>. When placed on the upper part of that vessel, it should be melted by fire; these words are to be supplied.

children.text: punaḥ oṣadhīnāṃ svarasena auṣadhyo granthāntare yathā
children.translated_text: Again, with the fresh juice of herbs. The herbs are given in another treatise as follows:
One should grind it until the paste becomes like collyrium.
Then, with the regulatory herbs such as <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>kandukī</s>, and <s>sudhā</s>,
so it is said.

children.text: śatāvaryādīnāṃ svakīyarasena niṣpiṣya pramardya vaṭikāṃ badarākarāṃ kurvīteti ||
children.translated_text: It means that, after crushing and thoroughly grinding it with the respective juices of <s>śatāvarī</s> and the other herbs, one should make a pellet the size of a jujube.
He states that too, beginning with "having placed."

children.text: tāṃ pūrvoktāṃ vaṭikāṃ chāyāśuṣkāṃ lohaphalake śastrapātre saṃsthāpya punaḥ laghulohakaṭorikayā pūrvoktalohaphalakāt laghvī yā lohakaṭorikā tayā sthagayitvā ācchādya dṛḍhaṃ gāḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā lepayet vakṣyamāṇeneti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After placing that previously mentioned pellet, dried in the shade, on an iron plate, in a <s>śastrapātra</s>, one should then cover it with a small iron bowl, smaller than the previously mentioned iron plate, and smear it firmly, tightly, in the manner to be stated.
He states that too, beginning with "salt."

children.text: tāṃ pūrvoditāṃ laghulohakaṭorikāṃ sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā lavaṇārdramṛdā lavaṇena saindhavādinā yutā yā ārdrā jalasiktā mṛt tayā liptāṃ kurvīta ||
children.translated_text: One should make that previously mentioned small iron bowl well smeared with moist salty clay, that is, with clay moistened with water and mixed with salt such as rock salt, so that it is very firm.

children.text: kimarthaṃ dhūmrarodhāya yathā yantrādbahirdhūmodgamo na syāt ||
children.translated_text: For what purpose? For blocking the smoke, so that smoke does not issue outside from the apparatus.

children.text: punaḥ sudṛḍhāṅgārān khadirādīnāṃ dattvā bhastrādvayavahninā khalu dvayāgninā dhamyād iti agrimaślokasaṃbandhāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, after placing firm charcoal from khadira and similar woods, one should blow it with the fire of two bellows, indeed with a double fire; this is connected with the next verse.

children.text: kva sati nirdhūme sati rase dhūmaniḥsaraṇavarjite sati ||
children.translated_text: When what is the case? When the <s>rasa</s> is smokeless, that is, when it is free from the emission of smoke.
He states that too, beginning with "so long."

children.text: sandhiliptā pūrvoktā lohaśarāvikā tāvadavadhau dhmātā kāryā yāvatkālapramāṇaṃ raktābhā raktadyutiyuktā khoṭikā bhavati khoṭasyeva ākṛtiryasyāḥ sā khoṭikā ||
children.translated_text: The previously mentioned small iron saucer, with its joints smeared, should be blown for that length of time, until a small lump, shaped like a lump and having a reddish appearance and red luster, is produced.

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ kaṭorikāṃ svabhāvaśītalāṃ svato himāṃ matvā jñātvā punaraṅgārānapanīya apasārya kaṭorikāmutkhanya raso grāhya iti śeṣaḥ āgamiślokasaṃbandhāt ||
children.translated_text: After that, having understood that the bowl has cooled by itself and is naturally cold, one should remove the charcoal, dig up the bowl, and take the <s>rasa</s>; this is to be supplied from connection with the following verse.
He states that too, beginning with "having dug up."

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ laghulohakaṭorikāṃ pūrvavarṇitāṃ utkhanyotkhanya prabalatvenotpāṭya rasaḥ sūto grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that, having dug up the previously described small iron bowl, forcefully prying it out, one should take the <s>rasa</s>, the <s>sūta</s>.
The repetition "having dug up, having dug up" is either because of its great hardness or from special care.

children.text: kutaḥ kaṭorikāsakāśāt eṣa itthamutpanno mṛtasūtarājo jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From where? From the bowl. This king of killed <s>sūta</s>, produced in this way, is to be known.

children.text: sa ca sukhādhmātaḥ san golakavadbhavati vajramūṣāyāṃ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when it has been easily blown, it becomes like a ball; the words "in a diamond-crucible" are to be supplied.

children.text: kācaḥ pratītaḥ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ tataḥ raso 'ti maryādāmatikramya dhmātaḥ san ekaraso bhavati samarasa ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāca</s> is well known; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s>. Then <s>rasa</s>, when blown beyond the limit, becomes of one essence, meaning homogeneous.

children.text: keṣāṃ śikhigalatāṃ śikhini galantīti vigrahaḥ śikhigalatāṃ dhātūnāṃ evaṃ galite rase triguṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ raṅgaṃ dadyāt tato vaṅgadānānantaraṃ krameṇa alpamalpadānena nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ ca dadyāditi ||
children.translated_text: Of which substances? Of the metals that melt in fire; the analysis is "they melt in fire." When <s>rasa</s> has melted in this way, one should add three times as much tin, <s>vaṅga</s> or <s>raṅga</s>; then, after adding the tin, one should gradually add lead, <s>nāga</s> or <s>sīsaka</s>, in small portions.
He states that too, beginning with "afterwards."

children.text: paścāt triguṇasīsakadānānantaraṃ hemnā kanakena saha rasabījaṃ mahābījaṃ yojyaṃ hemnā sārdhaṃ mahābījaṃ kīdṛgbhavati ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards, after the addition of lead in a triple amount, the <s>rasabīja</s>, the great <s>bīja</s>, should be joined with gold, <s>kanaka</s>. What kind does the great <s>bīja</s> become together with gold?

children.text: rasabandhakaraṃ pāradabandhapradaṃ ca punaḥ tālakaṃ haritālaṃ sūto rasaḥ tenāpi niyāmakauṣadhibhiśca śatāvaryādibhiḥ pūrvoktābhir guṭikāṃ kṛtvā nigṛhya dhūmaṃ rundhitadhūmaṃ yathā syāttathā sudhiyā matimatā rasajñena evamamunā vidhinā rasamāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ pāradabandhaḥ kārya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tālaka</s>, or yellow orpiment, is again what causes the binding of <s>rasa</s> and grants the binding of mercury. With that, and with <s>sūta</s>, mercury, and also with regulating medicines such as <s>śatāvarī</s> and the others mentioned before, a pill should be made; the smoke should be restrained, so that the smoke is blocked. By this method, a wise and intelligent knower of <s>rasa</s> should carry out the killing of <s>rasa</s>; that is, the binding of mercury should be performed.
He says something further, beginning with "or."

children.text: athavā vidhyantare śilayā manohvayā kṛtvā vā mākṣikayogena tāpyasaṃyogaṃ kṛtvā sādhitastālakayogavat sūto rasaḥ śuklavarṇo jayeta ||
children.translated_text: Or, by another procedure, with <s>śilā</s>, called <s>manohvā</s>, or by conjunction with <s>mākṣika</s>, having made a combination with <s>tāpya</s>, <s>sūta</s>, mercury, prepared as in the procedure with <s>tālaka</s>, becomes white in color.

children.text: kena dhūmarodhena saindhavārdramṛdā lepena vā tābhyāṃ śilāmākṣikābhyām ubhābhyāṃ tālakayogavat sādhitaḥ san sūtaḥ śuklavarṇo bhaved iti ||
children.translated_text: By what means? By blocking the smoke, or by a coating with moist clay mixed with rock salt. When it has been prepared with both of these, <s>śilā</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>, just as in the procedure with <s>tālaka</s>, <s>sūta</s> becomes white.
He says something further, beginning with "dead."

children.text: mṛtaśulbatāpyacūrṇaṃ mṛtaṃ ca yat śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ ca taccūrṇaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ kāntayutaṃ cumbakamiśritaṃ tena mṛtaśulbatāpyacūrṇena kāntayutena pūrvaṃ niṣpannaṃ khoṭaṃ rañjayet ||
children.translated_text: "Powder of killed copper and <s>tāpya</s>" means powder consisting of killed <s>śulba</s>, that is copper, and <s>tāpya</s>, gold-pyrites. Of what kind is it? It is joined with <s>kānta</s>, mixed with magnet. With that powder of killed copper and <s>tāpya</s>, joined with <s>kānta</s>, one should color the previously produced <s>khoṭa</s>.
Of what kind is it? It is joined with <s>ghana-sattva</s> and gold, that is, mixed with mica-essence and gold.
Such a <s>khoṭa</s> should be employed in <s>rasāyana</s>, the destruction of old age and disease.
He says something further, beginning with "with strong."

children.text: triguṇena balinā gandhakena saha rasaṃ sūtaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā marditaṃ kuryāt ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should make <s>rasa</s>, <s>sūta</s>, thoroughly ground with sulfur, the strong substance, in triple quantity; this is to be supplied.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭena balinā parpaṭikayutena parpaṭiko lohaparpaṭikaḥ pratītastena yutena militena niyamasaṃskāroktāḥ niyamakāḥ divyauṣadhayaḥ śatāvarīpramukhās tābhiḥ tato vaṭikā chāyāśuṣkā kāryā chāyāgharmarūpā śuṣkā nīrasā tathā kāryā iti ||
children.translated_text: With what kind of strong substance? With one joined to <s>parpaṭikā</s>. <s>Parpaṭikā</s> is the well-known iron <s>parpaṭikā</s>, and it is joined or combined with that. The restraining substances stated in the regulation process are divine medicines headed by <s>śatāvarī</s>. With these, then, a pellet should be made, dried in the shade: made dry in shade-heat, without moisture.
He says something further, beginning with "crucible."

children.text: mūṣādhṛtaparpaṭikā mūṣāyāṃ yā parpaṭikā pūrvoktalohaparpaṭikā sā nigūḍhasudṛḍhena nigūḍhaścāsau sudṛḍhaśca tena mūlakādikṣārabiḍena kṛtvā madhye svāntaḥ ācchādya dhmātaṃ kriyate punas tadūdhmātaṃ sat khoṭaṃ gacchati khoṭatvamāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: "The <s>parpaṭikā</s> held in a crucible" means the <s>parpaṭikā</s> in a crucible, the previously mentioned iron <s>parpaṭikā</s>. Having covered its middle, its own interior, with a concealed and very firm alkaline <s>biḍa</s> made from radish and the like, it is blown. When that has again been blown, it goes to the state of <s>khoṭa</s>, that is, it attains <s>khoṭa</s>-hood.

children.text: tatkhoṭaṃ hemayutaṃ svarṇamilitaṃ sūtabandhakaraṃ syāt rasabandhanapradam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, joined with gold, mixed with gold, becomes able to bind <s>sūta</s>; that is, it grants the binding of <s>rasa</s>.
He states another procedure, beginning with "strong."

children.text: pūrvoktā yā parpaṭikā lohaparpaṭikā baliyuktā gandhakamiśritā snuhyarkabhāvitā ca snuhī vajrī arko mandāras tābhyāṃ bhāvitā plutā etayoḥ payaseti bhāvaḥ mṛditā ca gharṣitā ca evaṃ kṛtavidhānā parpaṭikā sati guṭikā vaṭikā kāryā madhye guṭikāntaḥ gartā kāryā sā gartā tataḥ sūtabhṛtā sūtapūritā satī tadanu gartakaraṇānantaraṃ ācchāditā kāryā parpaṭikayeti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The previously mentioned <s>parpaṭikā</s>, the iron <s>parpaṭikā</s>, is joined with the strong substance, mixed with sulfur, and impregnated with <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>: <s>snuhī</s> is <s>vajrī</s>, and <s>arka</s> is <s>mandāra</s>; it is soaked with these two, meaning with their milky sap, and it is rubbed or ground. When the <s>parpaṭikā</s> has been prepared in this way, a pill or pellet should be made. In the middle, inside the pill, a pit should be made. Then, when that pit has been filled with <s>sūta</s>, filled with mercury, after making the pit it should be covered, meaning with <s>parpaṭikā</s>.
He states that with the words beginning "outside."

children.text: bāhye sūtodaraguṭikopari nigaḍaṃ dattvā suliptamūṣodare suliptā sāraṇakarmābhihitauṣadhīriti śeṣaḥ evaṃvidhā yā mūṣā tasyā yadudaraṃ tasmindṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā nigaḍaṃ nyastaṃ sthāpitaṃ kuryāditi śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the outside, over the pill whose interior contains <s>sūta</s>, a binding should be applied; in the belly of a well-smeared crucible, where the omitted phrase is "with the medicines described for the <s>sāraṇa</s> operation," one should place the binding firmly in the interior of such a crucible; this is to be supplied.

children.text: mūṣodaraguṭikāntasthaḥ sūtaḥ puṭito vahniyogāt mriyate pañcatvamāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: The <s>sūta</s> situated inside the pill in the belly of the crucible, when heated by a closed firing through the application of fire, dies, that is, attains the state of the five elements.
Then, when it is blown again, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
The indeclinable <s>eva</s> expresses exclusion of anything else.
He says something further, beginning with "thus."

children.text: evaṃ lohaparpaṭikāvidhānena tālaśilābhyāṃ dhmātaṃ sat yutaṃ yat khoṭaṃ tadvimalaṃ malavarjitaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the procedure for iron <s>parpaṭikā</s>, when the <s>khoṭa</s> joined with <s>tāla</s> and <s>śilā</s> has been blown, it becomes stainless, free from impurity.

children.text: ca punaḥ mākṣikarasakaistāpyakharparikaiḥ daradaśikhisahitaiśca hiṅgulaśikhimilitaiśca karaṇarūpairvimalaṃ ca punaḥ puṭayogād vahnisaṃparkāt dhmātaṃ mriyate ||
children.translated_text: And again, with <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>rasaka</s>, with <s>tāpya</s> and <s>kharparika</s>, and with substances accompanied by <s>darada</s> and <s>śikhi</s>, and with mixtures of cinnabar and <s>śikhi</s>, which serve as instruments, the stainless substance, when again exposed to closed heating, by contact with fire and blowing, dies.
At the outset the definition of impurity was stated.
He states that with "from the conjunction of slag and <s>pura</s>."

children.text: kiṭṭaṃ lohamalaṃ puro gugguluḥ tayoḥ saṃyogāt dhmātaiḥ mākṣikarasadaradarūpaiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ kiṭṭo bhavet punaḥ kiṭṭato rasasākaṃ sūtamiśritaṃ sattvaṃ sāraṃ nipatati tatsattvaṃ bhasma janayati utpādayati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kiṭṭa</s> is metallic slag, and <s>pura</s> is guggul resin. From the conjunction of these two, with the previously mentioned blown substances such as <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>rasa</s>, and <s>darada</s>, <s>kiṭṭa</s> comes into being. Then from the <s>kiṭṭa</s>, together with <s>rasa</s>, mixed with <s>sūta</s>, <s>sattva</s>, the essence, falls down. That <s>sattva</s> produces ash.
The meaning is that the <s>sattva</s> of that ash also falls down.
He states another procedure, beginning with "tin, mercury, sulfur, and <s>tāla</s>."

children.text: vaṅgaṃ trapu rasaḥ sūtaḥ gandhako baliḥ tālaṃ haritālaṃ etaccatuṣṭayaṃ khaṭikāyā yogataḥ khaṭikā citrakarajastasyā yogataḥ suparpaṭikāṃ pūrvoktāṃ lohaparpaṭikāṃ rañjayati sūtena vināpi kimuta rasamilitena tālasattveneti vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Tin is <s>vaṅga</s>; <s>rasa</s> is <s>sūta</s>; sulfur is the strong substance; and <s>tāla</s> is yellow orpiment. This set of four, through conjunction with <s>khaṭikā</s>, that is, the pollen of <s>citraka</s>, colors the excellent <s>parpaṭikā</s>, the previously mentioned iron <s>parpaṭikā</s>, even without <s>sūta</s>; how much more, then, with the essence of <s>tāla</s> mixed with <s>rasa</s>.
He states the special procedure for the great <s>bīja</s>s and the <s>bīja</s>s, beginning with "thus."

children.text: evam uktavidhānena bījaṃ vidhāya rañjanavidhinā rañjanavidhānena surañjanaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after preparing the <s>bīja</s> by the stated procedure, one should make it well colored by the coloring method, by the procedure of coloration.

children.text: tatkārye rasasya sūtasya triguṇaṃ hema saṃyojyaṃ punas tasya hemnaḥ triguṇaṃ varabījaṃ yojyaṃ iti viśeṣavidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that operation, gold in triple quantity to <s>rasa</s>, <s>sūta</s>, should be combined; then the excellent <s>bīja</s> in triple quantity to that gold should be added. This is the special procedure.
May <s>Bhāratī</s>, adorned by the continent of <s>Bharata</s>, cultivate a cluster of bliss.

children.text: kastayā na rasamalaṃ kuto jayā vakrapadmamadhisthayā sadā ||
children.translated_text: By her, who is always established upon the curved lotus, what taste would not be sufficient, and whence would there be no victory?
He states the praise of the external <s>druti</s> (liquefied state), beginning with "I shall say."

children.text: ahaṃ kaviḥ abhrakasattvādgaganasārato vimaladrutiṃ pakṣe vimalā cāsau drutiśceti vigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I, the poet, from mica-essence, from the essence of <s>gagana</s> (mica), produce a pure <s>druti</s>." Alternatively, the analysis is: it is pure, and it is <s>druti</s>.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭāṃ akhilaguṇagaṇādhārām akhilāśca te guṇagaṇāśca guṇapaṭalāśca teṣāṃ yā ādhārā tāṃ bahavo guṇās tiṣṭhantyasyāmiti vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of what sort? It is the support of the entire multitude of qualities. All those qualities and groups of qualities are the mass of qualities; it is their support. The explanation is that many qualities abide in it.

children.text: sā rasabhūtā drutiḥ rasaṃ sūtāṃ nibadhnāti niścayena badhnātītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>druti</s>, being of the nature of <s>rasa</s>, binds <s>sūta</s>; that is, it certainly binds mercury.
While being of what sort?

children.text: militā satī tulyamiśritā satī punaḥ drutiḥ sukhena milati patrāder durmilāpatvāt ||
children.translated_text: When joined, that is, when mixed in equal measure. Again, the <s>druti</s> combines easily, because leaves and the like are difficult to combine.
He states the procedure for <s>druti</s>, beginning with "by <s>vajravallī</s>."

children.text: vajravallyāḥ svarasena svakīyena rasena gaganamabhrasattvaṃ sauvarcalānvitaṃ rucakasahitaṃ piṣṭaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the fresh juice of <s>vajravallī</s>, that is, with its own juice, one should make <s>gagana</s>, mica-essence, pounded together with <s>sauvarcala</s> and mixed with <s>rucaka</s>; this is to be supplied.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ gaganaṃ niculapuṭair vetasadravabhāvanābhiḥ pakvaṃ vahnipuṭitaṃ tatpakvaṃ san nirlepaṃ saṃparkavarjitaṃ rasarūpaṃ bhavati pāradasya rūpamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind of <s>gagana</s>? Cooked by <s>nicula</s> heating-pits and by impregnations with liquid from cane, heated in the fire-pit, and, when so cooked, free from adhesion and devoid of contact, it becomes <s>rasa</s>-like; that is, it takes the form of mercury.
He states another method, beginning with "goat."

children.text: drujātarabhrakasattvaṃ abhrakasatvaṃ gaganasāraṃ mūṣāyāṃ vajrasaṃjñāyāṃ drutaṃ sat rasasaṃnibhaṃ bhavati pāradabhūtam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mica-essence produced from melted mica-essence, the essence of <s>gagana</s>, when melted in a crucible called <s>vajra</s>, becomes like <s>rasa</s>; that is, it becomes mercurial.

children.text: kena ajajalaśataparibhāvitakapitindukacūrṇavāpamātreṇa ajaḥ chāgastasya jalena mūtreṇa śataṃ śatavāraṃ paribhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ yatkapitindukacūrṇaṃ tasya vāpamātreṇa drute'bhrasattve vāpe ||
children.translated_text: By what means? Merely by casting in powder of <s>kapitinduka</s> that has been impregnated a hundred times with goat-water. The goat is a she-goat; its water is urine. The powder of <s>kapitinduka</s> is impregnated one hundred times and heated in a sweat-pit, and only that is cast into the melted mica-essence.
Mica-essence, melted by the application of fire, remains in a fluid form.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ sattvaṃ nijarasaśataparibhāvitetyādi nijarasena svakīyadraveṇa paribhāvitaṃ yatkañcukikandotthacūrṇaṃ tasya āvāpena yathā śatabhāvitakañcukikandotthacūrṇena sattvaṃ drutamāste tadvatsarvāṇi lohāni drutāni tiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: What sort of <s>sattva</s> (essence)? With powder produced from the tuber of <s>kañcukī</s>, impregnated with its own juice. When that is cast in, just as the <s>sattva</s> remains melted by powder from <s>kañcukī</s>-tuber impregnated a hundred times, so all metals remain melted.
He also states another procedure, beginning with "<s>gagana</s>."

children.text: gaganaṃ abhrasāraṃ cikuratailaghṛṣṭaṃ cikuratailaṃ keśatailaṃ pratītaṃ grantheṣu tena ghṛṣṭaṃ marditaṃ gomayaliptaṃ gomayena liptaṃ yathā syāttathā kuliśamūṣāyāṃ vajrābhidhānāyāṃ sudhmātaṃ sat acireṇālpakālena jalākāraṃ bhavatītyanvayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The construction is: <s>gagana</s>, the essence of mica, rubbed with <s>cikura</s>-oil, that is, the well-known hair-oil in the treatises, smeared with cow-dung, that is, coated with cow-dung, and thoroughly smelted in a crucible called <s>kuliśa</s> or <s>vajra</s>, quickly becomes water-like.
He states the general procedure for mica-<s>druti</s>, beginning with "<s>gagana</s>."

children.text: ihāsmin śāstre sattve gaganasāre jāte sāṅgatayā gaganadrutiḥ bhavatītyadhyāhāryam ||
children.translated_text: Here, in this treatise, when <s>sattva</s>, the essence of <s>gagana</s>, has arisen, one should supply: <s>gagana-druti</s> comes into being together with its ancillary parts.

children.text: ayaṃ pratyakṣāntargataḥ hi niścitaṃ rasasya sūtasya saṃpradāyo jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This should certainly be known as the tradition of <s>rasa</s>, that is, of <s>sūta</s>, included under direct perception.

children.text: punaḥ prathamādau sattvaṃ abhrasāraṃ nipātya tasmindrute sattve vahninā dravarūpe sati vāpaḥ kāryaḥ kathitauṣadhīnāṃ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, first mica-essence is to be made to fall; when that melted <s>sattva</s> has become fluid by fire, a casting-in of the stated medicines is to be performed; this is to be supplied.
Now he states the procedure for gold-<s>druti</s>, beginning with "the dust of the body of <s>suragopa</s>."

children.text: indragopaśarīracūrṇaṃ suradālīphalaiḥ samāṃśakaiḥ suragopacūrṇatulyabhāgaiḥ kṛtvā vāpo deyaḥ drute satyuparikṣepa iti suvarṇe vāpe kṛte suvarṇaṃ drutamāste kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ rasaprakhyaṃ jalatulyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should make the powder of the body of <s>indragopa</s> with equal parts of <s>suradālī</s> fruits, that is, with parts equal to the <s>suragopa</s> powder, and the casting-in should be given. When, after melting, this is thrown in from above, and when casting-in has been done in gold, the gold remains melted. Of what sort? Like <s>rasa</s>, that is, like water.
He states another procedure, beginning with "now."

children.text: athendragopadevadālīyogakathanānantaraṃ kanakaṃ hema nijarasaparibhāvitaṃ yat suradālīcūrṇaṃ tasya vāpamātreṇa galite hemni kṣepamātreṇa drutamevāste galitam evāvatiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ punaḥ kanakaṃ kāṭhinyaṃ sthiratvaṃ na labhate iti cirakālaprayojanam ||
children.translated_text: After the statement of the combination of <s>indragopa</s> and <s>devadālī</s>, gold, that is, <s>hema</s>, by the mere casting-in of powder of <s>suradālī</s> impregnated with its own juice, when it is thrown into melted gold, remains melted alone, that is, remains in the molten state. Again, the gold does not regain hardness or firmness. This is useful for a long time.
Now he states the procedure for <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, beginning with "<s>suradālī</s>."

children.text: suradālībhasmagalitaṃ suradālī devadālī tasyāḥ bhasma dāhasambhūtaṃ tena galitaṃ trisaptakṛtvā ekaviṃśativāraṃ gojalaṃ surabhimūtraṃ bhāvitaṃ kuryādityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Melted with the ash of <s>suradālī</s>: <s>suradālī</s> is <s>devadālī</s>; its ash is produced by burning. With that it is melted, and it should be impregnated with cow-water, that is, cow urine, three times seven times, namely twenty-one times; this is to be supplied.

children.text: atha mūṣāgataṃ vajrasaṃjñāyāṃ sthitaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāraṃ vāpena nikṣepaṇena jalasadṛśaṃ jalatulyaṃ kurute karmaviditi śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the knower of the operation makes <s>tīkṣṇa</s>-essence placed in the crucible called <s>vajra</s> water-like, equal to water, by casting-in.
Now he states the procedure for <s>mākṣika-druti</s>, beginning with "tortoise."

children.text: kūrmāsthi śilājatukaṃ pratītaṃ meṣī meṣapatnī mṛgo hariṇaḥ gauḥ pratītā pratīto vā teṣāṃ yānyasthīni tair nirvāpitā yā kāñcī svarṇamākṣikaṃ sā jalasadṛśī bhavati kiyatkālaparimāṇaṃ sadā nityaṃ punaḥ drutāyāṃ galitāyāṃ vāpo deyaḥ vāpo nikṣepaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Tortoise bone, the well-known <s>śilājatu</s>, a ewe, that is, the wife of a ram, a deer, and a cow are well known; or, with their bones, <s>kāñcī</s>, gold-<s>mākṣika</s>, when quenched, becomes like water. For how long? Always, continually. Again, when it has melted, a casting-in should be given; <s>vāpa</s> means casting-in.
He states the authority for the general mica-<s>druti</s>, beginning with "mica-<s>druti</s>."

children.text: gaganadravaḥ aviśeṣā sāmānyāpi vidhānena kṛtā nirlepā asparśā samā sūtatulyabhāgayojitā satī āroṭaṃ rasanajaṃ pūrvasaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaṃ sūtaṃ badhnāti kena dvandvayogena ubhayamelāpakauṣadhena ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gagana-drava</s>, the fluid of mica, even when not specific but common, if made according to the procedure, free from adhesion, without contact, and combined with an equal part like <s>sūta</s>, binds <s>āroṭa</s>, mercury born from <s>rasa</s> and refined by earlier processes. By what means? By <s>dvandva-yoga</s>, the medicine that joins the two together.
The word <s>hi</s> has the sense of what is appropriate.
He states the combining of the things mentioned earlier, beginning with "<s>kṛṣṇa</s>."

children.text: imā drutayaḥ soṣṇatuṣakarīṣādinā tāpite khalve mṛditāḥ satyo milanti rasena saha tathā kāryam ||
children.translated_text: These <s>druti</s>s (liquefying preparations), when heated in a mortar with warm husk, cow-dung, and the like and then triturated, combine with <s>rasa</s> (mercury); it should be done in that way.
By means of what? By black <s>aguru</s>, musk, and camphor.

children.text: kṛṣṇāgarukastūrikāghanasāraiḥ kṛtvā na kevalametaiḥ rasonasitarāmaṭhaiśca laśunaśarkarāhiṅgubhiḥ punaḥ strīkusumapalāśabījarasaiḥ strīkusumaṃ ca palāśasya bījāni ca rasaśceti dvaṃdvaḥ etaistribhiryogaiḥ pṛthagbhūtairmilanti sarvaiśceti ||
children.translated_text: By black <s>aguru</s>, musk, and <s>ghanasāra</s> (camphor); not only by these, but also by <s>rasona</s>, <s>sitā</s>, and <s>rāmaṭha</s>, that is, garlic, sugar, and asafoetida. Again, by the juices of <s>strīkusuma</s> and <s>palāśa</s> seeds: <s>strīkusuma</s>, the seeds of <s>palāśa</s>, and the juice form a compound. By these three formulae, taken separately, they combine; and they combine by all of them together as well.
Thus he states the greatness of bound <s>rasarāja</s>, beginning with "thus."

children.text: iti pūrvoktena drutividhānena baddho rasarājaḥ sūtaḥ ekena palena ṣoḍaśikayā kalpāyutaṃ jīvitaṃ kurute kalpānām ayutaṃ sahasraparimāṇaṃ jīvitamiti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the previously stated procedure for <s>druti</s>, <s>rasarāja</s>, that is <s>sūta</s> (mercury), when bound, produces a life of ten thousand kalpas with one <s>pala</s>, by a sixteenth part; that is, a life measured by an <s>ayuta</s>, a thousandfold number, of kalpas.

children.text: kasmāt nityaṃ yathā syāttathā guñjāmātropayogataḥ dinaṃ dinaṃ prati raktikāparimāṇasya rasasya yo'sau upayogastena ||
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because of constant use in a quantity of one <s>guñjā</s>, namely through the use, day by day, of a <s>raktikā</s>-measure of the <s>rasa</s>.
He says that <s>rasa</s> digested by the procedure of morsels is efficacious, beginning with "now."

children.text: atha drutiyogānantaraṃ rasaḥ sūtaḥ pūrvoktagrāsakramāt yojitakavalakramāt vidhivat śāstroktavidhānena biḍādinā jarate ca punaretāḥ pūrvoktadrutayo rasarājaphaladā bhavanti sūte prayuktāḥ phaladāḥ syurityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, after the <s>druti</s>-formula, the <s>rasa</s>, the <s>sūta</s>, is digested according to the previously stated sequence of morsels, that is, the arranged sequence of mouthfuls, in due form, by the method taught in the śāstra, with <s>biḍa</s> and the rest. Again, these previously stated <s>druti</s>s become bestowers of the fruit of <s>rasarāja</s>; the meaning is that, when applied to <s>sūta</s>, they give their fruit.

children.text: adhikadruter jāraṇād adhikaguṇe raso bhavatītyāha samajīrṇa iti ||
children.translated_text: He says that <s>rasa</s> becomes more efficacious from digesting an increased <s>druti</s>, beginning with "equally digested."
That means: that in which an equal, same-part <s>druti</s> has been digested.

children.text: drute dviguṇā yā drutiḥ tasyāścaraṇāt kramaśaḥ koṭivedhī koṭyaṃśena vedhakaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>druti</s> is double in the melted state, by its successive course it becomes capable of transmuting at the ratio of one part in a crore.
The point is that, as the portion of <s>druti</s> increases, it is certainly greater.
He states the qualities arising from increase of morsels, beginning with "sixteen."

children.text: yadā ṣoḍaśagrāsā vā dvātriṃśadgrāsā vā catuḥṣaṣṭigrāsā jīrṇā jāraṇamāpannā bhavanti tadā rasendraḥ sūtaḥ lohaṃ dhātusaṃjñakaṃ vidhyati vedhaṃ karoti kutaḥ dhūmāvalokanataḥ dhūmasya yadavalokanaṃ darśanaṃ ||
children.translated_text: When sixteen morsels, or thirty-two morsels, or sixty-four morsels have been digested and have undergone <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion), then <s>rasendra</s>, <s>sūta</s>, pierces metal, the substance called <s>loha</s>; it produces <s>vedha</s> (transmuting penetration). By what means? By the sight of smoke, that is, by the seeing of smoke.
With mind brought under the control of understanding, a person of disciplined self should perform action that benefits others,

children.text: arcīva śobhāṃ labhate parātparāṃ parāpavādādapi saṃnivṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, having turned away even from slandering others, he obtains a splendor beyond the highest, like a flame.
And the casting of gold and the like into <s>sūta</s> placed in an oiled apparatus,
