which produces an increase of <s>vedha</s> in metal, is called <s>sāraṇa</s>.
Thus runs the definition.
Considering <s>sāraṇa</s> excellent, he praises it, beginning with "thus."

children.text: iti pūrvoktena vidhānena rakto'pi rāgavānapi rasendraḥ sūtaḥ jaritabījo'pi jāritāni bījāni yasminniti sāraṇarahitaḥ sāraṇā vakṣyamāṇasaṃskārastena varjitaḥ vyāpī na bhavati dehe lohe ca vyāpako na syāt hi niścitaṃ athavāpi sāraṇārahito rasendraḥ ṣaṇḍhatāṃ yāti nirvīryatvam āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the previously stated procedure, even when red, that is, possessing coloration, and even when its <s>bīja</s>s have been digested, <s>rasendra</s>, <s>sūta</s>, if devoid of <s>sāraṇa</s>, the procedure to be explained below, does not become pervasive; it is not able to pervade the body and the metal. This is certain. Or else <s>rasendra</s> without <s>sāraṇa</s> falls into impotence, that is, loses its potency.
For <s>sāraṇa</s> he states fat-oil, beginning with "frog."

children.text: maṇḍūko bhekaḥ matsyo jalacaraviśeṣaḥ kacchapaḥ kamaṭhaḥ pratītaḥ jalaukāḥ pratītāḥ ahiḥ sarpaḥ sūkaro varāhaḥ ādiśabdād gomahiṣagajoṣṭrakharanarakarkaṭaśiśumārā api grāhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇḍūka</s> is a frog; <s>matsya</s> is a particular aquatic creature, a fish; <s>kacchapa</s> is the well-known tortoise; <s>jalaukā</s> is the well-known leech; <s>ahi</s> is a snake; <s>sūkara</s> is a boar. By the word "and so on," cow, buffalo, elephant, camel, donkey, human, crab, and porpoise are also to be included.

children.text: atha teṣāṃ madhye ekaikasya pṛthaktvena vasāṃ saṃyojya sāraṇaṃ tailaṃ sāraṇameva tailaṃ tatpacediti vahninā iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, among these, one should add the fat of each one separately and cook the <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, the oil that is itself <s>sāraṇa</s>; "with fire" is to be supplied.
He states a particular kind of <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, beginning with "<s>jyotiṣmatī</s>."

children.text: jyotiṣmatīvibhītakakarañjakaṭutumbītailaṃ jyotiṣmatī kaṅguṇī vibhītakaḥ kalidrumaḥ karañjaḥ pratītaḥ kaṭutumbī kaṭukā yā tumbī etāsāṃ tailaṃ ekaṃ ato dviguṇito yo raktakaṣāyaḥ raktagaṇasya kvāthaḥ taṃ niyojya pūrvasaṃbandhāt ||
children.translated_text: The oil of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>karañja</s>, and bitter gourd is meant: <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> is <s>kaṅguṇī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s> is <s>kalidruma</s>, <s>karañja</s> is well known, and <s>kaṭutumbī</s> is the bitter gourd. Having used one oil from these, one should add a red decoction twice that amount, namely a decoction of the red group, because of the connection with the preceding passage.

children.text: kena saha caturguṇavasayā tathā tailataḥ caturguṇitena dugdhena saha pacet pākaṃ kuryāditi ||
children.translated_text: With what? Together with fat four times that amount, and likewise with milk four times the oil, one should cook it, that is, perform the cooking.
For the preparation of <s>sāraṇa</s> oil he states the red group, beginning with "pomegranate."

children.text: dāḍimaṃ pratītaṃ palāśo brahmavṛkṣaḥ bandhūkapuṣpaṃ madhyāhnavikāśikusumaṃ rajanī haridrā etābhiḥ aruṇasahitābhiḥ aruṇaṃ āraktaṃ yaddravyaṃ kārpāsakusumādikaṃ tatsahitābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dāḍima</s>, pomegranate, is well known; <s>palāśa</s> is the <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>; <s>bandhūka</s> flower is the flower that opens at midday; <s>rajanī</s> is turmeric. These are to be used together with red substances, that is, with red-colored materials such as cotton flowers.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭo'yaṃ raktavargaḥ mañjiṣṭhālākṣārasacandanasahitaḥ mañjiṣṭhā pratītā lākṣārasaḥ alaktakaḥ candanaṃ raktacandanam ||
children.translated_text: Of what special kind is this red group? It is accompanied by <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s>, lac juice, and sandalwood: <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> is well known, lac juice is <s>alaktaka</s>, and sandalwood means red sandalwood.
He states the paste for the <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, beginning with "coral."

children.text: vidrumaṃ latāmaṇir bhūnāgamalaṃ gaṇḍūpadapurīṣaṃ makṣikādhvāṅkṣaśalabhānāṃ makṣikā jīvaviśeṣaḥ dhvāṅkṣāḥ kākāḥ śalabhaḥ pataṅgaḥ iti haimaḥ teṣāṃ viṭ śakṛt punarmahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalaṃ krameṇa kalāṃśena ṣoḍaśāṃśena kalkaṃ prativāpaṃ dattvā pūrvatailamuttārayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidruma</s> is coral; <s>bhūnāga-mala</s> is earthworm excrement; the excrement of flies, crows, and locusts is meant. <s>Makṣikā</s> is a particular living creature, <s>dhvāṅkṣa</s>s are crows, and <s>śalabha</s> is a moth, according to the <s>Haima</s>; their excrement is intended. Again, the earwax of she-buffaloes is to be added in sequence, in a <s>kalā</s> portion, a sixteenth part, as the paste, and then the previous oil should be taken off.
He states the use of the perfected oil, beginning with "cloth."

children.text: tatsiddhatailaṃ paṭagālitaṃ vastrapūtaṃ gṛhītvā tadanu tatpaścāt ||
children.translated_text: Having taken that perfected oil, strained through cloth, that is, filtered through a cloth, after that, namely thereafter...

children.text: sampūrṇadīrghamūṣāyāṃ gostanākārāyāṃ taptataile koṣṇasāraṇataile sūtaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: In a complete long crucible shaped like a cow's teat, he should place <s>sūta</s> in heated oil, that is, in the slightly warm oil used for <s>sāraṇa</s>.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā bījaṃ samaṃ samabhāgaṃ rasatulyaṃ yadbhāvyaṃ mahābījaṃ tat bhāvitaṃ kṛtvetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having made the <s>bīja</s> equal, of the same amount, equal to the <s>rasa</s>, the great <s>bīja</s> that is to be impregnated, that is, having made it impregnated.
He states the procedure for the <s>sāraṇa</s>-apparatus, beginning with "the crucible."

children.text: samakālam ekakālaṃ yathā syāttathā bījaṃ mūṣāntarnikṣipya tato'nantaraṃ mūṣāvaktraṃ sthagayet ācchādayet ||
children.translated_text: At the same time, that is, in one operation, in such a way, after placing the <s>bīja</s> inside the crucible, then immediately he should close the mouth of the crucible, that is, cover it.
With what? With a cloth moist with oil, a garment wetted with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭena latādvayena vastracīradvayena protaṃ ca tadvitataṃ vistīrṇaṃ ca tat naddhaṃ baddhaṃ tena ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind? With two strips, two torn pieces of cloth; and it is threaded and spread out, extended, and tied, bound with that.
Being undiminished, it combines; the meaning is that it is not diminished.

children.text: sūte milati baddho jñeyaḥ bījaiḥ saha milito baddho bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it combines with <s>sūta</s>, it should be known as bound; the meaning is that, when combined with the <s>bīja</s>s, it becomes bound.
By the statement of colors such as yellow, it is also indicated that this should be done.
After the <s>sāraṇa</s> of <s>sūta</s> and <s>bīja</s>, he states the <s>sāraṇa</s> with gold, beginning with "in the same way."

children.text: tadvat pūrvavidhānena gabhīramūṣe dīrghamūṣāyāṃ sāraṇatailārdraṃ sāraṇatailāplutaṃ eva niścayena rasarājaṃ kuryāditi śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, by the previous procedure, in a deep crucible, that is, a long crucible, one should certainly make the king of <s>rasa</s> soaked in <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil, that is, flooded with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil; this is what remains to be supplied.

children.text: tadanu tatpaścātsūtāddviguṇaṃ yatkanakaṃ hema tadatra dattvā pratisārayetsāraṇaṃ kuryātpūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: After that, subsequently, having put in here gold, <s>hema</s>, twice the amount of the <s>sūta</s>, one should cause it to undergo <s>sāraṇa</s>, as before.
He states another procedure, beginning with "with <s>bīja</s>."

children.text: prakāśasthaṃ prakāśamūṣāgataṃ sūtaṃ triguṇena bījena anusārayet pratisārayet ||
children.translated_text: One should make the <s>sūta</s> situated openly, placed in an open crucible, undergo <s>sāraṇa</s>, or repeated <s>sāraṇa</s>, with three times as much <s>bīja</s>.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā īṣadalpaṃ nāgaṃ dattvā trividhāyāṃ sāraṇāyāmevaṃ vidheyam iti ||
children.translated_text: Having done what? Having added a little <s>nāga</s>, lead, this is to be done in the threefold <s>sāraṇa</s> procedure.
He states the <s>sāraṇa</s>-apparatus, beginning with "having made."

children.text: prathamaṃ dīrghāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā ca punaḥ tāṃ bandhitatribhāgapraṇālikāṃ bandhitā tribhāge praṇālikā yasyāḥ sā tāṃ ca kṛtvā tasyāgre yantrasyāgre praṇālikāyāṃ mūṣāntarityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: First, after making a long crucible, and then making it one whose tube is fastened at one third, he should make such a crucible; at the front of that apparatus, in the tube, the meaning is inside the crucible.

children.text: sudṛḍhamṛttikāliptā sacchidrā randhrasahitā prakaṭamūṣā prakāśamūṣā kāryeti yantram ||
children.translated_text: The apparatus is that an open crucible, or exposed crucible, smeared with very firm clay and having holes, should be made.

children.text: tasminyantre sāraṇatailānvitaṃ rasaṃ prakṣipya tato'nantaraṃ tulyaṃ kanakaṃ pradrāvya gālayitvā tasminneva tapte yantre kṣipte sati raso milati ekatāṃ yāti ||
children.translated_text: After placing <s>rasa</s> furnished with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil in that apparatus, and then melting and pouring an equal amount of gold, when it is placed in that same heated apparatus, the <s>rasa</s> combines and becomes one.
He states another apparatus, beginning with "having made."

children.text: pūrvavaddīrghāṃ dhūrtakusumasaṃkāśāṃ dhattūrapuṣpasaṃkāśāṃ pūrvayantranalikāyāḥ sthāne evaṃvidhāṃ ṣaḍaṅgulāṃ nalikāṃ kuryād iti vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: As before, one should make a long tube, six fingers long, resembling a <s>dhūrta</s> flower, that is, resembling a <s>dhattūra</s> blossom, in place of the tube of the previous apparatus; this is the clear sense.

children.text: mūṣāpi adho vilagnā nalikāyāstalabhāge mūṣā vilagnā saṃlagnā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: A crucible too should be attached below: the crucible should be affixed, joined, to the lower part of the tube.
And that should be smeared with clay, with earthen paste.

children.text: punarapi aparā sūkṣmā nālikā saptāṅgulā saptāṅgulaparimāṇā sudṛḍhā manoharakaṭhinā kāryā yathā madhye ṣaḍaṅgulanālikāntaḥ praviśati tadvattathā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: Again, another fine tube, seven fingers long, of seven-finger measure, very firm and beautifully hard, should be made, in such a way that it enters within the middle, inside the six-finger tube.

children.text: kiṃbhūtā dṛḍhamukhā dṛḍhaṃ mukhaṃ yasyāḥ sā evaṃrūpā tasmin saṃsiddhe yantre sāraṇatailānvitaḥ sūtaḥ kṣiptaḥ san madanaruddhamukhaḥ kāryaḥ madanena sikthakena ruddhaṃ mudritaṃ mukhaṃ yasya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: What kind? Firm-mouthed, one whose mouth is firm, of such a form. When that apparatus has been prepared, <s>sūta</s> furnished with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil, once placed in it, should have its mouth closed with <s>madana</s>, that is, with wax, so that its mouth is stopped and sealed.

children.text: tadanu tatpaścāt hemakoṣṭhikayā hemno yā koṣṭhī eva koṣṭhikā tayā hema svarṇaṃ pradrāvya drāvayitvā tatra kṣipet ityadhyāhāryam ||
children.translated_text: After that, subsequently, with a gold vessel, that is, with a small vessel for gold, one should melt gold, <s>svarṇa</s>, and place it there; this must be supplied.

children.text: tasminyantre madhye'ntaḥ nalikāgraṃ nalikāyāḥ saptāṅgulāyā agrabhāgaṃ kṣiptvā adhomukhīṃ kuryāt punarūrdhvaṃ bhārākrāntāṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: In that apparatus, in the middle, inside, after inserting the tip of the tube, the front part of the seven-finger tube, he should turn it downward; then he should press it down from above with a weight.

children.text: iti kṛte sati rasaḥ sarati hemnā milati na saṃdehaḥ niyatamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this has been done, the <s>rasa</s> moves and combines with the gold; there is no doubt, the meaning is that it is certain.
He states the procedure for another apparatus, beginning with "having made."

children.text: aṣṭāṅgulamūṣāṃ aṣṭāṅgulaparimāṇadīrghāṃ dhūrtakusumopamāṃ kanakapuṣpasadṛśāṃ dṛḍhāṃ kaṭhināṃ ślakṣṇāṃ masṛṇāṃ evaṃvidhāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvā aparā dvitīyā saptāṅgulā saptāṅgulaparimāṇadīrghā sacchidrā randhrayuktā sā madhyagatā antaḥpraviṣṭā kāryā apītyavaśyaṃ iti mūṣādvayayantraṃ siddham ||
children.translated_text: After making an eight-finger crucible, long by an eight-finger measure, resembling a <s>dhūrta</s> flower, similar to a golden blossom, firm, hard, smooth, and polished, a second one, seven fingers long, long by a seven-finger measure, having holes and perforated, should also certainly be placed in the middle, inserted inside. Thus the apparatus of two crucibles is complete.

children.text: taccāha pūrvoktāyāmantaḥpraviṣṭāyāṃ saptāṅgulāyāṃ sūtaṃ tailasaṃyuktaṃ sāraṇatailasahitaṃ prakṣipya niruddhatāṃ ca kṛtvā nirdhūmaṃ yathā syāt tathā karṣāgnau mūṣāṃ sthāpya punaḥ kiṃ kṛtvā susaṃdhitāṃ sandhimudritāṃ kṛtvā pūrvavatsārayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He states that: in the previously described seven-finger crucible inserted inside, after placing <s>sūta</s> joined with oil, together with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil, and after making it closed, setting the crucible on a <s>karṣa</s>-fire so that it is smokeless, and then sealing the joints well, he should cause <s>sāraṇa</s> as before.
He states the procedure for another apparatus: two crucibles should be made.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭe tadagrato vitastimātranalike vitastiparimāṇe nalike yayoste evaṃvidhe sudṛḍhe ubhe kārye ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind? They have tubes in front of them measuring a span; the intended sense is that both should be very firm and of this kind.

children.text: tayormadhye ekā mūṣā uttānā kāryā aparā nimneti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Between the two, one crucible should be made upward-facing, and the sense is that the other is lowered.

children.text: uttānā kiṃviśiṣṭā niśchidrā nirvraṇā chidramudritā chidraṃ mudritaṃ yasyāṃ tanau mūṣāśarīre iti ||
children.translated_text: What kind is the upward-facing one? It is without holes, unbroken, its holes sealed in the body of the crucible.

children.text: taccāha pūrvaṃ prathamaṃ sūtaṃ yantre pūrvokte sāraṇatailānvitaṃ dattvā bhuvi nidhāpya tasyāṃ uktāyāṃ uttānāyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ bījaṃ mahābījaṃ samāvṛtya dravīkṛtya dattvetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He states that also. First, as previously described, after placing <s>sūta</s> in the apparatus together with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil and setting it on the ground, in that described upward-facing crucible one should cover the <s>bīja</s>, the great <s>bīja</s>, melt it, and introduce it; this is the meaning.

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ bījaṃ svacchamamalaṃ dravarūpaṃ jñātvā chidrasaṃsthitaṃ kuryāt chidrāntaḥ kṣipedityabhiprāyaḥ chidrāntaḥkṣepaṇāt bījaṃ rasasyopari patati sati sūtaṃ asaṃdehaṃ yathā syāttathā badhnāti bīje chidrāntaḥkṣepaṇānantaraṃ chidramacchidraṃ syādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after that, when one knows that the <s>bīja</s> is clear, stainless, and in liquid form, one should place it in the aperture; the intended meaning is that one should throw it inside the aperture. Because of its being thrown into the aperture, the <s>bīja</s> falls upon the <s>rasa</s>, and when that has happened it binds the <s>sūta</s> without doubt. After the <s>bīja</s> has been thrown into the aperture, the aperture should become without an aperture, meaning closed.
This is the passage beginning with "she."

children.text: punaḥ sā vitastimātranalikā prakāśamūṣā ardhāṅgulasuniviṣṭā mūṣāntaḥ praviṣṭā nyubjā adhomukhī kāryā tasyāḥ prakāśamūṣāyāḥ nalikā praṇālikā vidhinā śāstravārtikasaṃpradāyena kāryā yathordhve sūto bhavedadho bījamityarthaḥ mūṣām ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Again, that tube measuring a span, the open crucible, well inserted by half a finger's breadth and entered into the crucible, should be made inverted, facing downward. The tube, that is the channel, of that open crucible should be made according to rule, according to the teaching and transmitted instruction of the science, so that the <s>sūta</s> is above and the <s>bīja</s> below. This is the meaning. The passage begins with "the crucible."

children.text: mūṣāṃ nirudhya randhraṃ dūrīkṛtya vidhinā koṣṭhe koṣṭhīyantre sā mūṣā dhmātā kāryā drutaṃ dravarūpaṃ kṛtaṃ bījaṃ jñātvā parivartya ca mūṣāyāṃ bījasya parivartanaṃ kṛtvā tato bījaṃ sūtarājaṃ badhnātīti ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed the crucible and removed any opening, according to rule, in the furnace, the furnace-apparatus, that crucible should be blown. Having understood that the <s>bīja</s> has been melted and made liquid, and after turning it over, that is, after turning the <s>bīja</s> in the crucible, then the <s>bīja</s> should bind the king <s>sūta</s>.
Now he states another apparatus, beginning with "or."

children.text: vidhinā sāraṇavidhānena ḍamarukayantre uktalakṣaṇapātanakaraṇocite yantre sūto niyojitaḥ san sarati bījena milati ||
children.translated_text: According to rule, by the procedure of <s>sāraṇa</s>, in a <s>ḍamaruka</s>-apparatus, an apparatus suited to carrying out the previously described distillation, the <s>sūta</s>, when applied, flows; it joins with the <s>bīja</s>.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā rasendro niyojitaḥ jñātvā tatkarmakauśalyaṃ rasendrakarmaprāvīṇyaṃ jñātveti ||
children.translated_text: What has been done before <s>rasendra</s> is applied? Having understood skill in that operation, that is, having understood proficiency in the operation of <s>rasendra</s>.
To make the preceding statement firm, he says the passage beginning with "krāmaṇa."

children.text: sūto vidhinoktavidhānena krāmaṇocitā yā vasā maṇḍūkādīnāṃ tā eva ādayo yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ yogātsarati sāraṇā syāt punarbījayuto'pi sūtaḥ capalatvātilaghutvāt capalatvaṃ cañcalatvaṃ ca atilaghutvaṃ ca tasmāddhetoḥ avipluṣaḥ sthiraḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> flows by the prescribed procedure, through the conjunction of the fat suitable for <s>krāmaṇa</s>, namely the fats of frogs and the like. That is <s>sāraṇa</s>. Again, <s>sūta</s>, even when joined with <s>bīja</s>, because of its capillarity and extreme lightness, where capillarity is mobility and extreme lightness is also meant, should for that reason be made unscattered and stable.
He states the previously mentioned qualities, beginning with "it flows."

children.text: pūrvavidhānā sūtaḥ sarati sāritaḥ sūto mukhaṃ na dahati hastapādādi ca aṅgavibhāgaṃ naiva dahati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> flows by the preceding procedure. <s>Sūta</s> that has been caused to flow does not burn the mouth, nor does it burn divisions of the body such as hands and feet.

children.text: punaḥ phaṇiyogāt nāgasaṃyogataḥ mākṣikayutahemagairikayā saha tāpyamilitasvarṇagairikayā sārdhaṃ krāmati ||
children.translated_text: Again, through conjunction with <s>phaṇi</s>, that is, through conjunction with lead, it penetrates together with <s>mākṣika</s>-joined gold ochre, that is, with gold ochre combined with <s>tāpya</s>.
He states an easy procedure for <s>sāraṇa</s>, beginning with "mākṣika."

children.text: kanakaṃ hema mākṣikasattvayogāt phaṇisaṃyogānnāgasaṃyogācca śīghraṃ dravati kanake dravati sati vidhinā sāraṇatailādinā saṃsāryate sāraṇā kriyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Gold, that is, <s>hema</s>, quickly melts through conjunction with the essence of <s>mākṣika</s> and through conjunction with <s>phaṇi</s>, that is, through conjunction with lead. When the gold has melted, it is made to flow according to rule with <s>sāraṇa</s>-oil and so on; that is, <s>sāraṇa</s> is performed.
He states the qualities of mercury produced by <s>sāraṇa</s>, beginning with "therefore."

children.text: tasmāddhetoḥ sūto dravyavidhāyī syāt iti śeṣaḥ dravyakartetyartha ||
children.translated_text: For that reason <s>sūta</s> would be a producer of substance; this is to be supplied. The meaning is that it makes substance.

children.text: alaghunā bījena analpaparimāṇena mahābījena sāritaḥ san samasāritaḥ san baddho bhavet ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it has been made to flow with a not-light <s>bīja</s>, with a great <s>bīja</s> of no small measure, that is, when it has been made to flow equally, it becomes bound; this is to be supplied.

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ samāvarto dravaṇaṃ syāt vahnidhamanāt iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the crucible there is complete melting, liquefaction; "from blowing the fire" is to be supplied.
He states the sequence of <s>sāraṇa</s>, beginning with "having flowed."
"<s>Sūta</s> that has flowed and been turned" is to be analyzed as: it has been made to flow and it has been turned.

children.text: yaḥ samānabījena tulyamahābījena milati sa sāryaḥ yo dviguṇena milati saḥ pratisāryaḥ yaśca triguṇena so'nusārya iti sāraṇākramo darśitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which joins with an equal <s>bīja</s>, an equal great <s>bīja</s>, is <s>sārya</s>; that which joins with twice as much is <s>pratisārya</s>; and that which joins with three times as much is <s>anusārya</s>. Thus the sequence of <s>sāraṇa</s> is shown.
He states the qualities of the sequence of <s>sāraṇa</s>, beginning with "hundred."

children.text: yaḥ sāryaḥ samasāritaḥ sa śatavedhī syād ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intended meaning is that what is <s>sārya</s>, made to flow with an equal amount, is capable of a hundredfold penetration.

children.text: punaḥ pratisāritaḥ dviguṇabījena sārito yaḥ sūtaḥ sa sahasravedhī syāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, that <s>sūta</s> which is <s>pratisārita</s>, made to flow with twice as much <s>bīja</s>, is capable of a thousandfold penetration.

children.text: ca punaḥ anusāritaḥ triguṇabījena sāritaḥ sa ayutena ayutavedhī syāditi vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: And again, that which is <s>anusārita</s>, made to flow with three times as much <s>bīja</s>, is capable of ten thousandfold penetration; this is the explanation.
"According to rule" means by the procedure already stated.

children.text: balābalaṃ jñātvā nyūnādhikyaṃ matvā vidhinā yukta iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having known the strength and weakness, having considered deficiency and excess, it is joined according to rule; this is to be supplied.
He states the distinction of what is <s>anusārita</s> from what is <s>sārita</s> and <s>pratisārita</s>, beginning with "anu."

children.text: tu punaḥ svacchaḥ pradhānasaṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaḥ sūtaḥ anusāritena samaḥ triguṇabījena sārito'nusāritastena tulyo yadi syātsa ca lakṣavedhī syāt ||
children.translated_text: But again, if <s>sūta</s> that is clear and refined by principal operations is equal to what has been <s>anusārita</s>, that is, to what has been made to flow with threefold <s>bīja</s>, then it too is capable of a hundred-thousandfold penetration.

children.text: evaṃ pratisāritaḥ sūtaḥ samena sārito 'yutavedhī syāt ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, <s>sūta</s> that is <s>pratisārita</s>, when made to flow with an equal amount, is capable of ten-thousandfold penetration.

children.text: evaṃ svecchātisvacchavṛddhau vedhasyāpi vṛddhiḥ syāditi rahasyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus the secret is that, as clarity and exceptional clarity increase according to one's wish, penetration also increases.
Then he states the increase of qualities through a superior essence, beginning with "crore."

children.text: sūte sarito bījena grāsanyāyaṃ vihāya samena bījenānusārito yaḥ sa koṭisaṃkhyāṃ dhātūnāmiti śeṣaḥ sūto vidhyati ||
children.translated_text: In <s>sūta</s>, after abandoning the rule of morsel-taking with the <s>bīja</s>, that which has flowed and been <s>anusārita</s> with an equal <s>bīja</s> penetrates a number of metals amounting to a crore; this is to be supplied.
It should be understood that in <s>sūta</s> made to flow as described, there is everywhere a tenfold increase.
He states a special point, beginning with "prati."

children.text: pratisāritaḥ sūto dviguṇabījena vāraikena sārito rasaḥ abjasaṃkhyāṃ vidhyati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> that is <s>pratisārita</s>, <s>rasa</s> made to flow once with twice as much <s>bīja</s>, penetrates a number equal to an <s>abja</s>.

children.text: tu punar anusāritaḥ triguṇena bījena vāraikena sāritaḥ sūtaḥ kharvavedhī syāt kharvasaṃkhyāke dravyasaṃbandhaṃ karotītyabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But again, <s>sūta</s> that is <s>anusārita</s>, made to flow once with three times as much <s>bīja</s>, is capable of <s>kharva</s>-penetration; the intended meaning is that it brings about contact with a substance numbered as a <s>kharva</s>.

children.text: evamuktaprakāreṇa vidhinā śāstrajñavārtikasaṃpradāyena sāraṇayogāt yathepsitaṃ vedhaṃ kurute yathāvāñchitam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the procedure of the kind stated, by the rule and by the tradition of the teachers who know the śāstra and its vārttikas, through the application of <s>sāraṇa</s>, he performs the desired <s>vedha</s> (transmuting penetration); the meaning is, as wished.
Again he states a further detail, beginning with "having followed."

children.text: anusāritena triguṇaprathamagrāsanyāyena bījena sāritaḥ sūto nikharvasaṃkhyākaṃ śulbaṃ vidhyati tu punaḥ pratisāritaḥ ṣaḍguṇaprathamagrāsanyāyena sāritaḥ sūtaḥ padmasaṃkhyākaṃ vidhyati ||
children.translated_text: Mercury subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s> by a seed applied according to the rule of the first morsel being threefold pierces copper to the number called <s>nikharva</s>; again, when subjected to <s>pratisāraṇa</s>, that is, made to undergo <s>sāraṇa</s> according to the rule of the first morsel being sixfold, mercury pierces to the number called <s>padma</s>.

children.text: punar anusārito navaguṇagrāsanyāyena bījena sāritaḥ sūtaḥ śaṅkhasaṃkhyāṃ vidhyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Again, mercury made to undergo <s>sāraṇa</s> by a seed according to the rule of a ninefold morsel pierces to the number called <s>śaṅkha</s>.
Again he states a further detail, beginning with "one should pierce."

children.text: kanakaṃ hema dattvā śanakair nīcais tāvadanuvāhayet yāvaddivyaṃ pravaraṃ kanakaṃ bhavediti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having given gold, that is, <s>hema</s>, one should cause it to flow along slowly and gently until divine, excellent gold is produced; this is to be supplied.
Again, until it opens out all the <s>nāga</s> (lead) completely; the intention is that one should make it entirely exhausted.

children.text: punastatkanakaṃ dviguṇaṃ svato dravyaṃ vidhyet vā sūtakena sāritaṃ sat dravyaṃ kanakaṃ śatasahasrādisaṃkhyāto dviguṇasaṃkhyākaṃ dravyaṃ śulbādikaṃ vidhyed iti rahasyam ||
children.translated_text: Again, that gold, being doubled, may pierce its own substance; or, when a substance has been subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s> with mercury, gold pierces a substance such as copper in a number double the number beginning with a hundred thousand. This is the secret.
Well refined, lodged within the mouth, clear, and beneficial in meaning,
and likewise suited to another, purified, are the deathless-born utterances.
Now he states praise of <s>krāmaṇa</s>, beginning with "thus."

children.text: uktavidhānena kṛtaḥ sāraṇasya vidhir yasmin sūtarāje evaṃvidhiḥ sūtarāṭ balavān bhavediti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the procedure of <s>sāraṇa</s> has been performed by the stated rule in this king of mercury, <s>sūtarāj</s>, such a <s>sūtarāj</s> becomes powerful; this is to be supplied.
Because of what? Because of the conjunction with the operation, that is, because the required act has been performed.

children.text: yādṛk kṛtyaṃ kriyate tādṛk balavān syād ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intention is that it becomes powerful in accordance with whatever operation is performed.

children.text: evaṃvidho'pi krāmaṇārahitaḥ krāmaṇavarjito lohaṃ na viśati lohāntaḥpraveśaṃ na karoti tato hetor lohaṃ dhātuṃ saṃveṣṭya pariveṣṭanaṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhati bāhyarāgadāyī syāditi ||
children.translated_text: Even such a mercury, if without <s>krāmaṇa</s>, that is, deprived of <s>krāmaṇa</s>, does not enter metal; it does not penetrate within the metal. For that reason it remains after wrapping metal, that is, the metallic substance, around itself, having made an enclosing sheath; it only gives an external color.
He states the similarity between body and metal, beginning with "food."
The word "as" is used in the sense of similarity.

children.text: annaṃ godhūmādikaṃ vā dravyaṃ auṣadhaṃ anupānena saha jalādinā sārdhaṃ dhātuṣu māṃsādiṣu saptasu kramate vyāpnoti tathā amunā vakṣyamāṇavidhānena krāmaṇayogāt krāmaṇāya yogaḥ kunaṭīmākṣikaviṣādis tataḥ sūtarājo loharūpyādiṣu viśati bāhyābhyantaraṃ vidhyatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as food, such as wheat, or a medicinal substance, together with an <s>anupāna</s> such as water, proceeds into and pervades the seven bodily constituents such as flesh, so by this procedure to be stated, through the application for <s>krāmaṇa</s>, namely from the compound for <s>krāmaṇa</s> such as <s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and poison, the king of mercury enters metals such as iron and silver and pierces them externally and internally.
He states the <s>krāmaṇa</s> compound, beginning with "magnet and poison."

children.text: kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ viṣaṃ kandajaṃ viṣaṃ kandaviṣāṇi kālakūṭādīni trayodaśa daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ taiḥ ca punaḥ raktatailendragopādyaiḥ rakto raktakavargaḥ tailaṃ kaṅguṇyādeḥ indragopo jīvaviśeṣaḥ ityādyāḥ krāmaṇocitās tacca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> is magnet; <s>viṣa</s> is tuber-born poison, and the tuber-poisons are the thirteen such as <s>kālakūṭa</s>; <s>darada</s> is <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar). With these, and again with such things as red oil and <s>indragopa</s>: "red" means the red group, oil is that of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the like, and <s>indragopa</s> is a particular living creature. These and the like are suitable for <s>krāmaṇa</s>.

children.text: etat śreṣṭhaṃ sarvottamaṃ krāmaṇaṃ anena sūtaḥ krāmati viśati loheṣviti vyāptiḥ tatkrāmaṇaṃ kathitam ||
children.translated_text: This is the best, the most excellent, <s>krāmaṇa</s>. By it mercury advances, that is, enters the metals; that penetrating <s>krāmaṇa</s> has been taught.
The meaning is that it should be applied in coating and in casting-in.
He states another matter, beginning with "with <s>śilā</s>."

children.text: nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ śilayā manohvayā nihato māritaḥ punaḥ vaṅgaṃ śuddhena doṣavarjitena tālena nihataṃ kramaśaḥ krameṇa pīte hemakarmaṇi śukle rūpyakarmaṇi etatkrāmaṇaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ samyak prakāśitaṃ pītakarmaṇi nāgaḥ śuklakarmaṇi vaṅgaṃ ca niyojitavyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> is lead; when it has been struck down, that is, killed, by <s>śilā</s>, namely <s>manohvā</s>, and again when <s>vaṅga</s> has been killed by pure, faultless <s>tāla</s>, this <s>krāmaṇa</s> is fully taught respectively for yellow gold-work and white silver-work. The meaning is that lead is to be applied in gold-work and tin in silver-work.
He states another matter, beginning with "<s>tīkṣṇa</s>."

children.text: daradena hiṅgulena hataṃ māritaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ sāro vidhinā arivargavidhānena tāpyena svarṇamākṣikena māritaṃ śulbaṃ tāmraṃ etadapi krāmaṇaṃ kathitaṃ vā kāntamukhaṃ kāntaṃ lohajāti uktaṃ granthādau tat mukhaṃ pradhānaṃ yasya tat mākṣikairvā māritaṃ niyojyaṃ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tīkṣṇa</s>, the essence, killed with <s>darada</s>, that is, <s>hiṅgula</s>, and copper, killed by <s>tāpya</s>, that is, gold-<s>mākṣika</s>, according to the rule for the enemy-class, is also taught as <s>krāmaṇa</s>. Or else, a preparation whose chief element is <s>kānta</s>, the iron-kind called <s>kānta</s> that was mentioned at the beginning of the book, and which has been killed with <s>mākṣika</s>s, is to be applied; this is to be supplied.
He states a special rule, beginning with "<s>mākṣika</s>-essence."

children.text: mākṣikasattvaṃ tāpyasāraṃ nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ taṃ vihāya nānyatkimapyasti krāmaṇaṃ na krāmaṇamiti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Apart from <s>mākṣika-sattva</s>, the essence of <s>tāpya</s>, and <s>nāga</s>, lead, there is no other <s>krāmaṇa</s> at all; the sense is that it is not <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
The word <s>khalu</s> is used in the sense of inquiry.

children.text: dalasiddhe vidhau saṃskāraiḥ pūrṇatāṃ nīte sati asau vidhiḥ saphalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When, in the method where the leaves have been perfected, the procedure has been brought to fullness by the refining operations, that procedure is fruitful.
Mercury cast into a substance furnished with a diffusive medicine, indeed,

children.text: vedha ityucyate tajjñaiḥ sa ca naikavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: is called <s>vedha</s> by those who know; and that is remembered as being of many kinds.
Thus runs the definition.
He states the topic of the <s>krāmaṇa</s> refinement, beginning with "by this."

children.text: anayā uktayā sāraṇayā saha krāmaṇasaṃskāre kṛte sati raso viśati krāmati punarvedhavidhau kṛte sati rasaḥ svaguṇān prakāśayatīti veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>krāmaṇa</s> refinement has been performed together with this stated <s>sāraṇa</s>, <s>rasa</s> (mercury) enters, that is, advances; again, when the procedure of <s>vedha</s> has been performed, <s>rasa</s> should be known to manifest its own qualities.
He states the procedure of <s>vedha</s>, beginning with "mercury."

children.text: rasaḥ sūtaḥ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ tāpyaṃ mākṣikaṃ gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ manaḥśilā manohvā rājavarttakaṃ rājāvartaṃ vimalaṃ raupyamākṣikaṃ ekavadbhāvadvandvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is mercury; <s>darada</s> is <s>hiṅgula</s>; <s>tāpya</s> is <s>mākṣika</s>; <s>gandhaka</s> is well known; <s>manaḥśilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>; <s>rājavarttaka</s> is <s>rājāvarta</s>; <s>vimala</s> is silver-<s>mākṣika</s>. This is a copulative compound understood as forming one unit.
Copper killed in a covered heating, that is, killed by the covered heating of mercury and the other substances.

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ śulbaṃ tāre nirvāhitaṃ iyaṃ hemakṛṣṭiḥ svarṇakaraṇamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Copper of this kind, made to undergo the process in silver, is this <s>hema-kṛṣṭi</s>, that is, the making of gold.
He states the procedure of <s>vedha</s>, beginning with "ninety-eight."

children.text: eṣa rasadaradetyādiśatāṃśavedhavidhiḥ kathaṃ atra śatāṃśe aṣṭānavatirbhāgāstārasya rūpyasya punariha kanakabhāgaḥ syāt eka eveti punaḥ sūtasya daradādimilitarasasyaiko bhāgaḥ ekāṃśaḥ iti sarve śatāṃśāḥ śatāṃśena vedha iti ||
children.translated_text: This is the procedure for hundredth-part <s>vedha</s> (transmuting penetration), beginning with '<s>rasa-darada</s>.' How is it understood? Here, in the hundred parts, there should be ninety-eight parts of <s>tāra</s>, silver; again, here there should be just one part of gold; and again there is one part, a single part, of <s>sūta</s>, the <s>rasa</s> mixed with <s>darada</s> and the rest. Thus all are one hundred parts, and the <s>vedha</s> is by a hundredth part.
He states another case too, beginning with 'forty-nine less one.'

children.text: ekonapañcāśadbhāgāḥ tārasya rūpyasya kāryāḥ tathaiva śulvasya tāmrasya ekonapañcāśadbhāgāśca kāryāḥ punaḥ kanakasya hemnaśca eko bhāgaḥ kāryaḥ sūtasya ca ekena bhāgena vedha iti eṣo'pi śatāṃśavidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Forty-nine parts of <s>tāra</s>, silver, are to be made, and likewise forty-nine parts of <s>śulva</s>, copper, are to be made. Again, one part of gold, of <s>hema</s>, is to be made, and the <s>vedha</s> is with one part of <s>sūta</s>. This too is a hundredth-part procedure.
He states a special feature of the previously mentioned procedure, beginning with 'in this way.'
In this way, by the rule of hundredth-part <s>vedha</s>, with a division increased tenfold, it becomes capable of thousandfold <s>vedha</s>.

children.text: evaṃ ca jāraṇabījavaśena jāraṇāyāṃ yadbījaṃ kiyadguṇajāritamiti bhāvaḥ tadvaśena koṭivedhī ca syāt ||
children.translated_text: And thus, according to the <s>jāraṇa-bīja</s>, the digestive seed, it can also become capable of crore-fold <s>vedha</s>; the sense is: in <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion), by how many times has the seed been digested?

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā tenaiva jāraṇabījavaśena yattasya balābalaṃ nyūnādhikyaṃ tat jñātvetyabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having done what? The intended meaning is: having understood, by means of that very <s>jāraṇa-bīja</s>, its strength and weakness, its deficiency and excess.
He gives the procedure for <s>vedha</s> in detail, beginning with 'having given.'

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ lākṣāmatsyādipittabhāvanayā lākṣā pratītā matsyādipittāni matsyamāhiṣamayūrājasūkarasaṃbhavāni pittāni teṣāṃ bhāvanayā kṛtvā prativāpaṃ galite nikṣepaṃ tattāre dattvā athavā śulbe prativāpaṃ kuryāt athavā kṛṣṭau hemakaraṇe vāpaṃ dattvā niyuñjyāditi śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: First, at the beginning, by an impregnation with lac and the bile of fish and the like: lac is well known, and the biles of fish and the rest are biles produced from fish, buffalo, peacock, goat, and boar. After preparing by their impregnation, one should give a <s>prativāpa</s>, a casting-in, into that <s>tāra</s> when it is melted; or one should perform the <s>prativāpa</s> in <s>śulva</s> (copper); or, in a <s>kṛṣṭi</s>, that is, in making gold, after giving the casting-in, one should apply it. This is to be supplied.
He gives a further special detail, beginning with 'thereafter.'

children.text: tadanu lākṣāmatsyādipittabhāvanāyā anantaraṃ tasmin lākṣādikalke krāmaṇamṛdite kāntarasakadaradaraktatailendragopādyair mṛdite sati punastatkalkena taccūrṇenāpi piṇḍitarasena vedhaḥ kartavya iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thereafter, after the impregnation with lac and the bile of fish and the like, when that paste of lac and the rest has been rubbed with <s>krāmaṇa</s> substances, namely magnetic essence, <s>darada</s>, red oil, <s>indragopa</s>, and the like, then <s>vedha</s> should again be performed with that paste, that powder, and also with pelletized <s>rasa</s>. This is to be supplied.

children.text: kasmin tāre vā śulbe vā vidrute jalarūpe kārya ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In what is it to be done? In <s>tāra</s> or in <s>śulva</s> when melted, that is, when in a water-like state.
He states a special point, beginning with 'that.'

children.text: vedhyaṃ vedhocitaṃ dravyaṃ rasarājakrāmaṇārthaṃ yathā raso viśati tadarthaṃ taṃ tailārdrapaṭena sāraṇatailārdravastreṇa sthagayet ācchādayet vā palalena kenacinmāṃsena vā bhasmanā ācchādayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of making <s>rasarāja</s> enter the substance fit to be penetrated, the material appropriate for <s>vedha</s>, one should cover it with an oil-moistened cloth, a cloth wetted with <s>sāraṇa</s> oil, so that the <s>rasa</s> may enter it; or one should cover it with straw, or with some meat, or with ash. This is the meaning.
He states a special point, beginning with 'thus.'

children.text: sāritasya uktavidhānena sāraṇākṛtasya vedhādi krāmaṇaṃ karma vedhavidhānoditakrāmaṇaṃ karma kathitam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>krāmaṇa</s> operation and <s>vedha</s> and the rest for what has been subjected to <s>sāraṇa</s>, that is, what has undergone <s>sāraṇa</s> according to the stated procedure, have been described; the <s>krāmaṇa</s> operation taught in the procedure for <s>vedha</s> has been set forth.

children.text: pādādijīrṇabījaḥ pādādinā pādārdhena samato nyūnena ca jīrṇaṃ bījaṃ yasmin saḥ patralepena yujyate ataḥ patrarañjanaṃ syādityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That in which the seed has been digested by a quarter and so on, by a quarter, a half, an equal amount, or a lesser amount, is joined with leaf-smearing; therefore the intended meaning is that coloring of the leaf takes place.

children.text: atiśuddhaṃ nirmalaṃ amlādyudvartitaṃ tārāriṣṭaśabdātsitaṃ svarṇaṃ grāhyaṃ tataḥ rasenālipya tataḥ kramaṇālipte krāmaṇapiṇḍena lepe kṛte sati puṭeṣu utpalāgnau viśrāntaṃ sthāpitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: One should take extremely purified, stainless, acid-scrubbed white gold, because of the word <s>tāra-ariṣṭa</s>. Then, having smeared it with <s>rasa</s>, and then, when a coating has been made with a <s>krāmaṇa</s> pellet in a <s>krāmaṇa</s> smear, one should leave it at rest in <s>puṭa</s>s, in a fire of cow-dung cakes.
This is the procedure for coloring leaf.
Now he states the procedure for gold, beginning with 'by half.'
It should be understood as colored from the colored leaf and the rest by half, that is, by a half portion.

children.text: jyeṣṭhena hemnā pravarakanakena taddalaṃ rañjitapatraṃ miśrayitvā puṭitaṃ kuryāt yathā milati ||
children.translated_text: Having mixed that leaf, the colored sheet, with the best gold, with excellent <s>kanaka</s>, one should subject it to <s>puṭa</s> heating so that it combines.

children.text: punaḥ kṣitikhagapaṭuraktamṛdā kṛtvā kṣitiḥ sphaṭikaḥ khagaḥ pītakāsīsaṃ paṭu saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ raktamṛt gairikaṃ ekavadbhāvadvandvaḥ tena kṣityādinopari liptaṃ dalaṃ prati ayaṃ puṭo deyaḥ vanopalair iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, using earth, <s>khaga</s>, salt, and red clay: <s>kṣiti</s> is crystal, <s>khaga</s> is yellow vitriol, <s>paṭu</s> is rock salt, and <s>raktamṛt</s> is red ochre; this is a collective compound. With that mixture beginning with <s>kṣiti</s>, the leaf should be smeared on top, and this <s>puṭa</s> should be given to it with forest cow-dung cakes. This is to be supplied.
He states the procedure for color, beginning with '<s>bhūpati</s>.'

children.text: bhūpativartakacūrṇaṃ rājāvartarajaḥ bahuśo bahuvāraṃ śirīṣapuṣparasabhāvitaṃ kuryāt ityadhyāhāryam ||
children.translated_text: One should make powder of <s>bhūpati-vartaka</s>, that is, dust of <s>rājāvarta</s>, impregnated many times, repeatedly, with the juice of <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers. This is to be supplied.
The knower of the procedure knows that what has been impregnated is to be heated in a sun-<s>puṭa</s>. This is to be supplied.
He states another procedure too, beginning with '<s>rasa</s>.'

children.text: rasaḥ sūtaḥ daradaṃ hiṅgulaḥ vimalaṃ tāpyabhedaḥ paṭu saiṃdhavaṃ śilā manohvā mākṣikaṃ pratītaṃ vaṇigdravyaṃ nṛpo rājāvartaḥ pravālaṃ vidrumaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ gairikaṃ pratītaṃ etaiḥ prativāpitaṃ sitadravyaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet ityadhyāhāryam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is <s>sūta</s>; <s>darada</s> is cinnabar; <s>vimala</s> is a variety of <s>tāpya</s>; <s>paṭu</s> is rock salt; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>; <s>mākṣika</s> is well known; <s>vaṇig-dravya</s> is borax; <s>nṛpa</s> is <s>rājāvarta</s>; <s>pravāla</s> is coral; <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s>; <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s>; and <s>gairika</s> is well known. White material treated by casting-in with these becomes gold. This is to be supplied.
He states another procedure too, beginning with '<s>tāpī-bhava</s>.'

children.text: tāpībhavaṃ mākṣikasattvaṃ nṛpāvartaṃ rājāvartakaṃ etaddvayaṃ bījapūrarasārditaṃ mātuluṅgarasamarditaṃ kuryāt etadubhayoryogāt kanakaṃ puṭapākena vahnividhānena kanakaṃ pūrvoktaṃ yatkanakaṃ vā hīnavarṇakanakaṃ sindūrasannibhaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: One should prepare these two, <s>tāpī-bhava</s>, the essence of <s>mākṣika</s>, and <s>nṛpāvarta</s>, that is, <s>rājāvartaka</s>, moistened with the juice of <s>bījapūra</s>, triturated with citron juice. By the combination of these two, through <s>puṭa</s>-cooking, by the fire procedure, it makes gold, namely the previously mentioned gold, or gold of inferior color, resemble vermilion.
The compound means: that whose appearance is like vermilion.
Now he states the procedure for the color of <s>tāra</s> (silver), beginning with '<s>vaṅga</s>.'

children.text: vaṅgābhramiti vaṅgaṃ trapu abhraṃ śvetābhraṃ punaḥ sitamākṣīkaṃ vimalaṃ śailaṃ śvetaśilājatu vā site tāre vāhayet ||
children.translated_text: In the expression '<s>vaṅgābhram</s>,' <s>vaṅga</s> is tin and <s>abhra</s> is white mica. Again, white <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>vimala</s>, and <s>śaila</s>, or white <s>śilājatu</s>, should be made to flow into white <s>tāra</s>.

children.text: punardaśāṃśena etadauṣadhanicayaṃ tārato daśamavibhāgena kṛtvā hi niścitaṃ tārotkarṣaṃ karoti hīnavarṇata uttamaṃ karotītyabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, by a tenth part, after making this collection of medicines a tenth division in relation to <s>tāra</s> (silver), it certainly produces an improvement of the silver; the intention is that it makes it excellent from an inferior color.
He states a special point concerning <s>tāra</s>, beginning with "<s>nāga</s>."

children.text: nāgaḥ sīsakas tāre nirvyūḍho mṛdutāṃ komalatvaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s>, lead, when incorporated into <s>tāra</s>, produces softness, that is, delicacy.

children.text: punaḥ ravistāmraṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ sat tāṃ mṛdutāṃ ca punaḥ raktatāṃ lohitanibhāṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>ravi</s>, copper, when incorporated, produces that softness and also redness, a reddish appearance.

children.text: ca punastīkṣṇaṃ tāranirvyūḍhaṃ tāṃ raktatāṃ pītatāṃ ca karoti ||
children.translated_text: And again <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, when incorporated into <s>tāra</s>, produces that redness and also yellowness.

children.text: punaḥ kācaḥ pratīto loke sa kālikavināśaṃ karotīti tāre nirvyūḍha iti saṃbandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, glass, which is well known in the world, removes blackness; the connection is that it is incorporated into <s>tāra</s>.
He states a special point concerning gold, beginning with "gold and red."

children.text: kanakaṃ hema aruṇaṃ tāmraṃ samaṃ tulyabhāgaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ ayaṃ gaṇaḥ karañjatailapluto dhmātaḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Gold, that is <s>hema</s>, red copper in an equal part, and <s>mākṣika</s>, that is <s>tāpya</s>: this group is to be made steeped in <s>karañja</s> oil and heated by blowing.

children.text: punaḥ pāte pāte vāraṃvāraṃ nikṣepe sati daśa daśa guṇotkarṣaṃ vidanti dhmāta ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, when there is a casting-in at each fall, again and again, they know a tenfold improvement each time; "when heated" is to be supplied.
For it is certain.
For how long? Until it reaches a number of crores.
He states a special point, beginning with "that."

children.text: saḥ karañjatailapluto yogo bahuśo vāraṃvāraṃ kaṅguṇītailena secito yathā syāttathāyaṃ ati vilīnaḥ san mākṣikaravinivāpāṃ punaḥ kārya evaṃvidhaṃ ca kanakaṃ śatāṃśena śatavibhāgena vidhyati sitakanakam iti ||
children.translated_text: That formula steeped in <s>karañja</s> oil, being repeatedly sprinkled with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil, when very well melted in that manner, is again to be made with the casting-in of <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>ravi</s>. Gold of this kind transmutes white gold by a hundredth part.
He states a special point, beginning with "struck with copper."

children.text: śulbahataṃ śulbena saha hataṃ rasagandhaṃ sūtagandhaṃ tena āhataṃ pañcatvam āpannaṃ yatkhagapītaṃ pītakāsīsaṃ etadauṣadhasamuccayaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāttathā marditaṃ kuryāt punastat nirvyūḍhaṃ daśāṃśena vidhyati sitakanakaṃ kurute svarṇamiti viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should very firmly triturate this collection of medicines: yellow <s>kāsīsa</s>, called <s>khagapīta</s>, which has been struck with <s>rasagandha</s>, mercury-sulfur, itself struck with copper and brought to destruction. Then, when it is incorporated, it transmutes by a tenth part; in particular, it makes white gold into gold.
He states another point, beginning with "<s>rasaka</s>."

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ arkacandralepena kanakaṃ rasakasamaṃ dhmātaṃ kuryāt punaretadauṣadhaṃ bhuktvā kanakaṃ syāt punarmākṣikasattvaṃ hemnā saha jīrṇaṃ rasaṃ śatāṃśena vidhyatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that, one should heat gold with a coating of <s>arka</s> and <s>candra</s>, equal to <s>rasaka</s>. Then, after consuming this medicine, it becomes gold. Again, the meaning is that <s>rasa</s> in which the essence of <s>mākṣika</s> has been digested together with gold transmutes by a hundredth part.
He states another point, beginning with "eightfold."

children.text: aṣṭaguṇaṃ mṛtaśulbaṃ arivargeṇa saha hataṃ yat śulbaṃ tāmraṃ tataḥ kaladhautena ṣoḍaśāṃśena jīrṇaṃ śatārdhena pañcāśadvibhāgena tāraṃ vidhyati kanakaṃ karotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Copper killed eightfold, namely copper that has been struck down together with the group of enemies, then digested with purified silver in a sixteenth part, transmutes <s>tāra</s> by half a hundredth, that is, by a fiftieth part; the meaning is that it makes gold.
He states another point, beginning with "having enveloped."

children.text: kanakakariṇau samahemanāgau āvṛtya gālayitvā śilayā manohvayā prativāpitau tato'nantaraṃ dolāyantre kanakakariṇau bhuktvā gandhakajīrṇo yo rasaḥ sa tāre daśāṃśavedhī syāt daśāṃśena vidhyatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having enveloped and melted gold and the elephant, that is, equal parts gold and lead, and having cast them in with <s>śilā</s> called <s>manohvā</s>, thereafter the <s>rasa</s> in which sulfur has been digested, after consuming the gold and the elephant in a <s>dolāyantra</s>, becomes a tenth-part transmuter of <s>tāra</s>; the meaning is that it transmutes by a tenth part.
He states another point, beginning with "the six metals struck down by enemies."

children.text: ripunihatalohaṣaṭkaṃ ripubhir arivargair nihataṃ māritaṃ yat lohaṣaṭkaṃ svarṇatāratāmranāgavaṅgalohābhidhānaṃ tat caturmāsaṃ yathā syāttathā dhānyasthito'nnakoṣṭhīdhṛto raso jīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The six metals struck down by enemies, namely the six metals called gold, silver, copper, lead, tin, and iron, which have been killed by the enemies, the hostile group, are digested in <s>rasa</s> kept in grain, held in a grain-bin, for four months.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭo dhānyasthitaḥ purasurābhyāṃ guggulumadirābhyāṃ sahito militaḥ śatāṃśena ghoṣaṃ kāṃsyaṃ vidhyati kanakaṃ karotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of what sort is it while kept in grain? Combined and mixed with <s>pura</s> and liquor, that is, with guggulu and wine, it transmutes bell-metal, bronze, by a hundredth part; the meaning is that it makes gold.
He states a special point, beginning with "I shall state."

children.text: bho budhāḥ mayā prakāśyamānaṃ sat śṛṇuta sāvadhānā ityadhyāhāryam ||
children.translated_text: O wise ones, listen carefully to what is being set forth by me; this is to be supplied.

children.text: tatkiṃ saṃprati yad bījaṃ samarase tulyasūte samyak jīrṇaṃ jāraṇamāpannaṃ tadahaṃ govindanāmā vakṣye kathayāmi ||
children.translated_text: What is that? I, named <s>Govinda</s>, shall now state the seed which, fully digested in equal <s>rasa</s>, that is, in an equal amount of mercury, has undergone digestion.

children.text: punaḥ piṣṭistambhādividhiṃ piṣṭistambha ādir yasya vidhestaṃ vidhiṃ pāṭakhoṭajalaukākhyaṃ ca vakṣye ||
children.translated_text: Again, I shall state the procedure beginning with <s>piṣṭistambha</s>, that is, the procedure whose first item is <s>piṣṭistambha</s>, and also what is called <s>pāṭakhoṭajalaukā</s>.
Now he explains <s>nāga</s>, beginning with "<s>rājāvartaka</s>."

children.text: rājāvartakaṃ prasiddhaṃ vimalaṃ śvetamākṣikaṃ pītābhraṃ pītavarṇaṃ yadabhraṃ gandho gandhakaḥ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ rasakaṃ kharparikaṃ etaiḥ punaretaiḥ kāṅkṣī kāhīti loke kāsīsaṃ pītakāsīsaṃ śilā manohvā daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ taiśca samanvitaṃ militaṃ nāgaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The well-known <s>rājāvartaka</s>, <s>vimala</s>, white <s>mākṣika</s>, yellow mica, sulfur, <s>tāpya</s>, gold-<s>mākṣika</s>, and <s>rasaka</s>, <s>kharparika</s>; with these, and again with <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, known in the world as <s>kāhī</s>, yellow <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>śilā</s>, <s>manohvā</s>, <s>darada</s>, and <s>hiṅgula</s>, mixed together with them, one should make <s>nāga</s>.
He states that, beginning with "snake."

children.text: pūrvauṣadhasaṃyutaṃ nāgaṃ ahimārarasaiḥ karavīradrāvaiḥ puṭitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: One should calcine the <s>nāga</s> combined with the previous medicines with the juices that kill snakes, the fluids of <s>karavīra</s>.

children.text: nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ tāvanmāraya yāvannirutthakaṃ yathā punarutthitaṃ na syāt ||
children.translated_text: One should kill <s>nāga</s>, lead, until it is <s>nirutthaka</s>, so that it does not rise again.

children.text: tadanu tatpaścāt tasya nāgasya madhye śulbaṃ tāmraṃ gandhaṃ pratītaṃ lavaṇaṃ saindhavaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ etatsarvaṃ miśritaṃ kuryāt ityadhyāhāryam ||
children.translated_text: After that, afterwards, within that <s>nāga</s>, one should mix all this: <s>śulba</s>, copper; sulfur, which is well known; salt, rock salt; <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>; and <s>viraṅga</s>. This is to be supplied.
He states the <s>krāmaṇa</s> operation, beginning with "<s>krāmaṇa</s>."
"Earlier also" means: it was also stated in the preceding chapter; this is the remainder to be supplied.
Again, one should perform this quality of <s>krāmaṇa</s> that is about to be stated; this is to be supplied.
How is that? He states it, beginning with "<s>mākṣika</s>."

children.text: mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ śilā manohvā tābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>darada</s>, <s>hiṅgula</s>, the well-known sulfur, and <s>śilā</s>, <s>manohvā</s>: with these.
Again, beginning with "<s>rājāvartaka</s>," and so on.

children.text: rājāvartakaṃ lājavarada iti bhāṣāyāṃ vimalaṃ sitamākṣikaṃ pravālaṃ vidrumaṃ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ tutthakaṃ śikhigrīvaṃ viṣaṃ saktukādikandajaṃ etaiśca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvartaka</s> is called <s>lājavarada</s> in common speech. <s>Vimala</s>, white <s>mākṣika</s>, coral, <s>vidruma</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>viraṅga</s>, <s>tutthaka</s>, <s>śikhigrīva</s>, poison, and substances born from tubers such as <s>saktu</s>: with these also.

children.text: kāntetyādi kāntaṃ cumbakaṃ gairikaṃ pratītaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ saubhāgyaṃ bhūmilatā bhūnāgaḥ rudhiraṃ śakragopaḥ raso viṣaṃ punaruktādviṣamatra dviguṇaṃ taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The passage beginning with "<s>kānta</s>": <s>kānta</s> is lodestone, <s>gairika</s> is well known, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> is <s>saubhāgya</s>, <s>bhūmilatā</s> is <s>bhūnāga</s>, <s>rudhira</s> is <s>śakragopa</s>, and <s>rasa</s> is poison. Because it has been mentioned again, poison here is double in quantity; with these.

children.text: ca punar mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalair hayāripatnīnāṃ śravaṇayor malāni taiḥ saha mṛtalohaṃ mṛtaṃ ca tallohaṃ ceti vāyasasya kākasya viṣṭhā śakṛt ||
children.translated_text: And again, together with the ear-filth of buffalo cows, that is, the impurities from the two ears of the females of <s>hayāri</s>, and with dead metal, namely metal that has been killed, and the dung, excrement, of a crow.

children.text: pārāvatasya viṣṭhā kapotaśakṛt strīpayo nārīkṣīraṃ etatsarvaṃ mākṣikādistrīkṣīrāntam ekataḥ kṛtvā miśritaṃ vidhāya ca punaretatkrāmaṇakalkaṃ raktapītagaṇaiḥ kiṃśukādiharidrādyaiḥ śatavārān bhāvayedityāgāmiślokasaṃbandhāt ||
children.translated_text: The dung of a pigeon is pigeon-excrement; woman's milk is female milk. All this, from <s>mākṣika</s> up to woman's milk, should be put together and mixed. Then this <s>krāmaṇa</s>-paste should be levigated one hundred times with the red and yellow groups, such as <s>kiṃśuka</s> and turmeric, according to its connection with the following verse.
He states the preparation of the <s>sāraṇa</s>-paste, beginning with "it should be levigated."

children.text: pūrvoktasāraṇakalkaṃ kaṅguṇītaile jyotiṣmatīsnehe bhāvyaṃ tataḥ krauñcīpittabhāvanāḥ sapta deyāḥ dātavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The previously stated <s>sāraṇa</s>-paste should be levigated in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil, that is, in the unguent of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>. Then seven levigations with the bile of a <s>krauñcī</s> bird are to be given.

children.text: punaḥ sāritapiṣṭiṃ sāritā yā rasendrabījapiṣṭis tām anena kalkena haṇḍikāyāṃ pacet vahninā pākaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, the <s>sārita</s> piṣṭi, namely the <s>rasendra</s>-<s>bīja</s> piṣṭi that has undergone <s>sāraṇa</s>, should be cooked in a pot with this paste; cooking by fire is to be performed.
He states the cooking of the <s>sāraṇa</s>-paste, beginning with "until."

children.text: pūrvakalkasaṃyutāṃ piṣṭiṃ kiyatkālaṃ pacet yāvadraktā bhavati nāgaṃ ca gacchati nāganāśaḥ syāt nāge gacchati sati samuttārya punastāvatsarvasminsāraṇādau ca kṣepakrameṇa kṣepaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: For how long should one cook the piṣṭi joined with the previous paste? Until it becomes red and the lead disappears, that is, until the lead is destroyed. When the lead has disappeared, one should take it out, and again, in all the <s>sāraṇa</s> and related operations, add an addition according to the proper sequence of additions.
The intended meaning is that it grants enjoyments beginning with virility and extending as far as movement through the sky.
He states another method for piṣṭi, beginning with "mica."

children.text: abhrakaṃ pratītaṃ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ kanakaṃ hema nāgayutaṃ nāgena sīsakena yutaṃ sahitaṃ vidhinā kartavyopadeśena etatsarvaṃ sūte militaṃ sat piṣṭiḥ kāryā divyauṣadhiyogataḥ puṭitā piṣṭiḥ kāryā iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Abhraka</s> is well known; <s>mākṣika</s> is <s>tāpya</s>; gold is <s>hema</s>. Joined with lead, and prepared by the prescribed method and instruction, all this, when mixed with mercury, should be made into a piṣṭi. A piṣṭi calcined through a compound of divine herbs should be made.
He states the extraction of gold in silver, beginning with "six."

children.text: pūrvoktāyāṃ piṣṭyāṃ ṣaḍguṇagandhakadāhaḥ kāryaḥ punaḥ ṣaḍguṇaśilayā kṛtvā nāgaṃ samuttārya sīsakamapahāya sā niṣpannā piṣṭī ṣoḍaśāṃśena tāre rūpye militā satī hemākṛṣṭiḥ syātkanakoddhāraṇaṃ bhavet tāmranāgādiṣu dhātuṣu hema sthitameva tata ākṛṣṭiśabdo yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the previously stated piṣṭi, burning with six times as much sulfur should be performed. Again, after treating it with six times as much <s>śilā</s>, one should remove the lead, that is, cast off the lead. That finished piṣṭi, when mixed with silver in a sixteenth part, becomes an attraction of gold, an extraction of gold. Since gold is indeed present in metals such as copper and lead, the word "attraction" is appropriate.
He states the procedure for killing lead, beginning with "mākṣika."

children.text: mākṣikeṇa nihataṃ māritaṃ yat śulvaṃ śilayā manaḥśilayā nāgaṃ ca nihataṃ māritaṃ ubhayaṃ tulyāṃśaṃ samabhāgaṃ kāryaṃ punar jambīrarasaiḥ jambīradrāvaiḥ saindhavasahitam ubhayaṃ puṭitaṃ bhāvitaṃ satpacedvahninā pakvaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Copper that has been struck down, that is, killed, by <s>mākṣika</s>, and lead that has been struck down, that is, killed, by <s>śilā</s>, namely <s>manaḥśilā</s>, should both be made in equal parts. Then, with the juices of <s>jambīra</s> and together with rock salt, both, after being levigated and calcined, should be cooked by fire.
Where? In a pot, meaning in an earthen vessel.
He states the extraction of gold in lead and silver, beginning with "copper."

children.text: balinā gandhakena nihataṃ sat samabhāgaṃ tulyāṃśaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it has been struck down by powerful sulfur, it should be made in an equal part; this is to be supplied.

children.text: ubhayamekīkṛtya saṃmiśrya mātārasenaiva nārīkṣīreṇa puṭayet paced iti ślokārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having brought the two together and mixed them, one should calcine or cook them with mother's milk alone, that is, with woman's milk. This is the meaning of the verse.
He states the procedure for gold-attraction, beginning with "in silver."

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ cūrṇaṃ śulbajaṃ tīkṣṇajaṃ vā tāre triguṇaṃ vyūḍhaṃ vāhitaṃ sat mārjārākṣasaṃnibha otunetrābhaṃ tāraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The previously mentioned powder, whether produced from copper or produced from <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, when carried into silver in three times the quantity, makes the silver resemble a cat's eye, having the appearance of an <s>otu</s> eye.

children.text: hemārdhena mātrayā tārārdhabhāgena parimāṇena hemnā tulyam anyūnādhikaṃ rasena payasā ||
children.translated_text: With half as much gold, that is, by a measure equal to half the silver, neither deficient nor excessive, and with <s>rasa</s>, that is, with milk, it is equal to gold.
Again he states the procedure for lead, beginning with "smeared."

children.text: triguṇaṃ yathā syāt tathā pādayuktena rasena caturthāṃśasahitasūtena saha nāgaṃ sīsakaṃ kharparakasthaṃ mṛdbhājanakhaṇḍasthitaṃ kṛtvā vidhinā rasajñopadeśena dṛḍhaṃ tāpyaṃ vahniyutaṃ sat nihataṃ kuryāditi vākyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Lead, together with mercury joined with a quarter part so that it is threefold, should be placed in a <s>kharparaka</s>, that is, in a fragment of an earthen vessel. According to the rule, by the instruction of those who know <s>rasa</s>, it should be heated strongly; when joined with fire, it should be killed. This is the meaning of the sentence.
And he states that, beginning with "<s>nirguṇḍī</s>."

children.text: pakvaṃ nāgacūrṇaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ śreṣṭhavidhānaṃ yathā syāttathā śilayā vartitaṃ san nirguṇḍīrasabhāvitapuṭitaṃ pūrṇaṃ bhāvitaṃ gharmapuṭitaṃ paścātpuṭitaṃ vahnipuṭitaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Cooked lead-powder, made smooth and according to the best procedure, should be worked with <s>śilā</s>. Then it should be fully levigated and calcined with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, heat-calcined, afterward calcined, and fire-calcined.

children.text: punaryāvannirutthabhāvaṃ aśīratvaṃ vrajet tāvanmṛditapuṭitaṃ marditapācitaṃ kuryād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, until it reaches the state of being non-revivable, that is, incapable of rising again, it should be triturated and calcined, meaning ground and cooked.
And he states that, beginning with "in silver."

children.text: tannirutthanāgacūrṇaṃ yāvatpītaṃ pītavarṇaṃ tāraṃ bhavet tāvadvāraṃ nirvyūḍhaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: That non-revivable lead-powder should be introduced repeatedly, for as many times as are needed, until the silver becomes yellow in color.

children.text: punarhemasamena kanakatulyāṃśena mātrātulyaṃ militaṃ sat ruciraṃ manoramaṃ kanakaṃ sarvaṃ bhavedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, when it is mixed with an amount equal to gold, equal in measure to gold, all of it becomes beautiful and pleasing gold. This is the meaning.
He states the procedure for <s>tāpya</s>, beginning with "<s>tāpya</s>."

children.text: aṅgulisaṃjñaṃ tāpyaṃ svarṇamākṣikaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tadantare taccūrṇam antare madhye dattvā śulbasya tāmrasya guptamūṣā andhamūṣā kāryā tatra nale ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>tāpya</s> called <s>aṅguli</s>, namely gold-<s>mākṣika</s>, should be made into powder. Having placed that powder inside, in the middle, a hidden crucible of copper, a blind crucible, should be made; here the intended sense is "in the tube."

children.text: sā mūṣā puṭitā dhmātā kāryeti vidhānam uktam ||
children.translated_text: That crucible should be calcined and blown in the fire; this procedure is stated.
And he states that, beginning with "with gold."
The powder of <s>mākṣika</s> that has been cooked: that should be prepared with gold.

children.text: pādādijīrṇasūte pādādinā pādārdhasamānadinā jīrṇo yo'sau sūtaḥ tasmin hemakṛṣṭīnāṃ patrāṇi kaluṣakanakānāṃ patrāṇi lihyāt krāmaṇayogena lepayedityāgāmiślokāt ||
children.translated_text: In <s>sūta</s> digested by a quarter and so on: that <s>sūta</s> which has been digested by a quarter and so forth, in days corresponding to a quarter, a half, and the like; on that one should smear the sheets of gold-extract, the sheets of impure gold, that is, one should coat them with the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-compound, according to the following verse.
And he states that in the passage beginning with "<s>krāmaṇa</s>."

children.text: tato rasalepānantaraṃ krāmaṇayogena kunaṭīmākṣikaviṣam ityādinoktena vilipya tulyādhaḥ tulyaṃ yathā syāttathā adhobhāge nidhāya mūṣodare dhmātaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then, after the coating with <s>rasa</s>, having coated it with the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-compound described in the passage beginning "<s>kunaṭī</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, poison," he should place it below in such a way that the lower part is equal, and should make it blown in the belly of a crucible.

children.text: punaḥ paścāddhemnā kanakena sahitaṃ āvartya dhmātaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, afterwards, together with <s>hema</s>, that is, gold, he should melt it and make it blown.
And he states that in the passage beginning with "apparatus."

children.text: vā yantraṃ pañcamṛdā valmīkamṛt gairikaṃ khaṭikā saindhavaṃ iṣṭikā ceti pañcamṛdaḥ tayā kṛtvā haṇḍyāṃ sthālyāṃ pakvaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Or the apparatus: it should be made with the five earths, namely anthill earth, red ochre, chalk, rock salt, and brick; with that it should be cooked in a pot or cooking-vessel.
Now, "cooked by a <s>puṭa</s>" means that it is to be cooked by a <s>gajapuṭa</s> and the like.

children.text: lepanavidhiṃ vakṣyāmi yathā patreṣu lepaḥ kāryaḥ punar yathā patreṣu kramati svaguṇān prakāśayati punaryena vidhinā rañjanaṃ rāgaṃ dadāti samāsataḥ saṃkṣepataḥ vidhinā vidhānataḥ sūtarāja evaṃvidho bhavet tamupāyaṃ vakṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: I shall state the method of coating: how coating is to be done on the sheets, how it then penetrates the sheets and reveals its own qualities, and again by what method it gives coloring, that is, red coloration; in brief, according to rule, <s>sūtarāja</s> should become of such a kind. I shall state that means.
Now he states the coating, <s>krāmaṇa</s>, and coloring procedure, beginning with "having made a lac-colored cloth."

children.text: prathamaṃ ālaktakaṃ vastraṃ alaktena rañjitaṃ yadvastraṃ tad ālaktakaṃ anu paścāt snehaṃ kaṅguṇyādīnāṃ tailaṃ liptaṃ kāryaṃ tattailaliptavastropari vakṣyamāṇauṣadhānāṃ cūrṇena avacūrṇanaṃ kuryāt tailaliptavastraṃ gandhakaśilayā avacūrṇitaṃ kṛtvā tadupari dātavyaṃ darśayati ||
children.translated_text: First, a lac-colored cloth, a cloth dyed with lac, should be made; afterwards oil, the oil of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> and the like, should be smeared on. On top of that oil-smeared cloth one should sprinkle the powder of the medicines to be stated. He shows that, after making the oil-smeared cloth sprinkled with sulphur and <s>śilā</s>, it should be placed on top of it.

children.text: punastadupari gandhakaśilācūrṇopari śṛtaṃ dattvā punargandhakaśilācūrṇaṃ sūtavare sūtarājopari dattvā paścāttatkaraṇānantaraṃ vartiḥ kāryā sā vartir āyase lohamaye same samabhūmau pātre dhṛtvā tatropari kāryā ||
children.translated_text: Again, on top of that, above the powder of sulphur and <s>śilā</s>, after placing what has been boiled, and again placing powder of sulphur and <s>śilā</s> upon the excellent <s>sūta</s>, the king <s>sūta</s>, then, after that operation, a wick should be made. That wick should be placed in an iron, metal vessel, on an even, level surface, and the operation should be done thereupon.
He shows another procedure in the passage beginning with "lamp."

children.text: tato varteḥ pātropari karaṇānantaraṃ dīpaṃ pratibodhya prajvālya tato vāraṃvāraṃ stokamalpaṃ tailaṃ dattvā yāvadyāmasya praharasya ardhaṃ syāttāvatpākaṃ kuryāt iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after setting the wick upon the vessel, he should awaken the lamp, that is, light it; then, repeatedly giving a little oil, he should carry out the cooking until half a <s>yāma</s>, half a watch, has passed. This is to be supplied.

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ tatpatitaṃ tailaṃ svāṅgaśītaṃ kāryaṃ aṅge tailadravarūpe śarīre yathāsvaṃ svayameva śītaṃ yathā syāttathā kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Then, after that, the oil that has fallen there should be made cool by itself; it should be made such that, in its own body, in the form of liquid oil, it becomes cool by itself.
And he states that in the passage beginning with "one should take."
Now, after the cooling has been done.

children.text: sūtakṛṣṭīṃ ca gṛhṇīyāt karmavit iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One skilled in the operation should also take the <s>sūta-kṛṣṭī</s>; this is to be supplied.

children.text: tato'nantaraṃ sā sūtakṛṣṭī tena patreṇa liptā satī krāmaṇayogair liptvā hemni suvarṇe nirdhmātā kāryeti ||
children.translated_text: Then, after that, when that <s>sūta-kṛṣṭī</s> has been smeared on that sheet, it should be coated with the <s>krāmaṇa</s>-compounds and blown in <s>hema</s>, in gold.
He states another procedure in the passage beginning with "or else."

children.text: darado hiṅgulaḥ śilā manohvā ālaṃ haritālaṃ taiḥ gandhakaḥ pratītaḥ mākṣikaṃ yatpakvaṃ sindūrīkṛtaṃ mṛtanāgaśca taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Darada</s> is cinnabar; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>; <s>āla</s> is orpiment. With these, along with sulphur, which is well known, with <s>mākṣika</s> that has been cooked and made vermilion-colored, and with calcined lead.

children.text: punaḥ kaṅkuṣṭhapravālasahitaiḥ kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ viraṅgaṃ pravālaṃ vidrumaṃ tābhyāṃ sahitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, with <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> and coral, where <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> is <s>viraṅga</s> and coral is <s>vidruma</s>, together with those two.

children.text: punaretaiḥ kaṅguṇītaile jyotiṣmatītaile piṣṭaiś cūrṇīkṛtaiḥ madhye sūto yuktaḥ kārya ityagrimaślokasaṃbandhāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, these, ground in <s>kaṅguṇī</s>-oil and <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>-oil and made into powder, are to have <s>sūta</s> joined in their midst, because of the connection with the following verse.
And he states that in the passage beginning with "in the middle."

children.text: pūrvoktairauṣadhaiḥ kṛtvā madhye auṣadhāntaḥ sūto yuktaḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the medicines previously mentioned, <s>sūta</s> should be joined in the middle, inside the medicines.

children.text: punarmardayitvā vaṃśanalikāṃ riktodarāṃ prati saṃvedya dinatrayaṃ dolāyantreṇa sveditaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, after triturating it, one should introduce it into an empty-bellied bamboo tube and make it steamed for three days by means of a swing-apparatus; this is the meaning.
And he states that in the passage beginning with "having smeared."

children.text: etāni sveditauṣadhāni saṃyuktāni taiḥ kṛṣṇaiḥ kṛṣṇalavaṇaiḥ pūrvoktavidhānena sūtakṛṣṭīvidhānena patraṃ liptvā punaḥ prakaṭaṃ yathā syāt tathā stokaṃ alpamalpaṃ krameṇa nāgaṃ dattvā kanakaṃ jāyate ityagrimaślokasaṃbandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These steamed medicines are combined; with them, together with the black substances, the black salts, and according to the previously stated method, the method of <s>sūta-kṛṣṭī</s>, after coating the sheet, and again giving lead little by little in sequence so that it becomes manifest, gold is produced; this is connected with the following verse.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte sati akṣīṇaṃ akṣayaṃ divyaṃ pravaraṃ devayogyaṃ devā indrādayastadyogyaṃ kanakaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When this has been done, imperishable, inexhaustible, divine, excellent gold, fit for the gods, the gods such as Indra, is produced.
This meaning is appropriate.

children.text: evaṃ jāritasūte jāritakarmakṛte rase khalu niścitaṃ sarvā haṇḍikāḥ sarve dhātvādyāḥ sakalāḥ saprasavāḥ syurityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>sūta</s> has thus been digested, when the operation of digestion has been performed on the <s>rasa</s>, certainly all pots, all metals and the like, all of them, become productive; this is the meaning.
He states a special point in the passage beginning with "seedless."

children.text: nirbījaṃ yathā syāttathā samajīrṇaṃ pādena turyāṃśena phalaṃ dadāti tathā ardhena jīrṇena ṣoḍaśāṃśena phalaṃ dadāti ca punastadardhena jīrṇena tatpādayogaṃ tatpādena ekena tatpādayogaṃ phalaṃ dadātīti sarvatra vācyam ||
children.translated_text: When it is without <s>bīja</s>, and digested equally, it gives the result by a quarter, that is, by a fourth part. Likewise, when digested by a half, it gives the result by a sixteenth part. And again, when digested by half of that, it gives the result in conjunction with its quarter; "with one quarter of that" and "it gives the result" are to be supplied everywhere.

children.text: tulyakanakaṃ ca jīrṇaṃ pūrṇaṃ phalaṃ dadātīti ||
children.translated_text: And when digested with an equal amount of gold, it gives the full result.

children.text: hemākṛṣṭyanantaraṃ tārākṛṣṭiṃ vakṣye ahaṃ kaviḥ kathayāmi mṛtavaṅgaṃ māritaṃ vaṅgaṃ tālakena haritāleneti ||
children.translated_text: After gold-extraction, I shall state silver-extraction; I, the poet, declare: calcined tin, tin that has been killed, together with <s>tālaka</s>, that is, orpiment.

children.text: atha tāmraṃ tulyāṃśaṃ lambitaṃ vistīrṇaṃ yathā syāt tathā nirdhmātaṃ sat tārachaviṃ vahati rūpyadyutiṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now, <s>tāmra</s> (copper), in an equal part, drawn out and spread as appropriate, when smelted, bears the appearance of <s>tāra</s> (silver), that is, it obtains the lustre of <s>rūpya</s> (silver).
And he states that with the words beginning '<s>paścāt</s>' ('afterwards').

children.text: paścādvaṅgatāmrayogānantaraṃ prakāśamūṣāsu yāvat nirmalaṃ malavarjitaṃ syāttāvannāgaṃ deyaṃ punaryāvannirmalam ujjvalaṃ nistaraṅgaṃ nāgormivarjitaṃ syāt tāvadvidhinā dhmātaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards, that is, after the combination of <s>vaṅga</s> (tin) and copper, <s>nāga</s> (lead) should be added in open crucibles until it is pure and free from impurity. Again, it should be heated by the prescribed method until it is clear, bright, without ripples, and free from waves of lead.
He states a special point with the words beginning '<s>tāla</s>'.

children.text: tālaṃ haritālaṃ śilā manohvā sarjikā pratītā tābhiḥ saindhavaṃ ca tat lavaṇaṃ ca tena nayanahitasahitaiḥ etaiḥ kṛtvā ekaikaṃ pṛthaktvena vā sahitam ekatvena punaḥ śulve tāmre vedhaṃ pratidadhyāditi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāla</s> is <s>haritāla</s>; <s>śilā</s> is <s>manohvā</s>; <s>sarjikā</s> is well known. With these, and with <s>saindhava</s>, that is, that salt, together with <s>nayanahita</s>, one should again apply <s>vedha</s> (penetrative treatment) to <s>śulva</s>, copper, either with each one separately or with them combined as one.
He states the castings-in for the penetration of <s>tāra</s> with the words beginning '<s>chagaṇam</s>'.

children.text: chagaṇaṃ vanotpannaṃ māhiṣaṃ takraṃ mahiṣyāḥ idaṃ māhiṣaṃ snuhikṣīreṇa sehuṇḍadugdhena saha punaḥ sarpiṣā ghṛtena saha guḍadugdhamadhubhir miśraiḥ militaṃ kṛtvā kramaśo vedhakarmaṇi niṣekaḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Chagaṇa</s>, forest-born matter, <s>māhiṣa</s> <s>takra</s>, buffalo buttermilk, together with the milk of <s>snuhi</s>, the latex of <s>sehuṇḍa</s>, and again together with <s>sarpiṣ</s>, ghee, and mixed with jaggery, milk, and honey, should be combined. In this order a casting-in is to be made in the operation of <s>vedha</s>.
He states the attraction of <s>tāra</s> with the words beginning '<s>kāñcī</s>'.

children.text: kāñcī svarṇamākṣikaṃ brāhmī somāhvā kuṭilaṃ sīsaṃ tālakaṃ pratītaṃ etatsamayojitaṃ samāṃśamelitaṃ sat dhmātaṃ kuryāt punaranena kāñcyādigaṇena viddhaṃ śulbaṃ divyā manoramā tārākṛṣṭirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāñcī</s>, <s>svarṇamākṣika</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, called <s>somāhvā</s>, <s>kuṭila</s>, lead, and the well-known <s>tālaka</s>: these should be joined together, mixed in equal parts, and heated. Then copper penetrated by this group beginning with <s>kāñcī</s> becomes a fine and delightful attraction of <s>tāra</s>.
He states the attraction of <s>tāra</s> with the words beginning '<s>evam</s>'.

children.text: evaṃ uktavidhānena sāritena sāraṇākarmakṛtena liptvā viddhā satī tārākṛṣṭirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by the procedure already stated, when it has been smeared with what has been made to flow, that is, with the substance produced by the <s>sāraṇā</s> operation, and penetrated, it becomes an attraction of <s>tāra</s>.

children.text: punariyaṃ tārākṛṣṭiḥ tāraṃ vimalaṃ malavarjitaṃ karoti vā pādajīrṇādi pādena jīrṇaṃ yasmin ādiśabdād ardhasamagrahaṇaṃ kāryaṃ tat lepamiti ||
children.translated_text: Again, this attraction of <s>tāra</s> makes <s>tāra</s> pure and free from impurity. Or, in the phrase beginning '<s>pādajīrṇa</s>', 'digested by a quarter' means that in which one quarter has been digested; by the word 'and so on', a half and the whole are also to be included. This is the coating.
He states a special point with the words beginning '<s>iti</s>'.

children.text: iti pūrvoktavidhānena miśrīkṛtaṃ militaṃ viddhaṃ kramitaṃ mātṛkātulyaṃ samāṃśaṃ sat tāradalaṃ rūpyapatraṃ bhavati tadrūpyadalaṃ chedanatāḍananikaṣaiḥ chedanaṃ khaṇḍanaṃ tāḍanaṃ ghanaghātaḥ nikaṣaṃ śilopari parīkṣaṇaṃ tairiti tāpaiśca nirdoṣaṃ tadbhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the previously stated procedure, when it has been mixed, combined, penetrated, advanced, made equal to the matrix and equal in parts, it becomes <s>tāradala</s>, a sheet of silver. That silver sheet is faultless under cutting, hammering, testing on the touchstone, and heating: cutting means breaking into pieces, hammering means blows with a hammer, and testing means examination upon a stone.

children.text: evaṃ amunā prakāreṇa śāstravidhijñena śāstrasya vidhiṃ jānātīti saḥ tena karmanipuṇena saṃskārapravīṇena kuśalena kartrā gurūpadeśaṃ gururuktalakṣaṇo granthādau tasya upadeśaṃ jñātvā vedhavidhānaṃ kartavyam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this method, the procedure of <s>vedha</s> should be performed by an agent who knows the prescriptions of the treatise, is skilled in the work, expert in processing, and capable, after learning the instruction of the guru, namely the teaching described at the beginning of the work.
Now he states the procedure for consumption with the words beginning '<s>iti</s>'.

children.text: rasarājasya vidhau rasendrakarmavidhāne vedhavidhānaṃ prasaṅgataḥ prastāvataḥ proktaṃ na tu svaprajñāsamam ||
children.translated_text: In the procedure of <s>rasarāja</s>, that is, in the procedure for the operations of <s>rasendra</s>, the procedure of <s>vedha</s> has been stated incidentally, in connection with the topic, and not as something equal to one's own independent insight.

children.text: adhunā proktānapi api śabdādanubhūtānapi rasāyane jarāvyādhināśanavidhau yogān dravyasamudāyātkān vakṣyāmi kathayāmītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the formulas for <s>rasāyana</s>, for the method that destroys old age and disease, composed of groups of substances; by the word 'also', this includes even those already taught and also those experienced in practice.
He states the purification of the body with the words beginning '<s>ādau</s>'.

children.text: prathamaṃ prātaḥ prātaḥ pratyūṣe tridinaṃ saindhavamilitaṃ ghṛtam ājyaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: First, every morning at daybreak, for three days, one should drink ghee mixed with <s>saindhava</s> salt.

children.text: anyasaṃyogamāha tadanu ghṛtasaindhavānantaraṃ ketakītanujaṃ kvāthaṃ ketakyāḥ tanuḥ śarīraṃ tasmājjātaṃ ketakīmūlasaṃbhavam ityarthaḥ aṅge'pyanukte vihitaṃ tu mūlaṃ iti nyāyāt tridinaṃ prayuñjīyādityarthaḥ ||
