children.translated_text: He states another combination: after that, that is, after the ghee and rock salt, one should use for three days a decoction of the child of <s>ketakī</s>, meaning what is produced from the body of <s>ketakī</s>, that is, from the root of <s>ketakī</s>; according to the rule, 'when no limb is specified, the root is prescribed.'
He states another procedure with the words beginning '<s>vidhinā</s>'.

children.text: tato vidhinā svedavidhānena dehaḥ śarīraṃ vārtikendreṇa rasasaṃpradāyavidā svedyaḥ svinnaḥ kartavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, by the prescribed method, by the sweating procedure, the body should be sweated, made perspiring, by the chief adept in the tradition of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: anyatkiṃ kaṭurohiṇyāḥ tiktāyāḥ kvathitaṃ prasādhitaṃ samyak śuddhikaraṇaṃ anuprayuñjīta svedānantaram ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What else? After the sweating, one should apply a boiled and properly prepared decoction of <s>kaṭurohiṇī</s>, the bitter herb, for thorough purification.
He states another procedure with the words beginning '<s>tad</s>'.

children.text: tadanu kaṭukarohiṇīsevanānantaraṃ śuddhād ūrdhvaṃ yathā syāt tathā śleṣmāntarecite sati yathā śleṣmaṇo'ntaḥ syāttathā recite sati tridinaparimāṇaṃ yāvakapathyaṃ ghṛtasahitaṃ prayuñjīteti ||
children.translated_text: After that, after the use of <s>kaṭukarohiṇī</s>, when one has been purified above, and when purgation has been done so that the phlegm is removed to its end, one should use for a period of three days a wholesome barley preparation together with ghee.
He states another procedure with the words beginning '<s>punar api</s>'.

children.text: punarapīti yāvakapathyayogānantaraṃ ca punaḥ pānayogaṃ vakṣyāmi kimarthaṃ sakalabhuvanahitakṛtaye samastasaṃsārahitakaraṇāya idaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ cūrṇaṃ pathyādyaṃ uṣṇodakasamaṃ taptajalena saha prathamayāme prathamapraharāntaḥ pītvā śuddhaśarīro bhaved ityāgāmiślokasaṃbandhāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, after the regimen of wholesome barley, I shall describe another drinking formula. For what purpose? For producing the good of the whole world. The powder about to be described, beginning with <s>pathyā</s>, should be taken with hot water, within the first watch; by connection with the following verse, one thereby becomes purified in body.
He states the powder for purification with the words beginning '<s>pathyā</s>'.

children.text: pathyā harītakī saindhavaṃ pratītaṃ dhātrī āmalakaṃ marīcam ūṣaṇaṃ vacā ugragandhā guḍaḥ pratītaḥ viḍaṅgaṃ kṛmighnaṃ rajanī haridrā śuṇṭhīpippalyor apīti śuṇṭhī nāgaraṃ pippalī māgadhī āsāṃ auṣadhīnāṃ cūrṇaṃ tridinaṃ prayuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pathyā</s>, <s>harītakī</s>, the well-known <s>saindhava</s>, <s>dhātrī</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, <s>marīca</s>, <s>ūṣaṇa</s>, <s>vacā</s>, the strong-scented herb, the well-known jaggery, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, the worm-killer, <s>rajanī</s>, turmeric, and also <s>śuṇṭhī</s> and <s>pippalī</s>, namely <s>nāgara</s> and <s>māgadhī</s>: one should use the powder of these medicines for three days.
It should be understood to be taken with hot water.
With the words beginning '<s>amunā</s>', and so on.

children.text: amunā vakṣyamāṇavirecanena yāvakādinā śuddhaśarīraḥ san parihatasaṃsargadoṣabalī bhavati saṃsargeṇa ye doṣāḥ śarīrābhyantarāste saṃsargadoṣāḥ te parihatā jitā yena saḥ parihatasaṃsargadoṣaḥ tena balī balayuktaḥ doṣanivṛttau guṇapravṛttir ityavaśyam ||
children.translated_text: By this purgation to be described, with <s>yāvaka</s> and the like, a person whose body has been purified becomes strong, having removed the faults of contact. The faults which are inside the body because of contact are the <s>saṃsarga-doṣas</s>; one by whom they have been removed, conquered, is one who has removed the faults of contact. Through that he is strong, endowed with strength. When the <s>doṣas</s> cease, the operation of the virtues necessarily follows.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā parihatadoṣaḥ amunā payasā uṣṇodakena yāvakaṃ alaktaṃ pītvā śuddho bhavedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having done what does he become one whose faults are removed? Having drunk <s>yāvaka</s>, lac-red barley-water, with this milk or warm water, he should become purified: this is the meaning.
He states the fault in not performing purification, beginning with '<s>akṛta</s>.'

children.text: yo naraḥ pumān akṛtakṣetrīkaraṇe dehe iti śeṣaḥ na kṛtaṃ akṛtaṃ kṣetrīkaraṇaṃ yasmin tasminsati rasāyanaṃ jarāvyādhivināśanauṣadhaṃ prayuñjīta tasya puṃso raso na krāmati svaguṇānna prakāśayati tarhi kiṃ sarvāṅgadoṣakṛdbhavati bāhucaraṇādiṣu ṣaṭsvaṅgeṣu vikārakṛt syāt ||
children.translated_text: If a man, a male person, should apply a <s>rasāyana</s>, a medicine that destroys old age and disease, to a body in which preparation as a field has not been done, the word 'body' being supplied, then for that man the <s>rasa</s> does not proceed, that is, does not manifest its own qualities. What then? It becomes a producer of faults in every limb; it may produce disorder in the six limbs such as the arms and legs.
He states eligibility for <s>rasāyana</s>, beginning with '<s>iti</s>.'

children.text: pūrvoktavidhānena śuddhaḥ san yo jātabalo bhavati sa kṣetrīkṛtanijadehaḥ akṣetraṃ kṣetraṃ kriyata iti kṣetrīkṛto nijadehaḥ śarīraṃ yena saḥ matimān rasāyanaṃ vidhivatprakurvīta ||
children.translated_text: A wise man who, being purified by the previously stated procedure, has acquired strength, whose own body has been made into a field, should undertake <s>rasāyana</s> according to rule. 'His own body is made a field' means that what was not a field is made a field.

children.text: kaiḥ jātabalaḥ śālyodanaṃ ca yāvakākhyaṃ ca mudgāśca taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: By what has he acquired strength? By <s>śālyodana</s>, cooked rice from fine rice, by what is called <s>yāvaka</s>, and by <s>mudgas</s>.
He states another procedure, beginning with '<s>surataru</s>.'

children.text: antaritaśuddhaḥ antaritaṃ śuddhaṃ yasya saḥ grahaṇīrogādivarjita ityarthaḥ etāni auṣadhāni nirmathya pītvā viśuddhakoṣṭho bhavati viśuddhaṃ malavarjitaṃ koṣṭhaṃ udaraṃ kasyetyevaṃvidho bhavati ||
children.translated_text: One whose internal purification has been accomplished, that is, one whose purification is internal, meaning one free from <s>grahaṇī</s> disease and the like, becomes one with a completely purified bowel after churning these medicines together and drinking them. He becomes such that his bowel, his abdomen, is purified and free from fecal matter.

children.text: tāni kāni suratarutailetyādīni suratarur devavṛkṣaḥ tattailapeṣaṇaṃ tailamityarthaḥ ghṛtaṃ ājyaṃ madhu kṣaudraṃ dhātrīrasaḥ āmalakīsalilaṃ payo dugdhaṃ etāni sarvāṇi nirmathya ekīkṛtyetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What are those? <s>Surataru</s> oil and so on. <s>Surataru</s> is the divine tree; 'its oil-paste' means its oil. Ghee is clarified butter, honey is <s>kṣaudra</s>, <s>dhātrī-rasa</s> is the fluid of <s>āmalakī</s>, and <s>payaḥ</s> is milk. Having churned all these together means having combined them into one.
He states the benefit of eating this medicine in the order of months, beginning with '<s>māsena</s>.'

children.text: asya auṣadhasya māsena māsapramāṇena bhakṣaṇāt kāntir bhavati medhā ceti dvābhyāṃ dvimāsābhyāṃ doṣanikaraṃ gadasamudāyaṃ praśamayati śāntiṃ nayati punarmāsatritayena trimāsapramāṇena svāt svasāmānyaśarīrāt amaravapurdevaśarīro mahātejāḥ dīptimān syādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From eating this medicine for a month, for the measure of a month, beauty and intelligence arise. In two, that is, in two months, it calms the mass of faults, the aggregate of diseases, and brings them to peace. Again, in a period of three months, from his own ordinary body he becomes one with the body of an immortal, a divine body, and is very radiant, that is, brilliant.
He states another formula, beginning with '<s>suradāru</s>.'

children.text: suradārutailaṃ devadārutailaṃ ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ triphalārasasaṃyutaṃ triphalāyā rasena draveṇa saṃyutaṃ sahitaṃ ca punaḥ samabhāgaṃ tulyāṃśaṃ tatpītaṃ sat saptāhāt saptadinapramāṇataḥ nayanavikāraṃ netrasaṃbhavaṃ rogaṃ śamaṃ nayati śāntiṃ prāpayati ||
children.translated_text: <s>Suradāru</s> oil, that is, <s>devadāru</s> oil, together with ghee, clarified butter, and combined with <s>triphalā</s> juice, that is, accompanied by the liquid juice of <s>triphalā</s>, again in equal parts: when this has been drunk, in a week, in the measure of seven days, it brings an eye disorder, a disease arising in the eyes, to pacification and peace.
He states another formula, beginning with '<s>surataru-tailam</s>.'

children.text: devadārutailaṃ saghṛtaṃ sājyaṃ etadubhayaṃ pītvā sakṣīraṃ śālyodanaṃ bhuktvā ṣaṣṭikaudanam ityabhiprāyaḥ punarjīrṇāhāre pratidinaṃ dināntavīradvaye veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: Having drunk <s>devadāru</s> oil together with ghee, both of these with clarified butter, and having eaten <s>śālyodana</s> with milk, the intended meaning is cooked <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice, then again, when the food has been digested, it should be understood as two <s>vīras</s> at the end of each day.

children.text: ca punaḥ sakuṣṭhān kuṣṭhaiḥ saha vartante evaṃvidhān pīnasādīn rogān harati dūrīkaroti ||
children.translated_text: And again it removes, drives far away, diseases such as <s>pīnasa</s> and the others, including those that are accompanied by <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
He states another formula, beginning with '<s>ghṛta-sahita</s>.'

children.text: amaradāruraso devadārujalaṃ ghṛtasahitaṃ ājyamiśritaḥ pittakṛtān rogān harati nāśayati ||
children.translated_text: The juice of <s>amaradāru</s>, water of <s>devadāru</s>, mixed with ghee, that is, combined with clarified butter, removes and destroys diseases produced by bile.

children.text: punastailayutastailena miśrito devadārurasaḥ vātasaṃbhavān rogān hanti ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>devadāru</s> juice mixed with oil destroys diseases arising from wind.

children.text: punarguḍasahitaḥ vā madhunā kṣaudreṇa sahito devadārurasaḥ vātasaṃbhavān rogān hanti ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>devadāru</s> juice together with molasses, or together with honey, <s>kṣaudra</s>, destroys diseases arising from wind.

children.text: punar guḍasahitaḥ vā madhunā kṣaudreṇa sahito devadārurasaḥ kaphajān rogān hantīti vākyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>devadāru</s> juice together with molasses, or together with honey, <s>kṣaudra</s>, destroys diseases born of phlegm: this is the sentence meaning.
He states what is to be eaten and what is not to be eaten during <s>rasāyana</s>, beginning with '<s>varjita</s>.'

children.text: varjitakāñjikaśākaṃ varjitaṃ kāñjikaṃ sauvīraṃ śākaṃ vāstukādi ca yasmin tattathā payasā kṣīreṇa saha śālyodanaṃ bhuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: One should eat <s>śālyodana</s> with milk, in which sour gruel, <s>kāñjika</s> or <s>sauvīra</s>, and greens such as <s>vāstuka</s> have been excluded.
Again, what is the measure of the <s>śālyodana</s>? Its measure is two, four, or six <s>palas</s>.

Here the inferior, middle, and superior measures, consisting of two, four, and six <s>palas</s>, are to be applied respectively to persons of inferior, middle, and superior strength: this is the meaning.
Now he states the mercury formula, beginning with '<s>tad</s>.'

children.text: tadanu pathyamātropayogānantaraṃ pātanaśuddhaṃ pātanena śuddhaṃ sūtakaṃ āroṭam eva sāmānyam evāśnīyāt bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: After that, after the use of the prescribed quantity of wholesome diet, one should eat ordinary <s>āroṭa</s> itself, namely <s>sūtaka</s>, mercury, purified by <s>pātana</s>, purified through distillation.

children.text: ca punaḥ svedanamūrchotthāpanarodhāśca svedanaṃ ca mūrchā ca utthāpanaṃ ca pātanāni ca nirodhaśceti dvandvaḥ ete yadyapi santi niyamaśca yadyapyasti tathāpyāroṭaḥ pātanena syād ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And again, sweating, swooning, raising up, and checking: the compound means sweating, swooning, raising up, distillations, and restraint. Although these exist, and although there is a rule, still <s>āroṭa</s> is made by <s>pātana</s>: this is the meaning.
Incidentally he states <s>pātana</s>, beginning with '<s>abhraka</s>.'
<s>Sūta</s>, mercury, when combined with <s>abhraka</s>, that is, joined with mica, is to be distilled.
By what procedure? By means such as a <s>ḍamaruka-yantra</s>.
Again, so long as it becomes stable.

children.text: athavā vidhyantare sūto mākṣikasahitaḥ pātyo vidhānena ayamapi yāvatsthiro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Or, in another procedure, <s>sūta</s> (mercury) together with <s>mākṣika</s> is to be distilled according to rule, until this too becomes stable.
In the rasāyana section he states the procedure for <s>sūta</s>, such as <s>āroṭa</s>, beginning with "iti."

children.text: āroṭa iti pūrvoktena pātanakarmaṇā ūrdhvādhastiryagbhavena sādhita āroṭaḥ saḥ prathamaṃ yathā syāttathā rasāyane jarāvyādhināśane niyujyate iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āroṭa</s> means the <s>āroṭa</s> that has been prepared by the previously stated operation of distillation, whether upward, downward, or transverse. It is first applied in rasāyana, that is, in the destruction of old age and disease.

children.text: athavā kalkayogena rasādisambhūtena raso bhasma kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: Or, by means of a paste-preparation arising from <s>rasa</s> and the like, after making the <s>rasa</s> into ash.

children.text: dvividhaṃ bhasma ūrdhvagaṃ talabhasma ca varṇabhedena ṣaḍvidhaṃ śvetaṃ bhasma pītaṃ bhasma haritaṃ bhasma raktaṃ bhasma kṛṣṇaṃ bhasma karburaṃ bhasma iti ṣaḍvidhaṃ tatkṛtvā kṣetrīkaraṇe niyujyate prathamam ||
children.translated_text: There are two kinds of ash: that which goes upward and bottom-ash. By distinction of color it is sixfold: white ash, yellow ash, green ash, red ash, black ash, and variegated ash. Having made that sixfold ash, it is first employed for <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> (preparation of the body as the field).
He states the combination with <s>rasa</s>, beginning with "<s>mākṣika</s>."

children.text: mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ śilājatu prasiddhaṃ lohacūrṇaṃ māritamuṇḍasya rajaḥ pathyā harītakī akṣo vibhītakaḥ viḍaṅgaṃ kṛmighnaṃ ghṛtam ājyaṃ madhu kṣaudraṃ etaiḥ samprayuktaṃ rasaṃ kṣetrīkaraṇāya prayuñjīteti vākyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning of the sentence is that one should use <s>rasa</s> for <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s> when it is combined with these: <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, well-known <s>śilājatu</s>, iron powder, powder of killed <s>muṇḍa</s> iron, <s>pathyā</s> or harītakī, <s>akṣa</s> or vibhītaka, <s>viḍaṅga</s> the worm-killer, ghee, and honey.

children.text: ityuktavidhānena kalkīkṛtaṃ sūtaṃ bhuktvā amaratāṃ devatvaṃ gacchet ||
children.translated_text: Having eaten the <s>sūta</s> made into a paste by the procedure thus stated, one attains immortality, the state of a deity.

children.text: iti kiṃ ghanakāntamadhughṛtādisaṃyuktaṃ ghano'bhrakaḥ kāntaṃ lohajāti madhu kṣaudraṃ ghṛtam ājyaṃ ādiśabdāt sitā grāhyā etaiḥ saṃyuktaṃ sat kalkīkṛtaṃ idaṃ ca pradhānaṃ kṣetrīkaraṇaṃ kṣetrī kriyate'neneti ||
children.translated_text: What is meant by "iti"? It is joined with compact mica, magnetic iron, honey, ghee, and so forth. <s>Ghana</s> is mica; <s>kānta</s> is a kind of iron; <s>madhu</s> is honey; <s>ghṛta</s> is ghee; by the word "and so forth," sugar is to be understood. Being joined with these, this paste-preparation is the principal <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>, since the field is made by means of it.
Thus ends the <s>āroṭa</s> operation.
Now, the operation for leaf-mica.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ śyāmavarṇaṃ ghanaṃ abhraṃ pītaṃ pītavarṇaṃ ghanaṃ vā bahuśo naikavāraṃ śikhiprabhaṃ agniprabhaṃ sat surabhīkṣīraniṣiktaṃ secitaṃ kāryaṃ punargatagiridoṣaṃ yathā syāttathā gatā girijā doṣā mahīdharasaṃbhavā doṣā yasmāt tadevaṃ saṃśodhayitvā tat ghanaṃ rasāyane jarāvyādhivināśakaraṇe yojyam ||
children.translated_text: Black, dark-colored compact mica, or yellow, yellow-colored compact mica, should many times, not just once, be made flame-bright, fire-bright, and sprinkled with cow's milk. It should be so purified that the mountain-born defects have gone away from it; having thus purified it, that compact mica is to be used in rasāyana, for causing the destruction of old age and disease.
He states the mica formula, beginning with "<s>niścandrika</s>."

children.text: ghanaṃ niścandrikamapi śuddhaṃ candrikārahitamapi nirdoṣaṃ viḍaṅgatriphalājyamadhurasamāyuktaṃ kṛmighnaharītakīvibhītakāmalakaghṛtakṣaudramilitaṃ pratidivasaṃ pratidinaṃ ekapalapramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ bhuktvā vidhinā śuddhaśarīravidhānena kṣīrāśano bhavet kṣīreṇa saha śālyodanāśanaṃ samācaredityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even compact mica that is <s>niścandrika</s>, purified and free from glitter, free from defects, should be mixed with <s>viḍaṅga</s>, triphalā, ghee, honey, and <s>rasa</s>, that is, combined with the worm-killer, harītakī, vibhītaka, āmalaka, ghee, and honey. After eating one pala in measure of the whole each day, according to rule, with the procedure for a purified body, one should live on milk, meaning that one should take śāli rice-food together with milk.
And he states that, beginning with "trikaṭu."

One should eat <s>vyoma</s>, that is, mica, joined with trikaṭu, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, triphalā, <s>mākṣika</s>, and <s>śilājatu</s>, mixed with long pepper, black pepper, dry ginger, harītakī, vibhītaka, āmalaka, honey, and <s>śilājatu</s>.
Then one should eat milk-rice, which is wholesome.

children.text: eva kṛte sati jantuḥ śataṃ jīvati jantujanyuśarīriṇaḥ ityamaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this has been done, a creature lives for a hundred years; <s>jantu</s> means a living embodied being, according to the lexicon.
Thus ends the procedure for leaf-mica.
Showing what follows further concerning mica, he says, beginning with "iti."

children.text: ityevamādayaḥ iti pūrvoktā yogā ādayo yeṣāṃ te anye kāñjikayuktāśca kāñjikenāranālena yuktāḥ yogīkṛtāḥ granthāntare rasāvatārādau bahuśaḥ kīrtitāḥ kathitāḥ te patrābhrakayogāḥ niryuktikāḥ niryukte bhavā ikpratyayāntās te varjyāḥ sevane'yogyā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus those beginning in this way, that is, other formulas whose first members are the previously stated formulas, and those joined with <s>kāñjika</s>, that is, joined with sour gruel, which are frequently taught in other treatises such as the <s>Rasāvatāra</s>, are formulas for leaf-mica that are <s>niryuktika</s>; formed with the suffix <s>ik</s> from <s>niryukta</s>, they are to be avoided, meaning that they are unfit for use.

children.text: avidhinā patrābhrakayogo vikārāyetyata āha ya ityādi ||
children.translated_text: Since a formula for leaf-mica used contrary to rule leads to disorder, he says, beginning with "ya."

children.text: ye ajñātadravyaguṇaiḥ ajñātā dravyāṇāṃ abhrādināṃ guṇā yais tair evaṃvidhaiḥ puṃbhiḥ vidhinā sāmānyavidhānena patrābhrakayogāḥ rasāyanārthaṃ kīrtitās tair eva jarā mṛtyuśca upadiṣṭaḥ jarā pālityaṃ mṛtyur vyādhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those formulas for leaf-mica which have been declared for rasāyana by men who do not know the properties of substances, that is, by men of such a kind that the qualities of substances such as mica are unknown to them, and merely according to a general rule, by those very men old age and death have been prescribed: old age means greying, and death means disease.

children.text: jarāmṛtyorupadeśe hetumāha aprāptetyādi aprāptalokabhavaṃ yathā syāttathā asya kartuḥ ghanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He states the reason for prescribing old age and death, beginning with "aprāpta": when the compact mica of this maker is such that its effect in the world has not been obtained.

children.text: jaṭharāgniṃ vināpi pumān naśyati nāśaṃ prāpnoti ||
children.translated_text: Even without digestive fire, a man perishes; he comes to destruction.

children.text: kiṃbhūtaḥ san vividharogagaṇaiḥ nānārogasamūhaiḥ paribhūto vijitaḥ san iti vākyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of what sort is he? He is overcome and defeated by hosts of various diseases, by groups of many diseases. This is the sentence meaning.

children.text: kāṣṭhe sthitam api ghanapaṭalamadhye'pi abhre'bhrasattvaṃ sthitaṃ tadāha abhrasatvaṃ ghanasāraṃ ghanapaṭale sthitamapi nijakāryaṃ svakīyakṛtyaṃ tathā na kurute vahniragniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even if it is present in wood, even within a compact layer, the mica-essence is present in mica. He states this: the mica-essence, the core of the compact mica, though present in the compact layer, does not perform its own function, just as fire does not.

children.text: kāṣṭhe dāruṇi sthitaḥ san nijakāryaṃ na kurute tu punaḥ yathā ghṛtaṃ payasi dugdhe sthitaṃ sat svīkāryaṃ na kurute cāgrahir iva dhanasthamiva madhye sthitaṃ kāryaṃ kurute'tiniḥsṛtaṃ sat pṛthagbhūtaṃ sat nijakāryaṃ kuruta iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fire, while present in wood, does not perform its own function. Again, just as ghee present in milk does not perform its own function, but when extracted, separated out, as wealth does for one who has taken it, it performs its own function; this is the sense.
He states which mica is edible and inedible, beginning with "abhrasya."

children.text: abhrakasatvamiha kṣetrīkaraṇe rasāyanināṃ jarāvyādhivināśecchūnāṃ param utkṛṣṭaṃ bhakṣyaṃ aśanayogyaṃ kīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Here, in <s>kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>, mica-essence has been declared the supreme edible substance, fit to be eaten, for practitioners of rasāyana who desire the destruction of old age and disease.
But the threefold <s>gagana</s>, that is, mica of three kinds, is inedible, not fit to be eaten.

children.text: kiṃ tat kācaḥ kācarūpaṃ kiṭṭaṃ malarūpaṃ pattrarajaḥ sāmānyābhracūrṇaṃ ceti trividhamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is that? <s>kāca</s> is glass-like matter, <s>kiṭṭa</s> is waste-like matter, <s>pattra-rajas</s> is ordinary mica-powder; thus it is of three kinds. This is the meaning.
Now he states the preparation of compact essence and iron, beginning with "first."

children.text: ādau prathamaṃ ghanaloharajaḥ ghanamabhrasatvaṃ loharajaḥ kāntacūrṇaṃ triphalārasabhāvanaiḥ harītakīvibhītakāmalakadravapuṭanair nirghṛṣṭaṃ sat añjanasadṛśaṃ sauvīrāñjanatulyaṃ kurvīta kaiḥ kṛtvā sūryakaraiḥ kena sthagitavastreṇa ācchāditapaṭena vastreṇācchādya sūryakarasannidhau dhāryamityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: First, at the outset, compact iron-powder, that is, compact mica-essence, and iron-powder, that is, magnetic powder, should be ground down by <s>bhāvanā</s> with <s>triphala</s>-juice, by repeated soaking with the liquids of <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, and <s>āmalaka</s>, and should be made like collyrium, equal to <s>sauvīrāñjana</s>. By what means? By the rays of the sun. With what covered? With a cloth that has been spread over it, meaning that it should be covered with cloth and kept in the presence of the sun's rays.
He continues with "in this way."

children.text: itthamamunā prakāreṇa ślakṣṇam añjanasannibhaṃ yathā syāt tathā ghanasatvakāntaṃ kṛtvā punarlohaghanaṃ lohaṃ muṇḍādi ghanaṃ abhrasatvaṃ etadubhayaṃ vividhakāntalohacūrṇasamaṃ vividhā nānājātayaḥ ayaskāntabhedāḥ teṣāṃ cūrṇaṃ tatsamaṃ kṛtvā bhṛṅgeṇa ca bahuśo'nekavāraṃ sādhayedbhāvayedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this method, after making the compact essence and <s>kānta</s> so that they are smooth and collyrium-like, again iron and compact substance, namely iron such as <s>muṇḍa</s> and compact mica-essence, these two should be made equal to powders of various magnetic irons; "various" means many kinds, the varieties of lodestone. With <s>bhṛṅga</s> he should repeatedly prepare it, that is, subject it to <s>bhāvanā</s> many times.
And he states that with the passage beginning "with <s>triphala</s>."

children.text: tadbhṛṅgarājena bahuśo bhāvitaṃ ghanasatvakāntaṃ idam amṛtaṃ sudhāsamaṃ na mṛtamamṛtaṃ tat triphalāmadhughṛtamiśritaṃ harītakīvibhītakāmalakaghṛtakṣaudramilitaṃ dhānye kasyacidannasyāntaḥ māsasthitaṃ kuryāt māsaikaparimāṇaṃ tatra vidhātavyamiti vyaktiḥ ||
children.translated_text: That compact essence and <s>kānta</s>, repeatedly treated with <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, is this <s>amṛta</s>, equal to nectar and not dead. It should be mixed with <s>triphala</s>, honey, and ghee, that is, combined with <s>harītakī</s>, <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, ghee, and honey, and placed in grain, inside someone's food-grain, for a month; the explanation is that it should remain there for the measure of one month.
Of what kind is it? It is also worshipped with mantras.
Thus the mantra is as follows:
To her whose curls are crowded with a garland of <s>mandāra</s> flowers; to him whose crest is marked by a garland of skulls;

children.text: divyāmbarāyai ca digambarāya namaḥ śivāyai ca namaḥ śivāya
children.translated_text: to her wearing divine garments and to him clothed in the directions: homage to <s>Śivā</s> and homage to <s>Śiva</s>.
With such verses and the like.
And he states that in the passage beginning "after a month."

children.text: dhānyānmāsena māsaikaparimāṇenoddhṛtya bahirnītvā punarapi balaṃ jñātvā prayuñjīta bhoktre dadyāt atha viśeṣaṃ darśayati kāntaṃ vinā abhrakasatvameva kṛtvā prayuñjīta ca punargaganaṃ vinā kāntaṃ kevalaṃ pūrvavidhānena sādhayitvā prayuñjītetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After taking it out from the grain after a month, after the measure of one month, and bringing it outside, he should again determine its strength and administer it, that is, give it to the eater. Now he shows a special point: without <s>kānta</s>, he may prepare only mica-essence and administer it; and again, without <s>gagana</s>, he may prepare only <s>kānta</s> according to the previous rule and administer it. This is the meaning.
He states the result, beginning with "corpulence."

children.text: sthaulyamiti medorogaḥ paṭalakācatimirāṇi netrarogāḥ arbudaṃ granthiviśeṣaḥ karṇanādaḥ pratītaḥ śūlamaṣṭavidhaṃ etāni hanti arśāṃsi gudajāni bhagandaramehaplīhādi bhagandaraḥ gudavraṇaṃ mehaḥ pramehaḥ bījavikāraḥ plīhā plīharogaḥ ete rogā ādiryasya tat hanti pālityaṃ jarāṃ ca nāśayatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Corpulence" means the disease of fatness; <s>paṭala</s>, <s>kāca</s>, and <s>timira</s> are eye diseases; <s>arbuda</s> is a particular kind of tumor; ringing in the ears is well known; <s>śūla</s> is of eight kinds. It destroys these, and also piles born in the anus, fistula, urinary disorder, spleen disease, and so on: <s>bhagandara</s> is an anal ulcer, <s>meha</s> is <s>prameha</s>, disorder of the seed, and <s>plīhā</s> is spleen disease. It destroys diseases beginning with these, and it also removes greyness of hair and old age. This is the meaning.
He states the regimen, beginning with "this."

children.text: etanniṣpannauṣadhabhakṣaṇaṃ kurvan matimān puruṣaḥ gorasamastupradhānaṃ goraso godugdhaṃ mastu dadhimastu evaṃpradhānamannamaśnīyāt bhuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: A wise man who takes the medicine prepared from this should eat food chiefly consisting of cow-products and whey; <s>gorasa</s> is cow's milk, and <s>mastu</s> is the whey of curds. Such should be the chief food he eats.

children.text: punarjāṅgalamudgājyapayo'śnīyāt jāṅgalasyedaṃ jāṅgalaṃ svalpāmbuśākhīdeśaḥ jāṅgalaḥ mudgaḥ pratīto'nnaviśeṣaḥ ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ payo dugdhaṃ vā salilaṃ yanmudgājyapayaḥ taccāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: Again, he should eat products of dry-land country, mung beans, ghee, and milk: <s>jāṅgala</s> means belonging to a <s>jāṅgala</s> region, a country with little water and vegetation; <s>mudga</s> is the familiar kind of grain; <s>ājya</s> is ghee; <s>payaḥ</s> is milk or water. He should eat that which consists of mung beans, ghee, and milk or water.
And again, he should eat boiled rice made from <s>śāli</s> rice.
All this should be done with celibacy. This is the meaning.
Thus ends the procedure for mica-essence.
Now, showing the superiority of digested <s>rasa</s>, he says, beginning with "compact."
It is that in which <s>ghana-sattva</s> has been digested in the measure of a quarter.
"Digested with <s>kānta</s>" means digested with <s>kānta</s> in the measure of a quarter.
Again, it is a <s>rasa</s> of such a kind that <s>tīkṣṇa</s> has been digested in it in an equal amount.
<s>Kṣetrīkaraṇa</s>, the preparation of the body as a field, is everywhere the chief thing. This is the meaning.

children.text: baddho yaḥ khoṭatāṃ yāto dhmāto dhmātaḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: That which has been bound and has gone to the state of <s>khoṭa</s>, when blown again and again, may undergo loss.

children.text: khoṭo bandhaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ śīghraṃ sarvagadāpahaḥ
children.translated_text: That bond is to be known as <s>khoṭa</s>; it quickly removes all diseases.
So it is said in another treatise.

children.text: ghanasatvam abhrasāraḥ kāntaṃ cumbakotthaṃ sūto rasaḥ ekavadbhāvo dvandvasamāsāt tathā mṛtaṃ hema pañcatvamāptaṃ kanakaṃ ca etaccatuṣkaṃ śatāvarīrasopetaṃ śatamūlīdravabhāvitaṃ punarghṛtamadhulīḍhaṃ ghṛtamadhubhyāṃ līḍhaṃ āsvāditaṃ sat varṣādvarṣaparimāṇāt mṛtyuvyādhiṃ jarāṃ ca hanti nāśayatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ghana-sattva</s> is the essence of mica; <s>kānta</s> is what arises from a magnet; <s>sūta</s> is <s>rasa</s>. Because of the compound, they are to be understood as one set. Likewise dead gold, gold that has attained destruction, and refined gold: this group of four, accompanied by the juice of <s>śatāvarī</s>, that is, treated with the liquid of <s>śatamūlī</s>, and then licked with ghee and honey, that is, tasted together with ghee and honey, destroys death, disease, and old age within a year, after the measure of a year. This is the meaning.
He states a special point, beginning with "among these."

children.text: eṣāṃ pūrvoktānāṃ yogānāṃ madhye ādita ārambhataḥ ekaṃ yogaṃ kṛtvā niḥśreyaso mokṣaḥ tatsiddhaye niṣpattaye saṃvatsaraṃ varṣaparimāṇaṃ ayanaṃ ṣaṇmāsaparyantaṃ yojyaṃ bhoktṛṣu iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these formulas previously stated, after making one formula from the beginning, for the accomplishment of <s>niḥśreyasa</s>, that is, liberation, it should be applied among the eaters for a year, the measure of a year, or for an <s>ayana</s>, a period of six months; this is to be supplied.
"Liberation, isolation, extinction, good, supreme good, nectar"; so says the <s>Amara</s> lexicon.
While listing many items, he states a special point, beginning with "mica."

children.text: abhrakaḥ prasiddhaḥ sasyakaś capalaḥ mākṣikaṃ tāpyaṃ rasakaṃ kharparaṃ daradaṃ hiṅgulaṃ vimalaṃ sitamākṣikaṃ vajrakaṃ hīrakaṃ girijatu śilājatu etaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With these: mica, which is well known; <s>sasyaka</s>; <s>capala</s>; <s>mākṣika</s>; <s>tāpya</s>; <s>rasaka</s>; <s>kharpara</s>; <s>darada</s>; <s>hiṅgula</s>; <s>vimala</s>; white <s>mākṣika</s>; <s>vajraka</s>, that is, diamond; and mountain-born resin, that is, <s>śilājatu</s>.

children.text: punar vaikrāntetyādi vaikrāntaṃ vajrabhūmijaṃ rajaḥ kāntaṃ lohajāti tīkṣṇaṃ sāraḥ etaiśca ||
children.translated_text: Again, with the passage beginning "<s>vaikrānta</s>": and with these also: <s>vaikrānta</s>, born from diamond-ground; powder; <s>kānta</s>, a kind of iron; and <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, the essence.

children.text: hāṭakatārāratāmraiś ca hāṭakaṃ hema tāraṃ rūpyaṃ āraṃ rājarītiḥ tāmraṃ śulbaṃ etaiśca etair uddiṣṭaiḥ abhrakāditāmrāntaiḥ samastair ekatrīkṛtair vyastairvā pṛthakkṛtairvā yathālābhaṃ lābhamanatikramya bhavatīti yathālābhaṃ dvitricaturbhirvā abhrādyairjīrṇahato rasendro jīrṇābhrādīnāṃ hatiryasmin sa tathoktaḥ rasāyane jarāvyādhivināśane rasaśāstramarmajñaiḥ śasyate abhrādayaḥ praśastā uktā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And by gold, silver, brass, and copper: <s>hāṭaka</s> is gold; <s>tāra</s> is silver; <s>āra</s> is brass, the royal metal; <s>tāmra</s> is copper. With these, that is, with all these substances indicated from mica through copper, whether collected together or separately prepared, according to availability, that is, without exceeding what has been obtained, with two, three, or four substances beginning with mica as available, <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury), killed after those such as mica have been digested into it, is praised by those who know the essentials of <s>rasaśāstra</s> in <s>rasāyana</s>, the destruction of old age and disease. The meaning is that substances beginning with mica are called excellent.
This is a pair of verses.
<s>Sūta</s> treated with diamond and the like is another form equal to killed <s>sūta</s>.
It is called by the name <s>śṛṅkhalābaddha</s> and effects the body and metals.
By its power, rapid pervasion certainly occurs.
So in another treatise.
Showing a blameworthy procedure, he says, beginning with '<s>viṣa</s>.'

children.text: viṣanāgavaṅgabaddho rasaḥ viṣaṃ saktukādikaṃ nāgaḥ sīsakaḥ vaṅgaṃ trapu etairbaddho bandhanamāptaḥ sa bhuktaḥ san hi niścitaṃ kuṣṭhādīn kuṣṭhajvarakṣayādīn ||
children.translated_text: Mercury bound with poison, lead, and tin: <s>viṣa</s> is such things as <s>saktuka</s>; <s>nāga</s> is lead; <s>vaṅga</s> is tin. Bound with these, that is, having obtained binding, when it is eaten, it certainly produces <s>kuṣṭha</s> and the like, namely <s>kuṣṭha</s>, fever, wasting disease, and so on.

children.text: uparasabaddhe rase uparasair gandhādibhiḥ aṣṭabhiḥ baddho bandhanam āpanno yo'sau rasaḥ tasmin bhukte sati bhokturaṅgāni hastapādādīni sphuṭanti ||
children.translated_text: With regard to mercury bound with secondary minerals: when that mercury which is bound, which has obtained binding, by the eight secondary minerals such as sulphur, is eaten, the eater's limbs, such as hands and feet, split open.
He states the dose of digested mercury, beginning with '<s>ghana</s>.'

children.text: etaiścīrṇajīrṇaṃ pūrvaṃ cīrṇaṃ kavalitaṃ paścājjīrṇaṃ jāraṇam āpannaṃ tasya sūtasya guñjā mātrā bhakṣaṇāya guñjā yathā
children.translated_text: The <s>sūta</s> that has first been consumed and digested, that is, swallowed and then brought to digestive assimilation, with these substances has a dose for eating of one <s>guñjā</s>. The <s>guñjā</s> is as follows:
One barley-corn is made of six mustard seeds, and one <s>guñjā</s> is made of three barley-corns.
Thus.

children.text: parā anyā mātrā anyajīrṇasūtasya mātrā māṣamekaṃ māṣako yathā
children.translated_text: The other dose, the dose of mercury digested with another substance, is one <s>māṣa</s>. The <s>māṣaka</s> is as follows:
A <s>māṣaka</s> was formerly declared by <s>Brahmā</s> to consist of ten <s>guñjās</s>.
Thus.
With these: with what? With compact mica essence, magnetic iron, <s>kāñcī</s>, <s>bhāskara</s>, and sharp iron, that is, with the essences of mica, magnet, <s>tāpya</s>, copper, and iron.
Now, according to the special kind of penetration, he states the quantity, beginning with '<s>śata</s>.'

children.text: śatavedhinaḥ sūtasya guñjāpramāṇā mātrā jñeyā tathā tena prakāreṇa sahasraikavedhinaḥ sūtasyāpi guñjāmānameva lakṣavedhinaḥ sūtāt ardhā raktikā punaḥ koṭivedhinaḥ sūtāt siddhārthaḥ sarṣapamānā ||
children.translated_text: The dose of mercury with a hundredfold penetration should be known as the measure of one <s>guñjā</s>. In the same manner, for mercury with a thousandfold penetration also, the measure is just one <s>guñjā</s>. From mercury with a hundred-thousandfold penetration, the dose is half a <s>raktikā</s>; again, from mercury with a ten-millionfold penetration, it is a <s>siddhārtha</s>, the measure of a mustard seed.

children.text: śatāṃśena vedho vidyate yasmin sa śatavedhī tasya śatavedhinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That in which penetration is found in a hundredth part is a hundredfold penetrator; of that, the hundredfold penetrator.
In this way it is to be understood everywhere.

children.text: japaḥ aghorādijapaḥ homastaddaśāṃśena havanaṃ devatārcanaṃ devatānāṃ gaṇeśaviṣṇuraviśivacaṇḍīnāṃ arcanaṃ eteṣu nirataḥ saktaḥ evaṃvidhiḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Japa</s> is the muttering of <s>Aghora</s> and other mantras; <s>homa</s> is the oblation one tenth as great as that; worship of the deities is the worship of deities such as <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Sun, <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Caṇḍī</s>. A man of this kind is one devoted to these.

children.text: iti kiṃ hemaniyojitasūtaṃ dhārayet hemnā saha niyojito miśrito yaḥ sūtaḥ taṃ kāntamaṇiḥ kāntaścāsau maṇiśca vā kāntamaṇiḥ kāntasaṃjñako maṇiḥ ca punaḥ vividhaguṭikāḥ vividhāśca tā guṭikāśceti ||
children.translated_text: What is meant by this? He should wear mercury placed in gold, that is, mercury which has been set or mixed together with gold. And <s>kāntamaṇi</s> is a magnet-stone, or a stone called <s>kānta</s>; and again various pills, meaning pills of various kinds.
Now he states the wholesome foods, beginning with '<s>śāleḥ</s>.'

children.text: śāleḥ ṣaṣṭikādeḥ piṣṭodbhavabhojanaṃ piṣṭakotpannaṃ ca tadbhojanaṃ ceti ||
children.translated_text: Food produced from flour of <s>śāli</s> rice, such as <s>ṣaṣṭika</s>, means food that has arisen from a cake of flour.
<s>Ājya</s> means ghee.

children.text: kaiḥ saha mudgamāṃsarasaiḥ saha mudgāḥ pratītāḥ atra viśeṣāt māṃsāni bhojyāni gokṣīraṃ ca bhojyaṃ punarmastu gorasasaṃbhavaṃ viśeṣāt bhojyam ||
children.translated_text: With what? With the soups of mung beans and meat. Mung beans are well known. Here, in particular, meats are to be eaten, and cow's milk is also to be eaten; again, especially <s>mastu</s>, produced from cow products, is to be eaten.

children.text: pāne akṣāraṃ jalaṃ miṣṭajalaṃ prayojyaṃ punaḥ yāni kāni miṣṭāni dravyāṇi atrānuktatamāni praśastāni śreṣṭhāni punaḥ caturjātakakarpūrāmodamuditamukhaṃ yathā syāt tathā dravyaṃ peyaṃ pātavyaṃ caturjātakaṃ tvakpatrailānāgakesaraṃ karpūraṃ ghanasāraṃ eṣām āmodena parimalena muditaṃ yanmukhaṃ vāsitamukham ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For drinking, non-alkaline water, sweet water, should be used. Again, any sweet substances not mentioned here are praised and excellent. Again, the substance is to be drunk in such a way that the mouth is delighted by the fragrance of the four aromatics and camphor. The four aromatics are cinnamon bark, cinnamon leaf, cardamom, and nāgakeśara; camphor is <s>ghanasāra</s>. The meaning is that the mouth is delighted, perfumed, by the fragrance and scent of these.
Conversation with a young woman should be performed, and also massage of the limbs by a young woman.
By the mere touch of her, the <s>sūtaka</s> courses through the body.
This special rule is from another treatise.
He states what is unwholesome, beginning with '<s>madya</s>.'

children.text: madyāranāletyādi madyaṃ surā āranālaṃ kāñjikaṃ tayoḥ pānaṃ neṣṭaṃ na praśastaṃ vā tailaṃ dadhi na neṣṭaṃ tailaṃ tilodbhavaṃ dadhi dugdhavikāraḥ etayorapi pānaṃ na praśastaṃ kaṭutailena sarṣapatailena vapuṣi abhyaṅgaṃ mardanaṃ na kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Alcohol and sour gruel and so on: drinking alcohol, namely liquor, and <s>āranāla</s>, namely sour gruel, is not desired, that is, not approved. Likewise oil and curds are not desired: oil is produced from sesame, and curds are a transformation of milk. Drinking these two also is not approved. A wise man in the matter of <s>rasāyana</s> should not perform anointing or massage on the body with pungent oil, that is, mustard oil.
By '<s>matimān</s>' is meant in the section on <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: dagdhaṃ dravyaṃ rasāyane neṣṭaṃ apakvaṃ ca neṣṭaṃ amadhuraṃ kaṭutiktakaṣāyāmlalavaṇaṃ ca neṣṭaṃ uṣṇaṃ vahnitaptamiti tu punaḥ naṣṭamāṃsaṃ ninditamāṃsaṃ neṣṭaṃ punaḥ paryuṣitaṃ saṃdhānīkṛtaṃ evaṃvidhaṃ phalamūlaṃ phalaṃ mūlaṃ ca atra rasāyane bhakṣyaṃ na nirdiṣṭaṃ kathitaṃ
children.translated_text: A burnt substance is not desired in <s>rasāyana</s>; an uncooked one also is not desired; nor one that is not sweet, namely pungent, bitter, astringent, sour, or salty. Hot, that is, heated by fire, is likewise not desired. Again, spoiled meat, condemned meat, is not desired. Again, stale food, that is, food made by fermentation, and fruit and root of such a kind, fruit and root, are not prescribed, not stated, as edible here in <s>rasāyana</s>.
Pumpkin, cucumber, watermelon, and bitter gourd,
<s>kusumbhikā</s>, <s>karkoṭī</s>, plantain, and <s>kākamācikā</s>:
this set of eight beginning with the syllable ka should indeed be avoided by one who eats mercury.
So in another treatise.

children.text: asmin rasāyane laṅghanaṃ na kāryaṃ punar yāmādhaḥ praharamadhye bhojanaṃ na kāryam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this <s>rasāyana</s>, fasting is not to be done. Again, the meaning is that eating should not be done below a <s>yāma</s>, within a <s>prahara</s>.
And he states this with the words beginning "free from..."

children.text: varjitacintākopa iti cintā ca kopaśceti cintākopau tau varjitau yena saḥ evaṃvidhaḥ san sukhāmbunā sukhoṣṇāmbunā snānaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: "Free from worry and anger" means: worry and anger are <s>cintā-kopa</s>; the person by whom those two, worry and anger, have been abandoned is of such a kind. Being such, he should bathe with comfortable water, that is, pleasantly warm water.

children.text: graharākṣasabhūtāni noccāṭayet grahaṇādgrahāḥ piśācādayaḥ jvaro rogarājaḥ rākṣasāḥ kravyādāḥ bhūtāni devayonayaḥ etāni noccāṭayet svasthānānna cālayet ||
children.translated_text: He should not drive away <s>grahas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and <s>bhūtas</s>. <s>Grahas</s> are so called because they seize; they are beings such as <s>piśācas</s>. Fever is the king of diseases. <s>Rākṣasas</s> are flesh-eaters, and <s>bhūtas</s> are classes of divine beings. These he should not drive away, that is, he should not move them from their own places.

children.text: punarmātṛdevīṃśca mātaraḥ saptamātaraḥ devyo dakṣiṇyādayaḥ tā api noccāṭayet ||
children.translated_text: And again, he should not drive away the mother-goddesses: the mothers are the seven <s>mātṛs</s>, and the goddesses are those such as <s>Dākṣiṇyā</s>. Them too he should not drive away.
He states the reason for restraining worry and anger with the words beginning "in the supreme..."

children.text: rasāyanakartā parame brahmaṇi citsvarūpe līnaḥ tanmayatāṃ prāpto bhavet praśāntacittaśca viṣayebhyo nivṛttamanā bhavet samatvamāpannaḥ svasute śatrau ca nirvairo yathā syāt tathā trivargaṃ dharmārthakāmarūpaṃ vijitya rasānandaparitṛpto bhavet harṣaparipūrita ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The maker of the <s>rasāyana</s> should be absorbed in the supreme <s>brahman</s>, whose nature is consciousness, and should have attained identity with it. He should be tranquil in mind, his mind withdrawn from sense-objects. Having reached equanimity toward his own son and toward an enemy, being free from hostility in that way, and having conquered the three aims, <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>, he should be satisfied by the bliss of <s>rasa</s>, that is, filled with joy.
While showing that the rule is fixed, he says with the words beginning "he who..."

children.text: yaḥ pumān śāstravidhiṃ tyaktvā svecchayā ucchṛṅkhalamanasā rase sūte pravartate sa mūḍhaḥ jñānaśūnyaḥ tasya puṃsaḥ viruddhācārāt nitarāmatiśayena ajīrṇam utpadyate tadrasājīrṇamiti ||
children.translated_text: The man who abandons the rule of the treatise and, according to his own will, with an unrestrained mind, proceeds with <s>rasa</s>, that is, with <s>sūta</s> (mercury), is a fool, devoid of knowledge. Because of his contrary conduct, very severe indigestion arises for that man; that is called <s>rasājīrṇa</s>.
He states the symptoms of <s>rasājīrṇa</s> with the words beginning "there occurs..."

children.text: iha rasāyane ajīrṇaṃ yadā sambhavati utpadyate tadā etāni lakṣaṇāni syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, in the course of <s>rasāyana</s>, when indigestion occurs or arises, these symptoms appear.

children.text: nidrā atiśayena nidrā ālasyaṃ aṅgāṅgaśaithilyaṃ jvaraḥ prasiddhaḥ tamo mūrchā dāha ūṣmā punarnābhitale bastau alpamalpaṃ śūlaṃ jaḍatāsyasya aruciḥ nirabhilāpitā bhaṅgo'ṅgasya aṅgamardanaṃ bhokturetāni lakṣaṇāni rasājīrṇe syur ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sleep, excessive sleep; lassitude, looseness in every limb; fever, which is well known; darkness, that is, fainting; burning, heat; then slight pain in the navel region and in the bladder; dullness of the mouth; loss of appetite, absence of desire; and breaking of the body, that is, bodily pain: these are the symptoms that occur for the eater in <s>rasājīrṇa</s>.
He states the remedy even when there is indigestion, with the words beginning "having known..."

children.text: ityevam uktaprakāreṇa nidrādilakṣaṇenājīrṇaṃ jñātvā dhīmatā puṃsā asyājīrṇasya pracchādanāya vināśāya rasāyanaṃ saṃtyajya divasatritayaṃ yogaḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having known indigestion in just this stated manner, through symptoms such as sleep and the rest, an intelligent man should abandon the <s>rasāyana</s> and undertake a treatment for three days in order to cover over, that is, destroy, this indigestion.
He states that with the words beginning "<s>karkoṭī</s>..."

children.text: karkoṭīmūlarasaṃ karkoṭī yā vallī tasyāḥ mūlarasaṃ tridinaṃ pibet vātha kaṣāyaṃ kathaṃ sindhunā saindhavena sahitaṃ pibet vā tatkvāthaṃ gojalasahitaṃ gomūtramilitaṃ rasājīrṇe pibet sauvarcalasahitamiti sauvarcalasya prativāpaṃ karkoṭīrase nikṣipya pibet tridinaṃ sarvatretyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For three days one should drink the root-juice of <s>karkoṭī</s>, that is, the root-juice of the creeper called <s>karkoṭī</s>. Or one should drink its decoction together with <s>saindhava</s> rock salt. Or, in <s>rasājīrṇa</s>, one should drink that decoction together with cow urine. "Together with <s>sauvarcala</s>" means: having placed an admixture of <s>sauvarcala</s> salt in the <s>karkoṭī</s> juice, one should drink it for three days in every case.
He states another remedy with the words beginning "having ground..."

children.text: mātuluṅgasyeyaṃ jaṭā mātuluṅgī tāṃ piṣṭvā tasyā rasaṃ śuṇṭhī saindhavaṃ ca yaḥ pumān prātaḥ pibati tu punaḥ kvathitaṃ tasyāḥ kaṣāyaṃ gosalilena yaḥ pibati rasājīrṇe taṃ puruṣaṃ rakṣati na vināśayatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The root-fibre of <s>mātuluṅga</s> is called <s>mātuluṅgī</s>. The man who grinds it and drinks its juice in the morning together with dry ginger and <s>saindhava</s> rock salt, or who drinks the boiled decoction of it with cow urine when there is <s>rasājīrṇa</s>, is protected by it; it does not destroy him.
He states the remedy for one who has eaten <s>rasa</s> mixed with <s>nāga</s> and other metals, with the words beginning "somehow..."

children.text: ca punaḥ yat yasmāt nāgādikalaṅkito rasaḥ nāgavaṅgasahito raso'jñānātkathamapi bhuktaḥ tannodanāya tasya nāgavaṅgāṅkitarasasya nodanāya gojalakaṭukāravalliśiphāḥ gojalaṃ gomūtraṃ kaṭutiktā kāravallīśiphā kāravallīlatāyāḥ śiphā jaṭā etadauṣadhaṃ pibet tena nāgavaṅgādidoṣo vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: And again, because <s>rasa</s> tainted with <s>nāga</s> and the like, that is, mercury containing lead and tin, may somehow have been eaten through ignorance, one should drink cow urine and the root-fibres of bitter <s>kāravallī</s> for the expulsion of it, that is, for expelling the <s>rasa</s> marked by lead and tin. The medicine consists of cow urine and the root-fibre, the matted root, of the bitter <s>kāravallī</s> creeper. By it the fault arising from lead, tin, and the like is destroyed.
He states that with the words beginning "<s>śarapuṅkhā</s>..."

children.text: āsāṃ auṣadhīnāṃ madhye ekatamā yā uditā kathitā śṛtā kvathitā tāṃ hi niścitaṃ ajīrṇe seveta tena ajīrṇaṃ naśyatīti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among these medicines, whichever one has been mentioned and stated, after it has been boiled as a decoction, one should certainly use it in indigestion. The sense is that by it the indigestion is destroyed.

children.text: tāḥ kā auṣadhyaḥ śarapuṅkhā prasiddhā suradālī devadālī paṭolaṃ pratītaṃ nāma bimbī golā kākamācī prasiddhā etā ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What are those medicines? They are <s>śarapuṅkhā</s>, well known; <s>suradālī</s>, that is, <s>devadālī</s>; <s>paṭola</s>, known by that name; <s>bimbī</s>; <s>golā</s>; and <s>kākamācī</s>, well known. These are meant.
He states that with the words beginning "excessively sour..."

children.text: atyamlaṃ cukrādi atilavaṇaṃ kṣārādi atikaṭukaṃ nimbakaṭukītyādi etai rasasaṃsrāvo jaro jāraṇakaro bhavati jaratīti jaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: With substances that are excessively sour, such as <s>cukra</s>, excessively salty, such as alkali, and excessively pungent, such as neem and <s>kaṭukī</s>, there is a discharge of <s>rasa</s>; <s>jara</s> means what causes digestion, because it digests.

children.text: punarapi madhuraiḥ ikṣurasādibhiḥ satatabhuktaiḥ jaṭharavahniḥ koṣṭhāgniḥ vinaśyati abhyāśrayo vinaśyatītyabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, by sweet substances such as sugarcane juice, when continually eaten, the abdominal fire, the digestive fire in the belly, is destroyed. The intended sense is that its support is destroyed.
He states this particular point with the words beginning "he who..."

children.text: yaḥ punar mūḍho mūrkho 'jīrṇānantaraṃ atyamlalavaṇakaṭukāhāraṃ satataṃ nirantaraṃ karoti tasyāgniḥ koṣṭhāgnir vinaśyati rasaśca na krāmati svaguṇānna prakāśayati ||
children.translated_text: The fool who, after indigestion, constantly and without interruption takes food that is excessively sour, salty, and pungent has his fire, the digestive fire in the belly, destroyed, and the <s>rasa</s> does not proceed; it does not manifest its own qualities.
If one asks what would then occur, he says: disease would arise.

children.text: rasācchatasahasralakṣavedhī bhavet sa yatnāt anayā pūrvoktakriyayā sidhyati ||
children.translated_text: From <s>rasa</s> there may be efficacy extending to a hundred, a thousand, and a hundred thousand penetrations. Through effort it is accomplished by this previously stated procedure.
Now, by the subsequent procedure, he states the characteristic with the words beginning "hundred..."
The <s>rasa</s> is one that penetrates a hundred, a thousand, and a hundred thousand.

children.text: balisahitaṃ piṣṭaṃ rasaṃ bhuñjīta balinā gandhakena sahitam śatādārabhya sahasralakṣakoṭyarbudānāṃ krameṇa daśaguṇottaraṃ saṃkhyā jñātavyā ||
children.translated_text: One should eat the ground <s>rasa</s> together with <s>bali</s>, that is, together with sulfur. From a hundred onward, the sequence of numbers, increasing tenfold, should be understood as hundred, thousand, hundred-thousand, crore, and arbuda.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtaḥ san rasaḥ siddhido yathoktaguṇakṛdbhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When made in this way, the <s>rasa</s> grants accomplishment and produces the qualities stated above: this is the meaning.
Praising the previous procedure, he says, beginning with "krāmati."

children.text: tataḥ pūrvavidhānataḥ sūtaḥ krāmati svaguṇān prakāśayati sūte krāmati sati devagarbhābhān putrān janayati devagarbhavat ābhā kāntir yeṣāṃ te tān punaḥ strīṣu niścalaḥ sadāsthāyī kāmo ratyabhilāṣo vā madano yasya sa tathoktaḥ punar valīpalitanirmuktaḥ valyaśca palitāni ca tair nirmukto vivarjitaḥ valiścarma jarākṛtaṃ ityamaraḥ palitaṃ keśaśvetatvaṃ evaṃvidho bhavati pumān iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, by means of the previous procedure, <s>sūta</s> (mercury) advances, that is, manifests its own qualities. When the <s>sūta</s> advances, it begets sons in women who have the radiance of divine embryos, that is, whose splendor and beauty are like that of divine embryos. Further, in relation to women he has firm, constantly abiding desire, or erotic longing. Again, he is free from wrinkles and grey hair; wrinkles and grey hairs have left him. According to the lexicon, a wrinkle is skin caused by old age, and grey hair is the whiteness of the hair. It is implied that such a man becomes like this.
Again, saying what else would occur, he says, beginning with "buddhi."

children.text: rasāyaninaḥ rasāyanaṃ prāptasya hi puṃsaḥ buddhirvardhate balaṃ ca vardhate kena saha āyuṣā jīvitakālena saha punar divyabuddhiṃ prāptasya rasāyaninaḥ divyāḥ prakaraṇādguṇā medhādayaḥ pravardhante prakāśanta ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For a man who has obtained <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating elixir), his intelligence increases, and his strength also increases together with his lifespan. Again, for the practitioner of <s>rasāyana</s> who has obtained divine intelligence, divine qualities, such as understanding and the rest, increase, that is, become manifest.
He states that, beginning with "evam."

children.text: evamamunā prakāreṇa rasasaṃsiddhaḥ puruṣaḥ rasaḥ pāradaḥ saṃsiddhaḥ samyak siddho yasya vā rasena saṃsiddhaḥ jarāmaraṇavarjito bhavati vṛddhatvavyādhirahita ityarthaḥ guṇavāṃśca bhavati guṇā medhādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by this procedure, the man perfected by <s>rasa</s> becomes free from old age and death. Either his <s>rasa</s>, mercury, has been perfected, completely accomplished, or he has been perfected by <s>rasa</s>; the meaning is that he is free from old age and disease. He also becomes endowed with qualities, such as understanding and the rest.

children.text: punaḥ khegamanena ākāśagamanena nityaṃ sakalabhuvaneṣu samastalokeṣu saṃcarate ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, through <s>khegamana</s>, movement through the sky, he constantly moves about in all worlds, that is, throughout every realm.

children.text: dātā bhuvanatritaye svargamṛtyupātāle bhavati sarvādhika ityabhiprāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the three worlds, heaven, the mortal world, and the underworld, he becomes a giver; the intended sense is that he is supreme over all.

children.text: so'pi pumān iha bhuvanatritaye svargamṛtyupātāle sraṣṭā sarjako bhavati ||
children.translated_text: That man too becomes here, in the three worlds, heaven, the mortal world, and the underworld, a creator, one who brings forth.
Like whom? Like <s>Padmayoni</s>, that is, like <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: punaḥ bhartā pālanārthaṃ trikasya viṣṇuriva ca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Again, he becomes the maintainer of the three for the sake of protection, like <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: punaḥ saṃhartā rudravat bhavati sṛṣṭisthitivināśeṣu brahmādīnāṃ trayīva syādityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, he becomes a destroyer like <s>Rudra</s>; the meaning is that in creation, maintenance, and destruction he is like the triad beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.
He states the procedure and qualities of the <s>Amarasundarī-guṭikā</s>, beginning with "kānta."
<s>Kānta</s> is magnet; <s>abhra</s> is mica; these are a pair.

children.text: abhrakasattvaṃ pratītaṃ hema kanakaṃ tāraṃ ca tat ekavadbhāvo dvandvatvāt punararkaḥ tāmram eṣāṃ kāntādīnāṃ saṃkhyā gaṇanā samāṃśataḥ samabhāgato jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: The essence of mica is well known; <s>hema</s> is gold, <s>tāra</s> is silver, and <s>arka</s> is copper. Since there is a compound with dual value, these are treated as one expression. The measure of these, beginning with <s>kānta</s>, is to be known in equal parts.

children.text: punaḥ sūtasamāṃśaṃ pāradena tulyabhāgaṃ dhmātaṃ kuryāt andhamūṣāyāṃ iti śeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, it should be smelted in a part equal to the <s>sūta</s>, equal in measure to the mercury; the words "in a closed crucible" are supplied.

children.text: kiṃkṛtaṃ sat bāhye baddhagolopari rasena māraṇāyām uktadraveṇa liptaṃ sat dhmātaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: When it has been coated externally, on top of the bound pellet, with the liquid stated in the killing procedure for <s>rasa</s>, it should be smelted.

children.text: itthaṃ kṛtaṃ khoṭaṃ piṣṭistambhaḥ golākāraṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The mass thus made becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>, a compact lump of paste, spherical in form.

children.text: tat vadanagataṃ mukhāntaḥsthitaṃ śastravārakaṃ syāt asmiṃśca vadanaṃ gate sati śarīre khaḍgādīnāṃ prahāro na lagati ||
children.translated_text: When that is placed in the mouth, situated inside the mouth, it wards off weapons. When it has entered the mouth, blows from swords and the like do not fall upon the body.

children.text: guṭir iyaṃ nāmnā abhidhānena amarasundarīguṭikā jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: This pill should be known by the name <s>Amarasundarī-guṭikā</s>.

children.text: iyaṃ śarīrasthā mukhe anyasthale vā sthitā satī śarīrasthān rogān hanti vināśayati ||
children.translated_text: When this is located on the body, whether in the mouth or in another place, it destroys and eliminates diseases situated in the body.
Although not stated, its measure should be understood as five <s>niṣkas</s>.
Thus ends the <s>Amarasundarī-guṭikā</s>.

children.text: hemnā vā rajatena vāpi sahito dhmāto vrajatyekatāmakṣīṇo niviḍo guḍaśca guṭikāḥ karoti dīrghojjvalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When smelted together with gold or also with silver, it reaches unity. Unwasted and compact, it makes bright, elongated pills.

children.text: cūrṇaṃ tatpaṭuvatprayāti vihitaghṛṣṭo na muñcenmalaṃ nirgandho dravati kṣaṇātsa hi mato baddhābhidhāno rasaḥ
children.translated_text: That powder becomes potent like salt; when properly rubbed, it does not release impurity. Odorless, it melts in an instant. This indeed is regarded as the <s>rasa</s> called bound.
Thus in another treatise.
He states the procedure and qualities of the <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī-guṭikā</s>, beginning with "ya."

children.text: yaḥ pūrvoktaḥ sūto lakṣādūrdhvaṃ koṭyarbudādi lohān rūpyādīn vedhate tasminbaddhe sūte mukhasthe prakāśamukhayantre sthāpite sāraṇayogaiḥ sāraṇatailādibhiḥ ratnaṃ vajrādikaṃ jārayet ||
children.translated_text: The previously mentioned <s>sūta</s>, which pierces metals such as silver above a lakh, a crore, an arbuda, and so on, should, when that bound <s>sūta</s> is in the mouth and placed in the bright-mouthed apparatus, digest a jewel such as diamond by means of <s>sāraṇa</s> preparations such as <s>sāraṇa</s> oil.

children.text: punaḥ samāṃśanāgais tulyāṃśasīsakaiḥ sūto yuktaḥ kāryaḥ suralohāyaskāntatāpyasattvaiśca yuktaḥ kāryaḥ suralohaṃ kanakaṃ ayaskāntaḥ kāntalohaṃ tāpyasattvaṃ mākṣikasāraṃ etaiḥ abhrakasattvasametā satī mṛtasaṃjīvanī nāma guṭikā bhavati punastatra mūṣāyāmiyaṃ hemayutā kāryā ||
children.translated_text: Again, the <s>sūta</s> should be made joined with equal parts of <s>nāga</s>, that is, with lead of equal measure, and it should be joined with the essences of divine metal, magnetic iron, and <s>tāpya</s>. Divine metal is gold; magnetic iron is <s>kāntaloha</s>; <s>tāpya-sattva</s> is the essence of <s>mākṣika</s>. Together with the essence of mica, this becomes the pill named <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s>. Again, there in the crucible, it should be made together with gold.

children.text: punar iyaṃ guṭikā nityaṃ yasya gulucchake nihitā bhavati vā mukuṭe kirīṭe vā kaṇṭhasūtrakarṇe kaṇṭhasūtraṃ ca karṇaśca kaṇṭhasūtrakarṇaṃ tasmin vā aṅge hastapādādau tasya mṛtyubhayaśokarogaśastrajarāsatataduḥkhasaṃghātaṃ naśyati ityadhyāhāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, for the person whose pill is always placed in a <s>gulucchaka</s>, or in a crown, or on a necklace or ear, or on a limb such as a hand or foot, the whole mass of death, fear, sorrow, disease, weapons, old age, and constant suffering is destroyed; this is to be supplied.

children.text: eteṣu sthāneṣu yasyeyaṃ nihitā sthāpitā bhavati sa asurayakṣakinnarapūjyatamaḥ asurā daityāḥ yakṣā devayonayaḥ kinnarāḥ turaṅgavaktrāḥ teṣāṃ pūjyatamo bhavati atiśayena pūjyaḥ pūjyatamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In whatever places this has been set and placed for someone, he becomes most worthy of worship by <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>kinnaras</s>. <s>Asuras</s> are demons, <s>yakṣas</s> are divine beings, and <s>kinnaras</s> are horse-faced beings; he is exceedingly worthy of worship among them.

children.text: siddhayogīndraiḥ pūjyatamaḥ siddhā devaviśeṣāḥ yogīndrā nāgārjunādayaḥ tato'nantaraṃ mṛtajīvanī jalamadhye kṣiptvā prakṣālya ghaṭikādvayaṃ vadanagatā satī mṛtakasya puruṣasyotthāpanaṃ prabodhanaṃ kurute yaḥ pumān puruṣaḥ tadeva toyaṃ guṭikākṣālanaṃ svacchaṃ nirmalaṃ pibati kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ pathyānvito hitāvahadravyabhakṣaṇayuktaḥ sa puruṣo divyaṃ vapuḥ devaśarīraṃ labhate kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ divyaṃ punaḥ mṛtyujarāvarjitaṃ vyādhipālityarahitaṃ punaḥ sudṛḍhaṃ vajravad guṭikāparimāṇaṃ pākavidhānaṃ ca pūrvavad ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Siddhas are special divine beings; the lords of yogins are <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and others. Thereafter, when the <s>Mṛtajīvanī</s> is thrown into water and washed, if it remains in the mouth for two <s>ghaṭikās</s>, it brings about the raising, that is, the awakening, of a dead man. The very man who drinks that water, the clear and pure water from washing the pill, while observing <s>pathya</s>, that is, taking wholesome substances, obtains a divine body, a body of the gods. Of what kind? Divine, and again free from death and old age, without disease and greying, and very firm like a thunderbolt. The measure of the pill and the method of cooking are as before. This is the meaning.
Thus ends the <s>Mṛtajīvanī-guṭikā</s>.
He states the procedure and the qualities of the <s>Vajriṇī-guṭikā</s>, beginning with "kānta."

children.text: kāntaṃ ca ghanaṃ ca anayoḥ sattvaṃ kāntaghanasattvaṃ kāntasattvaṃ cumbakasattvaṃ ghanasattvaṃ abhrakasāraṃ kamalaṃ ceti kamalaṃ tāmraṃ ca punarhema svarṇaṃ tāraṃ ca rūpyaṃ pūrvavat yathā yena vidhānena kṛtadvandvaṃ kṛtaṃ ca tat dvandvaṃ ceti bījavaraṃ samajīrṇaṃ kāryaṃ kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ bījavaraṃ vajrayutaṃ hīrakayutam iyaṃ guṭikā nāmato vajriṇī punareṣā vajriṇīguṭikā mukhakuharagatā satī mukhāntaḥprāptā satī navanāgatulyabalaṃ navasaṃkhyākā nāgāḥ hastinastaistulyaṃ tatsamaṃ yadbalaṃ tatkurute tadvapustasya mukhe guṭikādhāriṇo vapuḥ śarīraṃ durbhedyaṃ duḥkhena bhettuṃ śakyaṃ punarmṛtyujarāvyādhibhir nirmuktam ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s> and <s>ghana</s>: the essence of these two is <s>kānta-ghana-sattva</s>. <s>Kānta-sattva</s> is the essence of lodestone; <s>ghana-sattva</s> is the essence of mica; and <s>kamala</s> is copper. Again, <s>hema</s> is gold, and <s>tāra</s> is silver. As before, according to the procedure by which the pair was made, the excellent seed, consisting of that made pair, should be made equally digested. Of what kind is this excellent seed? Joined with <s>vajra</s>, that is, with diamond. This pill is called <s>Vajriṇī</s>. Again, when this <s>Vajriṇī-guṭikā</s> has entered the cavity of the mouth, it produces strength equal to that of nine elephants; nine <s>nāgas</s> are elephants, and the strength equal to them is what it produces. The body of the person who holds the pill in his mouth becomes hard to pierce, capable of being pierced only with difficulty, and is freed from death, old age, and diseases. This is the meaning.
Thus ends the <s>Vajriṇī-guṭikā</s>.
He states the procedure and the qualities of the <s>Khecarī-guṭikā</s>, beginning with "dhūma."

children.text: dhūmāvalokite dhūmavedhini rase sūte pañcamahāratnajārite pañcasaṃkhyākair mahāratnair vajrādibhiḥ tathā ca
children.translated_text: In <s>rasa</s>, that is, mercury, called <s>dhūmāvalokita</s> and <s>dhūmavedhin</s>, digested with the five great jewels, namely the five great jewels beginning with diamond, and likewise:

children.text: vajraṃ ca mauktikaṃ caiva māṇikyaṃ nīlameva ca
children.translated_text: "Diamond and pearl, and also ruby and sapphire,
and emerald should be known as the five kinds of great jewels."
Thus it is said.

children.text: punar mākṣikakāntaprayuktena tāpyacumbakamilitena bījena rase gaganasattve sārite sati khecarasaṃjñā guṭikā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Again, when, by means of a seed prepared with <s>mākṣika</s> and <s>kānta</s>, that is, with <s>tāpya</s> mixed with lodestone, the <s>rasa</s> has been caused to take in the essence of <s>gagana</s>, the pill called <s>Khecara</s> comes into being.

children.text: tasmin guṭikārūpe rase kṣiptamātreṇa mukhe patati sati indrādyaiḥ devāsurasiddhagaṇaiśca pūjyatamo bhavati indro maghavā ādyo yeṣāṃ te taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When that <s>rasa</s> in the form of a pill is merely placed in the mouth, when it has fallen into the mouth, the person becomes most worthy of worship by <s>Indra</s> and the rest, and by the hosts of gods, demons, and Siddhas; <s>Indra</s> is <s>Maghavan</s>, and those whose first member is he are meant by "<s>Indra</s> and the rest."

children.text: devā amarāḥ asurāḥ daityāḥ siddhā devaviśeṣāḥ teṣāṃ ye gaṇāḥ samūhāḥ taiḥ kṛtvā atiśayena pūjyo bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods are immortals; the demons are Daityas; the Siddhas are special divine beings. By the hosts, that is, the groups, of these, he becomes exceedingly worthy of worship. This is the meaning.
Thus ends the pill called <s>Khecara</s>.
Indicating the endlessness of <s>rasavāda</s>, he says, beginning with "rasa."

children.text: rasavādo 'nantaguṇaḥ anantā guṇā yasya sa tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rasavāda</s> has endless qualities; it is so called because its qualities are endless.
"Endless" means immeasurable.

children.text: kena kṛtvā rasavādo'nantaḥ dravagolakakalkānāṃ pratyekamanantatvāt rasavādo'pyanantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By reason of what is <s>rasavāda</s> endless? Because liquids, balls, and pastes are each endless, <s>rasavāda</s> too is endless.
Of what kind is it? Fashioned, that is, composed, by the foremost Siddhas, such as <s>Nityanātha</s>.

children.text: yairmahadbhiḥ siddhaiḥ rasavādo dṛṣṭaste narā jayanti sarvotkarṣeṇa vartante ||
children.translated_text: The men by whom, as great Siddhas, <s>rasavāda</s> has been seen, are victorious; they abide in complete preeminence.
Now he describes the lineage of the maker of the treatise, beginning with "śītāṃśu-vaṃśa."

children.text: śrīmadano madanābhidho rājā jayati sarvotkarṣeṇa vartate ||
children.translated_text: The illustrious <s>Madana</s>, the king named <s>Madana</s>, is victorious; he abides in complete preeminence.
Of what kind is he? Lord of the Kirātas; the Kirātas are Bhillas, and he is their master.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭaḥ śītāṃśuvaṃśasaṃbhavahaihayakulajanmajanitaguṇamahimā śītāṃśuvaṃśe candravaṃśe saṃbhava utpattiryasya tat evaṃvidhaṃ yat haihayakulaṃ tatra kule janmanā udbhavena janito guṇānāṃ mahimā yena sa tathoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what kind is he? He is one whose greatness of qualities was produced by birth in the Haihaya family, born in the lineage of the moon. <s>Śītāṃśu-vaṃśa</s> means the lunar lineage, in which he had origin; and in that Haihaya family, by birth, that is, by arising there, the greatness of his qualities was produced. Thus he is so described.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃviśiṣṭo madanaḥ rasācāryaḥ rasavidyājanaka ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what kind is <s>Madana</s>? He is a teacher of <s>rasa</s>, that is, a founder of the science of <s>rasa</s>.
And now he describes the qualities of this maker, beginning with "yasya."

children.text: yasya kārayituḥ śrīmadanasaṃjñasya rasavidyā svayaṃ svarūpatvenāvatīrṇā prādurbhūtā ||
children.translated_text: For this maker, the one called the illustrious <s>Madana</s>, <s>rasavidyā</s> herself descended, that is, became manifest, in her own form.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭā rasavidyā sakalamaṅgalādhārā sakalāni ca tāni maṅgalāni uttamarūpāṇi teṣāmādhāraḥ āśrayo yasyāṃ sā ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind is <s>rasavidyā</s>? She is the support of all auspicious things: all those auspicious things, of the highest form, have their support and basis in her.

children.text: eṣā rasavidyā śarīraṃ ajarāmaraṇaṃ ajarāmaraṃ kurute śarīraṃ ca dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ mūlaṃ ataḥ sakalamaṅgalādhāreti yuktam ||
children.translated_text: This <s>rasavidyā</s> makes the body free from old age and death; and the body is the root of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>. Therefore it is fitting that she is the support of all auspicious things.

children.text: punaḥ rasavidyā śreyase muktau parama utkṛṣṭo hetuḥ kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Again, <s>rasavidyā</s> is the supreme, the highest, cause of <s>śreyas</s>, that is, liberation.

children.text: anayaiva rasavidyayā parameṣṭhino brahmaṇaḥ pūrvaṃ prathamaṃ śreyo 'jarāmaraṇarūpaṃ saṃjātam ||
children.translated_text: By this very <s>rasavidyā</s>, in the beginning, <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, obtained <s>śreyas</s> in the form of freedom from old age and death.
Indicating the greatness of his own name, the author says, beginning with "tasmāt."

children.text: idaṃ rasatantraṃ śāstraṃ viracitavān kṛtavāniti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He composed this <s>rasatantra</s>, this treatise; such is the sense.

children.text: kiṃviśiṣṭaṃ idaṃ tantraṃ rasahṛdayākhyaṃ kiṃ kṛtvā tasmādityādi ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind is this <s>tantra</s>? It is called <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>. Having done what? This is to be understood from the passage beginning with "tasmāt."
